model_requirements.description: I am an electric and gas utility with energy generation, transmission, and distribution to serve residential and commercial customers

model.name: Power and Utilities
model.description: I am an electric and gas utility with energy generation, transmission, and distribution to serve residential and commercial customers
model.core_business_processes: Energy Generation (fossil fuel; nuclear; renewable power plant operations), Power Transmission (high-voltage bulk electricity transport across grid infrastructure), Electric Distribution (last-mile delivery of electricity to end-use customers), Gas Distribution (natural gas pipeline delivery to residential and commercial customers), Metering and Meter Data Management (AMI deployment; smart meter reads; interval data collection), Customer Enrollment and Account Management (service applications; move-in/move-out; account maintenance), Billing and Revenue Management (rate application; invoice generation; payment processing; collections), Demand Response and Load Management (peak shaving; demand-side management programs; curtailment events), Asset Management and Maintenance (preventive and corrective maintenance of generation; transmission; and distribution assets), Regulatory Compliance and Rate Case Management (tariff filings; rate case preparation; regulatory reporting to PUCs and FERC)
model.data_domains: Customer, Metering, Billing, Generation, Transmission, Distribution, Asset Management, Workforce, Regulatory, Energy Market, Supply Chain, Finance
model.common_business_jargons: kWh (Kilowatt-Hour), MWh (Megawatt-Hour), MW (Megawatt), kW (Kilowatt), MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet of gas), Therm (unit of heat energy for gas billing), AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure), AMR (Automated Meter Reading), SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition), OMS (Outage Management System), DMS (Distribution Management System), EMS (Energy Management System), GIS (Geographic Information System), CIS (Customer Information System), MDMS (Meter Data Management System), DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System), DER (Distributed Energy Resource), RTO (Regional Transmission Organization), ISO (Independent System Operator), PUC (Public Utility Commission), FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission), NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation), SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index), SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index), CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index), T&D (Transmission and Distribution), O&M (Operations and Maintenance), CPCN (Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity), IRP (Integrated Resource Plan), RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard), PPA (Power Purchase Agreement), LMP (Locational Marginal Price), DAM (Day-Ahead Market), RTM (Real-Time Market), OATT (Open Access Transmission Tariff), NEM (Net Energy Metering), TOU (Time-of-Use rate), CPP (Critical Peak Pricing), EV (Electric Vehicle), DR (Demand Response), DSM (Demand-Side Management), EE (Energy Efficiency), GHG (Greenhouse Gas), REC (Renewable Energy Certificate), SoCalGas-style BCF (Billion Cubic Feet), EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest Taxes Depreciation and Amortization), ROE (Return on Equity), ROI (Return on Investment), CAPEX (Capital Expenditure), OPEX (Operating Expenditure), PBR (Performance-Based Ratemaking), CHP (Combined Heat and Power), HRSG (Heat Recovery Steam Generator), CT (Combustion Turbine), CC (Combined Cycle), BES (Bulk Electric System), FAC Management System), CRM (Customer Relationship Management), ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning), ETL (Extract Transform Load), SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act), GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles)
model.operational_systems_of_records: Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U (Customer Information and Billing System), Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo (Enterprise Asset Management), ESRI ArcGIS (Geospatial Information System for network mapping), OSIsoft PI or GE Proficy (Historian / SCADA data platform), Oracle Utilities MDMS or Itron Analytics (Meter Data Management System), Schneider Electric AMS or GE PowerOn (Outage Management System / DMS), SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud (Enterprise Resource Planning - Finance; HR; Supply Chain), Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud (Customer Relationship Management), ABB or GE Energy Management System (Generation dispatch and grid balancing), SuccessFactors or Workday (Human Capital Management)
model.industry_governing_body: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), State Public Utility Commissions (PUCs), U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC), Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), American Gas Association (AGA)

domains.name: generation
domains.description: Owns all data related to energy generation assets and operations — fossil fuel, nuclear, and renewable power plant operations including unit dispatch, fuel management, capacity planning, heat rate optimization, emissions monitoring, and generation output (MWh). Serves as the SSOT for generation facility master data, real-time EMS/SCADA telemetry, and plant performance metrics. Supports IRP, RPS compliance, and PPA tracking.
domains.references: NERC Reliability Standards, IEEE C37, EPA

products.name: plant
products.description: Master record for each power generation facility operated by the utility — fossil fuel (CT, CC, coal), nuclear, and renewable (solar, wind, hydro). Captures plant name, NERC plant code, fuel type, technology type (combined cycle, combustion turbine, steam, photovoltaic, wind turbine, hydro), ISO/RTO interconnection region, nameplate capacity (MW), commercial operation date, retirement date, FERC plant ID, state/county location, GIS coordinates, regulatory jurisdiction (PUC, FERC), plant status (operating, mothballed, retired, under construction), and ownership percentage. Serves as the SSOT for generation facility master data and the anchor entity for all generation domain products. Sourced from ABB/GE Energy Management System and SAP S/4HANA asset registry.
products.reference: NERC Generating Unit Registration / FERC Form 860

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the power generation facility. Primary key for the plant entity.

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Generation plants are subject to specific compliance obligations (emissions limits, reliability standards, renewable portfolio standards) based on their fuel type, capacity, and jurisdiction. Linking

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Plants are cost centers for O&M expense tracking, budget allocation, and FERC functional accounting. Required for monthly variance reporting, budget vs actual analysis, and regulatory cost allocation

attributes.name: cpcn_docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Each generation plant's legal authority to operate originates from a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) proceeding conducted through a regulatory docket. Tracking the authorizing d

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Generation plants are physical capital assets that must be tracked in the enterprise asset management system. This FK enables lifecycle tracking, maintenance scheduling, and regulatory asset base calc

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: Generation plants physically interconnect to transmission substations at specific voltage levels. Essential for real-time dispatch coordination, NERC compliance (MOD-001, TOP-002), outage coordination

attributes.name: balancing_authority
attributes.description: The NERC-registered balancing authority responsible for real-time generation-load balance and frequency control in the area where the plant operates. Critical for SCADA integration and dispatch coordination.
attributes.references: NERC Balancing Authority Registry; NERC Standard BAL-001

attributes.name: capacity_factor_percent
attributes.description: Ratio of actual energy output to maximum possible output over a reporting period, expressed as a percentage. Used for renewable energy performance tracking, asset utilization analysis, and Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) performance guarantees.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923; NERC Generation Availability Data System (GADS)

attributes.name: commercial_operation_date
attributes.description: Date when the generation facility began commercial electricity production and became eligible for market participation and revenue generation. Used for depreciation calculations, Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) milestone tracking, and Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) eligibility.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; ISO/RTO Interconnection Agreements

attributes.name: construction_year
attributes.description: Year when the generation facility was originally constructed or substantially completed. Used for depreciation calculations, asset age analysis, and capital planning.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP Fixed Asset Accounting

attributes.name: county
attributes.description: County or parish where the generation facility is located. Used for property tax assessment, local permitting, and environmental impact reporting.
attributes.references: U.S. Census Bureau County Codes; Local Government Tax Records

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the plant master record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage tracking and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Data Governance Framework; SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: eia_plant_code
attributes.description: U.S. Department of Energy EIA-assigned unique identifier for the generation facility used in EIA-860 and EIA-923 reporting.

attributes.name: emissions_controlled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation facility is equipped with emissions control technology (scrubbers, selective catalytic reduction, carbon capture). Used for EPA compliance reporting, Greenhouse Gas (GHG) inventory, and environmental cost allocation.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act; EPA Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) Requirements

attributes.name: ems_resource_reference
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned to the generation facility within the utility's Energy Management System (EMS) or SCADA platform. Used for real-time dispatch instructions, telemetry data correlation, and outage coordination.
attributes.references: ABB/GE EMS Configuration Standards; ISO/RTO Telemetry Protocols

attributes.name: ferc_plant_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Identifier
attributes.description: FERC-assigned unique identifier for the generation facility used in FERC Form 1 reporting and rate case filings.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Primary fuel source used by the generation facility for energy production. Critical for fuel management, emissions tracking, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|nuclear|solar|wind|hydro|oil|biomass|geothermal|dual_fuel — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EIA Fuel Type Classification; EPA Emissions Reporting

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heat Rate (British Thermal Units per Kilowatt-Hour)
attributes.description: Thermal efficiency measure representing the amount of fuel energy (BTU) required to produce one kilowatt-hour (kWh) of electricity. Lower values indicate higher efficiency. Used for fuel cost forecasting, dispatch merit order, and performance benchmarking.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923; FERC Form 1; ASME Performance Test Codes

attributes.name: interconnection_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Voltage level in kilovolts (kV) at which the generation facility connects to the transmission or distribution grid. Determines transmission access charges and Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) applicability.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; IEEE Voltage Standards; ISO/RTO Interconnection Agreements

attributes.name: iso_rto_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Region
attributes.description: The ISO or RTO market region where the generation facility is interconnected and participates in wholesale electricity markets. Determines market rules, Locational Marginal Price (LMP) settlement, and transmission tariff obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CAISO|ERCOT|ISONE|MISO|NYISO|PJM|SPP|non_iso — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; ISO/RTO Tariffs; NERC Regional Entity Boundaries

attributes.name: last_major_upgrade_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent major capital upgrade or refurbishment that extended the useful life or increased the capacity of the generation facility. Used for depreciation recalculation and Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the plant master record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and synchronization with downstream systems.
attributes.references: Data Governance Framework; SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the generation facility in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, weather correlation analysis, and transmission planning.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate System; ESRI ArcGIS Standards

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the generation facility in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, and transmission line routing.
attributes.references: WGS84 Coordinate System; ESRI ArcGIS Standards

attributes.name: minimum_load_mw
attributes.description: Minimum stable operating output level in megawatts (MW) below which the generation unit cannot operate reliably. Used for unit commitment decisions, ancillary service qualification, and dispatch constraint modeling.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Market Rules; NERC Operating Reliability Standards

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum rated electrical output capacity of the generation facility in megawatts (MW) under ideal operating conditions. Used for capacity market obligations, resource adequacy planning, and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) modeling.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; NERC Resource Registration; ISO/RTO Capacity Market Rules

attributes.name: nerc_plant_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Plant Code
attributes.description: NERC-assigned unique identifier for the generation facility used in Bulk Electric System (BES) registration and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: net_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Actual electrical output capacity available for delivery to the grid after accounting for auxiliary load and station service requirements. Used for dispatch scheduling and market settlement.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Registration; ISO/RTO Market Settlement

attributes.name: operator_name
attributes.description: Name of the entity responsible for day-to-day operations and maintenance of the generation facility. May differ from the owner in cases of third-party operations and maintenance (O&M) contracts.
attributes.references: NERC Compliance Registry; ISO/RTO Market Participant Registration

attributes.name: ownership_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the generation facility owned by the utility, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 100.00 for wholly-owned, 50.00 for joint venture). Used for capacity allocation, cost allocation, and FERC Form 1 reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: plant_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to the generation facility for operational and regulatory identification. Used in dispatch instructions, market bids, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: NERC Plant Code Standard; ISO/RTO Registration

attributes.name: plant_name
attributes.description: Official name of the power generation facility as registered with regulatory authorities and used in operational communications.

attributes.name: plant_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle state of the generation facility. Determines availability for dispatch, capacity market participation, and regulatory reporting obligations.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Registration; ISO/RTO Market Rules

attributes.name: ppa_contract_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation facility operates under a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the utility or third-party offtaker. Used for revenue forecasting, contract administration, and regulatory cost recovery filings.
attributes.references: FERC PPA Filing Requirements; State PUC Contract Approval Rules

attributes.name: primary_use
attributes.description: Operational dispatch classification describing the typical role of the generation facility in meeting system load. Used for unit commitment optimization, capacity factor analysis, and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) modeling.
attributes.references: NERC Generation Resource Types; ISO/RTO Market Participation Rules

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_minute
attributes.description: Maximum rate at which the generation facility can increase or decrease output, measured in megawatts per minute. Critical for frequency regulation, load following, and renewable integration support.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Ancillary Service Requirements; NERC Standard BAL-001

attributes.name: rec_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation facility is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) for compliance with state RPS mandates or voluntary green power programs.
attributes.references: State RPS Regulations; NERC e-Tag Standards for REC Tracking

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Primary regulatory authority with rate-setting and operational oversight for the generation facility. Determines rate case filing requirements, prudency review processes, and cost recovery mechanisms.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act; State PUC Enabling Statutes; FERC Jurisdictional Determinations

attributes.name: renewable_energy_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation facility qualifies as a renewable energy resource under state Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) programs and federal Production Tax Credit (PTC) or Investment Tax Credit (ITC) eligibility.
attributes.references: State RPS Statutes; IRS Publication 946; EIA Renewable Energy Classification

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when the generation facility ceased or will cease commercial operations. Used for capacity planning, asset retirement obligation (ARO) accounting, and regulatory decommissioning filings.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; State PUC Retirement Filings; GAAP ASC 410

attributes.name: scada_integration_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Integration Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation facility is integrated with the utility's Energy Management System (EMS) or SCADA platform for real-time telemetry, dispatch control, and automatic generation control (AGC).
attributes.references: NERC Standard CIP-002; ISO/RTO Telemetry Requirements

attributes.name: startup_time_hours
attributes.description: Time required in hours to bring the generation unit from offline to minimum load under normal conditions. Used for day-ahead market bidding, unit commitment optimization, and reliability planning.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Market Rules; NERC Generation Availability Data System (GADS)

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state abbreviation where the generation facility is physically located. Determines state Public Utility Commission (PUC) jurisdiction, Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) eligibility, and emissions regulations.

attributes.name: technology_type
attributes.description: Generation technology classification describing the conversion process from fuel to electricity. Used for heat rate analysis, dispatch optimization, and capacity planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: combined_cycle|combustion_turbine|steam_turbine|photovoltaic|wind_turbine|hydroelectric|nuclear_reactor|battery_storage — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EIA Technology Classification; NERC Generation Resource Types

products.name: generating_unit
products.description: Individual generating unit (boiler-turbine set, nuclear reactor unit, wind turbine, solar inverter block, hydro unit) within a plant. Tracks unit name, unit type, prime mover code (ST, GT, IC, HY, PV, WT per EIA-860), fuel primary/secondary, installed capacity (MW), net summer capacity (MW), net winter capacity (MW), heat rate (BTU/kWh), minimum stable load (MW), ramp rate (MW/min), unit status (available, forced outage, planned outage, derated, retired), synchronization date, and NERC unit ID. Enables unit-level dispatch, heat rate optimization, and capacity reporting. Sourced from ABB/GE EMS and NERC GADS submissions.
products.reference: EIA Form 860 / NERC GADS Unit Record

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the generating unit. Primary key for the generating unit entity.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Individual generating units track O&M costs separately for unit-level performance analysis, heat rate economics, and regulatory cost allocation. Essential for unit profitability analysis and FERC Form

attributes.name: cpcn_docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Individual generating units often require separate CPCN approval, especially for capacity additions or repowering projects. Linking units to their authorizing dockets supports cost recovery filings, p

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Generating units (turbines, generators, boilers) are major capital assets requiring comprehensive asset management. This FK enables work order tracking, failure analysis, and depreciation calculations

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent generation plant or facility where this unit is located.

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: Individual generating units interconnect at specific substations for unit-level dispatch instructions and protection coordination. Required for security-constrained unit commitment, real-time AGC sign

attributes.name: ancillary_services_capable
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ancillary services the generating unit is technically capable of providing (e.g., regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support, black start).
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, RTO/ISO Ancillary Service Markets

attributes.name: balancing_authority
attributes.description: NERC-registered Balancing Authority responsible for integrating resource plans, maintaining load-interchange-generation balance, and supporting interconnection frequency in real time for the area where this unit operates.

attributes.name: black_start_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generating unit has black start capability, meaning it can start without external electrical supply and help restore the grid after a blackout. True if capable, False otherwise.

attributes.name: capacity_factor_target_pct
attributes.description: Target or expected capacity factor for the generating unit, expressed as a percentage. Capacity factor is the ratio of actual output over a period to the maximum possible output if the unit operated at full capacity continuously.

attributes.name: carbon_capture_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generating unit is equipped with carbon capture and storage (CCS) or carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technology. True if equipped, False otherwise.

attributes.name: commercial_operation_date
attributes.description: Date when the generating unit first entered commercial service and began producing electricity for sale or delivery to the grid.

attributes.name: cooling_system_type
attributes.description: Type of cooling system used by the generating unit for thermal plants. Once Through=direct water cooling, Recirculating=cooling tower with water reuse, Dry Cooling=air-cooled condenser, Hybrid=combination system, None=not applicable for non-thermal units.

attributes.name: dispatch_priority
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking used by the Energy Management System (EMS) for economic dispatch and unit commitment decisions. Lower numbers indicate higher priority.

attributes.name: eia_generator_code
attributes.description: Energy Information Administration (EIA) unique identifier for the generator, used in EIA-860 and EIA-923 regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: emissions_control_equipment
attributes.description: Description of installed emissions control technologies (e.g., Selective Catalytic Reduction for NOx, Flue Gas Desulfurization for SO2, Electrostatic Precipitator for particulates, Carbon Capture and Storage).
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Reporting, EIA-860

attributes.name: fuel_primary
attributes.description: Primary fuel type consumed by the generating unit (e.g., natural gas, coal, uranium, wind, solar, water). Aligns with EIA fuel type codes.

attributes.name: fuel_secondary
attributes.description: Secondary or backup fuel type that the unit can consume, if applicable. Null for units with single fuel capability.

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: Measure of generating unit thermal efficiency, expressed as British Thermal Units (BTU) of fuel energy input required to produce one kilowatt-hour (kWh) of electrical output. Lower values indicate higher efficiency.

attributes.name: interconnection_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Voltage level in kilovolts (kV) at which the generating unit interconnects to the transmission or distribution grid.

attributes.name: last_major_overhaul_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent major overhaul, refurbishment, or life-extension project performed on the generating unit.

attributes.name: manufacturer
attributes.description: Name of the manufacturer or original equipment manufacturer (OEM) of the primary generating equipment (turbine, generator, or inverter).

attributes.name: minimum_stable_load_mw
attributes.description: Minimum output level at which the generating unit can operate continuously in a stable manner without shutting down, measured in Megawatts (MW).

attributes.name: model_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer model number or designation of the generating equipment.

attributes.name: must_run_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generating unit has been designated as a must-run or reliability-must-run (RMR) unit by the RTO/ISO or Balancing Authority for grid reliability purposes. True if designated, False otherwise.

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum rated output of the generator under ideal conditions as specified by the manufacturer, measured in Megawatts (MW).

attributes.name: nerc_unit_code
attributes.description: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) unique identifier for the generating unit, used in NERC GADS reporting and reliability coordination.

attributes.name: net_summer_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum net output the unit can sustain over a specified period under summer ambient conditions, accounting for station service loads, measured in Megawatts (MW).

attributes.name: net_winter_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum net output the unit can sustain over a specified period under winter ambient conditions, accounting for station service loads, measured in Megawatts (MW).

attributes.name: next_scheduled_outage_date
attributes.description: Date of the next planned maintenance outage for the generating unit. Used for outage coordination and resource adequacy planning.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Legal ownership or contractual arrangement for the generating unit. Owned=utility-owned asset, Leased=leased from third party, PPA=Power Purchase Agreement with independent producer, Tolling=fuel conversion service agreement, Joint Ownership=shared ownership with other utilities.

attributes.name: planned_retirement_date
attributes.description: Anticipated date for permanent retirement of the generating unit, if known. Used for long-term resource planning and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) development.

attributes.name: prime_mover_code
attributes.description: EIA-860 standard code identifying the type of prime mover (engine or turbine) that drives the generator. ST=Steam Turbine, GT=Gas Turbine, IC=Internal Combustion, CA=Combined Cycle Steam, CT=Combustion Turbine, CS=Combined Cycle Single Shaft, CC=Combined Cycle, CE=Compressed Air Energy Storage, HY=Hydraulic Turbine, PS=Pumped Storage, PV=Photovoltaic, WT=Wind Turbine, WS=Wind Turbine Offshore, FC=Fuel Cell, ES=Energy Storage, OT=Other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ST|GT|IC|CA|CT|CS|CC|CE|HY|PS|PV|WT|WS|FC|ES|OT — 16 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_min
attributes.description: Maximum rate at which the generating unit can increase or decrease its output, measured in Megawatts per minute (MW/min). Critical for dispatch flexibility and grid balancing.

attributes.name: renewable_energy_credit_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generating unit is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) under applicable Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) programs. True if eligible, False otherwise.
attributes.references: State RPS Programs, REC Tracking Systems

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date when the generating unit was permanently retired from service. Null for active units.

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.description: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) market region in which the generating unit participates (e.g., PJM, CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP).

attributes.name: scada_point_reference
attributes.description: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system identifier or tag name for real-time telemetry data from this generating unit.

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number assigned by the manufacturer to the generating equipment unit.

attributes.name: synchronization_date
attributes.description: Date when the generating unit was first synchronized to the electrical grid for testing or initial operation.

attributes.name: technology_type
attributes.description: Detailed technology classification of the generating unit (e.g., supercritical coal, combined cycle gas turbine, pressurized water reactor, onshore wind, utility-scale solar PV, pumped hydro storage).

attributes.name: unit_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code or designation for the generating unit, used in operational systems and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: unit_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the generating unit (e.g., Boiler 1, Turbine A, Wind Turbine 42, Solar Inverter Block 3).

attributes.name: unit_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the generating unit in its lifecycle. Available=ready for dispatch, Operating=currently generating, Forced Outage=unplanned unavailability, Planned Outage=scheduled maintenance, Derated=operating below full capacity, Standby=ready but not dispatched, Retired=permanently out of service, Mothballed=temporarily preserved for potential future use. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: available|operating|forced_outage|planned_outage|derated|standby|retired|mothballed — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: unit_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the generating unit by energy source or technology type. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fossil|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|geothermal|biomass|storage|other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: water_source
attributes.description: Primary water source used for cooling or other plant operations (e.g., river, lake, ocean, groundwater, municipal supply). Applicable to thermal and hydro units.

products.name: dispatch_schedule
products.description: Day-ahead and real-time generation dispatch schedule for each generating unit, produced by the ABB/GE Energy Management System (EMS) in coordination with the RTO/ISO. Records schedule date, operating hour, scheduled MW output, economic dispatch MW, must-run flag, dispatch type (economic, reliability, emergency), fuel burn forecast (MMBTU), associated LMP node, RTO/ISO control area, and schedule version. Supports unit commitment optimization, fuel procurement planning, and RTO settlement reconciliation. Distinct from unit_output which captures actual generation — this product captures the planned/scheduled generation that drives commitment decisions. Sourced from ABB/GE EMS dispatch engine.
products.reference: NERC MOD-025 / RTO Day-Ahead Market Schedule

attributes.name: dispatch_schedule_id
attributes.description: Primary key for dispatch_schedule

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific generating unit (power plant unit) for which this dispatch schedule applies. Links to the generating unit master data.

attributes.name: grid_topology_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.grid_topology. Business justification: Dispatch schedules are calculated against specific network topology models for security-constrained economic dispatch. Critical for day-ahead and real-time market clearing, congestion management, and

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) contract if this generation is procured under a PPA rather than owned generation. Used for contract settlement and cost allocation.

attributes.name: pricing_node_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) pricing node associated with this generating unit. Used for settlement and revenue calculation in wholesale energy markets.

attributes.name: ancillary_service_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether the unit is scheduled to provide ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support) during this operating hour.

attributes.name: commitment_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether the unit commitment decision has been finalized for this schedule. True indicates the unit is committed to operate; False indicates the schedule is preliminary or advisory.

attributes.name: control_area
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Control Area
attributes.description: The RTO/ISO control area or balancing authority area in which the generating unit operates. Examples include PJM, CAISO, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP.

attributes.name: dispatch_instruction_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the dispatch instruction was issued by the Energy Management System (EMS) or RTO/ISO. Represents the business event time for the dispatch decision.

attributes.name: dispatch_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the dispatch schedule. Scheduled indicates initial plan; committed means unit commitment decision made; dispatched means unit is operating per schedule; cancelled or revised indicate changes.

attributes.name: dispatch_type
attributes.description: Classification of the dispatch instruction based on the operational driver. Economic dispatch follows least-cost optimization; reliability dispatch addresses grid constraints; emergency dispatch responds to system contingencies; regulation and load-following provide ancillary services.

attributes.name: economic_dispatch_mw
attributes.description: The economically optimal generation output in megawatts based on marginal cost optimization and Locational Marginal Price (LMP) signals. May differ from scheduled MW if reliability or must-run constraints apply.

attributes.name: emissions_rate_lbs_per_mwh
attributes.description: The forecasted emissions rate in pounds per megawatt-hour for the scheduled generation. Typically represents CO2, NOx, or SO2 emissions depending on regulatory reporting requirements.

attributes.name: forecast_load_mw
attributes.description: The forecasted system load in megawatts for the control area during the scheduled operating hour. Provides context for the dispatch decision and unit commitment optimization.

attributes.name: fuel_burn_forecast_mmbtu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fuel Burn Forecast Million British Thermal Units (MMBTU)
attributes.description: Forecasted fuel consumption in million British Thermal Units (MMBTU) required to produce the scheduled generation output. Used for fuel procurement planning and cost forecasting.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The primary fuel source used by the generating unit. Used for fuel procurement planning, emissions tracking, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|oil|biomass — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heat Rate British Thermal Units (BTU) per Kilowatt-Hour (kWh)
attributes.description: The expected heat rate in BTU per kWh for the unit at the scheduled output level. Represents the thermal efficiency of the generating unit. Lower heat rates indicate higher efficiency.

attributes.name: marginal_cost_usd_per_mwh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Marginal Cost United States Dollars (USD) per Megawatt-Hour (MWh)
attributes.description: The incremental cost in US dollars per megawatt-hour to produce the next unit of energy at the scheduled output level. Used in economic dispatch optimization and bid cost recovery calculations.

attributes.name: maximum_generation_mw
attributes.description: The maximum generation capacity in megawatts available from the unit during the operating hour. Represents the upper operating limit considering unit capability and any derates.

attributes.name: minimum_down_time_hours
attributes.description: The minimum number of consecutive hours the unit must remain offline once shut down. Operational constraint based on cooling requirements and thermal stress limits.

attributes.name: minimum_generation_mw
attributes.description: The minimum stable generation level in megawatts that the unit can sustain during the operating hour. Represents the lower operating limit for the unit.

attributes.name: minimum_up_time_hours
attributes.description: The minimum number of consecutive hours the unit must remain online once started. Operational constraint based on unit design and thermal stress limits.

attributes.name: must_run_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether the unit is designated as must-run for reliability purposes. Must-run units are committed regardless of economic merit to maintain grid stability, voltage support, or local reliability.

attributes.name: operating_hour
attributes.description: The hour of the day (0-23) for which this dispatch schedule applies. Represents the hour-ending convention used in energy markets.

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_min
attributes.description: The maximum rate at which the generating unit can increase or decrease output, measured in megawatts per minute. Critical for load-following and frequency regulation services.

attributes.name: regulation_reserve_mw
attributes.description: The amount of generation capacity in megawatts reserved for automatic generation control (AGC) regulation service. This capacity is held back from energy dispatch to provide frequency regulation.

attributes.name: schedule_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this dispatch schedule record was first created in the system. Audit timestamp for record creation.

attributes.name: schedule_date
attributes.description: The calendar date for which this dispatch schedule is effective. Used for day-ahead and real-time dispatch planning.

attributes.name: schedule_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, comments, or special instructions related to the dispatch schedule. May include reasons for out-of-merit dispatch, coordination notes, or operator remarks.

attributes.name: schedule_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system that generated this dispatch schedule. Typically the ABB or GE Energy Management System (EMS) dispatch engine, or the RTO/ISO market system.

attributes.name: schedule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the dispatch schedule based on market timing and purpose. Day-ahead schedules are produced 24 hours in advance; real-time schedules are produced hourly; reliability and emergency schedules address grid stability needs.

attributes.name: schedule_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this dispatch schedule record was last modified. Audit timestamp for record updates, capturing schedule revisions.

attributes.name: schedule_version
attributes.description: Version number of the dispatch schedule. Increments when schedules are revised due to updated forecasts, unit availability changes, or market conditions. Version 1 is typically the day-ahead schedule.

attributes.name: scheduled_mw_output
attributes.description: The planned generation output in megawatts (MW) for the generating unit during the specified operating hour. This is the target output level determined by the Energy Management System (EMS) dispatch optimization.

attributes.name: settlement_interval
attributes.description: The sub-hourly settlement interval (typically 5, 10, or 15 minutes) within the operating hour for which this schedule applies. Used in real-time markets with sub-hourly dispatch and settlement.

attributes.name: spinning_reserve_mw
attributes.description: The amount of synchronized generation capacity in megawatts held in reserve to respond to sudden generation or transmission outages within 10 minutes.

attributes.name: startup_cost_usd
attributes.description: The estimated cost in US dollars to start the generating unit from an offline state. Includes fuel, labor, and wear-and-tear costs. Used in unit commitment optimization.

attributes.name: startup_type
attributes.description: Classification of the unit startup condition if the unit is being committed from an offline state. Hot startup occurs within 8 hours of shutdown; warm startup within 8-48 hours; cold startup after 48+ hours. Affects startup time and costs.

attributes.name: transmission_constraint_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether transmission system constraints influenced the dispatch schedule. True indicates the unit was dispatched out-of-economic-merit to address transmission congestion or voltage issues.

products.name: unit_output
products.description: Actual real-time and interval generation output telemetry for each generating unit, collected via OSIsoft PI / GE Proficy SCADA historian at sub-hourly intervals (typically 5-minute or 15-minute). Captures interval timestamp, gross generation (MWh), net generation (MWh), auxiliary load (MWh), reactive power (MVAR), frequency, voltage, capacity factor (%), heat rate actual (BTU/kWh), steam flow, and data quality flag. Serves as the SSOT for actual MWh production used in RTO settlement, RPS compliance, and plant performance benchmarking. Sourced from OSIsoft PI historian.
products.reference: NERC GADS Performance Data / EIA Form 923

attributes.name: unit_output_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each unit output telemetry record. Primary key for the unit output data product.

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the generating unit (power plant unit) that produced this output measurement. Links to the generation unit master data.

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) contract under which this generation output was produced and sold. Null for merchant generation or utility-owned generation not under a PPA.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: Ambient air temperature at the plant site during the interval, measured in degrees Fahrenheit. Affects unit performance, especially for combustion turbines and air-cooled condensers. Used for temperature-corrected performance analysis.

attributes.name: auxiliary_load_mwh
attributes.description: Electrical energy consumed by the power plant's own auxiliary equipment (pumps, fans, controls, lighting) during the interval, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh). Deducted from gross generation to calculate net generation.

attributes.name: barometric_pressure_inhg
attributes.description: Barometric pressure at the plant site during the interval, measured in inches of mercury (inHg). Affects combustion turbine performance and is used for altitude and weather corrections in performance calculations.

attributes.name: capacity_factor_percent
attributes.description: Ratio of actual net generation to maximum possible generation (nameplate capacity) during the interval, expressed as a percentage. Key performance indicator for unit utilization and efficiency.

attributes.name: co2_emissions_tons
attributes.description: Carbon dioxide emissions produced during the interval, measured in short tons. Calculated from fuel consumption and emission factors or measured via continuous emissions monitoring system (CEMS). Required for greenhouse gas (GHG) reporting and carbon compliance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this unit output record was first created in the MDMS or data warehouse. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicates the quality and reliability of the telemetry data for this interval. Valid data passed all validation checks; estimated data was calculated due to sensor failure; missing data was not received; suspect data failed range checks; manual data was operator-entered; failed_validation data did not meet NERC or EPA quality standards.

attributes.name: dispatch_mode
attributes.description: The operational dispatch mode of the unit during the interval. Indicates how the unit was being operated: baseload (continuous), cycling (load-following), peaking (on-demand), must-run (reliability), economic (market-driven), or manual (operator-controlled).

attributes.name: frequency_hz
attributes.description: Average electrical frequency at the generator terminals during the interval, measured in hertz (Hz). Standard grid frequency is 60 Hz in North America. Deviations indicate grid imbalance.

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_mmbtu
attributes.description: Total fuel energy consumed during the interval, measured in millions of British Thermal Units (MMBtu). Calculated from fuel flow meters and fuel heating value. Used for fuel cost allocation and emissions calculation.

attributes.name: gross_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy generated by the unit during the interval, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh), before deducting station auxiliary load. Represents the total output at the generator terminals.

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: Actual thermal efficiency of the generating unit during the interval, measured in British Thermal Units (BTU) of fuel energy input per kilowatt-hour (kWh) of electrical energy output. Lower values indicate higher efficiency. Critical for fuel cost optimization and performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The duration of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values are 5, 15, or 60 minutes. Used to normalize interval data to hourly or daily totals.

attributes.name: interval_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this generation output measurement was recorded by the SCADA historian system. Represents the end of the measurement interval. Typically recorded at 5-minute or 15-minute intervals depending on unit type and regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this unit output record was last modified or updated. Used for change tracking and data quality auditing.

attributes.name: net_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Net electrical energy delivered to the grid during the interval, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh). Calculated as gross generation minus auxiliary load. This is the sellable energy used for RTO settlement and revenue calculation.

attributes.name: nox_emissions_lbs
attributes.description: Nitrogen oxides emissions produced during the interval, measured in pounds. Monitored via CEMS for air quality compliance. Subject to EPA and state air quality regulations.

attributes.name: reactive_power_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power output during the interval, measured in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAR). Used for voltage support and grid stability. May be positive (generation) or negative (consumption).

attributes.name: rec_quantity
attributes.description: Number of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) generated during this interval. Typically one REC equals one MWh of renewable generation. Used for RPS compliance tracking and REC trading.

attributes.name: relative_humidity_percent
attributes.description: Relative humidity at the plant site during the interval, expressed as a percentage. Affects combustion turbine performance and cooling tower efficiency. Used for environmental correction factors.

attributes.name: rps_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the generation output during this interval is eligible for Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance credit. True for renewable energy generation that meets state RPS criteria; false for fossil fuel or non-qualifying generation.

attributes.name: rto_settlement_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this interval's generation output has been submitted to the RTO/ISO for energy market settlement. True means the data has been used for settlement; false means it has not yet been submitted or was excluded.

attributes.name: scada_source_tag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Source Tag
attributes.description: The SCADA historian tag name or point identifier from which this telemetry data was sourced. Typically an OSIsoft PI tag or GE Proficy tag. Used for data lineage and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: so2_emissions_lbs
attributes.description: Sulfur dioxide emissions produced during the interval, measured in pounds. Monitored via CEMS for acid rain program compliance and air quality regulations.

attributes.name: steam_flow_klb_per_hr
attributes.description: Steam flow rate through the turbine during the interval, measured in thousands of pounds per hour (klb/hr). Applicable to steam turbine units (fossil, nuclear, combined cycle). Used for thermodynamic performance analysis.

attributes.name: unit_status
attributes.description: Operational status of the generating unit during the interval. Indicates whether the unit was actively generating, offline, or in a transitional state. Used for availability analysis and outage tracking.

attributes.name: voltage_kv
attributes.description: Average voltage at the generator terminals during the interval, measured in kilovolts (kV). Varies by unit design and step-up transformer configuration.

products.name: generation_outage_event
products.description: Planned and forced outage records for generating units, aligned with NERC GADS (Generating Availability Data System) reporting requirements. Captures outage type (planned, forced, maintenance, extension, startup failure, shutdown), outage cause code (NERC GADS cause code), outage start timestamp, return-to-service timestamp, derated capacity (MW), equivalent forced outage rate (EFOR) contribution, responsible crew, outage notification to RTO/ISO, and regulatory reporting flag. Also covers unit startup and shutdown events that result in capacity unavailability. Supports NERC GADS submissions, generation reliability metrics (EFOR, EAF, capacity factor impact), and maintenance planning. Sourced from Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo work management and ABB/GE EMS.
products.reference: NERC GADS Outage Record / IEEE 762

attributes.name: generation_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the generation outage event record. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: compliance_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_event. Business justification: Forced outages trigger compliance events such as NERC GADS reporting, availability violations, or penalty assessments. Linking outages to compliance events enables tracking of regulatory consequences,

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the generating unit (power plant unit) that experienced the outage. Links to the generation asset master data.

attributes.name: affected_system
attributes.description: Primary system or component of the generating unit that was affected by the outage (e.g., boiler, turbine, generator, condenser, cooling system, fuel handling, emissions control, electrical auxiliary).

attributes.name: available_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Remaining generating capacity (in megawatts) available during a partial outage. Zero for full outages. Used to calculate net capacity impact and dispatch availability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this outage event record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: derated_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Amount of generating capacity (in megawatts) that was unavailable during the outage. For full outages, this equals the unit's nameplate capacity. For partial outages, this is the reduction in available capacity.

attributes.name: efor_contribution_hours
attributes.description: Equivalent forced outage hours contributed by this event to the unit's Equivalent Forced Outage Rate (EFOR) calculation. Accounts for both full and partial forced outages weighted by capacity impact.

attributes.name: environmental_incident_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether the outage was associated with an environmental incident (e.g., emissions exceedance, spill, discharge violation). True if EPA or state environmental reporting is required.

attributes.name: estimated_revenue_impact_usd
attributes.description: Estimated financial impact of the outage in US dollars, calculated based on lost generation and applicable market prices (LMP, PPA rates, or avoided cost). Used for financial reporting and outage cost-benefit analysis.

attributes.name: extension_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why a planned outage was extended beyond its scheduled duration (e.g., additional repairs discovered, parts delay, weather, contractor availability). Null if no extension occurred.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Type of fuel or energy source used by the generating unit that experienced the outage. Used for fuel-specific reliability analysis and RPS compliance tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|oil|biomass|geothermal — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this outage event record was most recently modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: lost_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy generation lost due to the outage, measured in megawatt-hours. Calculated as derated capacity multiplied by outage duration. Used for revenue impact analysis and capacity factor calculations.

attributes.name: maintenance_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total cost of maintenance or repair work performed during the outage in US dollars, including labor, materials, and contractor expenses. Sourced from work order cost actuals in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.

attributes.name: nerc_gads_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether this outage event must be reported to NERC under the Generating Availability Data System (GADS) reporting requirements. True for events meeting NERC reporting thresholds.

attributes.name: nerc_gads_submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the outage event data was submitted to NERC GADS for regulatory compliance reporting. Null if not yet submitted or not reportable.

attributes.name: outage_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the planned outage was approved by management, operations, or the RTO/ISO outage coordination process. Null for forced outages.

attributes.name: outage_cause_code
attributes.description: Standardized NERC GADS cause code identifying the root cause of the outage (e.g., boiler tube leak, turbine blade failure, transformer fault, fuel supply interruption). Required for NERC GADS submissions and reliability analysis.

attributes.name: outage_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the root cause and circumstances of the outage event. Provides context beyond the standardized cause code for engineering analysis and lessons learned.

attributes.name: outage_coordinator
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual responsible for coordinating the outage event, including scheduling, RTO/ISO notification, work order management, and return-to-service activities.

attributes.name: outage_duration_hours
attributes.description: Total duration of the outage event in hours, calculated as the difference between outage_start_timestamp and outage_end_timestamp. Used for SAIDI-equivalent generation reliability metrics and maintenance planning.

attributes.name: outage_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the generating unit returned to service at full or partial capacity. Null if the outage is still ongoing. Used to calculate outage duration and availability metrics.

attributes.name: outage_extension_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether a planned outage was extended beyond its originally scheduled end date. True if actual duration exceeded scheduled duration.

attributes.name: outage_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the outage event, typically assigned by the work management system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) or EMS. Used for tracking and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: outage_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the generating unit became unavailable or derated. Represents the moment the unit went offline or capacity was reduced. Critical for EFOR and availability calculations.

attributes.name: outage_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the outage event. Active indicates the unit is currently offline. Completed means the unit has returned to service. Extended indicates a planned outage that exceeded its scheduled duration. Cancelled applies to planned outages that were aborted before execution.

attributes.name: outage_type
attributes.description: Classification of the outage event. Planned outages are scheduled in advance for maintenance or upgrades. Forced outages are unplanned events due to equipment failure or external factors. Maintenance outages are routine preventive work. Extension indicates a planned outage that ran longer than scheduled. Startup failure occurs when a unit fails to start. Shutdown captures events where a unit is taken offline.

attributes.name: puc_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether this outage event must be reported to the state Public Utility Commission under state regulatory requirements. True for events meeting state reporting thresholds.

attributes.name: replacement_power_cost_usd
attributes.description: Cost of purchasing replacement power from the wholesale market or other sources to cover the capacity shortfall during the outage. Used for total outage cost analysis.

attributes.name: responsible_crew
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the maintenance crew, operations team, or contractor responsible for managing the outage and performing repair or maintenance work.

attributes.name: return_to_service_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the unit was officially declared available for dispatch by the RTO/ISO or grid operator. May differ from outage_end_timestamp if testing or ramp-up is required.

attributes.name: rto_iso_notification_method
attributes.description: Method used to notify the RTO/ISO of the outage event (phone call, email, EMS system integration, web portal submission, or automated system notification).

attributes.name: rto_iso_notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the Regional Transmission Organization or Independent System Operator was notified of the outage. Required for compliance with RTO/ISO operating procedures and market rules.

attributes.name: safety_incident_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether the outage was associated with a safety incident (injury, near-miss, OSHA recordable event). True if OSHA reporting is required.

attributes.name: scheduled_duration_hours
attributes.description: Originally planned duration of the outage in hours for planned or maintenance outages. Used to calculate schedule variance and extension impact. Null for forced outages.

attributes.name: scheduled_end_date
attributes.description: Originally planned end date for planned or maintenance outages. Used to identify outage extensions and schedule variance. Null for forced outages.

attributes.name: scheduled_start_date
attributes.description: Originally planned start date for planned or maintenance outages. Used to track schedule adherence and compare planned versus actual outage timing. Null for forced outages.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system that originated this outage event record (Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo, ABB EMS, GE EMS, or manual entry). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: weather_related_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether the outage was caused by or significantly influenced by weather conditions (e.g., extreme heat, cold, wind, lightning, ice). Used for climate resilience analysis.

attributes.name: work_order_number
attributes.description: Work order identifier from the Enterprise Asset Management system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) associated with the outage maintenance or repair activities. Links outage events to work management records.

products.name: fuel_inventory
products.description: Fuel stock inventory records for thermal and nuclear generation facilities — coal tonnage, natural gas in storage (MCF/BCF), nuclear fuel assemblies (uranium enrichment batches), oil (barrels), and biomass. Tracks fuel type, storage location (coal pile, tank farm, gas holder), quantity on hand, unit of measure, inventory date, minimum operating reserve level, maximum storage capacity, fuel quality parameters (BTU content, sulfur content, ash content, moisture content), days of burn remaining at current consumption rate, and supplier contract reference. Supports fuel procurement planning, FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause) cost tracking, burn forecast modeling, and environmental compliance (GHG, SO2, NOx). Sourced from SAP S/4HANA materials management and plant fuel management systems.
products.reference: EIA Form 923 Fuel Receipts / FAC Fuel Tracking

attributes.name: fuel_inventory_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fuel inventory record. Primary key for the fuel inventory product.

attributes.name: fuel_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to generation.fuel_contract. Business justification: Fuel inventory records should be traceable to the fuel supply contract under which the fuel was delivered. This is essential for: (1) Cost reconciliation - matching inventory costs to contract pricing

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the generation facility (power plant) where the fuel is stored. Links to the generation facility master data.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 - Electric Plant in Service

attributes.name: warehouse_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.warehouse. Business justification: Fuel storage at generation plants uses centralized warehouse management for inventory tracking, safety stock monitoring, and physical count reconciliation. Monthly fuel inventory reconciliation proces

attributes.name: ash_content_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of ash by weight in the fuel (primarily applicable to coal and biomass). Affects combustion efficiency and waste disposal requirements.
attributes.references: ASTM D3174 - Ash in the Analysis Sample of Coal

attributes.name: average_daily_consumption_rate
attributes.description: Average daily fuel consumption rate at the facility, measured in the same unit as quantity_on_hand. Used to calculate days of burn remaining and forecast fuel needs.

attributes.name: batch_number
attributes.description: Batch or lot number assigned to the fuel shipment for traceability and quality control. Enables tracking of fuel quality issues back to specific deliveries.

attributes.name: btu_content
attributes.description: Heat content of the fuel measured in BTU per unit (e.g., BTU per pound for coal, BTU per cubic foot for gas). Critical for heat rate calculations and energy output forecasting.
attributes.references: ASTM D5865 - Gross Calorific Value of Coal

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the fuel inventory record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: days_of_burn_remaining
attributes.description: Estimated number of days the current fuel inventory will last at the current consumption rate. Calculated metric used for fuel procurement planning and supply chain risk management.

attributes.name: economic_order_quantity
attributes.description: Optimal order quantity that minimizes total inventory holding costs and ordering costs. Used for fuel procurement optimization and cost management.

attributes.name: enrichment_level_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of fissile isotope U-235 in nuclear fuel assemblies. Applicable only to nuclear fuel inventory. Critical for reactor physics and fuel cycle planning.
attributes.references: NRC 10 CFR Part 50 - Nuclear Fuel Specifications

attributes.name: environmental_permit_number
attributes.description: Permit number issued by EPA or state environmental agency authorizing the storage and use of the fuel type. Required for compliance with Clean Air Act and state environmental regulations.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - Title V Operating Permits

attributes.name: fac_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the fuel costs are eligible for recovery through the Fuel Adjustment Clause mechanism in customer rates. True indicates FAC-eligible, False indicates costs must be absorbed or recovered through base rates.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff - Fuel Adjustment Clause

attributes.name: fuel_grade
attributes.description: Grade or quality classification of the fuel (e.g., bituminous coal, sub-bituminous coal, pipeline-quality natural gas, enriched uranium U-235). Indicates fuel specification and quality tier.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Type of fuel stored in inventory. Categorizes fuel by primary energy source used for thermal or nuclear generation.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923 - Power Plant Operations Report

attributes.name: ghg_emissions_factor
attributes.description: Greenhouse gas emissions factor for the fuel type, measured in metric tons of CO2 equivalent per unit of fuel consumed. Used for GHG emissions reporting and carbon accounting under EPA regulations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 - Greenhouse Gas Reporting

attributes.name: inventory_date
attributes.description: Date when the inventory quantity was measured or recorded. Represents the as-of date for the inventory snapshot.

attributes.name: inventory_status
attributes.description: Current status of the fuel inventory. Available indicates fuel ready for consumption, reserved indicates fuel allocated to specific generation schedule, in_transit indicates fuel en route to storage, quarantined indicates fuel held for quality testing, depleted indicates storage location is empty.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Materials Management - Stock Status

attributes.name: last_physical_count_date
attributes.description: Date when the last physical inventory count was performed at the storage location. Used for inventory reconciliation and audit compliance.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the fuel inventory record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data freshness monitoring.

attributes.name: maximum_storage_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum fuel quantity that can be physically stored at the location. Represents the storage facility design capacity in the same unit as quantity_on_hand.

attributes.name: minimum_operating_reserve
attributes.description: Minimum fuel quantity that must be maintained to ensure continuous plant operations and meet reliability requirements. Measured in the same unit as quantity_on_hand.

attributes.name: moisture_content_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of moisture by weight in the fuel. Impacts combustion efficiency, heat rate, and fuel handling characteristics.
attributes.references: ASTM D3173 - Moisture in the Analysis Sample of Coal

attributes.name: nitrogen_content_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of nitrogen by weight in the fuel. Relevant for NOx emissions calculations and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - NOx Emissions Standards

attributes.name: quality_certification_number
attributes.description: Certification or test report number from the laboratory that performed fuel quality analysis. Provides traceability to quality assurance documentation.

attributes.name: quality_test_date
attributes.description: Date when the most recent fuel quality test was performed. Quality parameters such as BTU content, sulfur content, and ash content are validated through periodic testing.

attributes.name: quantity_on_hand
attributes.description: Current quantity of fuel in inventory at the storage location. Measured in the unit specified in unit_of_measure field.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Materials Management - Stock Overview

attributes.name: receipt_date
attributes.description: Date when the fuel was received at the storage location. Used for inventory aging analysis and FIFO/LIFO accounting methods.

attributes.name: reorder_point
attributes.description: Inventory level at which a new fuel order should be triggered to maintain adequate supply. Used for automated procurement planning and supply chain optimization.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Materials Management - Reorder Point Planning

attributes.name: storage_pressure
attributes.description: Current pressure in the fuel storage container, measured in pounds per square inch (PSI). Applicable to natural gas storage holders and pressurized fuel systems.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 - Gas Pipeline Safety

attributes.name: storage_temperature
attributes.description: Current temperature of the fuel storage location, measured in degrees Fahrenheit. Relevant for liquid fuels (oil, diesel) and nuclear fuel pool cooling monitoring.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 - Fuel Storage Safety Standards

attributes.name: sulfur_content_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of sulfur by weight in the fuel. Critical for SO2 emissions compliance and environmental permitting under Clean Air Act regulations.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - SO2 Emissions Standards

attributes.name: total_inventory_value
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the fuel inventory at the storage location, calculated as quantity_on_hand multiplied by unit_cost. Reported in USD for financial accounting and regulatory rate case filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts - Account 151 Fuel Stock

attributes.name: unit_cost
attributes.description: Cost per unit of fuel in inventory, measured in USD per unit of measure. Used for inventory valuation and Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) cost tracking.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the fuel quantity. Tons for coal/biomass, MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet) or BCF (Billion Cubic Feet) for natural gas, barrels for oil, assemblies for nuclear fuel, MMBTU (Million British Thermal Units) for energy content.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923 - Fuel Receipts and Costs

attributes.name: variance_quantity
attributes.description: Difference between book inventory and physical count from the last inventory reconciliation. Positive values indicate overage, negative values indicate shortage. Measured in the same unit as quantity_on_hand.

products.name: fuel_consumption
products.description: Actual fuel consumed per generating unit per operating period, used for heat rate calculation, FAC cost recovery, and EPA emissions reporting. Records consumption date, fuel type, quantity consumed (MMBTU, MCF, tons, barrels), heat content (BTU/unit), cost per unit, total fuel cost ($), associated generation output (MWh), calculated heat rate (BTU/kWh), and emissions factors applied (CO2, SO2, NOx, CH4 lbs/MMBTU). Supports EIA Form 923 monthly fuel consumption reporting, EPA CEMS reconciliation, and IRP fuel cost modeling. Sourced from plant DCS/SCADA and SAP S/4HANA.
products.reference: EIA Form 923 / EPA 40 CFR Part 75 CEMS

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each fuel consumption record. Primary key for the fuel consumption data product.

attributes.name: fuel_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the fuel supply contract under which the fuel was purchased. Links to contract master data for cost allocation and contract performance tracking.

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the generating unit that consumed the fuel. Links to the generation asset master data.

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Fuel costs must post to specific GL accounts (FERC account 501 for steam, 547 for gas) for financial statement preparation, monthly fuel expense accrual, and regulatory reporting. Direct posting relat

attributes.name: goods_receipt_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.goods_receipt. Business justification: Each fuel consumption event must trace to the goods receipt that brought that fuel batch into inventory for audit trail and quality tracking. Fuel quality issue root cause analysis requires tracing co

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the power plant facility where fuel was consumed. Links to generation facility master data.

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.purchase_order. Business justification: Fuel deliveries under long-term contracts require associated POs for invoice reconciliation and payment processing. Three-way match process (delivery ticket, PO, vendor invoice) is mandatory for fuel

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the fuel supplier or vendor who delivered the fuel. Links to supply chain vendor master data for procurement tracking and contract management.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: The ambient air temperature at the power plant during the fuel consumption period, measured in degrees Fahrenheit. Affects unit efficiency and heat rate, particularly for combustion turbines and combined cycle units.

attributes.name: cems_reconciliation_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) Reconciliation Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this fuel consumption record has been reconciled with EPA CEMS (Continuous Emissions Monitoring System) emissions data. True indicates reconciliation is complete; False indicates pending reconciliation.

attributes.name: ch4_emissions_factor
attributes.description: The methane emissions factor applied to the fuel type, expressed in pounds of CH4 per MMBTU of fuel consumed. Used to calculate total CH4 emissions for EPA GHG reporting and climate disclosure.

attributes.name: co2_emissions_factor
attributes.business_glossary_term: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Emissions Factor (lbs per MMBTU)
attributes.description: The carbon dioxide emissions factor applied to the fuel type, expressed in pounds of CO2 per MMBTU of fuel consumed. Used to calculate total CO2 emissions for EPA GHG reporting and RPS compliance.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, exceptions, or explanations related to the fuel consumption record (e.g., unit startup, fuel quality issues, meter calibration, data corrections). Used for audit trail and operational analysis.

attributes.name: consumption_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the fuel was consumed by the generating unit. Used for daily fuel tracking and reconciliation.
