attributes.name: consumption_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the fuel consumption measurement was recorded, typically from SCADA or DCS systems. Supports real-time fuel monitoring and interval-level analysis.

attributes.name: data_quality_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the quality and validation status of the fuel consumption record. Verified indicates the data has passed all validation checks; Estimated indicates the data was calculated or interpolated; Provisional indicates preliminary data subject to revision; Suspect indicates data that failed quality checks.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: The source system or method from which the fuel consumption data was captured (e.g., SCADA, DCS, manual entry, EMS, PI Historian). Used for data quality assessment and audit trail.

attributes.name: delivery_method
attributes.description: The transportation method used to deliver the fuel to the power plant (e.g., pipeline for natural gas, rail for coal, truck for oil). Used for logistics planning and transportation cost allocation.

attributes.name: eia_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this fuel consumption record has been included in EIA Form 923 monthly fuel consumption reporting. True indicates the record has been reported; False indicates it has not yet been reported.

attributes.name: fac_recovery_eligible_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) Recovery Eligible Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the fuel costs associated with this consumption record are eligible for recovery through the Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) mechanism. True indicates eligible; False indicates not eligible (e.g., due to imprudence findings or contract limitations).

attributes.name: fuel_cost_per_unit
attributes.description: The delivered cost of fuel per unit of measure (e.g., dollars per ton, dollars per MCF, dollars per barrel). Includes transportation and handling costs. Used for fuel cost allocation and FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause) calculations.

attributes.name: fuel_subtype
attributes.description: Detailed subclassification of fuel type (e.g., bituminous coal, sub-bituminous coal, anthracite, pipeline natural gas, LNG, No. 2 fuel oil, No. 6 fuel oil). Used for precise heat content and emissions factor application.

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The type of fuel consumed by the generating unit. Primary classification for fuel inventory management, cost allocation, and emissions reporting.

attributes.name: generation_output_mwh
attributes.description: The gross electrical energy output produced by the generating unit during the fuel consumption period, measured in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Used as the denominator in heat rate calculation.

attributes.name: heat_content_per_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heat Content Per Unit (BTU per Unit)
attributes.description: The average heat content (energy value) of the fuel per unit of measure, expressed in BTU per unit (e.g., BTU per ton, BTU per MCF, BTU per barrel). Used to convert physical fuel quantity to energy equivalent.

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: The thermal efficiency of the generating unit, calculated as total_heat_content_mmbtu × 1,000,000 ÷ (generation_output_mwh × 1,000). Expressed in BTU per kilowatt-hour. Lower heat rate indicates higher efficiency. Key performance metric for generation operations and IRP modeling.

attributes.name: nox_emissions_factor
attributes.business_glossary_term: Nitrogen Oxides (NOx) Emissions Factor (lbs per MMBTU)
attributes.description: The nitrogen oxides emissions factor applied to the fuel type, expressed in pounds of NOx per MMBTU of fuel consumed. Used to calculate total NOx emissions for EPA Clean Air Act compliance and ozone transport region reporting.

attributes.name: operating_mode
attributes.description: The operating mode of the generating unit during the fuel consumption period. Affects fuel efficiency and heat rate. Used for operational analysis and dispatch optimization.

attributes.name: quantity_consumed
attributes.description: The physical quantity of fuel consumed during the operating period, measured in the native unit of measure (tons for coal, MCF for gas, barrels for oil, pounds for nuclear fuel).

attributes.name: quantity_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the quantity consumed field. Varies by fuel type: tons for coal, MCF (thousand cubic feet) for natural gas, barrels for oil, pounds for nuclear fuel.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this fuel consumption record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this fuel consumption record was last modified in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: so2_emissions_factor
attributes.business_glossary_term: Sulfur Dioxide (SO2) Emissions Factor (lbs per MMBTU)
attributes.description: The sulfur dioxide emissions factor applied to the fuel type, expressed in pounds of SO2 per MMBTU of fuel consumed. Used to calculate total SO2 emissions for EPA Clean Air Act compliance and acid rain program reporting.

attributes.name: total_co2_emissions_tons
attributes.description: The total carbon dioxide emissions produced from the fuel consumed, calculated as (total_heat_content_mmbtu × co2_emissions_factor) ÷ 2000. Expressed in short tons. Primary metric for EPA GHG reporting and carbon accounting.

attributes.name: total_fuel_cost_usd
attributes.description: The total cost of fuel consumed during the operating period, expressed in US dollars. Calculated as quantity_consumed × fuel_cost_per_unit. Used for FAC cost recovery, rate case preparation, and financial reporting.

attributes.name: total_heat_content_mmbtu
attributes.description: The total energy content of the fuel consumed, expressed in Million British Thermal Units (MMBTU). Calculated as quantity_consumed × heat_content_per_unit. Primary metric for heat rate calculation and fuel cost recovery.

attributes.name: total_nox_emissions_tons
attributes.description: The total nitrogen oxides emissions produced from the fuel consumed, calculated as (total_heat_content_mmbtu × nox_emissions_factor) ÷ 2000. Expressed in short tons. Used for EPA Clean Air Act compliance and ozone transport region reporting.

attributes.name: total_so2_emissions_tons
attributes.description: The total sulfur dioxide emissions produced from the fuel consumed, calculated as (total_heat_content_mmbtu × so2_emissions_factor) ÷ 2000. Expressed in short tons. Used for EPA Clean Air Act compliance and acid rain program reporting.

products.name: emissions_record
products.description: Continuous emissions monitoring (CEMS) and calculated emissions data per generating unit per reporting period, required for EPA compliance under Clean Air Act Title IV and Title V. Captures pollutant type (CO2, SO2, NOx, Hg, PM2.5, CH4), measurement method (CEMS, fuel-factor, mass balance), hourly/daily/monthly emission quantity (tons), emission rate (lbs/MMBTU), allowance consumption, CEMS monitor status, data substitution flag, and EPA ECMPS submission status. Supports EPA ECMPS reporting, GHG inventory, RPS compliance, and carbon accounting. Sourced from plant CEMS and OSIsoft PI.
products.reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 / EPA ECMPS / NERC CIP

attributes.name: emissions_record_id
attributes.description: Primary key for emissions_record

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Emissions compliance costs (allowance purchases, penalties, monitoring equipment) are allocated to plant cost centers for environmental cost tracking and regulatory cost recovery in rate cases. Requir

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the generating unit that produced these emissions. Links to the generation asset master data.

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the power generation facility where the emissions occurred. Links to the facility master data.

attributes.name: allowance_account_number
attributes.description: The EPA allowance tracking system account number from which allowances were retired to cover these emissions. Used for compliance reconciliation.

attributes.name: allowance_consumption
attributes.description: The number of emissions allowances consumed or required for this emissions record under cap-and-trade programs such as the EPA Acid Rain Program or state-level programs. One allowance typically equals one ton of SO2 or NOx.
attributes.references: EPA Acid Rain Program (40 CFR Part 73)

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: The ambient air temperature during the reporting period in degrees Fahrenheit. Affects unit efficiency and emissions characteristics.

attributes.name: carbon_content_percent
attributes.description: The carbon content of the fuel as a percentage by weight. Used in mass balance calculations for CO2 emissions when CEMS is unavailable.

attributes.name: carbon_cost_total
attributes.description: The total carbon cost for this emissions record, calculated as emission quantity multiplied by carbon price. Used for financial reporting and cost allocation.

attributes.name: carbon_price_per_ton
attributes.description: The carbon price applied to CO2 emissions for this record, expressed in dollars per ton. Used for carbon accounting, internal carbon pricing, and compliance with carbon pricing programs.

attributes.name: cems_monitor_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) Monitor Status
attributes.description: The operational status of the CEMS monitor during the reporting period. Operational indicates normal functioning. Out of service, calibration, maintenance, and failed QA indicate periods when direct measurement was unavailable and substitute data may have been used.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, explanations, or context regarding this emissions record. May include information about unusual operating conditions, equipment issues, or data quality concerns.

attributes.name: control_efficiency_percent
attributes.description: The removal efficiency of emissions control equipment during the reporting period, expressed as a percentage. For example, a scrubber with 95% efficiency removes 95% of SO2 from flue gas.

attributes.name: control_equipment_status
attributes.description: The operational status of emissions control equipment (scrubbers, SCR, baghouses, etc.) during the reporting period. Bypassed or out-of-service status may result in higher emissions.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: A calculated score representing the overall quality and reliability of this emissions record, typically ranging from 0 to 100. Factors include measurement method, CEMS status, QA test results, and data completeness.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The source system from which this emissions record was extracted. Typically OSIsoft PI historian for CEMS data or plant DCS (Distributed Control System) for calculated emissions.

attributes.name: data_substitution_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether substitute data was used for this emissions record due to CEMS monitor unavailability. True indicates substitute data was used; False indicates actual measured or calculated data.

attributes.name: ecmps_submission_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) Submission Date
attributes.description: The date this emissions record was submitted to EPA ECMPS for regulatory compliance reporting. Quarterly submissions are typically required within 30 days of quarter end.

attributes.name: ecmps_submission_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) Submission Status
attributes.description: The status of this emissions record in the EPA ECMPS reporting system. Tracks the lifecycle from pending submission through acceptance or rejection by EPA.

attributes.name: ecmps_tracking_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS) Tracking Number
attributes.description: The unique tracking number assigned by EPA ECMPS upon submission. Used to track the status and history of the regulatory filing.

attributes.name: emission_quantity_tons
attributes.description: The total quantity of pollutant emitted during the reporting period, measured in short tons. This is the primary emissions metric reported to EPA ECMPS.

attributes.name: emission_rate_lbs_per_mmbtu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Emission Rate (Pounds per Million British Thermal Units)
attributes.description: The emission rate expressed as pounds of pollutant per million British Thermal Units (MMBTU) of heat input. This normalized rate allows comparison across units of different sizes and fuel types.

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_quantity
attributes.description: The quantity of fuel consumed during the reporting period. Units vary by fuel type: tons for coal, MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet) for natural gas, barrels for oil.

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure for fuel consumption quantity. Common units include tons (coal), MCF or Thousand Cubic Feet (natural gas), barrels (oil), or MMBTU (heat content).

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The primary fuel type consumed by the generating unit during this reporting period. Fuel type significantly impacts emission factors and pollutant profiles. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|oil|biomass|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ghg_inventory_category
attributes.description: The GHG inventory category for this emissions record under EPA GHG reporting and corporate carbon accounting frameworks. Stationary combustion is the primary category for power generation.

attributes.name: gross_generation_mwh
attributes.description: The total gross electrical energy generated by the unit during the reporting period, measured in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Used to calculate emission intensity per unit of generation.

attributes.name: heat_input_mmbtu
attributes.description: The total heat input to the generating unit during the reporting period, measured in Million British Thermal Units (MMBTU). Used to calculate emission rates and heat rate efficiency.

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: The method used to determine emissions quantity. CEMS indicates Continuous Emissions Monitoring System direct measurement. Fuel factor uses fuel consumption and emission factors. Mass balance calculates emissions from material inputs and outputs. Engineering estimate and default factor are used when direct measurement is unavailable. Substitute indicates data substitution during monitor downtime.

attributes.name: operating_hours
attributes.description: The number of hours the generating unit was in operation during the reporting period. Used for availability calculations and emissions rate normalization.

attributes.name: pollutant_concentration_ppm
attributes.description: The concentration of the pollutant in the flue gas as measured by CEMS, expressed in parts per million (ppm) or parts per billion (ppb) for mercury. Combined with stack flow rate to calculate mass emissions.

attributes.name: pollutant_type
attributes.description: The type of pollutant emitted. Standard pollutants tracked include Carbon Dioxide (CO2), Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), Nitrogen Oxides (NOx), Mercury (Hg), Particulate Matter 2.5 microns (PM2.5), and Methane (CH4).

attributes.name: qa_certification_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent CEMS quality assurance certification test. EPA requires periodic QA testing to ensure monitor accuracy.

attributes.name: qa_test_result
attributes.description: The result of the most recent CEMS quality assurance test. Passed indicates the monitor meets EPA accuracy requirements. Failed or conditional results may require corrective action and data substitution.

attributes.name: rec_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the generation associated with this emissions record is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs). Typically true for renewable generation with zero emissions.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this emissions record was first created in the data management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this emissions record was last updated in the data management system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: reporting_period_end
attributes.description: The end date and time of the emissions reporting period. Defines the boundary of the measurement interval.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV and Title V

attributes.name: reporting_period_start
attributes.description: The start date and time of the emissions reporting period. Typically hourly for CEMS data, but may be daily or monthly for aggregated reporting.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act Title IV and Title V

attributes.name: rps_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this generation and its associated emissions are eligible for Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance credit. True for renewable generation with zero or low emissions.

attributes.name: stack_flow_rate_scfh
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stack Flow Rate (Standard Cubic Feet per Hour)
attributes.description: The volumetric flow rate of flue gas through the stack during the reporting period, measured in Standard Cubic Feet per Hour (SCFH). Used in CEMS calculations to convert pollutant concentration to mass emissions.

attributes.name: substitution_method
attributes.description: The specific method used to substitute emissions data when CEMS was unavailable. Methods include maximum potential emissions, fuel-specific default factors, load-based estimation, or EPA-approved missing data procedures.

attributes.name: sulfur_content_percent
attributes.description: The sulfur content of the fuel as a percentage by weight. Used to estimate SO2 emissions when CEMS is unavailable and to verify CEMS accuracy.

products.name: capacity_resource
products.description: Capacity resource registration and accreditation records for each generating unit participating in RTO/ISO capacity markets (e.g., PJM Capacity Performance, MISO Planning Resource Auction, SPP, CAISO RA). Captures resource ID, accredited capacity (MW), unforced capacity (UCAP), installed capacity (ICAP), capacity zone, performance obligation (MW), capacity market product type (base capacity, capacity performance, must-offer), accreditation period (planning year), RTO/ISO registration status, capacity auction clearing price ($/MW-day), non-performance charge rate, and bonus payment eligibility. Supports IRP capacity planning, RTO capacity market revenue tracking, capacity performance penalty/bonus accounting, and FERC Order 841 compliance. Sourced from ABB/GE EMS and RTO market portals.
products.reference: NERC MOD-025 / RTO Capacity Market Registration

attributes.name: capacity_resource_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the capacity resource registration record in the RTO/ISO capacity market.

attributes.name: approval_docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Capacity market participation and resource accreditation often require state regulatory approval through dockets, particularly for cost recovery of capacity revenues or obligations. Tracking the appro

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Capacity market participation often requires capital upgrades (performance improvements, winterization) tracked as projects for rate base inclusion and cost recovery. Links capacity revenue to enablin

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical generating unit or aggregated resource participating in the capacity market.

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated power purchase agreement (PPA) contract if the capacity resource is tied to a bilateral capacity contract.

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: Capacity resources must specify delivery points for capacity market participation and deliverability studies. Required for PJM/NYISO/ISO-NE capacity auctions, FERC Form 1 reporting, and resource adequ

attributes.name: accreditation_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the accreditation period during which the resource is qualified to provide capacity.

attributes.name: accreditation_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the accreditation period during which the resource is qualified to provide capacity.

attributes.name: accredited_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The accredited capacity value in megawatts (MW) that the resource is qualified to provide based on RTO/ISO testing and performance criteria.
attributes.references: NERC MOD Standards, RTO/ISO Accreditation Procedures

attributes.name: auction_clearing_price_per_mw_day
attributes.description: The capacity auction clearing price in dollars per megawatt-day ($/MW-day) at which this resource cleared in the capacity market auction.

attributes.name: bonus_payment_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resource is eligible for bonus payments for over-performance during capacity performance events (True/False).

attributes.name: capacity_commitment_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the capacity commitment period during which the resource must be available to deliver committed capacity.

attributes.name: capacity_commitment_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the capacity commitment period during which the resource must be available to deliver committed capacity.

attributes.name: capacity_interconnection_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resource has secured capacity interconnection rights (CIR) or capacity network resource interconnection service (CNRIS) (True/False).

attributes.name: capacity_market_product_type
attributes.description: Type of capacity product offered in the RTO/ISO market (e.g., base capacity, capacity performance, must-offer obligation).
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance, MISO Planning Resource Auction Rules

attributes.name: capacity_revenue_amount
attributes.description: The total capacity market revenue amount in dollars earned by this resource for the planning year based on cleared capacity and auction price.

attributes.name: capacity_transfer_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resource has capacity transfer rights allowing capacity to be sold or transferred to other zones (True/False).

attributes.name: capacity_zone
attributes.description: The RTO/ISO capacity zone or locational deliverability area (LDA) where the resource is located and registered.

attributes.name: demand_response_resource_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the capacity resource is a demand response (DR) resource rather than a generation asset (True/False).

attributes.name: energy_storage_resource_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the capacity resource is an energy storage system (e.g., battery, pumped hydro) participating in the capacity market (True/False).
attributes.references: FERC Order 841, RTO/ISO Energy Storage Participation Rules

attributes.name: equivalent_forced_outage_rate_eford
attributes.business_glossary_term: Equivalent Forced Outage Rate on Demand (EFORd)
attributes.description: The equivalent forced outage rate on demand (EFORd) expressed as a decimal, used to calculate UCAP from ICAP.

attributes.name: installed_capacity_icap_mw
attributes.description: The installed capacity (ICAP) rating in megawatts representing the maximum nameplate capacity of the resource.

attributes.name: last_accreditation_test_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent accreditation test or performance verification conducted by the RTO/ISO to validate the resource's capacity rating.

attributes.name: must_offer_obligation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resource has a must-offer obligation requiring it to bid into energy and ancillary service markets (True/False).

attributes.name: next_accreditation_test_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next accreditation test or performance verification required by the RTO/ISO.

attributes.name: non_performance_charge_rate
attributes.description: The penalty charge rate in dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh) applied when the resource fails to deliver committed capacity during performance assessment intervals.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Penalty Rules, FERC Order 825

attributes.name: performance_obligation_mw
attributes.description: The committed capacity performance obligation in megawatts that the resource must deliver during capacity performance events or face penalties.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Rules, FERC Order 825

attributes.name: planning_year
attributes.description: The capacity market planning year or delivery year for which this resource is registered (e.g., 2024/2025).

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this capacity resource record was first created in the data platform.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this capacity resource record was last updated in the data platform.

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The date when the capacity resource was initially registered with the RTO/ISO for capacity market participation.

attributes.name: registration_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the capacity resource registration with the RTO/ISO.

attributes.name: renewable_resource_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the capacity resource is a renewable energy resource (wind, solar, hydro, biomass) (True/False).
attributes.references: State RPS Requirements, FERC Renewable Energy Standards

attributes.name: resource_adequacy_status
attributes.description: The resource adequacy qualification status indicating whether the resource meets RTO/ISO reliability and performance standards.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards, CAISO Resource Adequacy Rules

attributes.name: resource_registration_number
attributes.description: External registration identifier assigned by the RTO/ISO for this capacity resource (e.g., PJM resource ID, MISO planning resource ID).

attributes.name: rto_iso_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Name
attributes.description: The name of the RTO or ISO administering the capacity market in which this resource participates. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|MISO|SPP|CAISO|NYISO|ISO_NE|ERCOT — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: seasonal_capacity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resource is registered as a seasonal capacity resource with different capacity values for summer and winter periods (True/False).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this capacity resource registration data was sourced (e.g., ABB EMS, GE EMS, RTO market portal).

attributes.name: unforced_capacity_ucap_mw
attributes.description: The unforced capacity (UCAP) value in megawatts, calculated as ICAP adjusted for the resource's equivalent forced outage rate (EFORd).
attributes.references: PJM UCAP Calculation Manual, NERC GADS

products.name: fuel_contract
products.description: Fuel supply contract master records for coal, natural gas, nuclear fuel, and oil procurement agreements with fuel suppliers. Captures supplier name, fuel type, contract type (firm, interruptible, spot), contracted volume (tons/MCF/MMBTU per period), delivery point (plant-specific), pricing mechanism (fixed, index, cost-plus), contract start/end date, minimum take obligation, force majeure provisions, fuel quality specifications (BTU content, sulfur limit, ash limit), transportation arrangement (pipeline, rail, barge), and contract status. This product is the generation domains SSOT for fuel procurement terms — distinct from the supply domains general vendor contracts, which cover non-fuel materials and services. Supports FAC fuel cost recovery filings, fuel procurement planning, burn forecast modeling, and supply chain risk management. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA contract management.
products.reference: FAC Fuel Procurement / EIA Form 923 Fuel Contract

attributes.name: fuel_contract_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the fuel supply contract record. Primary key for the fuel contract entity.

attributes.name: delivery_point_plant_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the generation facility where fuel is to be delivered. Plant-specific delivery terms are critical for transportation cost allocation and logistics planning.

attributes.name: primary_fuel_vendor_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the fuel supplier party providing coal, natural gas, nuclear fuel, or oil under this contract.

attributes.name: prudency_review_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.prudency_review. Business justification: Fuel procurement contracts are subject to prudency review to determine if costs are reasonable and recoverable through rates. Linking contracts to their prudency reviews supports fuel adjustment claus

attributes.name: wholesale_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.wholesale_counterparty. Business justification: Fuel contracts with wholesale market participants require tracking counterparty credit ratings, FERC market-based rate authorizations, master agreements, and collateral requirements for bilateral trad

attributes.name: ash_content_limit_percent
attributes.description: Maximum allowable ash content as a percentage of fuel weight. High ash content reduces combustion efficiency and increases disposal costs. Primarily applicable to coal contracts.

attributes.name: base_price
attributes.description: Base price per unit of fuel under this contract. For fixed-price contracts, this is the contract price. For index or escalation contracts, this is the starting reference price. Currency is USD unless otherwise specified.

attributes.name: btu_content_specification
attributes.description: Contractually specified heat content of the fuel in British Thermal Units per unit (e.g., BTU per pound for coal, BTU per cubic foot for gas). Critical for heat rate calculations and fuel quality compliance.

attributes.name: contract_amendment_count
attributes.description: Number of formal amendments made to the original contract. Tracks contract change history for audit and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: contract_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the fuel supply contract for business reference and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: contract_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the fuel supply contract. Used in procurement documentation, regulatory filings, and supplier communications.

attributes.name: contract_owner_employee_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the utility employee responsible for managing this fuel supply contract. Typically a fuel procurement manager or supply chain analyst.

attributes.name: contract_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the fuel supply contract. Active contracts are in force; expired contracts have passed their end date; terminated contracts were ended early.

attributes.name: contract_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fuel supply agreement based on delivery commitment and flexibility. Firm contracts guarantee supply; interruptible contracts allow curtailment; spot contracts are short-term market purchases.

attributes.name: contract_value_total
attributes.description: Total estimated monetary value of the fuel contract over its full term, calculated as contracted volume multiplied by base price. Used for CAPEX/OPEX planning and regulatory rate case cost studies. Currency is USD.

attributes.name: contracted_volume
attributes.description: Total quantity of fuel committed under this contract for the specified period. Units vary by fuel type: tons for coal, MCF or MMBTU for natural gas, assemblies for nuclear fuel, barrels for oil.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel contract record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for contract pricing and payments. Predominantly USD for U.S. utilities.

attributes.name: delivery_period
attributes.description: Frequency or time period over which the contracted volume is to be delivered. Supports burn forecast modeling and inventory planning.

attributes.name: delivery_point_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the fuel delivery location, including plant name, receiving facility, or pipeline interconnection point.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the fuel supply contract expires or terminates. Nullable for evergreen contracts. Critical for supply chain risk management and contract renewal planning.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the fuel supply contract becomes binding and deliveries may commence. Used for contract lifecycle management and fuel procurement planning.

attributes.name: force_majeure_provision_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contract includes force majeure clauses allowing suspension of obligations due to unforeseeable circumstances (natural disasters, strikes, regulatory changes).

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Type of fuel covered by this supply contract. Determines applicable quality specifications, transportation modes, and regulatory compliance requirements.

attributes.name: last_amendment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent contract amendment. Null if no amendments have been made.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fuel contract record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: minimum_take_obligation
attributes.description: Minimum quantity of fuel the utility is obligated to purchase during the contract period, regardless of actual need. Used for supply commitment analysis and FAC cost recovery.

attributes.name: minimum_take_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the minimum take obligation quantity.

attributes.name: moisture_content_limit_percent
attributes.description: Maximum allowable moisture content as a percentage of fuel weight. Excess moisture reduces heat content and combustion efficiency. Primarily applicable to coal and biomass contracts.

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Number of days from invoice date within which payment is due to the supplier. Standard terms are Net 30, Net 60, etc.

attributes.name: price_index_reference
attributes.description: Name of the published market index used for index-based pricing (e.g., Henry Hub, NYMEX, Platts Coal Index). Null for fixed-price contracts.

attributes.name: price_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the fuel price. Must align with volume unit of measure for cost calculations.

attributes.name: pricing_mechanism
attributes.description: Method by which fuel price is determined. Fixed = constant price; index = tied to published market index (e.g., Henry Hub for gas); cost-plus = supplier cost plus markup; escalation = base price with periodic adjustments.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the contract received regulatory approval from the PUC or FERC. Null if approval is not required or not yet granted.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fuel contract requires Public Utility Commission (PUC) or FERC approval before execution. Large or long-term contracts often require regulatory review.

attributes.name: renewable_fuel_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the fuel qualifies as renewable under state Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) regulations. Applicable to biomass, biogas, and renewable natural gas contracts.

attributes.name: rps_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether fuel deliveries under this contract are eligible for Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance credit. Supports RPS tracking and Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) generation.

attributes.name: sulfur_content_limit_percent
attributes.description: Maximum allowable sulfur content as a percentage of fuel weight. Enforced to meet EPA emissions standards and state air quality regulations. Primarily applicable to coal and oil contracts.

attributes.name: transportation_arrangement
attributes.description: Mode and responsibility for transporting fuel from supplier to delivery point. Pipeline (natural gas), rail/barge/truck (coal, oil). Supplier-arranged = supplier bears transportation cost and risk; utility-arranged = utility contracts transportation separately.

attributes.name: transportation_cost_responsibility
attributes.description: Party responsible for bearing fuel transportation costs. Impacts delivered fuel cost and FAC cost recovery calculations.

attributes.name: volume_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the contracted fuel volume. MCF = Thousand Cubic Feet (gas), MMBTU = Million British Thermal Units (energy content), assemblies (nuclear fuel). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tons|mcf|mmbtu|barrels|assemblies|kg|mwh_thermal — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

products.name: environmental_permit
products.description: Master record for environmental permits and compliance authorizations held by each generation facility — Title V air operating permits, NPDES water discharge permits (including 316(b) cooling water intake structure requirements), state air quality construction permits, PSD (Prevention of Significant Deterioration) permits, and hazardous waste permits. Captures permit type, issuing agency (EPA, state DEQ), permit number, issuance date, expiration date, renewal date, permitted emission limits (tons/year by pollutant), permitted water discharge limits (temperature, flow, chemical concentrations), cooling water intake flow limits (316(b)), compliance status, permit conditions/stipulations, and associated generating units. Supports environmental compliance tracking, permit renewal management, and regulatory audit readiness. Distinct from emissions_record which captures actual measured emissions — this product captures the permitted limits and regulatory authorizations. Sourced from state DEQ permit databases and internal environmental compliance systems.

attributes.name: environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the environmental permit record. Primary key for the environmental permit entity.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Environmental compliance projects (scrubbers, SCR/SNCR, wastewater treatment) are major capital investments requiring project tracking for CWIP, AFUDC calculation, and rate base inclusion. Essential f

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Environmental permits are issued, modified, or renewed through regulatory dockets. Permit approval orders reference specific docket numbers. Utilities must track which docket authorized each permit fo

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generating unit covered by this environmental permit. Links permit to specific generation asset.

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generation facility holding this environmental permit. Links permit to facility-level compliance tracking.

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current compliance status of the facility with respect to this environmental permit. Indicates whether the facility is operating within permitted limits and conditions.

attributes.name: contact_email
attributes.description: Primary email address for permit-related communications with the regulatory authority. Business contact information for the facility environmental compliance office.

attributes.name: contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary phone number for permit-related communications with the regulatory authority. Business contact information for the facility environmental compliance office.

attributes.name: control_efficiency_required_percent
attributes.description: Minimum required control efficiency percentage for pollution control equipment as specified in the permit. Represents the percentage reduction in pollutant concentration that must be achieved.

attributes.name: control_equipment_required
attributes.description: Description of pollution control equipment or technologies required by the permit to achieve compliance with emission or discharge limits. May include scrubbers, baghouses, electrostatic precipitators, cooling towers, or wastewater treatment systems.
attributes.references: EPA Best Available Control Technology Standards

attributes.name: cooling_water_intake_limit_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cooling Water Intake Flow Limit (Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable cooling water intake flow rate in million gallons per day as specified under Clean Water Act Section 316(b) requirements. Regulates intake structure impacts on aquatic organisms.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 316 Section 316(b) Cooling Water Intake Structures

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system from which this permit record was extracted. May include state DEQ permit databases, EPA ECHO database, or internal environmental compliance management systems.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the environmental permit becomes legally binding and enforceable. May differ from issuance date if permit includes a delayed effective date.

attributes.name: emission_limit_tons_per_year
attributes.description: Maximum allowable emission quantity in tons per year for the regulated pollutant as specified in the air permit. Applies to Title V and PSD air permits.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 70 Title V Permit Program

attributes.name: emission_rate_limit_lbs_per_mmbtu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Permitted Emission Rate Limit (Pounds per Million British Thermal Units)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable emission rate in pounds per million BTU of heat input for the regulated pollutant. Common metric for fossil fuel combustion sources.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 60 New Source Performance Standards

attributes.name: enforcement_action_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit is currently subject to regulatory enforcement action such as notice of violation, consent decree, or administrative order.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the environmental permit authorization expires and renewal is required. Critical for compliance tracking and renewal planning.

attributes.name: hazardous_waste_quantity_limit_tons_per_month
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hazardous Waste Quantity Limit (Tons per Month)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable quantity of hazardous waste that may be generated or stored per month under the RCRA permit. Applies to facilities with hazardous waste generation or treatment operations.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 262 Hazardous Waste Generator Standards

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the environmental permit was officially issued by the regulatory authority. Marks the beginning of the permit authorization period.

attributes.name: issuing_agency
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory authority that issued the environmental permit. May be EPA, state Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), or other environmental regulatory body with jurisdiction over the facility.

attributes.name: issuing_agency_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the regulatory agency that issued the permit. Enables consistent tracking across multiple jurisdictions.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent regulatory inspection conducted by the issuing agency to verify permit compliance. Supports audit readiness and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: last_inspection_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the most recent regulatory inspection. Indicates whether the facility was found in compliance or if violations were identified.

attributes.name: last_violation_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent permit violation or non-compliance event. Critical for tracking compliance history and enforcement actions.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency of compliance monitoring and reporting as specified in the permit. Determines how often emissions, discharges, or waste parameters must be measured and reported. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: continuous|hourly|daily|weekly|monthly|quarterly|annual — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: penalty_amount_usd
attributes.description: Total monetary penalties assessed for permit violations in US dollars. Includes civil penalties, fines, and settlement amounts related to this permit.

attributes.name: permit_conditions
attributes.description: Detailed text of special conditions, operational restrictions, monitoring requirements, and compliance stipulations imposed by the regulatory authority as part of the permit authorization.

attributes.name: permit_fee_amount_usd
attributes.description: Annual or one-time permit fee paid to the regulatory authority in US dollars. Title V permits typically require annual fees based on actual emissions.

attributes.name: permit_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name or title of the environmental permit as documented in the permit authorization.

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: Official permit number assigned by the issuing regulatory agency. Serves as the externally-recognized identifier for this authorization.

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the environmental permit. Indicates whether the permit is active and in compliance, expired and requiring renewal, pending regulatory review, suspended due to violations, or revoked by the issuing authority.

attributes.name: permit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the environmental permit by regulatory program. Categorizes the permit into major environmental compliance frameworks such as Title V air operating permits, NPDES water discharge permits, PSD construction permits, state air quality permits, hazardous waste permits, or 316(b) cooling water intake structure permits.

attributes.name: pollutant_type
attributes.description: Primary pollutant or environmental parameter regulated by this permit. May include air pollutants (NOx, SO2, CO2, PM), water discharge parameters (temperature, pH, chemical concentrations), or waste categories.

attributes.name: public_notice_date
attributes.description: Date on which public notice of the permit application or renewal was published. Marks the beginning of the public comment period.

attributes.name: public_notice_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether public notice and comment period is required for permit issuance or renewal under applicable regulations. Typically required for major source permits.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was first created in the data management system. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was last updated in the data management system. Tracks the currency of permit information for compliance reporting.

attributes.name: renewal_application_deadline
attributes.description: Deadline by which the permit renewal application must be submitted to the regulatory authority. Typically 180 days before expiration for Title V permits.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 70 Title V Permit Program

attributes.name: renewal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the permit was last renewed or is scheduled for renewal. Supports proactive permit renewal management and compliance planning.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency of compliance reports to be submitted to the regulatory authority. Specifies how often the facility must file monitoring data and compliance certifications.

attributes.name: responsible_party_name
attributes.description: Name of the individual or organization legally responsible for permit compliance. Typically the facility operator or designated responsible official.

attributes.name: responsible_party_title
attributes.description: Job title or position of the responsible party. Common titles include Environmental Manager, Plant Manager, or Compliance Officer.

attributes.name: violation_count
attributes.description: Total number of permit violations recorded for this permit during the current permit term. Supports compliance performance tracking and enforcement risk assessment.

attributes.name: water_discharge_limit_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Permitted Water Discharge Limit (Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable water discharge flow rate in million gallons per day as specified in the NPDES permit. Applies to cooling water discharge and wastewater effluent.

attributes.name: water_temperature_limit_f
attributes.description: Maximum allowable temperature in degrees Fahrenheit for water discharged under the NPDES permit. Critical for thermal pollution control at steam electric generating facilities.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 423 Steam Electric Power Generating Effluent Guidelines

attributes.name: renewed_environmental_permit_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on environmental_permit (renewed_environmental_permit_id)

domains.name: transmission
domains.description: Governs high-voltage bulk electric system (BES) infrastructure for power transport across the grid — transmission lines, substations, transformers, and switching equipment. Manages grid topology, OATT compliance, RTO/ISO interchange scheduling, LMP data, transmission capacity, congestion, and interconnection requests. Critical for NERC CIP compliance and FERC jurisdictional reporting.
domains.references: FERC OATT, NERC CIP & Reliability Standards, RTO/ISO

products.name: line
products.description: Master record for high-voltage bulk electric system (BES) transmission lines owned and operated by the utility. Captures line identifier, voltage class (kV), circuit configuration (single/double), conductor type, rated thermal capacity (MVA), line length (miles), in-service date, NERC BES classification, FERC jurisdiction flag, RTO/ISO region, GIS route reference, operating status, and ownership percentage. Serves as the SSOT for transmission line infrastructure identity and physical characteristics. Source system: ESRI ArcGIS and Oracle WAM/IBM Maximo.
products.reference: NERC BES Transmission Line

attributes.name: line_id
attributes.description: Primary key for line

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Links completed transmission lines to their originating capital projects for CWIP-to-plant transfer tracking, AFUDC capitalization verification, project closeout reconciliation, and audit trail from a

attributes.name: conductor_material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Transmission lines are constructed from specific conductor materials (ACSR, ACCR, etc.). Material master enables procurement planning for line construction/rebuild projects, standardization of conduct

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Transmission lines are subject to CPCN proceedings for siting/construction, rate base inclusion in rate cases, and FERC jurisdictional oversight. Business process: FERC Form 1 reporting, prudency revi

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Transmission lines are capitalized plant assets with book values, accumulated depreciation, and rate base treatment tracked in fixed_asset. Required for FERC Form 1 reporting, depreciation studies, an

attributes.name: from_bus_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.bus. Business justification: Transmission lines connect two buses (electrical connection points). The from_bus_id FK establishes the origin bus. This is a critical topological relationship for power flow modeling and grid analysi

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Transmission lines are major capital assets requiring comprehensive lifecycle management, maintenance scheduling, and regulatory compliance tracking. Other transmission products (substation, transform

attributes.name: to_transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: FK to transmission.transmission_substation

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: Transmission lines connect two substations. The from_substation_code (STRING) should be replaced with a proper FK from_substation_id → transmission_substation.transmission_substation_id. This allows j

attributes.name: available_transfer_capability_mw
attributes.description: Available Transfer Capability of the transmission line in Megawatts (MW), representing the remaining transfer capacity available for additional transactions after accounting for existing commitments and reliability margins. Published on OASIS per FERC OATT requirements.
attributes.references: FERC OATT; NERC MOD-001 (Available Transmission System Capability)

attributes.name: bes_classified
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transmission line is classified as part of the NERC Bulk Electric System (BES). BES-classified lines are subject to NERC Reliability Standards (CIP, FAC, TPL, etc.) and FERC jurisdiction. True = BES; False = non-BES (sub-transmission or distribution).
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition (Effective July 1, 2014); FERC Order 773

attributes.name: circuit_configuration
attributes.description: Physical circuit arrangement of the transmission line structure. Single circuit carries one three-phase circuit; double circuit carries two three-phase circuits on the same tower structure, affecting redundancy and contingency analysis.
attributes.references: NERC TPL Transmission Planning Standards; IEEE Std 738

attributes.name: co_owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the joint owner(s) of the transmission line when ownership_percentage is less than 100%. Relevant for joint-use agreements, cost-sharing arrangements, and FERC Form 1 disclosure of jointly-owned plant.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; FERC OATT Joint Ownership provisions

attributes.name: commissioning_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total capital cost incurred to construct and commission the transmission line, expressed in US dollars. Represents the gross plant-in-service value for FERC rate base inclusion, depreciation base, and CAPEX tracking. Classified confidential as it contains sensitive financial data.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 (Account 350–359 Electric Plant in Service); GAAP ASC 360; SOX

attributes.name: depreciation_rate_pct
attributes.description: Annual straight-line depreciation rate applied to the transmission line as a percentage of original cost. Established through PUC-approved depreciation studies and used for regulatory accounting, rate case filings, and FERC Form 1 reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 360; PUC depreciation orders

attributes.name: emergency_rating_mva
attributes.description: Short-term emergency thermal rating of the transmission line in Megavolt-Amperes (MVA). Represents the maximum allowable power flow for a limited duration (typically 15–30 minutes) during contingency conditions. Used in N-1 and N-2 contingency analysis.

attributes.name: ems_element_reference
attributes.description: Identifier for this transmission line element within the ABB or GE Energy Management System (EMS) / SCADA platform. Used for real-time monitoring, state estimation, and contingency analysis in the EMS network model.
attributes.references: ABB / GE Energy Management System; NERC MOD-032

attributes.name: ferc_jurisdictional
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Jurisdictional Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transmission line is subject to FERC jurisdiction under the Federal Power Act. FERC-jurisdictional lines must comply with OATT requirements, transmission pricing rules, and FERC Form 1 reporting obligations.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 205/206; FERC OATT; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: gis_feature_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the transmission line feature in the ESRI ArcGIS geospatial network model. Enables spatial joins, route tracing, and GIS-based outage analysis.

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: Date the transmission line was placed into commercial service and energized. Used for depreciation calculations, AFUDC capitalization cutoff, FERC rate base inclusion, and asset age tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 360 (Property, Plant and Equipment); Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: insulation_type
attributes.description: Type of insulation used on the transmission line conductors or cable. For overhead lines: ceramic, glass, or polymer insulators. For underground/submarine cables: XLPE or oil-paper. Affects dielectric performance, maintenance intervals, and failure mode analysis.
attributes.references: IEEE Std C2 (NESC); ESRI ArcGIS Network Model

attributes.name: interconnection_type
attributes.description: Classification of the transmission line based on the entities it interconnects. Intra-utility lines connect points within the same utility system; inter-utility lines connect different utilities; interstate lines cross state boundaries; international lines cross national borders.
attributes.references: FERC OATT; NERC Reliability Coordinator boundaries

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent physical inspection of the transmission line (aerial patrol, ground patrol, or detailed inspection). Used to track compliance with NERC FAC-003 vegetation management and internal maintenance standards.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-003; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: length_miles
attributes.description: Total route length of the transmission line in miles, as measured along the physical corridor. Used for impedance calculations, O&M cost allocation, FERC Form 1 reporting, and rate base determination.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 (Electric Utility Annual Report); ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: line_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code or tag uniquely identifying the transmission line across operational systems (GIS, EMS, SCADA, WAM). Serves as the business key for cross-system integration.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: line_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation assigned to the transmission line (e.g., 'Northgate–Riverside 345kV'). Used in operational communications, SCADA displays, and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: line_type
attributes.description: Physical construction type of the transmission line. Overhead lines use towers/poles with air insulation; underground lines use buried cable; submarine lines cross bodies of water. Affects maintenance practices, outage risk, and capital cost classification.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; ESRI ArcGIS Network Model

attributes.name: multi_state_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission line crosses state boundaries. Multi-state lines may be subject to multiple PUC jurisdictions and require coordinated regulatory reporting. True = crosses state lines; False = single-state.
attributes.references: State PUC jurisdictional rules; FERC Federal Power Act

attributes.name: nerc_cip_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transmission line is within scope of NERC CIP cybersecurity standards as a Critical Cyber Asset or associated Physical Security Perimeter. Drives cybersecurity and physical security compliance obligations.

attributes.name: next_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date on which the next scheduled inspection of the transmission line is due. Drives preventive maintenance work order generation in the EAM system and ensures compliance with inspection frequency requirements.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-003; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: number_of_structures
attributes.description: Total count of towers, poles, or support structures along the transmission line route. Used for asset inventory, maintenance planning, and storm restoration resource estimation.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: operating_status
attributes.description: Current operational lifecycle status of the transmission line. Drives inclusion in power flow models, maintenance scheduling, NERC compliance scope, and FERC rate base eligibility. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: in_service|out_of_service|mothballed|retired|under_construction|planned — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition; FERC Form 1; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: ownership_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the transmission line owned by this utility (0.00–100.00). Lines may be jointly owned with other utilities or transmission companies. Drives rate base allocation, O&M cost sharing, and FERC Form 1 reporting of owned vs. leased plant.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 810 (Consolidation); FERC OATT

attributes.name: protection_scheme
attributes.description: Description of the primary relay protection scheme applied to the transmission line (e.g., distance relay, differential relay, pilot protection, directional overcurrent). Critical for NERC PRC (Protection and Control) compliance and fault clearing time analysis.
attributes.references: NERC PRC-023 (Transmission Relay Loadability); IEEE Std C37.113

attributes.name: rated_capacity_mva
attributes.description: Normal (continuous) thermal rating of the transmission line expressed in Megavolt-Amperes (MVA). Represents the maximum power flow the line can carry under normal operating conditions without exceeding conductor temperature limits. Used in power flow studies, congestion management, and OATT ATC calculations.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-008 (Facility Ratings); FERC OATT; IEEE Std 738

attributes.name: reactance_ohms_per_mile
attributes.description: Positive-sequence inductive reactance of the conductor in ohms per mile. Essential parameter for power flow, stability, and short-circuit analysis in the transmission network model.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission line master record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle management.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this transmission line master record in the Silver Layer. Used for change data capture, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Databricks Delta Lake change data feed

attributes.name: resistance_ohms_per_mile
attributes.description: Positive-sequence AC resistance of the conductor in ohms per mile at operating temperature. Core electrical parameter used in power flow models, load flow studies, and loss calculations.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 738; NERC MOD-032 (Data for Power Flow and Stability Models)

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date the transmission line was permanently retired from service. Triggers removal from rate base, cessation of depreciation, and decommissioning obligations. Null if the line is still active.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 360; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: right_of_way_width_ft
attributes.description: Width of the transmission line right-of-way corridor in feet. Used for vegetation management compliance (NERC FAC-003), land use planning, encroachment management, and environmental permitting.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-003 (Transmission Vegetation Management); ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Region
attributes.description: Name or code of the RTO or ISO within whose footprint this transmission line operates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE). Determines market rules, LMP pricing nodes, and interchange scheduling protocols.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000 (RTO Formation); NERC Reliability Coordinator boundaries

attributes.name: scada_monitored
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transmission line is monitored and controllable via the SCADA/EMS system. SCADA-monitored lines provide real-time telemetry (MW flow, MVAr, voltage, breaker status) to the Energy Management System for grid operations.
attributes.references: NERC COM-001 (Telecommunications); ABB / GE Energy Management System

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code (USPS abbreviation) for the primary state in which the transmission line is located. For multi-state lines, represents the state of the majority of the route length. Used for PUC jurisdictional determination and state regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) jurisdictional rules; USPS State Abbreviations

attributes.name: structure_type
attributes.description: Type of tower or pole structure supporting the overhead transmission line. Affects structural loading calculations, maintenance practices, and asset replacement planning.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Network Model; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; NESC (National Electrical Safety Code)

attributes.name: total_transfer_capability_mw
attributes.description: Total Transfer Capability of the transmission line in Megawatts (MW), representing the maximum amount of electric power that can be transferred reliably over the line under specified system conditions. Basis for ATC calculations published on OASIS.

attributes.name: voltage_class_kv
attributes.description: Nominal operating voltage class of the transmission line expressed in kilovolts (kV). Common BES voltage classes include 69 kV, 115 kV, 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, 500 kV, and 765 kV. Determines NERC BES applicability threshold (≥100 kV) and FERC jurisdictional classification.
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1110

attributes.name: wam_asset_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Work and Asset Management (WAM) Asset ID
attributes.description: Asset identifier assigned by the Enterprise Asset Management system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) for maintenance scheduling, work order management, and asset lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: year_constructed
attributes.description: Calendar year in which the transmission line was originally constructed. Distinct from in_service_date; used for asset age analysis, infrastructure investment planning, and IRP long-range capital forecasting.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; FERC Form 1

products.name: transmission_substation
products.description: Master record for transmission substations including switching stations and transformer banks at the bulk electric system level. Captures substation name, NERC node ID, voltage levels served (kV high/low), substation type (switching, step-down, converter), installed transformer capacity (MVA), bus configuration, SCADA point reference, GIS coordinates, NERC CIP classification (high/medium/low impact), in-service date, and operating status. SSOT for substation identity across the transmission network. Source system: ESRI ArcGIS, OSIsoft PI/GE Proficy, ABB/GE EMS.
products.reference: NERC BES Substation / IEC CIM Substation

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the transmission substation record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this master resource entity.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 693, NERC Glossary of Terms

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Substations are constructed via capital projects; link enables CWIP accounting, project cost rollup to FERC plant accounts, regulatory cost recovery documentation, and variance analysis between author

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.control_area. Business justification: Transmission substations operate within control areas. The transmission_substation table has control_area STRING. Normalizing to FK to control_area. Removes control_area string.

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Substations require CPCN approval for construction, are included in rate base for cost recovery, and are subject to environmental/siting proceedings. Business process: capital project approval filings

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Substations are major capital assets requiring financial tracking of original cost, depreciation, and net book value for regulatory reporting, rate base calculations, and asset retirement obligation a

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Asset identifier for this substation in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management system. Used to link to preventive and corrective maintenance work orders, inspection records, and asset health scores.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo; ISO 55000 Asset Management

attributes.name: operator_id
attributes.description: FK to transmission.operator

attributes.name: bes_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this substation is classified as part of the Bulk Electric System (BES) per the NERC BES definition. BES classification triggers NERC reliability standard applicability including CIP, FAC, TPL, and PRC standards.
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition; NERC FAC-001; NERC CIP-002

attributes.name: bus_configuration
attributes.description: Electrical bus arrangement scheme of the substation switchyard. Determines switching flexibility, reliability, and maintenance capability. Used in protection coordination studies and reliability modeling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: single_bus|double_bus|ring_bus|breaker_and_half|main_and_transfer|double_bus_double_breaker — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date the substation completed commissioning testing and was accepted as ready for service, prior to the official in-service date. Distinct from in_service_date; used for warranty tracking and construction project closeout in SAP S/4HANA.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 693; SAP S/4HANA Project Systems; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: communications_type
attributes.description: Primary telecommunications medium used for SCADA telemetry and protection signaling at this substation. Relevant for NERC CIP-005 Electronic Security Perimeter and CIP-006 Physical Security compliance assessments.

attributes.name: county
attributes.description: County or parish in which the substation is located. Used for property tax jurisdiction, permitting authority determination, and state PUC service territory reporting.
attributes.references: State PUC reporting requirements; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: decommission_date
attributes.description: Date the substation was or is planned to be permanently removed from service and decommissioned. Nullable for active substations. Used for asset retirement accounting, regulatory notification to FERC under FPA Section 203, and IRP planning.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; FPA Section 203; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: elevation_m
attributes.description: Elevation of the substation site above mean sea level in meters. Used for equipment insulation coordination (altitude derating), flood risk assessment, and GIS spatial modeling.
attributes.references: IEEE Std C57.12.00; ESRI ArcGIS; WGS84

attributes.name: ems_node_reference
attributes.description: Node or bus identifier within the ABB or GE Energy Management System (EMS) network topology model corresponding to this substation. Used for state estimation, contingency analysis, and generation dispatch coordination.
attributes.references: IEC 61970 CIM; ABB Network Manager; GE EMS

attributes.name: ferc_account_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Number
attributes.description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USofA) account number under which the substation assets are recorded (e.g., Account 352 for Structures and Improvements, Account 353 for Station Equipment). Used for FERC Form 1 plant-in-service reporting and rate base determination.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: ferc_jurisdiction_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Jurisdiction Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this substation is subject to FERC jurisdictional oversight under the Federal Power Act (FPA). True for interstate transmission facilities; False for state-jurisdictional or non-jurisdictional assets. Drives FERC Form 1 inclusion and OATT applicability.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act (FPA) Section 201; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: gis_feature_reference
attributes.description: Unique feature identifier for this substation in the ESRI ArcGIS geospatial network model. Used to link the substation record to its spatial geometry, network connectivity, and GIS-based asset layers.

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: Date the substation was officially placed into commercial or operational service on the bulk electric system. Used for asset age calculations, depreciation schedules in SAP S/4HANA, FERC Form 1 plant-in-service reporting, and AFUDC capitalization cutoff.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: installed_capacity_mva
attributes.description: Total installed transformer capacity at the substation in Megavolt-Amperes (MVA), summing all transformer banks. The principal quantitative measure of the substation's power handling capability. Used for capacity planning, congestion analysis, and FERC Form 1 reporting.
attributes.references: IEEE Std C57.12.00; FERC Form 1; NERC TPL standards

attributes.name: land_ownership_type
attributes.description: Classification of the land tenure arrangement for the substation site. Affects property accounting treatment under GAAP, FERC Uniform System of Accounts land account classification, and site access rights for maintenance.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 842

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal inspection or condition assessment of the substation. Used to track compliance with NERC FAC-003 vegetation management, NERC CIP-006 physical security inspections, and internal O&M maintenance schedules.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-003; NERC CIP-006; IEEE Std 693

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the substation site in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS mapping, emergency response routing, and spatial analysis of grid topology.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the substation site in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS mapping, emergency response routing, and spatial analysis of grid topology.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection (NERC CIP) Classification
attributes.description: NERC CIP impact classification of the substation per NERC CIP-002 BES Cyber System Categorization. Determines the cybersecurity control requirements applicable to associated BES Cyber Systems. Classified as confidential due to critical infrastructure sensitivity.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-002-5.1a; NERC CIP-003 through CIP-014

attributes.name: nerc_node_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Node ID
attributes.description: NERC-assigned unique node identifier for this substation within the bulk electric system (BES) topology model. Used for NERC compliance reporting, reliability assessments, and RTO/ISO power flow models.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms; NERC FAC-001; NERC FAC-002

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the next planned preventive maintenance activity for the substation as scheduled in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo. Used for maintenance planning, outage coordination, and NERC maintenance interval compliance tracking.
attributes.references: NERC PRC-005; Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo; ISO 55000

attributes.name: num_transformer_banks
