attributes.description: Name or identifier of the generation resource or energy source associated with the transmission service request at the point of receipt. Used for interconnection queue coordination and system impact studies.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003; FERC OATT Pro Forma

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time the transmission service request was formally submitted to the transmission provider via the OASIS portal. This is the principal business event timestamp establishing queue priority.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; OATT Pro Forma Section 17

attributes.name: system_impact_study_completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the System Impact Study was completed and results were communicated to the requesting entity. FERC mandates specific timelines for study completion under the OATT.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003; OATT Pro Forma Section 36

attributes.name: system_impact_study_status
attributes.description: Current status of the System Impact Study (SIS) evaluating the effect of the requested transmission service on the reliability and security of the bulk electric system. Second study phase under FERC Order 2003.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003; NERC FAC-002; OATT Pro Forma

attributes.name: tariff_rate_schedule
attributes.business_glossary_term: Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) Rate Schedule
attributes.description: The specific OATT rate schedule applicable to this transmission service request (e.g., Schedule 7 for firm PTP, Schedule 8 for non-firm PTP). Determines the transmission rate and ancillary service charges applied.
attributes.references: FERC OATT Pro Forma; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: transmission_provider_code
attributes.description: NERC-assigned or FERC-registered code identifying the transmission provider (utility) responsible for processing this service request. Required for OASIS filings and FERC Form 1 reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 889; NERC Glossary; OASIS Standards

attributes.name: transmission_rate_mw_per_year
attributes.business_glossary_term: Transmission Rate (USD per MW per Year)
attributes.description: The applicable transmission rate in US Dollars per Megawatt per year as specified in the OATT rate schedule for this service request. Used for revenue requirement calculation and billing.
attributes.references: FERC OATT Pro Forma; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission service request record was last modified in the data platform. Used for change tracking and incremental data processing.

attributes.name: withdrawal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the requesting entity formally withdrew the transmission service request from the queue. Null for active or completed requests. Used for queue management and capacity release tracking.
attributes.references: FERC OATT Pro Forma Section 13; FERC Order 890

products.name: interconnection_request
products.description: Manages generator and large-load interconnection requests submitted under FERC Order 2003/2006 (LGIP/SGIP) processes. Captures request ID, applicant entity, project type (generation/load), technology type (thermal/wind/solar/storage), requested capacity (MW), proposed point of interconnection (POI), queue position, study phase (feasibility/system impact/facilities), estimated upgrade cost ($), commercial operation date (COD) target, and request status. SSOT for interconnection queue management. Source system: Transmission planning and interconnection management systems.
products.reference: FERC Order 2003 LGIP / FERC Order 2006 SGIP

attributes.name: interconnection_request_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the interconnection request record. Primary key for the interconnection request entity.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Approved interconnection requests trigger network upgrade capital projects. Link tracks cost responsibility allocation, CIAC vs. utility-funded determination, reimbursement accounting, and financial s

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Interconnection processes must comply with FERC Order 2023, state interconnection standards, and RTO tariff study timeline obligations. Business process: queue management compliance, study milestone t

attributes.name: participant_registration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.participant_registration. Business justification: Interconnection requests are submitted by registered market participants (generators/developers). RTO queue management, study coordination, cost allocation, and capacity market qualification all requi

attributes.name: plant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to generation.plant. Business justification: Tracks lifecycle from interconnection request to operational plant after commercial operation date. Essential for project development tracking, queue management, FERC Form 556 reporting, and reconcili

attributes.name: poi_bus_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.bus. Business justification: Interconnection requests specify a point of interconnection (POI), which is a specific bus in the transmission system. This FK links the request to the actual bus. Removes poi_voltage_kv as redundant

attributes.name: regulatory_asset_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.regulatory_asset_entry. Business justification: Network upgrade costs funded by utility and recovered over time are recorded as regulatory assets per FERC Order 2003. Link tracks cost recovery, amortization, and carrying charges for interconnection

attributes.name: rto_iso_id
attributes.description: FK to market.rto_iso

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: Interconnection requests specify a point of interconnection (POI) at a transmission substation. The poi_substation_name (STRING) should be replaced with a proper FK poi_substation_id → transmission_su

attributes.name: actual_cod
attributes.description: Actual date when the project achieved commercial operation. Populated only after the project is energized and operational.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: applicant_contact_email
attributes.description: Primary email address for the applicant or their authorized representative for interconnection request communications.

attributes.name: applicant_contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number for the applicant or their authorized representative.

attributes.name: applicant_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the entity or individual submitting the interconnection request. May be a generation developer, industrial customer, or distributed energy resource owner.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interconnection request record was first created in the system. Used for audit and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: environmental_permit_status
attributes.description: Status of required environmental permits (e.g., EPA air quality permits, state environmental permits, wetlands permits) for the generation project.

attributes.name: estimated_interconnection_facility_cost
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Interconnection Facility Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Estimated cost in USD for the direct interconnection facilities (e.g., generator lead line, metering equipment, protective relays) required to connect the project to the point of interconnection.

attributes.name: estimated_network_upgrade_cost
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Network Upgrade Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Estimated total cost in USD for transmission network upgrades required to accommodate the interconnection. Includes substation modifications, line upgrades, and protection system enhancements. Based on facilities study results.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, FERC Transmission Planning Standards

attributes.name: facilities_study_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when the facilities study was completed and results delivered to the applicant.

attributes.name: facilities_study_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the facilities study phase commenced. Facilities study provides detailed engineering design and final cost estimates for required upgrades.

attributes.name: feasibility_study_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when the feasibility study was completed and results delivered to the applicant.

attributes.name: feasibility_study_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the feasibility study phase commenced. Feasibility study evaluates high-level technical viability and preliminary cost estimates.

attributes.name: interconnection_agreement_executed_date
attributes.description: Date when the formal interconnection agreement (IA) or generator interconnection agreement (GIA) was executed between the applicant and the transmission provider.

attributes.name: is_energy_only
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the applicant requested Energy Resource Interconnection Service (ERIS), which allows energy-only delivery without firm capacity rights.

attributes.name: is_network_resource
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the applicant requested Network Resource Interconnection Service (NRIS), which allows the generator to be designated as a network resource for capacity and energy delivery.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interconnection request record was last updated. Used for audit and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special conditions, or clarifications related to the interconnection request. Used for internal coordination and regulatory reporting context.

attributes.name: poi_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the proposed point of interconnection in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and transmission planning analysis.

attributes.name: poi_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the proposed point of interconnection in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and transmission planning analysis.

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.description: Business name or title of the generation or load project seeking interconnection. Used for public queue reporting and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: project_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interconnection request by project category: generation (new power plant), load (large industrial customer), or storage (battery/pumped hydro).

attributes.name: queue_position
attributes.description: Numeric position of this request in the interconnection queue, determining study and construction priority. Lower numbers indicate earlier queue entry.

attributes.name: request_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the interconnection request, typically assigned by the transmission provider or RTO/ISO. Used in regulatory filings and customer communications.

attributes.name: request_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the interconnection request in the queue management process. Tracks progression through FERC-mandated study phases. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: submitted|under_review|feasibility_study|system_impact_study|facilities_study|approved|withdrawn|suspended|rejected|completed — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: requested_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total generating or load capacity in megawatts (MW) requested for interconnection. Determines study scope and network upgrade requirements.

attributes.name: requires_nerc_registration
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Registration Required Indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the project will require NERC registration as a Generator Owner (GO) or Generator Operator (GOP) based on capacity and voltage thresholds.

attributes.name: study_phase
attributes.description: Current phase of the FERC-mandated interconnection study process. Progresses from feasibility study through system impact study to facilities study.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the interconnection request was formally submitted to the transmission provider or RTO/ISO. Establishes queue position priority.

attributes.name: system_impact_study_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when the system impact study was completed and results delivered to the applicant.

attributes.name: system_impact_study_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the system impact study phase commenced. System impact study analyzes detailed grid impacts and required network upgrades.

attributes.name: target_cod
attributes.description: Applicant's proposed date for the project to achieve commercial operation and begin delivering energy or capacity to the grid. Critical for transmission planning and resource adequacy forecasting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003, NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: technology_type

products.name: congestion_event
products.description: Records transmission congestion events on the BES — instances where physical or economic constraints limit power flow on a transmission path, flowgate, or monitored element. Each record represents a single binding or near-binding constraint event. Captures event ID, constrained element reference (line/transformer/flowgate), constraint type (thermal/voltage/stability/contractual), start/end datetime, duration (hours), binding constraint flag, shadow price ($/MWh), congestion cost ($), curtailed MW, TLR level (if applicable), RTO/ISO constraint name, associated LMP congestion component reference, and resolution action taken (redispatch/TLR/switching/load shed). Used for congestion cost tracking, FTR/ARR hedging analysis, transmission upgrade economic justification, and NERC TPL compliance. Source system: ABB/GE EMS, RTO/ISO constraint and LMP data feeds.
products.reference: NERC TPL / RTO ISO Congestion Management

attributes.name: outage_id

attributes.description: Indicates whether the constrained element is classified as part of the Bulk Electric System (true) under NERC definitions, which determines applicability of NERC reliability standards and FERC jurisdiction.

attributes.name: binding_constraint_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the constraint was fully binding (true) or near-binding/monitoring (false) during the event. Binding constraints directly impact dispatch and pricing.

attributes.name: congestion_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total economic cost of the congestion event in US dollars, calculated as the product of shadow price, curtailed MW, and duration. Used for transmission upgrade economic justification and FTR/ARR hedging analysis.

attributes.name: constraint_name
attributes.description: The RTO/ISO-assigned name or identifier for the binding constraint as reported in the market systems (e.g., constraint ID from day-ahead or real-time market).

attributes.name: constraint_type
attributes.description: Classification of the physical or economic constraint that caused the congestion event: thermal (line/transformer loading limit), voltage (voltage stability limit), stability (transient or dynamic stability limit), contractual (OATT or tariff-based limit), or other.

attributes.name: contingency_element_name
attributes.description: The name of the transmission element whose outage or failure would cause the monitored element to exceed its limit. Used for N-1 and N-2 contingency analysis and NERC TPL compliance.

attributes.name: curtailed_mw
attributes.description: The amount of power flow in megawatts that was curtailed or limited due to the binding constraint. Represents the difference between desired and actual flow on the constrained element.

attributes.name: duration_hours
attributes.description: Total duration of the congestion event in hours, calculated as the difference between event start and end timestamps. Used for congestion cost allocation and transmission planning analysis.

attributes.name: element_rating_mw
attributes.description: The thermal, voltage, or stability rating of the constrained element in megawatts, representing the maximum allowable power flow under the applicable operating conditions (normal, emergency, or contingency).

attributes.name: event_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the transmission constraint was relieved and the congestion event concluded. Null if the event is still active. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the transmission constraint became binding or near-binding, marking the beginning of the congestion event. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the congestion event: active (constraint is currently binding), resolved (constraint has been relieved), monitoring (near-binding, under observation), or escalated (requires TLR or emergency action).

attributes.name: generation_redispatch_mw
attributes.description: The total amount of generation redispatch in megawatts that was required to relieve the congestion event. Represents the change in generation output across multiple units to reduce constraint loading.

attributes.name: interconnection_name
attributes.description: The North American electric interconnection in which the congestion event occurred: Eastern, Western, ERCOT (Texas), or Quebec. Interconnections operate as synchronous grids with limited DC ties between them.

attributes.name: load_shed_mw
attributes.description: The amount of customer load in megawatts that was curtailed or shed as a last-resort action to relieve the congestion event. Non-zero values indicate emergency operating conditions.

attributes.name: market_interval_type
attributes.description: The market timeframe in which the congestion event occurred: day_ahead (DAM), real_time (RTM), or intra_day (intermediate market run). Used for market settlement and congestion revenue rights allocation.

attributes.name: monitored_element_name
attributes.description: The name or designation of the specific transmission element (line, transformer, or interface) that was monitored and experienced the constraint. May differ from the constrained element if the constraint is a proxy or aggregate.

attributes.name: nerc_region

attributes.description: The NERC regional entity jurisdiction in which the congestion event occurred: WECC (Western), ERCOT (Texas), MRO (Midwest), NPCC (Northeast), RF (ReliabilityFirst), SERC (Southeast), SPP (Southwest), or TRE (Texas RE). attributes.name: outage_related_flag

attributes.name: post_contingency_flow_mw
attributes.description: The projected or actual power flow in megawatts on the monitored element following the contingency event. Used to determine constraint severity and required relief actions.

attributes.name: pre_contingency_flow_mw
attributes.description: The power flow in megawatts on the monitored element under normal (pre-contingency) operating conditions, before the contingency event that triggered the constraint.

attributes.name: rating_type
attributes.description: The type of facility rating that was exceeded or approached during the congestion event: normal (continuous rating), emergency (short-term rating for system disturbances), or contingency (post-contingency rating for N-1 or N-2 analysis).

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this congestion event record was first created in the source system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this congestion event record was last modified in the source system. Used for change tracking and incremental data processing.

attributes.name: resolution_action
attributes.description: The operational action taken to resolve or mitigate the congestion event: redispatch (generation re-optimization), tlr (Transmission Loading Relief procedure), switching (network reconfiguration), load_shed (demand curtailment), topology_change (line/transformer switching), or none (constraint self-resolved).

attributes.name: shadow_price_per_mwh
attributes.description: The marginal cost of the transmission constraint in dollars per MWh, representing the economic value of relieving the constraint by one additional MWh. Also known as the congestion component of LMP.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system that recorded or reported the congestion event data (e.g., ABB EMS, GE EMS, RTO market system, SCADA historian). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Description of the weather conditions at the time of the congestion event (e.g., high temperature, storm, wind, ice). Weather is a common driver of transmission congestion due to increased load or reduced line ratings.

products.name: outage
products.description: Records planned, forced, and maintenance outages of BES transmission elements (lines, transformers, substations, buses, switching equipment) for maintenance, construction, emergency restoration, or third-party accommodation. Each record represents a distinct BES cyber system (e.g., EMS, SCADA RTU, relay communication processor) within a CIP-regulated substation or control center. Captures asset ID, associated substation or control center, BES cyber system identifier, impact rating (high/medium/low per CIP-002-5.1a), applicable CIP standard requirements (CIP-002 through CIP-014), electronic security perimeter (ESP) membership, physical security perimeter (PSP) membership, responsible entity, last vulnerability assessment date, last CIP audit date, evidence artifact reference, compliance status, remediation plan reference, and next assessment due date. attributes.description: Indicates whether transmission congestion charges (based on Locational Marginal Price differences) apply in addition to the stated transmission rate. Typically true in RTO/ISO markets with nodal pricing.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission rate record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this rate record. Power and Utilities operates exclusively in United States dollars (USD).

attributes.name: demand_charge_per_kw_month
attributes.business_glossary_term: Demand Charge per Kilowatt (kW) per Month
attributes.description: Monthly demand charge component of the transmission rate, expressed in dollars per kilowatt (kW) of reserved transmission capacity per month. This is the primary cost driver for firm transmission service.

attributes.name: discount_policy_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate schedule permits discounting below the stated maximum rate. FERC allows transmission providers to offer discounted rates for competitive reasons, subject to non-discrimination requirements.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, FERC Discount Policy Statement

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this transmission rate becomes effective and applicable to transmission service agreements. Rates cannot be applied retroactively prior to FERC approval and the effective date specified in the tariff filing.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, FERC Tariff Filing Standards

attributes.name: energy_charge_per_mwh
attributes.description: Energy-based charge component of the transmission rate, expressed in dollars per megawatt-hour (MWh) of energy transmitted. Typically applies to non-firm or short-term point-to-point service.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this transmission rate expires and is superseded by a new rate schedule. Nullable for rates that remain in effect until explicitly superseded by a subsequent FERC-approved filing.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, FERC Tariff Filing Standards

attributes.name: ferc_docket_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Docket Number
attributes.description: FERC docket number under which this transmission rate was filed, reviewed, and approved. Format follows FERC convention: ER (Electric Rate), EL (Electric Litigation), or RM (Rulemaking) followed by year and sequential number.
attributes.references: FERC eTariff Filing System, FERC Docket Management

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission rate record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_rate_case_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent general transmission rate case filing that established or modified this rate. Rate cases are comprehensive regulatory proceedings to review and approve transmission revenue requirements and rate design.

attributes.name: loss_compensation_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of transmitted energy that must be provided by the transmission customer to compensate for electrical losses on the transmission system. Typically ranges from 1% to 5% depending on distance and voltage class.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, IEEE Transmission Loss Standards

attributes.name: maximum_reservation_kw
attributes.description: Maximum transmission capacity reservation allowed under this rate schedule, expressed in kilowatts (kW). Null if no maximum applies.

attributes.name: minimum_reservation_kw
attributes.description: Minimum transmission capacity reservation required to qualify for this rate, expressed in kilowatts (kW). Some rate schedules have minimum thresholds below which different rates or service terms apply.

attributes.name: nerc_region_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region Code
attributes.description: NERC regional reliability entity code indicating the geographic reliability region in which this transmission rate applies. Used for compliance reporting and reliability coordination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|ERCOT|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|TRE|SPP — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: next_rate_case_scheduled_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next general transmission rate case filing, if known. Null if no rate case is currently scheduled. Some formula rates update annually without full rate case proceedings.

attributes.name: point_of_delivery
attributes.description: Transmission system location or pricing node where power is withdrawn from the transmission system under a point-to-point transmission service agreement. Null for network integration transmission service.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, OATT Point-to-Point Service Standards

attributes.name: rate_basis
attributes.description: Methodology used to determine the transmission rate. Cost-of-service rates are based on embedded transmission system costs and allowed return on equity (ROE); market-based rates reflect competitive market conditions; formula rates adjust automatically based on actual costs; negotiated rates are bilaterally agreed; stated rates are fixed tariff rates.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, FERC Policy Statement on Formula Rates

attributes.name: rate_pancaking_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate is subject to pancaking (multiple transmission rate charges applied sequentially as power crosses multiple transmission owner service territories). FERC has worked to eliminate pancaking through RTO/ISO formation.

attributes.name: rate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the transmission rate based on the type of service provided. Network rates apply to bundled transmission service; point-to-point rates apply to firm or non-firm transmission reservations; ancillary service rates cover scheduling, voltage support, and operating reserves.

attributes.name: rate_zone_code
attributes.description: Geographic or operational zone identifier to which this transmission rate applies. Rate zones segment the transmission system for cost allocation and pricing purposes, often aligned with load-serving areas or transmission owner territories.
attributes.references: FERC Tariff Filing Requirements, RTO/ISO Tariff Structures

attributes.name: reactive_supply_charge
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reactive Supply and Voltage Control Charge
attributes.description: Charge for reactive power supply and voltage control service necessary to maintain transmission system voltage within acceptable limits. Typically expressed in dollars per kilovar (kVAR) or as a percentage of demand charge.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, IEEE Voltage Control Standards

attributes.name: rollover_rights_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether customers holding long-term firm point-to-point transmission service under this rate have rollover rights to renew their service at contract expiration, subject to system capability.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
attributes.description: Identifier for the RTO or ISO that administers this transmission rate, if applicable. Non-RTO indicates the transmission provider operates outside of an organized wholesale market. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CAISO|ERCOT|ISO_NE|MISO|NYISO|PJM|SPP|non_rto — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000, NERC Regional Entity Registration

attributes.name: scheduling_coordination_charge
attributes.business_glossary_term: Scheduling, System Control, and Dispatch Charge
attributes.description: Charge for scheduling, system control, and dispatch services provided by the transmission provider to coordinate the movement of power across the transmission system.

attributes.name: service_class
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission service is firm (guaranteed delivery with curtailment only under emergency conditions), non-firm (interruptible), or conditional firm (firm subject to specific conditions).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which this transmission rate data originated. Rates may be sourced from the Customer Information System (SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B), directly from FERC eTariff filings, or entered manually by regulatory affairs staff.

attributes.name: tariff_version
attributes.description: Version number of the OATT tariff document in which this rate is published. Follows semantic versioning convention to track tariff amendments and supersessions.

attributes.name: transmission_owner_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the transmission owner or transmission provider to whom this rate applies. In multi-owner transmission systems, different owners may have different rate schedules within the same OATT.
attributes.references: NERC Transmission Owner Registration, FERC Tariff Standards

attributes.name: voltage_class_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage class of the transmission facilities to which this rate applies, expressed in kilovolts (kV). Common transmission voltage classes include 69 kV, 115 kV, 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, 500 kV, and 765 kV. Higher voltage classes typically have different rate structures due to differences in cost and capacity.
attributes.references: IEEE Transmission Voltage Standards, NERC Bulk Electric System Definition

products.name: switching_order
products.description: Records switching orders (also called clearance orders or tagout orders) that authorize the opening/closing of breakers, disconnects, and switches on the BES to isolate or energize transmission elements. Captures order ID, requesting operator, authorizing operator, associated transmission element(s), switching sequence steps, clearance tag references, safety ground placement, planned start/end datetime, actual execution datetime, order status (draft/approved/in-progress/completed/cancelled), associated outage reference, and NERC IRO compliance flag. SSOT for all switching operations on the transmission system — the primary daily operational workflow for transmission dispatchers and field crews. Source system: ABB/GE EMS, Schneider/GE OMS.

attributes.name: switching_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the switching order. Primary key for the switching order record.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1686-2013 (Substation Intelligent Electronic Devices Cyber Security Capabilities)

attributes.name: authorizing_operator_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission system operator or supervisor who approved and authorized the switching order for execution. Required for compliance with switching authority protocols.

attributes.name: compliance_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_event. Business justification: Switching errors or unauthorized operations result in NERC TOP/IRO standard violations requiring compliance event tracking. Business process: self-reporting of switching violations, operations audit t

attributes.name: executing_crew_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the field crew assigned to physically execute the switching operations. Links to workforce management system for crew scheduling and dispatch.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 (Electric Power Generation, Transmission, and Distribution)

attributes.name: opex_transaction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.opex_transaction. Business justification: Switching operations incur labor and operational costs recorded in O&M expense accounts. Required for functional cost allocation to transmission operations, maintenance expense tracking, and FERC func

attributes.name: outage_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the associated transmission outage record that this switching order supports. Links to the broader outage management workflow and NERC Transmission Availability Data System (TADS) reporting.

attributes.name: switched_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.line. Business justification: Switching orders operate on specific transmission elements. The current schema uses polymorphic pattern (transmission_element_reference BIGINT + transmission_element_name STRING + transmission_element

attributes.name: switched_transformer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.transformer. Business justification: Switching orders also operate on transformers. This FK links switching orders to transformers being switched. Together with switched_line_id, replaces the polymorphic transmission_element_reference pa

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission substation where the switching operation will be performed. Links to transmission substation master data.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1686-2013 (Substation Intelligent Electronic Devices Cyber Security Capabilities)

attributes.name: actual_end_datetime
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the switching operation was completed. Enables calculation of actual duration and comparison against planned schedule for operational efficiency metrics.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: actual_start_datetime
attributes.description: Actual date and time when the switching operation execution began. Used for performance tracking, variance analysis, and regulatory reporting of switching activities.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the switching order was formally approved by the authorizing operator. Marks the transition from draft to approved status and authorization for execution.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: authorizing_operator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the transmission system operator or supervisor who approved and authorized the switching order for execution.

attributes.name: bes_element_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transmission element being switched is classified as part of the Bulk Electric System under NERC definitions. BES elements require additional coordination and reporting.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms (Bulk Electric System Definition)

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the switching order was cancelled. Common reasons include weather conditions, equipment unavailability, system conditions, or work completion by alternative means.

attributes.name: cancellation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the switching order was cancelled. Populated only for orders that were cancelled before completion.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: clearance_tag_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the physical clearance tag(s) or tagout permit(s) associated with this switching order. Used for lockout/tagout compliance and worker safety protection.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 (The Control of Hazardous Energy - Lockout/Tagout)

attributes.name: contingency_analysis_performed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a contingency analysis was performed to assess system reliability impacts of the switching operation. Required for planned outages affecting BES elements.

attributes.name: control_area
attributes.description: Balancing Authority control area where the switching operation occurs. Used for coordination of generation and load balancing during switching activities.
attributes.references: NERC Standard BAL-001-2 (Real Power Balancing Control Performance)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this switching order record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and operational analytics.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 (Management Assessment of Internal Controls)

attributes.name: ems_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier from the Energy Management System (ABB or GE EMS) where this switching order was created or synchronized. Enables bidirectional integration between EMS and switching order management.

attributes.name: executing_crew_name
attributes.description: Name or designation of the field crew assigned to physically execute the switching operations.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 (Electric Power Generation, Transmission, and Distribution)

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this switching order record was most recently modified. Tracks the latest change to any field in the record for change management and audit purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 (Management Assessment of Internal Controls)

attributes.name: load_impact_mw
attributes.description: Estimated or actual load in megawatts that will be interrupted or affected by this switching operation. Used for customer impact assessment and restoration priority planning.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1366-2012 (Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices)

attributes.name: nerc_cip_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this switching order involves Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) assets requiring cyber security and physical security controls under NERC CIP standards.
attributes.references: NERC Standard CIP-002-5.1a (BES Cyber System Categorization)

attributes.name: nerc_iro_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this switching order requires coordination with the Reliability Coordinator under NERC Interchange and Reliability Operations (IRO) standards. True for switching operations affecting Bulk Electric System (BES) reliability.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional operational notes, special instructions, coordination requirements, or lessons learned. Used by operators and field crews for information not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: NERC Standard COM-002-4 (Operating Personnel Communications Protocols)

attributes.name: oms_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier from the Outage Management System (Schneider Electric AMS or GE PowerOn) where this switching order was created or synchronized. Links switching operations to outage restoration workflows.

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Human-readable business identifier for the switching order, typically assigned by the Energy Management System (EMS) or Outage Management System (OMS). Used by transmission dispatchers and field crews for operational reference.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the switching order. Tracks progression from draft through approval, execution, and completion or cancellation.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the switching order based on operational purpose. Planned orders support scheduled maintenance or outages; emergency orders respond to unplanned events; restoration orders return equipment to service.

attributes.name: planned_end_datetime
attributes.description: Scheduled date and time when the switching operation is planned to be completed and equipment returned to normal state. Critical for outage duration planning and customer impact assessment.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: planned_start_datetime
attributes.description: Scheduled date and time when the switching operation is planned to begin. Used for coordination with field crews, outage scheduling, and system operator shift planning.
attributes.references: NERC Standard IRO-005-6 (Reliability Coordination - Current Day Operations)

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Operational priority level assigned to the switching order. Critical priority indicates immediate safety or reliability concerns requiring expedited execution.

attributes.name: requesting_operator_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission system operator or dispatcher who initiated the switching order request. Used for accountability and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: requesting_operator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the transmission system operator or dispatcher who initiated the switching order request.

attributes.name: rto_iso_notification_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this switching order requires notification to the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) due to potential impact on transmission capacity or market operations.

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.description: Name or code of the Regional Transmission Organization or Independent System Operator region where this switching operation occurs. Examples include PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE.

attributes.name: safety_ground_placement
attributes.description: Description of safety ground locations and installation requirements for this switching order. Specifies where protective grounds must be installed to protect workers from induced voltage or backfeed.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 (Electric Power Generation, Transmission, and Distribution)

attributes.name: substation_name
attributes.description: Name of the transmission substation where the switching operation will be performed. Used for field crew dispatch and geographic coordination.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1686-2013 (Substation Intelligent Electronic Devices Cyber Security Capabilities)

attributes.name: switching_sequence_steps
attributes.description: Detailed step-by-step instructions for the switching operation sequence. Specifies the order of breaker and disconnect operations, verification steps, and safety checkpoints. May reference standard operating procedures.

attributes.name: transfer_capability_impact_mw
attributes.description: Estimated reduction in Available Transfer Capability (ATC) in megawatts resulting from this switching operation. Critical for transmission service scheduling and market operations.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage class in kilovolts of the transmission element being switched. Critical for determining safety clearance distances and personal protective equipment requirements.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1427-2006 (Guide for Recommended Electrical Clearances and Insulation Levels in Air-Insulated Electrical Power Substations)

attributes.name: work_order_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the maintenance or construction work order that necessitates this switching operation. Links to Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system for work coordination.

attributes.name: superseded_switching_order_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on switching_order (superseded_switching_order_id)

products.name: protection_system

Captures protection system ID, associated transmission element, relay type (distance/differential/overcurrent/pilot), relay manufacturer and model, CT/PT ratios, protection zone, trip settings, coordination study reference, firmware version, last calibration date, NERC PRC compliance status, and operational status. Required for NERC PRC (Protection and Control) standard compliance, fault analysis, and misoperation tracking. Source system: SEL/GE/ABB relay management systems, Oracle WAM/IBM Maximo.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the protective relay system or protection scheme. Primary key for the protection system entity. Serves as the authoritative reference for all protection equipment records across relay management systems, Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), and NERC Protection and Control (PRC) compliance tracking.

attributes.name: backup_protection_system_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the backup or redundant protection system that provides secondary protection for the same transmission element. Used for coordination studies and reliability analysis per NERC PRC-023 requirements.

Business justification: Protection system misoperations or testing failures generate NERC PRC-004 compliance events requiring investigation and reporting. attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business process: relay testing program scheduling, compliance evidence collection, main

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Protection relays and systems are capitalized assets with book values and depreciation tracked in fixed_asset. Required for asset accounting, depreciation expense calculation, retirement accounting, a

attributes.description: External reference to the protection system record in the Enterprise Asset Management system (Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo). Links protection data to work orders, maintenance history, spare parts inventory, and financial asset records.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.line. Business justification: Protection systems protect specific transmission elements. The current schema uses a polymorphic pattern (transmission_element_reference BIGINT + transmission_element_type STRING). Normalizing to expl

attributes.name: relay_material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Protection relays are procured equipment with manufacturer part numbers and specifications. Material master enables spare parts inventory management, standardization of relay types across substations,

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the transmission substation where this protection system is physically located. Links protection equipment to facility for maintenance dispatch, outage coordination, and physical security management.
attributes.references: Utility GIS and Asset Management Standards

attributes.name: communication_protocol
attributes.description: Communication protocol used by the relay for SCADA integration, synchrophasor data exchange, or remote monitoring (e.g., DNP3, IEC 61850 GOOSE/MMS, Modbus, IEEE C37.118 for PMUs). Critical for cybersecurity assessments and NERC CIP compliance.

attributes.name: coordination_study_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the protection coordination study that validated this systems settings and selectivity with adjacent devices. Links to engineering analysis documentation required for NERC PRC compliance and fault investigation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protection system record was first created in the data management system. Used for data lineage tracking and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: ct_ratio
attributes.description: Current transformer turns ratio (e.g., 2000:5, 1200:1) that scales primary current to secondary relay input. Essential for relay setting calculations, coordination studies, and accurate fault current measurement.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.13 Standard Requirements for Instrument Transformers

attributes.name: fault_record_count
attributes.description: Total number of fault events recorded by this protection system since commissioning or last counter reset. Used for reliability analysis, equipment stress assessment, and predictive maintenance planning.

attributes.name: ferc_account_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
attributes.description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts classification code for capitalization and depreciation of the protection system asset (typically Account 353 - Station Equipment). Required for regulatory financial reporting and rate case cost studies.

attributes.name: firmware_version
attributes.description: Current firmware or software version installed on the protective relay. Critical for cybersecurity vulnerability management, NERC CIP compliance, and ensuring compatibility with protection coordination studies.

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: Date when the protection system was commissioned and placed into active service protecting the transmission element. Marks the start of the operational lifecycle and NERC compliance obligations.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the protection system was physically installed at the substation or transmission facility. Used for asset lifecycle tracking, depreciation calculations, and replacement planning.

attributes.name: is_bes_protection
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this protection system is classified as protecting a BES element and therefore subject to NERC reliability standards. Determines applicability of NERC PRC and CIP compliance requirements.

attributes.name: last_calibration_date
attributes.description: Date when the protective relay was last tested, calibrated, and verified to be operating within manufacturer specifications. Critical for NERC PRC-005 maintenance compliance and reliability assurance.
attributes.references: NERC PRC-005 Protection System, Automatic Reclosing, and Sudden Pressure Relaying Maintenance

attributes.name: last_fault_date
attributes.description: Date when this protection system last detected and responded to a fault condition. Used for operational trending and to correlate protection performance with transmission outage events.

attributes.name: last_misoperation_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent documented protection system misoperation. Triggers NERC PRC-004 investigation and corrective action plan requirements. Nullable if no misoperations have occurred.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this protection system record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: misoperation_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of documented protection system misoperations (incorrect trips or failures to trip) as defined by NERC PRC-004. Used for reliability trending, root cause analysis, and identification of systematic protection issues.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_applicable

attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this protection system is a BES Cyber System subject to NERC CIP cybersecurity standards (CIP-002 through CIP-014). Determines requirements for electronic security perimeters, access controls, and vulnerability assessments.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-002 BES Cyber System Categorization

attributes.name: nerc_prc_compliance_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: NERC Protection and Control (PRC) Compliance Status
attributes.description: Current compliance status with applicable NERC PRC standards (PRC-005, PRC-019, PRC-023, PRC-025, PRC-027). Tracks whether maintenance, testing, coordination, and documentation requirements are met. Critical for regulatory audits and reliability assurance.

attributes.name: next_calibration_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required calibration or maintenance test based on NERC PRC-005 time-based or performance-based maintenance intervals. Used for preventive maintenance planning and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special configuration details, known issues, or historical context about the protection system. Used by protection engineers and maintenance personnel for knowledge transfer and troubleshooting.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the protection system. Indicates whether the system is actively protecting the transmission element, temporarily out for testing/maintenance, or permanently retired. Critical for real-time grid operations and SCADA monitoring.

attributes.name: original_cost_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Original installed cost of the protection system in US dollars, including equipment, engineering, installation labor, and commissioning. Used for FERC rate base calculations, depreciation, and capital expenditure tracking.

attributes.name: protection_scheme_type
attributes.description: Primary protection principle or relay logic employed by this system (e.g., distance protection for transmission lines, differential for transformers, pilot schemes for critical circuits). Defines the protection philosophy and coordination requirements per IEEE and NERC standards. attributes.name: protection_system_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code or tag number assigned to the protection system for asset tracking, SCADA integration, and maintenance scheduling. Often follows utility-specific naming conventions aligned with substation or transmission line designations.

attributes.name: protection_system_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the protection system, typically including location and function identifiers (e.g., 'Main-1 Line Differential', 'Bus 5 Overcurrent'). Used for operational identification and work order references.

attributes.name: protection_zone
attributes.description: Protection zone classification defining the reach and coordination tier of the relay (e.g., Zone 1 instantaneous, Zone 2 time-delayed, Zone 3 remote backup). Critical for selectivity and coordination with adjacent protection systems per IEEE standards.
attributes.references: IEEE C37.113 Guide for Protective Relay Applications

attributes.name: pt_ratio
attributes.description: Potential (voltage) transformer turns ratio (e.g., 115000:115, 345000:120) that scales primary voltage to secondary relay input. Required for distance relay reach calculations and voltage-based protection schemes.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.13 Standard Requirements for Instrument Transformers

attributes.name: relay_management_system_reference
attributes.description: External reference to the protection system record in the relay management system (SEL AcSELerator, GE UR Setup, ABB PCM600). Links to relay settings files, event records, and firmware management.

attributes.name: relay_serial_number
attributes.description: Unique manufacturer-assigned serial number for the physical relay device. Used for warranty tracking, asset inventory, and device-specific configuration management in relay management systems.

attributes.name: retirement_date

attributes.name: scada_point_reference

attributes.name: settings_last_modified_date

attributes.name: settings_modified_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the engineer or technician who last modified the relay settings. Required for audit trails, accountability, and NERC CIP access control compliance.

attributes.name: trip_setting_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or file path to the approved relay settings document, including pickup values, time delays, reach settings, and logic configurations. Required for NERC PRC-019 compliance and protection coordination verification.
attributes.references: NERC PRC-019 Coordination of Generating Unit or Plant Capabilities, Voltage Regulating Controls, and Protection

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv

attributes.name: area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the control area or balancing authority area to which this bus belongs. Used for interchange scheduling and area control error (ACE) calculations.

attributes.name: operator_id
attributes.description: Reference to the transmission owner or operator responsible for this bus. Critical for NERC CIP compliance and jurisdictional reporting.

attributes.name: substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the substation where this bus is physically located. Links to the substation master table.

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the transmission zone or pricing zone for locational marginal pricing (LMP) and congestion management. Used by RTO/ISO for market operations.

attributes.name: active_power_mw
attributes.description: Net active power injection or withdrawal at the bus in megawatts (MW). Positive values indicate generation; negative values indicate load.

attributes.name: base_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Base voltage used for per-unit calculations in power flow and stability studies. Typically matches the nominal voltage level but may differ for analytical purposes.

attributes.name: bes_designation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this bus is part of the NERC-defined Bulk Electric System (BES). True if the bus meets BES criteria and is subject to NERC reliability standards and CIP compliance.

attributes.name: bus_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the bus, often reflecting the substation or geographic location it serves (e.g., 'Main Street 345kV Bus A').

attributes.name: bus_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier for the bus used in operational systems, SCADA, and interchange scheduling. Typically assigned by the transmission operator or RTO/ISO.

attributes.name: bus_type
attributes.description: Classification of the bus based on its role in power flow analysis. Slack (swing) bus maintains system voltage and frequency reference; generator bus has active generation; load bus serves demand; isolated bus is disconnected.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bus record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit purposes.

attributes.name: critical_infrastructure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this bus is designated as critical infrastructure requiring enhanced physical and cyber security measures under NERC CIP standards.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Additional descriptive information about the bus, including configuration details, special operating characteristics, or notes relevant to operations and planning.

attributes.name: ferc_jurisdiction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this bus is under FERC jurisdiction for interstate transmission. True for facilities subject to FERC rate regulation and OATT compliance.

attributes.name: generation_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power generation at the bus in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAR). Sum of all generator reactive outputs connected to this bus.

attributes.name: generation_mw
attributes.description: Active power generation at the bus in megawatts (MW). Sum of all generator outputs connected to this bus.

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: Date when the bus was first energized and placed into commercial operation. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and depreciation calculations.

attributes.name: last_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent scheduled maintenance or inspection performed on the bus and associated equipment.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the bus location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, outage management, and spatial analysis.

attributes.name: load_mvar
attributes.description: Reactive power load at the bus in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAR). Represents reactive demand connected to this bus.

attributes.name: load_mw
attributes.description: Active power load served at the bus in megawatts (MW). Represents demand connected to this bus.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the bus location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, outage management, and spatial analysis.

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.description: NERC regional entity with jurisdiction over this bus. Used for compliance reporting and regional coordination.

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next planned maintenance or inspection of the bus and associated equipment.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the bus. In-service indicates the bus is energized and available; out-of-service indicates the bus is de-energized; testing and maintenance indicate temporary unavailability; retired indicates permanent decommissioning; planned indicates future installation.

attributes.name: reactive_power_mvar
attributes.description: Net reactive power injection or withdrawal at the bus in megavolt-amperes reactive (MVAR). Critical for voltage control and VAR management.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual date when the bus was or will be permanently de-energized and retired from service. Null for active buses.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the RTO or ISO that operates the market and manages transmission service for this bus (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP).

attributes.name: shunt_susceptance_mvar
attributes.description: Fixed shunt susceptance at the bus in MVAR at nominal voltage. Represents capacitor banks or reactor banks permanently connected to the bus for voltage support.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bus record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data synchronization.

attributes.name: voltage_angle_degrees
attributes.description: Phase angle of the bus voltage in degrees relative to the system reference (slack bus). Critical for power flow analysis and stability assessment.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level of the bus in kilovolts (kV). Defines the operating voltage class for the bus (e.g., 69, 115, 138, 230, 345, 500, 765 kV).

attributes.name: voltage_magnitude_pu
attributes.description: Voltage magnitude at the bus expressed in per-unit (pu) of the base voltage. Typically maintained between 0.95 and 1.05 pu under normal operating conditions.

products.name: operator
products.description: Master reference table for operator. Referenced by authorizing_operator_id.

attributes.name: operator_id
attributes.description: Primary key for operator

attributes.name: control_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to transmission.control_area. Business justification: Operators manage control areas. The operator table has control_area_name STRING. Normalizing to FK to control_area. Removes control_area_name string.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this operator record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: deregistration_date
attributes.description: Date when the operator ceased operations or was deregistered from NERC, if applicable.

attributes.name: emergency_contact_phone
attributes.description: 24/7 emergency hotline number for system emergencies, outages, and reliability events.

attributes.name: ferc_jurisdiction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the operator is subject to FERC jurisdictional oversight for transmission services and rates.

attributes.name: headquarters_address
attributes.description: Physical street address of the operator's headquarters or primary control center.

attributes.name: headquarters_city
attributes.description: City where the operator's headquarters or primary control center is located.

attributes.name: headquarters_country
attributes.description: Country where the operator's headquarters is located. Three-letter ISO country code.

attributes.name: headquarters_postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code for the operator's headquarters address.

attributes.name: headquarters_state_province
attributes.description: State or province where the operator's headquarters is located. Use two-letter abbreviation for US states and Canadian provinces.

attributes.name: interconnection
attributes.description: The major North American interconnection to which the operator belongs. Defines synchronous grid boundaries.

attributes.name: last_audit_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent NERC compliance audit or reliability assessment conducted for this operator.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the operator is subject to NERC CIP cybersecurity standards for bulk electric system protection.

attributes.name: nerc_registration_number
attributes.description: Official NERC registry identifier for the operator entity. Required for compliance reporting and CIP standards applicability.

attributes.name: next_audit_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next NERC compliance audit or reliability assessment.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or special considerations regarding the transmission operator.

attributes.name: oasis_node_url
attributes.description: Web address of the operator's OASIS node for posting available transmission capacity and accepting transmission service requests.

attributes.name: oatt_tariff_number
attributes.description: FERC-approved tariff number under which the operator provides transmission service. Required for FERC jurisdictional operators.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the transmission operator within the NERC registry and interconnection.

attributes.name: operator_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the transmission operator within the interconnection. Used for interchange scheduling and NERC reporting.

attributes.name: operator_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the transmission system operator or control area operator.

attributes.name: operator_type
attributes.description: Functional classification of the operator within the bulk electric system. Defines the operational role and regulatory responsibilities.

attributes.name: parent_company_name
attributes.description: Name of the parent holding company or corporate entity that owns the transmission operator, if applicable.

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: Primary email address for operational coordination and interchange scheduling communications.

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary operational contact person for the transmission operator.

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number for operational coordination and emergency contact with the transmission operator.

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: Date when the operator was first registered with NERC or began transmission operations.

attributes.name: rto_iso_affiliation
attributes.description: Name of the RTO or ISO market to which the operator belongs, if applicable. Examples: PJM, CAISO, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE, ERCOT.

attributes.name: service_territory_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the geographic service territory covered by the transmission operator.

attributes.name: total_transmission_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total rated transmission capacity in megawatts managed by the operator across all transmission lines and substations.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this operator record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: voltage_class_range
attributes.description: Range of voltage classes operated by the transmission operator, typically expressed as minimum to maximum kilovolts (e.g., 115 kV to 500 kV).

attributes.name: authorizing_operator_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on operator (authorizing_operator_id)

products.name: crew
products.description: Master reference table for crew. Referenced by executing_crew_id.

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Primary key for crew

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary depot, yard, or service center where this crew is based. Used for resource allocation and travel time calculations.

attributes.name: active_from_date
attributes.description: Date this crew became active and available for work assignments. Used for crew lifecycle tracking and historical analysis.

attributes.name: active_until_date
attributes.description: Date this crew is scheduled to become inactive or contract ends. Null for indefinite assignments. Used for resource planning and contract management.

attributes.name: certification_level
attributes.description: Overall qualification level of the crew based on training, experience, and certifications. Determines complexity of work assignments the crew can execute.

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the contract period for contractor crews. Null for internal crews or open-ended contracts. Used for contract renewal planning.

attributes.name: contract_number
attributes.description: Contract or purchase order number governing the engagement of this contractor crew. Null for internal crews. Used for financial tracking and compliance.

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the contract period for contractor crews. Null for internal crews. Used for contract lifecycle management.

attributes.name: contractor_company_name
attributes.description: Name of the contracting company if this is a contractor crew. Null for internal utility crews. Used for vendor management and billing.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crew record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: crew_classification
attributes.description: Organizational classification of the crew. Internal crews are utility employees, contractor crews are third-party resources, mutual aid crews are from other utilities under mutual assistance agreements, emergency support crews are specialized external resources for major events.

attributes.name: crew_lead_contact
attributes.description: Primary contact phone number for the crew lead. Used for dispatch coordination and emergency communication.

attributes.name: crew_lead_name
attributes.description: Full name of the crew lead or foreman responsible for directing crew activities and ensuring safety compliance.

attributes.name: crew_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the crew (e.g., 'North Region Line Crew A', 'Substation Maintenance Team 3').

attributes.name: crew_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the crew, used in work orders and dispatch systems. Externally visible crew designation.

attributes.name: crew_size
attributes.description: Number of personnel assigned to this crew. Used for resource planning and safety compliance (minimum crew size requirements per OSHA).

attributes.name: crew_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the crew. Active crews are available for dispatch, on_assignment crews are currently executing work, available crews are ready for immediate dispatch, training crews are in qualification activities, suspended crews are temporarily unavailable, inactive crews are not in service.

attributes.name: crew_type
attributes.description: Classification of crew based on primary function: line crews for transmission line work, substation crews for substation equipment, switching crews for switching operations, emergency response for outage restoration, maintenance for scheduled upkeep, construction for new installations.

attributes.name: days_since_last_incident
attributes.description: Number of days since the last safety incident. Used for safety performance recognition and monitoring.

attributes.name: emergency_response_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this crew is equipped and trained for emergency outage restoration and storm response. Emergency-capable crews have specialized equipment and 24/7 availability.

attributes.name: hot_line_qualified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew is qualified to perform energized (hot) work on transmission lines. Requires specialized training and equipment per OSHA 1910.269.

attributes.name: hourly_rate
attributes.description: Standard hourly billing rate for this crew in USD. Used for cost estimation and budget planning. Applies to contractor crews; may be average rate for internal crews.

attributes.name: last_incident_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent safety incident involving this crew. Null if no incidents have occurred. Used for safety trend analysis.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crew record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_training_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent safety or technical training completed by this crew. Used to track training currency and compliance with NERC PER standards.

attributes.name: mutual_aid_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this crew can be deployed to assist other utilities under mutual assistance agreements during major events or emergencies.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_clearance
attributes.description: Indicates whether all crew members hold valid NERC CIP personnel risk assessment clearances required for access to Bulk Electric System (BES) Cyber Systems and associated physical security perimeters.

attributes.name: next_training_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the crew must complete next required training to maintain qualifications. Used for training schedule planning and compliance tracking.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional information about the crew, such as special capabilities, equipment limitations, scheduling constraints, or operational notes.

attributes.name: overtime_rate
attributes.description: Overtime hourly billing rate for this crew in USD. Used for after-hours and emergency work cost calculations.

attributes.name: primary_equipment_specialization
attributes.description: Type of transmission equipment this crew specializes in (e.g., 'transmission towers', 'power transformers', 'circuit breakers', 'disconnect switches', 'series capacitors', 'static VAR compensators'). Free text to accommodate diverse equipment types.

attributes.name: safety_incident_count
attributes.description: Cumulative count of OSHA-recordable safety incidents involving this crew. Used for safety performance tracking and risk assessment.

attributes.name: service_territory
attributes.description: Geographic region or territory this crew is assigned to serve. May reference transmission planning zones or operational areas.

attributes.name: shift_schedule
attributes.description: Standard work schedule pattern for this crew. Day crews work standard business hours, night crews work overnight, rotating crews alternate shifts, on-call crews respond to emergencies, 24x7 crews provide continuous coverage.

attributes.name: substation_access_authorized
attributes.description: Indicates whether the crew is authorized for unescorted access to transmission substations. Requires NERC CIP training and background checks.

attributes.name: vehicle_fleet_assigned
attributes.description: List or description of vehicles and mobile equipment assigned to this crew (e.g., bucket trucks, digger derricks, line trucks, trailers). Used for resource tracking and dispatch planning.

attributes.name: voltage_class_qualified
attributes.description: Voltage levels this crew is qualified and authorized to work on (e.g., '69kV', '138kV', '230kV', '345kV', '500kV'). Pipe-separated list for crews qualified at multiple voltage classes. Critical for safety and NERC CIP compliance.

attributes.name: relieved_crew_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on crew (relieved_crew_id)

domains.name: distribution
domains.description: Manages last-mile electric and gas delivery infrastructure to end-use customers — distribution feeders, poles, service transformers, gas mains, service laterals, and associated GIS network topology. Serves as the SSOT for OMS/DMS outage events, SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability indices, NEM interconnections, DER/DERMS integration, voltage regulation, and gas pipeline safety data under PHMSA.
domains.references: IEEE 1547, PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations, PUC

products.name: feeder
