products.description: Master record for electric distribution feeders — the primary medium-voltage circuits (typically 4kV–35kV) emanating from distribution substations to deliver electricity to end-use customers. Captures feeder identifier, nominal voltage, circuit configuration (radial/loop/networked), rated capacity (MVA), peak load, substation source bus, feeder length (miles), conductor type, phase configuration, GIS network topology reference, SCADA point ID, operational status, and service territory. SSOT for feeder-level reliability metrics (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI) and OMS/DMS circuit topology. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS and Schneider Electric AMS/GE PowerOn.
products.reference: IEEE 1547 / ESRI ArcGIS Distribution Network

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the electric distribution feeder circuit. Primary key.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Feeder construction, upgrades, and extensions are capital projects requiring project tracking for budget management, AFUDC calculation, and regulatory reporting. Essential for capital investment manag

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Feeders must meet vegetation management cycles, reliability standards, and inspection obligations. Direct compliance tracking: linking feeders to their primary regulatory obligations for scheduling an

attributes.name: conductor_material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Feeders use standardized conductor materials tracked by type and size. Enables lifecycle replacement planning, material standardization programs, and accurate cost estimation for feeder reconductoring

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Feeders incur operational and maintenance expenses that must be allocated to cost centers for FERC functional accounting and regulatory reporting. Essential for O&M expense tracking and rate case cost

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the distribution substation from which this feeder originates. Links to the substation master record.

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Feeders are subject to regulatory proceedings for reliability standards, infrastructure investments, and rate recovery. Utilities must track which dockets authorize feeder upgrades and impose performa

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Feeders are capitalized plant assets tracked in the fixed asset register for depreciation, rate base calculation, and FERC Form 1 reporting. Essential for utility asset accounting.

attributes.name: pricing_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.pricing_node. Business justification: ISO/RTO market operations require feeder-to-pricing-node mapping for distribution-level LMP analysis, DER hosting capacity valuation, and locational marginal value studies. Essential for integrated di

attributes.name: caidi_annual
attributes.business_glossary_term: CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index) Annual
attributes.description: The annual Customer Average Interruption Duration Index for this feeder, measured in minutes. Represents the average outage duration per interruption event.

attributes.name: capacitor_bank_count
attributes.description: The number of capacitor banks installed on the feeder for power factor correction and voltage support.

attributes.name: circuit_configuration
attributes.description: The topology or architecture of the feeder circuit. Radial feeders have a single source path; loop feeders have alternate paths with normally-open points; networked feeders have multiple energized sources.

attributes.name: conductor_size_kcmil
attributes.description: The cross-sectional area of the conductor in thousand circular mils, which determines current-carrying capacity and voltage drop characteristics.

attributes.name: customer_count
attributes.description: The total number of end-use customers served by this feeder. Critical for calculating SAIFI and SAIDI reliability indices.

attributes.name: der_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The total nameplate generation capacity of all DER interconnections on this feeder in megawatts. Critical for hosting capacity analysis and grid stability studies.

attributes.name: der_interconnection_count
attributes.description: The total number of distributed energy resources (solar PV, wind, battery storage, etc.) interconnected to this feeder under IEEE 1547 or state interconnection standards.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547, FERC Order 2222, State Interconnection Rules

attributes.name: dms_circuit_code
attributes.description: The circuit identifier used in the Distribution Management System for real-time network analysis, switching operations, and voltage optimization.

attributes.name: feeder_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation for the feeder, often incorporating geographic or landmark references for operational clarity.

attributes.name: feeder_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the feeder circuit, typically assigned by the utility following internal naming conventions. Used in operational communications, OMS displays, and field work orders.

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the feeder circuit in the utility GIS system, linking to spatial network topology, pole locations, and asset mapping.

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: The date the feeder was first energized and placed into commercial operation. Used for asset age analysis and depreciation calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts, GAAP

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent comprehensive inspection of the feeder circuit, including poles, conductors, and equipment.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this feeder record was last updated in the system, capturing configuration changes, status updates, or data corrections.

attributes.name: length_miles
attributes.description: The total circuit length of the feeder from substation to the furthest endpoint, measured in miles. Used for voltage drop calculations, reliability metrics, and maintenance planning.

attributes.name: nem_customer_count
attributes.description: The number of customers on this feeder enrolled in net energy metering programs, typically residential or commercial solar installations.

attributes.name: next_inspection_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next comprehensive feeder inspection, based on regulatory requirements and utility maintenance cycles.

attributes.name: nominal_voltage_kv
attributes.description: The nominal operating voltage of the feeder circuit in kilovolts, typically ranging from 4 kV to 35 kV for distribution feeders.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special operating instructions, known issues, or other contextual information relevant to the feeder.

attributes.name: oms_circuit_code
attributes.description: The circuit identifier used in the Outage Management System for tracking outage events, restoration activities, and customer impact analysis.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the feeder circuit. In-service feeders are energized and serving load; out-of-service feeders are temporarily de-energized for maintenance or emergency conditions.

attributes.name: peak_load_mw
attributes.description: The highest recorded real power demand on the feeder in megawatts, typically measured during system peak periods. Used for capacity planning and reliability analysis.

attributes.name: phase_configuration
attributes.description: The number of electrical phases carried by the feeder. Most distribution feeders are three-phase; some rural or light-load circuits may be single-phase or two-phase.

attributes.name: protection_scheme
attributes.description: The type of protective relay and coordination scheme applied to the feeder, such as overcurrent, distance, differential, or adaptive protection.
attributes.references: IEEE C37 Series, NERC PRC Standards

attributes.name: rated_capacity_mva
attributes.description: The maximum continuous load capacity of the feeder in megavolt-amperes, determined by conductor thermal limits, protection settings, and substation transformer capacity allocation.

attributes.name: recloser_count
attributes.description: The number of automatic reclosing devices installed on the feeder to isolate faults and minimize customer interruptions.

attributes.name: saidi_annual
attributes.business_glossary_term: SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index) Annual
attributes.description: The annual System Average Interruption Duration Index for this feeder, measured in minutes. Represents the average total outage duration per customer served by the feeder.

attributes.name: saifi_annual
attributes.business_glossary_term: SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index) Annual
attributes.description: The annual System Average Interruption Frequency Index for this feeder, representing the average number of sustained interruptions per customer.

attributes.name: scada_point_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Point Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the SCADA monitoring point associated with this feeder, used to retrieve real-time telemetry data such as voltage, current, power flow, and breaker status.

attributes.name: service_territory
attributes.description: The geographic service area or operating region served by this feeder, used for regulatory reporting and operational planning.

attributes.name: source_bus_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific bus or breaker position within the substation from which this feeder is energized.

attributes.name: tree_trimming_cycle_months
attributes.description: The scheduled vegetation management cycle for this feeder in months. Critical for reliability improvement and wildfire risk mitigation.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-003, State Wildfire Mitigation Plans

attributes.name: underground_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of the feeder circuit length that is underground cable versus overhead conductor. Underground circuits typically have higher reliability but higher installation costs.

attributes.name: voltage_regulator_count
attributes.description: The number of voltage regulation devices (line regulators or load tap changers) installed on the feeder to maintain voltage within acceptable limits per ANSI C84.1.

products.name: service_transformer
products.description: Master record for distribution service transformers — pad-mounted, pole-mounted, or vault transformers that step down medium-voltage feeder voltage to utilization voltage (120/240V residential; 277/480V commercial) for last-mile delivery. Captures transformer ID, kVA rating, primary/secondary voltage, phase configuration (single/three-phase), installation type, GPS coordinates, feeder association, pole/structure number, manufacturer, model, serial number, installation date, oil/dry type, load factor, and operational status. Critical for load balancing, outage isolation, and asset lifecycle management. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS and Oracle WAM/IBM Maximo.
products.reference: IEEE C57 / ESRI ArcGIS Distribution Network

attributes.name: service_transformer_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the distribution service transformer record. Primary key for the service transformer entity.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Transformer maintenance and operational costs are allocated to cost centers for expense tracking and regulatory reporting. Required for FERC Form 1 functional cost allocation and rate case preparation

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution substation that sources the feeder supplying this transformer. Used for hierarchical network topology and capacity planning.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Electric Utility Data Model

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary distribution feeder circuit that supplies this transformer. Critical for outage isolation, load flow analysis, and SCADA integration.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Electric Utility Data Model

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Transformers are capitalized distribution assets requiring fixed asset tracking for depreciation, rate base inclusion, and FERC plant accounting. Essential for regulatory asset management.

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Service transformers are capital assets requiring lifecycle management, depreciation tracking (FERC/NARUC accounts), condition assessments, PM schedules, work orders, and regulatory asset base reporti

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Distribution transformers are procured materials with standardized part numbers tracked in material master. Enables warranty tracking, lifecycle cost analysis, and standardized procurement for transfo

attributes.name: pole_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.pole. Business justification: Service transformers are physically mounted on poles (pole-mounted configuration). The service_transformer table currently has pole_number (STRING) as a denormalized reference. Adding pole_id FK enabl

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Transformer investments are included in rate base and depreciation schedules in rate cases. Cost recovery tracking: linking transformers to the rate case that authorized their inclusion in rate base.

attributes.name: acquisition_cost
attributes.description: Original purchase and installation cost of the transformer in US dollars. Used for capitalization, depreciation, and rate base calculations under FERC Uniform System of Accounts.

attributes.name: asset_condition_score
attributes.description: Composite health index (0-100 scale) derived from inspection findings, age, load history, and failure risk models. Guides capital investment prioritization and replacement planning.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Health

attributes.name: book_value
attributes.description: Current net book value after accumulated depreciation. Represents the asset's carrying value on the utility's balance sheet.
attributes.references: GAAP / FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality where the transformer is located. Used for jurisdictional reporting and regional analysis.

attributes.name: connected_customer_count
attributes.description: Number of customer service points (meters) served by this transformer. Used for outage impact assessment and SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability calculations.

attributes.name: cooling_type
attributes.description: Insulation and cooling medium classification. Oil-immersed transformers require spill containment and environmental monitoring; dry-type are used indoors or where fire safety is critical.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service transformer record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and governance.

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Business criticality classification based on customer count, load served, and service area importance. Drives prioritization for emergency response and capital investment.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Risk Management

attributes.name: der_interconnection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more Distributed Energy Resources (solar PV, battery storage, EV chargers) are interconnected to this transformer under Net Energy Metering (NEM) or other programs. Critical for DERMS integration and voltage management.

attributes.name: impedance_percent
attributes.description: Nameplate impedance of the transformer expressed as a percentage. Critical for short-circuit analysis, protective device coordination, and voltage regulation studies.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the transformer was placed into service in the distribution network. Marks the start of the asset's operational lifecycle and depreciation period.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Lifecycle

attributes.name: kva_rating
attributes.description: Nameplate capacity of the service transformer in kilovolt-amperes. Principal measurement for load balancing, capacity planning, and determining service adequacy for connected customers.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent field inspection or preventive maintenance activity. Used to schedule future inspections and assess compliance with maintenance programs.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Work Management

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service transformer record was most recently modified. Audit field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the transformer installation. Enables GIS mapping, mobile workforce dispatch, and spatial analytics.

attributes.name: load_factor_percent
attributes.description: Ratio of average load to peak load over a measurement period, expressed as a percentage. Indicates utilization efficiency and guides capacity planning.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the transformer installation. Enables GIS mapping, mobile workforce dispatch, and spatial analytics.

attributes.name: manufacture_year
attributes.description: Year the transformer was manufactured. Used for age-based risk assessment, depreciation calculations, and replacement prioritization.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Hierarchy

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next preventive maintenance inspection. Drives work order generation and compliance with regulatory maintenance standards.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Work Management

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the service transformer in the distribution network. Drives availability for load calculations, outage management, and asset planning.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Legal ownership classification of the transformer asset. Determines maintenance responsibility, capital treatment, and regulatory rate base inclusion.

attributes.name: peak_load_kva
attributes.description: Maximum observed load on the transformer in kilovolt-amperes. Used to assess overload risk and determine upgrade or replacement needs.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.91 (Loading Guide for Mineral-Oil-Immersed Transformers)

attributes.name: phase_configuration
attributes.description: Electrical phase design of the transformer. Single-phase serves residential and small commercial; three-phase serves larger commercial and industrial loads.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code for the transformer location. Used for geographic segmentation and service territory mapping.

attributes.name: primary_voltage
attributes.description: Medium-voltage input from the distribution feeder in kilovolts. Typical values include 4.16kV, 12.47kV, 13.2kV, 13.8kV, 24.9kV, 34.5kV depending on utility standards.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date the transformer was permanently removed from service. Nullable for active assets. Marks the end of the asset's operational lifecycle.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Lifecycle

attributes.name: scada_monitored_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the transformer is equipped with real-time monitoring via SCADA or Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS). Enables proactive outage detection and load management.

attributes.name: secondary_voltage
attributes.description: Utilization voltage output to end-use customers in volts. Typical residential values: 120/240V single-phase; typical commercial values: 208Y/120V or 480Y/277V three-phase.
attributes.references: ANSI C84.1 (Voltage Ratings for Electric Power Systems)

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Unique factory-assigned serial number for the individual transformer unit. Critical for warranty claims, recall tracking, and asset provenance.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Hierarchy

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State or province where the transformer is located. Used for regulatory reporting to state Public Utility Commissions (PUCs).

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Physical street address or nearest address reference for the transformer location. Used for field crew navigation and customer service inquiries.

attributes.name: tap_position
attributes.description: Current tap setting for voltage regulation (e.g., +2.5%, nominal, -5%). Adjusts secondary voltage to maintain service quality within ANSI C84.1 limits.

attributes.name: transformer_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the service transformer, used in field operations, work orders, and GIS mapping. Unique across the utility's distribution network.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Electric Utility Data Model

attributes.name: transformer_type
attributes.description: Physical installation configuration of the service transformer. Determines accessibility, maintenance procedures, and safety protocols.

attributes.name: winding_configuration
attributes.description: Primary and secondary winding connection topology. Affects voltage transformation, grounding, and harmonic performance.

products.name: distribution_substation
products.description: Master record for distribution substations — facilities that receive bulk power from the transmission system and step down voltage for distribution feeder circuits. Captures substation ID, name, location (GPS/GIS), service territory, nominal primary voltage (transmission side), secondary voltage (distribution side), total installed transformer capacity (MVA), number of distribution feeders served, SCADA integration point, ownership type, commissioning date, and operational status. Distinct from transmission substations (owned by the transmission domain). Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS and Schneider Electric AMS/GE PowerOn.
products.reference: NERC FAC-001 / ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the distribution substation record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — represents a physical facility owned and operated by the utility to step down transmission voltage for last-mile electric distribution.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Substation construction and major upgrades are capital projects requiring project tracking for budget management, AFUDC calculation, CWIP accounting, and regulatory approval. Critical for capital plan

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Substations are major operational cost centers for utilities, tracking all O&M expenses for regulatory reporting, budgeting, and rate case cost studies. Essential for FERC functional accounting.

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Substations are major capital assets requiring CPCN approval and rate base treatment. Essential for tracking regulatory proceedings authorizing substation construction, upgrades, and cost recovery in

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Substations are major capitalized assets requiring fixed asset tracking for depreciation, rate base calculation, and FERC Form 1 plant accounting. Critical for regulatory financial reporting.

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Asset identifier for this substation facility in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management system. Links to preventive and corrective maintenance work orders, inspection records, and asset lifecycle cost tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo EAM; PAS 55 / ISO 55000 (Asset Management)

attributes.name: pricing_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.pricing_node. Business justification: Substations are primary wholesale delivery points; LMP settlement, transmission cost allocation, and network upgrade cost assignment require substation-to-pricing-node mapping. Critical for FERC Open

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date on which the substation was first energized and placed into commercial service (yyyy-MM-dd). Used to calculate asset age, depreciation schedules (AFUDC capitalization cutoff), and maintenance interval triggers in Oracle WAM/IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (AFUDC); GAAP ASC 360; IEEE Std 1109

attributes.name: construction_work_order
attributes.description: Work order number from Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo associated with the original construction or most recent major capital project at this substation. Links to CAPEX project records, WIP accounting, and AFUDC capitalization in SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; FERC Uniform System of Accounts (AFUDC/WIP); GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: county_name
attributes.description: Name of the county or parish in which the substation is located. Used for local franchise agreement compliance, county emergency management coordination, and property tax assessment records.
attributes.references: State PUC Franchise Agreement; Local Government Property Tax Records

attributes.name: customers_served_count
attributes.description: Total number of end-use customer accounts (residential and commercial) served by distribution feeders emanating from this substation. Used as the denominator for SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability index calculations and outage impact reporting to the PUC.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1366 (SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI); State PUC Annual Reliability Report

attributes.name: decommission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the substation was permanently retired from service (yyyy-MM-dd). Null if the substation is still active. Used for asset retirement accounting, rate base removal, and regulatory decommissioning filings with the PUC.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; State PUC Asset Retirement Rules

attributes.name: der_hosting_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum additional Distributed Energy Resource (DER) generation capacity (in MW) that can be interconnected to feeders served by this substation without requiring infrastructure upgrades, per the utility's hosting capacity analysis. Used for NEM interconnection screening and DERMS planning.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222; State PUC NEM/DER Interconnection Rules; IEEE Std 1547 (DER Interconnection)

attributes.name: division_code
attributes.description: Internal organizational division or district code responsible for operating and maintaining this substation. Maps to the utility's organizational hierarchy in SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP for O&M cost allocation and workforce dispatch.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Organizational Structure; Internal O&M Cost Allocation Policy

attributes.name: ems_node_code
attributes.description: Node identifier for this substation within the ABB or GE Energy Management System (EMS) network model. Used for power flow analysis, state estimation, and real-time grid balancing. Distinct from the SCADA point ID which references the historian tag.
attributes.references: ABB / GE EMS Network Model; IEC 61970 (CIM Transmission); NERC FAC-002

attributes.name: feeder_count
attributes.description: Count of active distribution feeder circuits emanating from this substation's distribution bus. Used for load balancing analysis, SAIDI/SAIFI reliability reporting, and outage impact assessment. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS network topology and Schneider Electric AMS.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1366 (Distribution Reliability Indices); PUC Reliability Reporting

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Unique feature identifier assigned to this substation in the ESRI ArcGIS enterprise geodatabase. Serves as the cross-reference key for spatial joins, network tracing, and GIS-to-OMS/DMS integration. Distinct from the surrogate primary key.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Enterprise Geodatabase; Schneider Electric AMS GIS Integration

attributes.name: installed_capacity_mva
attributes.description: Sum of the nameplate ratings of all power transformers installed at the substation, expressed in Megavolt-Amperes (MVA). Represents the maximum apparent power the substation can deliver to distribution feeders under normal operating conditions. Used for capacity planning, IRP, and FERC Form 1 reporting. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; IEEE Std C57.12.00 (Power Transformers)

attributes.name: is_automated_switching
attributes.description: Indicates whether the substation is equipped with automated switching devices (e.g., automated reclosers, sectionalizers, or FLISR-capable switches) that enable self-healing grid restoration without manual crew dispatch (True/False). Key metric for AMI/DERMS integration and reliability improvement programs.
attributes.references: Schneider Electric AMS FLISR; IEEE Std 1366; PUC Distribution Automation Plans

attributes.name: is_normally_open_tie
attributes.description: Indicates whether this substation serves as a normally-open tie point between two distribution circuits or substations (True) or operates as a radial/normally-closed facility (False). Critical for OMS/DMS switching order generation and restoration planning.
attributes.references: Schneider Electric AMS / GE PowerOn DMS Network Model; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: is_scada_monitored
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this substation has real-time SCADA telemetry integrated into the OSIsoft PI historian or ABB/GE EMS (True) or relies on manual reads and field inspection (False). Affects outage detection latency and SAIDI/SAIFI calculation methodology.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Asset Framework; NERC CIP-005; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: land_parcel_number
attributes.description: County assessor parcel number (APN) or land parcel identifier for the property on which the substation is sited. Used for property tax filings, easement management, and real estate records in SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP.
attributes.references: County Assessor Records; SAP S/4HANA Real Estate Module; FERC Form 1 Land Account

attributes.name: last_major_upgrade_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent major capital upgrade or refurbishment of the substation (e.g., transformer replacement, bus reconfiguration, protection system modernization). Used for CAPEX project tracking, asset condition assessment, and IRP planning.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Work Order History; FERC Form 1 CAPEX Reporting

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: WGS 84 geographic latitude of the substation site centroid in decimal degrees. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS GIS feature class. Used for spatial analysis, storm outage correlation, mutual aid dispatch, and PHMSA/FERC geographic reporting.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; WGS 84 (EPSG:4326); FERC eLibrary Geographic Data Standards

attributes.name: load_factor_pct
attributes.description: Ratio of average load to peak load at this substation over the most recent 12-month period, expressed as a percentage. Indicates utilization efficiency; a higher load factor means more uniform loading. Used in rate case cost studies and capacity planning.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; IRP Load Analysis

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: WGS 84 geographic longitude of the substation site centroid in decimal degrees. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS GIS feature class. Used in conjunction with latitude for spatial analysis, outage mapping, and regulatory geographic reporting.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; WGS 84 (EPSG:4326); FERC eLibrary Geographic Data Standards

attributes.name: nem_interconnection_count
attributes.description: Number of active Net Energy Metering (NEM) customer interconnections (e.g., rooftop solar, small wind) on feeders served by this substation. Used to assess reverse power flow risk, hosting capacity consumption, and DERMS dispatch requirements.
attributes.references: State PUC NEM Tariff; FERC Order 2222; IEEE Std 1547

attributes.name: nerc_bes_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Bulk Electric System (BES) Applicable Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this substation meets the NERC Bulk Electric System (BES) definition thresholds (e.g., connected at 100 kV or above, or meeting generation/load criteria) and is therefore subject to NERC reliability standards (True/False). Drives CIP cybersecurity and FAC compliance obligations.
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition (Effective 2014); NERC CIP-002; FERC Order 773

attributes.name: nerc_cip_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Classification
attributes.description: NERC CIP cyber security impact classification for this substation's Electronic Security Perimeter (ESP) and associated BES Cyber Systems. 'high', 'medium', or 'low' impact per NERC CIP-002-5.1a; 'not_applicable' if BES threshold not met. Governs physical and cyber security control requirements.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-002-5.1a; FERC Order 791; DOE Cybersecurity Guidelines

attributes.name: oms_facility_code
attributes.description: Facility identifier for this substation in the Schneider Electric AMS or GE PowerOn Outage Management System / Distribution Management System (OMS/DMS). Used to associate outage events, switching orders, and restoration activities with this substation.
attributes.references: Schneider Electric AMS / GE PowerOn OMS-DMS; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the distribution substation. 'in_service' = energized and serving load; 'out_of_service' = de-energized for maintenance or fault; 'under_construction' = not yet commissioned; 'decommissioned' = permanently retired; 'mothballed' = temporarily idled. Drives OMS/DMS outage eligibility and asset management workflows. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
attributes.references: Schneider Electric AMS / GE PowerOn OMS; IEEE Std 1109

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Indicates the ownership arrangement for the substation facility and equipment. 'utility_owned' = fully owned by the utility; 'jointly_owned' = shared ownership with another entity (e.g., another utility or municipality); 'customer_owned' = owned by a large industrial customer; 'leased' = utility operates but does not own the facility. Affects CAPEX/OPEX accounting, CIAC treatment, and rate base inclusion.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: peak_load_mw
attributes.description: Maximum recorded real power demand (in Megawatts) observed at this substation during the most recent annual peak period. Used for capacity planning, demand response (DR) program sizing, and IRP load forecasting. Sourced from OSIsoft PI historian interval data.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; FERC Form 1; IRP Load Forecasting Standards

attributes.name: primary_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level on the high-voltage (transmission) side of the substation transformer, expressed in kilovolts (kV). Typical values for distribution substations include 69 kV, 115 kV, 138 kV, or 230 kV. Used for interconnection studies, OATT compliance, and NERC BES applicability determination.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms; FERC OATT; IEEE Std C57.12.00

attributes.name: protection_scheme
attributes.description: Type of protective relay scheme deployed at the substation for fault detection and isolation. Drives maintenance inspection intervals, NERC PRC compliance tracking, and equipment procurement for relay upgrades.
attributes.references: NERC PRC-001 / PRC-002 (Protection Systems); IEEE Std C37.2 (Relay Nomenclature)

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this distribution substation record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for data lineage, audit trail, and ETL reconciliation. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 (Internal Controls); GAAP Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this distribution substation record in the Silver Layer lakehouse (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture (CDC), incremental ETL processing, and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 (Internal Controls); Databricks Delta Lake CDC

attributes.name: saidi_contribution_min
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Contribution (Minutes)
attributes.description: This substation's contribution to the utility's annual System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), expressed in customer-minutes per customer. Calculated from outage events originating at or upstream of this substation. Used for PUC reliability benchmarking and Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) incentive calculations.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1366; State PUC Reliability Standards; PBR Mechanism

attributes.name: scada_point_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: Identifier of the SCADA integration point (RTU/IED address or OSIsoft PI tag prefix) associated with this substation in the OSIsoft PI or GE Proficy historian and the ABB/GE Energy Management System. Enables real-time telemetry linkage for voltage, load, and breaker status monitoring.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Asset Framework; IEC 61968 (CIM Distribution); NERC CIP-005

attributes.name: secondary_voltage_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level on the low-voltage (distribution) side of the substation transformer, expressed in kilovolts (kV). Typical values include 4.16 kV, 12.47 kV, 13.2 kV, 13.8 kV, 25 kV, or 34.5 kV. Determines feeder voltage class and equipment ratings for downstream distribution assets.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1109; ANSI C84.1 (Electric Power Systems Voltage Ratings)

attributes.name: service_territory_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the utility's certificated service territory zone or district in which this substation is located. Used for PUC jurisdictional reporting, rate zone assignment, and load forecasting segmentation. Aligns with the utility's CPCN boundary definitions.
attributes.references: State PUC Service Territory Maps; CPCN Filing

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this substation record was sourced. Supports data lineage tracking and conflict resolution when multiple systems contribute attributes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: arcgis|schneider_ams|ge_poweron|maximo|oracle_wam|pi_historian|manual — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Enterprise Data Governance Policy; Databricks Silver Layer Lineage Standards

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state abbreviation (USPS standard) for the state in which the substation is located. Used for jurisdictional regulatory reporting to state PUCs and for multi-state utility operational segmentation.
attributes.references: USPS State Abbreviations; State PUC Jurisdictional Reporting

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Physical street address of the substation facility (street number, street name, city, state, ZIP). Used for field crew dispatch, emergency response coordination, and permit filings. Classified confidential as organizational location data.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 (Emergency Response); State PUC Facility Registration

attributes.name: substation_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the substation, as assigned by the utility's GIS and OMS/DMS systems (e.g., 'ESRI ArcGIS feature ID' or Schneider Electric AMS station code). Used in SCADA tags, outage tickets, and regulatory filings. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Network Dataset; Schneider Electric AMS

attributes.name: substation_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the distribution substation (e.g., 'Riverside Distribution Substation'). Used in customer-facing outage communications, regulatory filings, and operational dashboards. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE IDENTITY_LABEL category.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1109; NERC Glossary of Terms

attributes.name: substation_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the substation by function within the distribution network. 'distribution' = standard step-down facility; 'switching' = bus-tie/sectionalizing point; 'network' = secondary network vault; 'customer_owned' = customer-sited facility interconnected to the utility grid. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category.
attributes.references: IEEE Std 1109; NERC Glossary of Terms

attributes.name: transformer_count
attributes.description: Total count of power transformers (including main bank and spare/standby units) installed at the substation. Relevant for N-1 contingency analysis, maintenance scheduling in Oracle WAM/IBM Maximo, and capacity redundancy assessment.
attributes.references: IEEE Std C57.12.00; NERC TPL Standards

attributes.name: voltage_regulation_scheme
attributes.description: Primary voltage regulation technology deployed at the substation. 'ltc' = Load Tap Changer on main transformer; 'svr' = Step Voltage Regulator on feeder; 'capacitor_bank' = switched capacitor bank; 'statcom' = Static Synchronous Compensator; 'none' = no active regulation. Relevant for DER/DERMS integration and power quality compliance.
attributes.references: IEEE Std C57.15 (Voltage Regulators); ANSI C84.1; DERMS Integration Standards

products.name: service_point
products.description: Master record for electric and gas service delivery points — the physical location where utility service is delivered to an end-use customer premise. Captures service point ID, service address, GPS coordinates, GIS parcel reference, service type (electric/gas/dual), premise type (residential/commercial/industrial), meter socket ID, feeder or gas main association, transformer association, service lateral details, load classification, NEM eligibility flag, DER interconnection flag, and active/inactive status. Serves as the geographic and physical SSOT linking the distribution network topology to customer accounts and metering infrastructure. Each service point represents one service delivery of a given type at a premise — a dual-service premise has separate electric and gas service points. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS and Oracle CC&B/SAP IS-U.
products.reference: CIM IEC 61968-11 ServiceLocation

attributes.name: service_point_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the service point record in the distribution domain. Primary key for the master record of a physical utility service delivery location. Role: MASTER_RESOURCE.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account currently associated with this service point. Links the physical delivery location to the billing and customer relationship record in the CIS.

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Reference to the electric distribution feeder circuit that supplies power to this service point. Used for outage management, SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability reporting, and load flow analysis.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; Schneider Electric AMS / GE PowerOn (OMS/DMS)

attributes.name: gas_main_id
attributes.description: Reference to the gas distribution main pipeline segment supplying this service point. Applicable only for gas or dual-service service points. Used for PHMSA pipeline safety reporting and gas network topology.

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the metering device currently installed at this service point. Links the service delivery location to the AMI/AMR meter asset record in the MDMS and EAM.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDMS / Itron Analytics; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical premise (property/parcel) at which this service point is located. A single premise may have multiple service points (e.g., separate electric and gas service points for a dual-service premise).
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: pricing_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.pricing_node. Business justification: Retail choice markets require service point to pricing node mapping for LMP-based customer billing and settlement. Load-serving entities need this link for retail rate calculation and wholesale cost a

attributes.name: service_equipment_material_master_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Service Equipment Material Master Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Service points have standardized service equipment (meter sockets, service entrance cables, disconnects) tracked as materials. Enables new service installation cost estimation, AMI deployment material

attributes.name: service_transformer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.service_transformer. Business justification: Service points (customer delivery points) are served by distribution service transformers. This is a fundamental distribution network relationship essential for outage management, service restoration,

attributes.name: tariff_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.tariff_schedule. Business justification: Each service point is billed under a specific approved tariff schedule. Fundamental billing relationship: tariff determines rates, charges, and terms of service. Replaces denormalized rate_schedule_co

attributes.name: ami_enabled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this service point is equipped with an Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meter capable of two-way communication and interval data collection. Distinguishes AMI from legacy AMR or manual-read meters.
attributes.references: Oracle Utilities MDMS / Itron Analytics; State PUC AMI Deployment Plans

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality of the service delivery location. Used for geographic reporting, franchise territory validation, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; NARUC Utility Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: connect_date
attributes.description: Date on which utility service was first connected and activated at this service point. Used for service tenure analysis, asset age tracking, and move-in/move-out processing.

attributes.name: contract_demand_kw
attributes.description: Contracted maximum demand in kilowatts (kW) for this service point as agreed in the service agreement or tariff schedule. Used for demand charge billing, transformer sizing, and capacity planning.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; State PUC Tariff Schedules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service point record was first created in the source system of record. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and record lifecycle management. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: der_capacity_kw
attributes.description: Nameplate installed capacity in kilowatts (kW) of the Distributed Energy Resource (DER) interconnected at this service point. Populated only when der_interconnect_flag is true. Used for hosting capacity analysis and DERMS dispatch.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547; FERC Order 2222; State PUC Interconnection Rules

attributes.name: der_interconnect_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Distributed Energy Resource (DER) — such as rooftop solar PV, battery storage, or small wind — is interconnected at this service point. Used by DERMS for grid visibility, voltage regulation, and DER dispatch coordination.
attributes.references: IEEE 1547 (DER Interconnection Standard); FERC Order 2222; State PUC Interconnection Rules

attributes.name: disconnect_date
attributes.description: Date on which utility service was permanently disconnected at this service point. Null for active service points. Used for move-out processing, final billing, and service point lifecycle management.

attributes.name: dr_program_enrolled_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this service point is currently enrolled in a Demand Response (DR) or load management program. Used for peak shaving event dispatch, DSM program tracking, and regulatory DR reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; State PUC DSM Program Rules; Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U

attributes.name: ev_charger_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an Electric Vehicle (EV) charging station is installed at this service point. Used for load forecasting, grid impact analysis, and EV-specific rate program eligibility (e.g., TOU-EV rates).
attributes.references: State PUC EV Tariff Rules; DOE EV Infrastructure Programs

attributes.name: gas_meter_set_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the gas meter set assembly (regulator, meter, and associated fittings) at this service point. Used for gas asset management, safety inspection scheduling, and PHMSA compliance tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: gas_pressure_class
attributes.description: Operating pressure classification of the gas service lateral at this service point (low, medium, or high pressure). Applicable only for gas or dual-service service points. Required for PHMSA pipeline safety management and gas distribution system design.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; AGA Distribution Integrity Management Program (DIMP)

attributes.name: gis_last_updated_date
attributes.description: Date on which the GIS spatial record for this service point was last updated in ESRI ArcGIS. Used for GIS data quality monitoring and network model synchronization with OMS/DMS.

attributes.name: gis_parcel_code
attributes.description: County assessor parcel identification number (APN) or GIS parcel reference linking the service point to the land parcel record in the ESRI ArcGIS system. Used for property-level spatial analysis and CIAC/AFUDC cost allocation.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent safety or compliance inspection performed at this service point. Used for inspection scheduling, regulatory compliance tracking (PHMSA, OSHA), and asset maintenance planning.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; OSHA

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the service point in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS network topology, field crew navigation, and spatial analytics.

attributes.name: load_class_code
attributes.description: Utility-defined load classification code assigned to the service point for rate design, load forecasting, and demand-side management program targeting (e.g., RES-1, COM-2, IND-3). Sourced from Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U rate class assignment.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Tariff Schedules

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the service point in decimal degrees (WGS84 datum). Used for GIS network topology, field crew navigation, and spatial analytics.

attributes.name: meter_read_cycle
attributes.description: Billing cycle code or route identifier that determines the scheduled meter reading frequency and sequence for this service point (e.g., monthly cycle 01, bi-monthly cycle 02). Used for meter reading route optimization and billing cycle management.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; Oracle Utilities MDMS

attributes.name: meter_socket_code
attributes.description: Physical identifier of the meter socket or meter base at the service point. Distinguishes the physical installation point from the meter device itself, enabling meter change-out tracking without losing service point continuity.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; Oracle Utilities MDMS

attributes.name: nem_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this service point is eligible for Net Energy Metering (NEM) — the billing arrangement allowing customers with on-site generation (e.g., rooftop solar) to receive credit for excess energy exported to the grid. Drives NEM tariff application and bidirectional metering requirements.
attributes.references: State PUC NEM Tariff Rules; IEEE 1547; CPUC Decision (NEM)

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: US ZIP or ZIP+4 postal code for the service delivery location. Used for geographic analysis, franchise territory mapping, and demographic segmentation.

attributes.name: premise_type
attributes.description: Classification of the customer premise by end-use category. Drives tariff schedule assignment, load classification, and regulatory reporting segmentation (e.g., residential vs. commercial/industrial rate classes). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: residential|commercial|industrial|agricultural|lighting|other — promote to reference product if additional classes are needed]
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: service_address_line1
attributes.description: Primary street address line of the physical service delivery location. Used for field crew dispatch, GIS geocoding, and customer correspondence. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE IDENTITY_LABEL category.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; USPS Postal Addressing Standards

attributes.name: service_address_line2
attributes.description: Secondary address line for the service delivery location (e.g., apartment, suite, unit number). Supplements the primary address for multi-unit premises.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; USPS Postal Addressing Standards

attributes.name: service_lateral_length_ft
attributes.description: Length in feet of the service lateral — the conductor or pipe segment connecting the distribution main or transformer to the customer's meter. Used for CIAC cost estimation, line loss calculations, and asset inventory.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: service_lateral_material
attributes.description: Material type of the service lateral conductor (electric) or pipe (gas). Used for asset condition assessment, replacement prioritization, and PHMSA gas pipeline safety reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overhead_aluminum|overhead_copper|underground_xlpe|underground_pvc|steel_pipe|polyethylene_pipe|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: service_phase
attributes.description: Electrical phase configuration of the service delivery: single_phase (residential/small commercial) or three_phase (large commercial/industrial). Drives transformer sizing, load analysis, and rate eligibility.

attributes.name: service_point_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the service point indicating whether utility service is being actively delivered. Drives field work orders, billing eligibility, and OMS outage event correlation. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE LIFECYCLE_STATUS category. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|inactive|pending_connect|pending_disconnect|disconnected|abandoned — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Indicates the commodity type delivered at this service point: electric (electricity only), gas (natural gas only), or dual (both electric and gas). Drives rate application, metering configuration, and regulatory reporting segmentation. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; NARUC Utility Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: service_voltage_v
attributes.description: Nominal utilization voltage delivered at the service point in volts (e.g., 120, 240, 480). Used for voltage regulation analysis, equipment compatibility verification, and DMS load flow studies. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category.
attributes.references: IEEE C84.1 (Voltage Ratings for Electric Power Systems); ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this service point record was sourced (e.g., CCB for Oracle CC&B, SAP_ISU for SAP IS-U, ARCGIS for ESRI ArcGIS). Used for data lineage and master data management reconciliation.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U

attributes.name: sp_external_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the service point as assigned by the source system of record (Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U / ESRI ArcGIS). Used for cross-system reconciliation between the CIS, GIS, and MDMS. Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state abbreviation for the service delivery location. Used for regulatory jurisdiction assignment (PUC, FERC) and geographic segmentation.
attributes.references: USPS State Abbreviations; FERC; State PUCs

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service point record was last modified in the source system of record. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U; SOX Section 404

products.name: gas_main
products.description: Master record for gas distribution mains — the pressurized pipeline segments that transport natural gas from city gate stations through the distribution network to service laterals and end-use customers. Captures main ID, pipe material (steel/PE/cast iron), nominal diameter (inches), operating pressure (PSIG), MAOP (Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure), installation year, coating type, cathodic protection status, GIS route geometry, district/pressure zone, leak survey date, PHMSA class location, and operational status. SSOT for PHMSA pipeline safety compliance and gas distribution network topology. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS.
products.reference: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 / AGA Pipeline Safety

attributes.name: gas_main_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for a gas distribution main segment record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — represents a physical pipeline asset owned and operated by the utility.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Gas Network Feature Class

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Gas main installations and replacements are capital projects requiring project tracking for budget management, AFUDC calculation, and regulatory reporting. Essential for pipeline investment management

attributes.name: city_gate_station_id
attributes.description: Reference to the city gate or gate station that feeds the pressure zone containing this gas main segment. Used for supply traceability, pressure management, and gas quality tracking.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Gas Network Topology; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Gas main maintenance, leak surveys, and operational costs are allocated to cost centers for FERC gas utility accounting and regulatory reporting. Required for rate case cost allocation.

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Gas main replacements and upgrades are subject to rate cases and CPCN proceedings for cost recovery. Business need: tracking which dockets authorize gas infrastructure investments and allow rate base

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Gas mains are capitalized pipeline assets tracked in fixed asset register for depreciation, rate base inclusion, and FERC gas plant accounting. Essential for regulatory asset management.

attributes.name: from_node_id
attributes.description: GIS network node identifier at the upstream (supply) end of the gas main segment. Used for network topology traversal, hydraulic modeling, and outage/isolation analysis.

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Gas mains are major capital assets requiring depreciation, FERC accounting, DIMP compliance, condition monitoring, integrity management programs, and regulatory asset base tracking. Critical for pipel

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Gas mains are procured pipe materials tracked by specification, diameter, and grade. Critical for PHMSA material traceability requirements, DIMP threat assessment, and pipeline integrity management. E

attributes.name: cathodic_protection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the gas main segment is covered by an active cathodic protection (CP) system. True = CP system in place and active; False = no cathodic protection. Required for PHMSA corrosion control compliance on steel mains per 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart I.

attributes.name: cathodic_protection_type
attributes.description: Type of cathodic protection system applied to the gas main segment. Impressed-current systems use rectifiers; sacrificial-anode systems use zinc or magnesium anodes. Used in corrosion control program documentation and PHMSA compliance records.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart I; NACE SP0169

attributes.name: coating_type
attributes.description: External corrosion protection coating applied to the pipe. Relevant primarily for steel mains. Used in corrosion control program management and PHMSA integrity management. Values: fusion-bonded-epoxy, coal-tar, polyethylene-tape, bare (no coating), other, unknown.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart I; NACE SP0169

attributes.name: county
attributes.description: County in which the gas main segment is located. Used for PHMSA annual mileage reporting by county, permit coordination, and emergency response jurisdiction mapping.

attributes.name: crossing_type
attributes.description: Type of infrastructure crossing associated with this gas main segment, if applicable. Used for permit tracking, inspection scheduling, and PHMSA high-consequence area (HCA) assessments. Values: road, railroad, water, aerial, none.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; DOT Crossing Permit Requirements

attributes.name: dimp_threat_rank
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distribution Integrity Management Program (DIMP) Threat Rank
attributes.description: Risk/threat ranking assigned to this gas main segment under the utility's Distribution Integrity Management Program (DIMP) as required by PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart P. Drives prioritization of inspection, repair, and replacement activities.

attributes.name: district_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the gas distribution operating district or service territory subdivision responsible for this main segment. Used for O&M cost allocation, workforce dispatch, and regulatory reporting by district.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; SAP S/4HANA Cost Center Structure

attributes.name: encased_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the gas main segment is installed within a casing pipe (e.g., at road crossings, railroad crossings, or water crossings). True = encased; False = direct burial. Relevant for PHMSA integrity management and maintenance access planning.

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: Native feature identifier assigned by ESRI ArcGIS to this gas main segment in the geospatial network dataset. Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the authoritative GIS source system.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Gas Network Feature Class

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the gas main segment was physically installed and placed in service. Used for asset age calculations, replacement prioritization, depreciation schedules, and PHMSA pipeline records. Maps to installation year in legacy GIS records where only year is known.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Asset Record

attributes.name: installation_year
attributes.description: Year the gas main segment was installed, retained as a separate field for legacy records where only the year (not full date) is known from historical GIS or paper records. Used in PHMSA annual mileage reporting by decade of installation.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 191 Annual Report; ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: installed_by
attributes.description: Name of the contractor or utility crew that installed the gas main segment. Used for construction quality traceability and warranty/liability tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Work Order Records

attributes.name: joint_type
attributes.description: Type of pipe joint used in the gas main segment construction. Relevant for integrity assessment and leak history analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: butt-fusion|electrofusion|mechanical|threaded|welded|bell-spigot|other — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: leak_survey_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent leak survey conducted on this gas main segment. Used to track compliance with PHMSA-mandated leak survey frequency requirements, which vary by pipe material, pressure tier, and class location.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 §192.723; AGA Distribution Integrity Management

attributes.name: leak_survey_method
attributes.description: Method used in the most recent leak survey of this gas main segment. Values: bar-hole (soil probe), walking (combustible gas indicator on foot), mobile (vehicle-mounted methane detector), aerial (helicopter/drone), other.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 §192.723; AGA Leak Survey Guidelines

attributes.name: main_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the gas main segment as assigned in the GIS (ESRI ArcGIS) and referenced in PHMSA pipeline safety records, work orders, and field documentation. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER / natural key for cross-system traceability.

attributes.name: main_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name or label for the gas main segment (e.g., 'Oak Street 4-inch PE Main'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for operational reference and field crew communication.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Gas Network Feature Class

attributes.name: maop_psig
attributes.description: Maximum Allowable Operating Pressure in pounds per square inch gauge (PSIG) as established per PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192. The regulatory ceiling for operating pressure on this segment. Critical for pipeline safety compliance and integrity management programs.

attributes.name: municipality
attributes.description: Name of the city, town, or municipality in which the gas main segment is located. Used for regulatory reporting, permit management, and service territory mapping.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 191 Annual Report; State PUC Reporting

attributes.name: nominal_diameter_in
attributes.description: Nominal pipe diameter in inches (e.g., 2, 4, 6, 8, 12). MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE for this pipeline asset. Used for capacity calculations, flow modeling, and replacement cost estimation. Standard nominal sizes per ASME B36.10M.

attributes.name: operating_pressure_psig
attributes.description: Normal operating pressure of the gas main in pounds per square inch gauge (PSIG). Used for pressure zone management, DMS/SCADA monitoring, and PHMSA compliance. Must not exceed MAOP.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the gas main segment. Drives PHMSA reporting scope, maintenance scheduling, and GIS network topology. LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this MASTER_RESOURCE. Values: in-service (active, pressurized), out-of-service (isolated, not pressurized), abandoned (physically in place but permanently decommissioned), proposed (planned, not yet installed), under-construction (installation in progress).

attributes.name: phmsa_class_location
attributes.description: Pipeline class location (1 through 4) as defined by PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 §192.5, based on population density within a sliding-mile corridor along the pipeline. Class 1 = rural/low density; Class 4 = high-density urban. Determines design factor, testing requirements, and integrity management obligations.

attributes.name: pipe_depth_in
attributes.description: Depth of cover over the gas main in inches, measured from ground surface to top of pipe. Used to verify compliance with minimum cover requirements per PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 §192.327 and to assess third-party damage risk.

attributes.name: pipe_grade
attributes.description: Material grade or specification of the pipe (e.g., ASTM D2513 for PE, API 5L Grade B for steel). Used in integrity management calculations, MAOP determination, and PHMSA compliance documentation.

attributes.name: pipe_material
attributes.description: Material composition of the gas main pipe. Critical for PHMSA pipeline integrity management, leak survey frequency determination, and replacement prioritization. Common values: PE (polyethylene — modern standard), steel (bare or coated), cast-iron (legacy, high leak risk), wrought-iron (legacy), copper, PVC, other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PE|steel|cast-iron|wrought-iron|copper|PVC|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; AGA Pipeline Safety Standards

attributes.name: pressure_tier
attributes.description: Pressure classification tier of the gas main segment. Drives operational procedures, regulator station requirements, and customer service pressure expectations. Values: high (typically >60 PSIG), medium (typically 0.5–60 PSIG), low (typically <0.5 PSIG), very-low (inches of water column).
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; AGA Distribution Integrity Management

attributes.name: pressure_zone_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the gas distribution pressure zone or district regulator area to which this main segment belongs. Used for hydraulic network modeling, pressure management, and operational dispatch. Sourced from ESRI ArcGIS network topology.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS Gas Network; AGA Distribution Integrity Management

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this gas main record was first created in the source GIS system or the lakehouse Silver Layer. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED tracking per MASTER_RESOURCE canonical requirements.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this gas main record in the lakehouse Silver Layer. Used for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date the gas main segment was retired, abandoned, or permanently taken out of service. Null for active segments. Used for asset lifecycle management, PHMSA abandoned pipeline records, and depreciation accounting.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 §192.727; Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo

attributes.name: route_geometry_wkt
attributes.description: GIS route geometry of the gas main segment encoded as Well-Known Text (WKT) LINESTRING in WGS84 coordinate reference system. Enables spatial analysis, proximity queries, and map visualization in the lakehouse without requiring a live GIS connection.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; OGC WKT Standard; ISO 19125

attributes.name: seam_type
attributes.description: Longitudinal seam type for steel pipe mains (e.g., seamless, ERW — Electric Resistance Welded, DSAW — Double Submerged Arc Welded). Used in integrity management threat identification per PHMSA Distribution Integrity Management Program (DIMP) requirements.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 Subpart O; API 5L

attributes.name: segment_length_ft
attributes.description: Physical length of the gas main segment in feet as measured in the GIS network. Used for leak survey scheduling, replacement cost estimation, PHMSA mileage reporting, and O&M planning.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 191 Annual Report; ESRI ArcGIS

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this gas main record was sourced. Supports data lineage and master data management. Values: GIS (ESRI ArcGIS), EAM (Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo), SCADA (OSIsoft PI / GE Proficy), MANUAL (manual entry).
attributes.references: Enterprise Data Governance; ETL Lineage Standards

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state abbreviation (e.g., CA, TX, NY) where the gas main segment is located. Used for PHMSA state pipeline safety program reporting and state PUC regulatory filings.

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Street name and address range along which the gas main is routed (e.g., '100-400 Oak Street'). Used for field crew dispatch, permit coordination, and customer impact assessment during maintenance or emergency events.

attributes.name: to_node_code
attributes.description: GIS network node identifier at the downstream (delivery) end of the gas main segment. Used for network topology traversal, hydraulic modeling, and isolation analysis.

attributes.name: wall_thickness_in
attributes.description: Nominal pipe wall thickness in inches. Used in MAOP calculations per PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 hoop stress formula and in integrity management assessments.

products.name: distribution_outage_event
products.description: Transactional record for electric distribution outage events — unplanned or planned interruptions to customer electric service tracked through the OMS/DMS. Captures outage event ID, outage type (unplanned/planned/momentary), cause code (weather/equipment failure/animal/vegetation/etc.), affected feeder, affected transformer, estimated customers affected, actual customers affected, outage start timestamp, restoration timestamp, outage duration (minutes), crew dispatch reference, SAIDI contribution (minutes), SAIFI contribution (count), CAIDI calculation, IEEE 1366 exclusion flag, and restoration method. Primary source for SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability index calculations reported to PUCs. Sourced from Schneider Electric AMS/GE PowerOn OMS.
products.reference: IEEE 1366 / OMS Outage Event

attributes.name: distribution_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the outage event record in the distribution domain Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366-2012 Guide for Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: compliance_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_event. Business justification: Outages violating reliability standards generate compliance events with potential penalties. Core regulatory reporting: linking outages to compliance violations for SAIDI/SAIFI standard enforcement an

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Outage restoration costs (labor, materials, equipment) are allocated to cost centers for expense tracking, budgeting, and regulatory reporting. Essential for storm cost recovery and rate case preparat

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution substation from which the affected feeder originates. Links to the substation master record. Used for substation-level outage aggregation and reliability performance reporting.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS GIS Network Model; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Major outages trigger regulatory investigations, penalty proceedings, and reliability improvement orders. Direct business need: linking outage events to resulting regulatory dockets for penalty tracki

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder (circuit) on which the outage event originated or had the greatest impact. Links to the distribution feeder master record in the GIS/network model. Used for feeder-level reliability performance analysis and SAIDI/SAIFI disaggregation.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS GIS Network Model; IEEE 1366-2012

attributes.name: opex_transaction_id
