[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|authorized|in_progress|completed|cancelled|failed|rolled_back — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: operation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the switching operation was physically executed in the field. Represents the actual moment the device state changed. Distinct from authorization or completion timestamps. Critical for outage duration calculations and SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability index computation.

attributes.name: operation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the switching operation based on its purpose and planning status. Planned operations are scheduled in advance; emergency operations respond to unplanned events; restoration operations return circuits to normal configuration; maintenance operations support asset work; reconfiguration operations optimize load distribution; fault isolation operations isolate faulted sections.

attributes.name: operator_employee_number
attributes.description: Identifier of the field technician or operator who physically executed the switching operation. Links to workforce management system for operator qualifications, certifications, and training records. Critical for OSHA lockout/tagout compliance and safety audit trails.

attributes.name: post_switch_configuration
attributes.description: State of the device after the switching operation was completed. Represents the new configuration achieved by the switching action.
attributes.references: IEEE C37 Series, NERC FAC Standards

attributes.name: pre_switch_configuration
attributes.description: State of the device immediately before the switching operation was executed. Open indicates no current flow; closed indicates energized and conducting; grounded indicates connected to ground; isolated indicates disconnected from all sources.
attributes.references: IEEE C37 Series, NERC FAC Standards

attributes.name: rollback_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the switching operation was subsequently reversed or rolled back to the original configuration due to operational issues, equipment problems, or changed conditions. True if the operation was rolled back; False if the new configuration was maintained.

attributes.name: rollback_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why the switching operation was rolled back to the original configuration. Null if rollback_flag is False.

attributes.name: safety_clearance_number
attributes.description: Reference number for the safety clearance or work permit authorizing personnel to work on or near the device. Links to the safety management system for clearance scope, authorized personnel, and expiration. Required for all switching operations involving worker access to energized or de-energized equipment.

attributes.name: scada_command_issued_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Command Issued Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the switching operation was executed via remote SCADA command from the control center (True) or manually in the field (False). Remote SCADA operations enable faster response and reduce field crew dispatch requirements.

attributes.name: scada_verification_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Verification Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the post-switching device state was verified via SCADA telemetry (True) or required manual field verification (False). SCADA verification provides real-time confirmation of device state.

attributes.name: scheduled_timestamp
attributes.description: Planned date and time for the switching operation to be executed. Applicable to planned and maintenance operations. Null for emergency and unplanned operations.

attributes.name: service_territory_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code where the switching operation occurred. Used for regulatory reporting to state Public Utility Commissions (PUCs) and geographic analysis of switching activity.

attributes.name: switching_order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known switching order number issued by the Distribution Management System (DMS) or Outage Management System (OMS) authorizing the switching operation. Serves as the business identifier for tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: switching_reason_code
attributes.description: Categorized reason for the switching operation. Fault isolation responds to detected faults; load transfer balances circuit loading; voltage regulation addresses voltage issues; maintenance support enables asset work; storm restoration recovers from weather events; planned outage supports scheduled work; equipment failure responds to device malfunction; customer request fulfills service requests. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fault_isolation|load_transfer|voltage_regulation|maintenance_support|storm_restoration|planned_outage|equipment_failure|customer_request — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: switching_reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative describing the specific business or operational reason for the switching operation. Provides context beyond the categorized reason code, including details of the fault, maintenance activity, or operational need.

attributes.name: tag_lockout_status
attributes.description: OSHA lockout/tagout (LOTO) status of the device during the switching operation. Tagged indicates warning tag applied; locked out indicates physical lock preventing operation; tagged and locked indicates both controls applied; cleared indicates LOTO removed and device returned to service. Critical for worker safety compliance.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the switching operation record was last modified in the source system. Tracks changes to status, completion, or other operational details as the switching operation progresses through its lifecycle.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the circuit or equipment operated. Typical distribution voltage levels include 4.16 kV, 12.47 kV, 13.2 kV, 13.8 kV, 23 kV, 34.5 kV. Voltage level determines safety clearances, equipment ratings, and operational procedures.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Weather condition at the time of the switching operation. Weather context is critical for understanding emergency switching operations, storm restoration activities, and equipment failure root causes. Used for major event day (MED) exclusion analysis in reliability reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|rain|snow|ice|wind|storm|lightning|fog|extreme_heat|extreme_cold — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: work_order_number
attributes.description: Work order number from the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) or Work Management System (WMS) associated with the switching operation. Links to Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo, or equivalent system for maintenance activity tracking, labor costs, and asset history. Applicable when switching supports planned maintenance or capital work.

products.name: gas_leak_survey
products.description: Transactional record for PHMSA-mandated gas leak surveys and leak investigations on gas distribution mains, service laterals, and associated facilities. Captures survey ID, survey type (leak survey/leak investigation/follow-up), survey date, surveyor ID, pipeline segment surveyed (gas main reference), survey method (bar-hole/CGI/flame ionization), leak grade (Grade 1 hazardous/Grade 2 non-hazardous/Grade 3 non-hazardous), leak location (GPS), leak size estimate (MCF/day), repair priority, repair due date, repair completion date, and regulatory reporting status. SSOT for PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 pipeline safety compliance and AGA leak survey reporting.
products.reference: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192 / AGA Gas Leak Survey

attributes.name: gas_leak_survey_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the gas leak survey record. Primary key for the gas leak survey transaction.

attributes.name: compliance_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_event. Business justification: Detected leaks violating safety standards become compliance events with repair deadlines and potential penalties. Core safety regulatory process: linking leak findings to compliance violations for PHM

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Leak surveys fulfill PHMSA pipeline safety obligations and state-mandated inspection frequencies. Direct regulatory compliance: linking surveys to the specific obligations they satisfy for audit and p

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Leak survey program costs are allocated to cost centers for O&M expense tracking, PHMSA compliance reporting, and regulatory cost recovery. Essential for gas safety program accounting.

attributes.name: gas_main_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the gas distribution main or service lateral segment that was surveyed. Links to the GIS network topology for the pipeline segment.

attributes.name: opex_transaction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.opex_transaction. Business justification: Leak survey activities generate O&M expense transactions for labor and equipment costs. Required for PHMSA compliance cost tracking and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: repair_work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the work order created for leak repair. Links to EAM system (Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo) for repair tracking and completion verification. Null if no repair required.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the employee or contractor who performed the leak survey. Links to workforce management system for qualification tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: Ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of survey. Temperature affects gas dispersion and detector sensitivity.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this gas leak survey record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system from which this survey record originated (e.g., Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo, ESRI ArcGIS mobile survey app). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: gas_concentration_ppm
attributes.description: Measured natural gas concentration in parts per million (PPM) at the leak location. Used for leak grade classification and hazard assessment. Null if no leak detected.

attributes.name: leak_detected_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether a gas leak was detected during this survey. True if leak found; False if no leak detected.

attributes.name: leak_grade
attributes.description: AGA and PHMSA leak classification. Grade 1 is hazardous requiring immediate repair; Grade 2 is non-hazardous requiring scheduled repair within one year; Grade 3 is non-hazardous monitored annually.
attributes.references: AGA Leak Classification Standard, PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192.703

attributes.name: leak_latitude
attributes.description: GPS latitude coordinate of the detected leak location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and spatial analysis of leak patterns.

attributes.name: leak_location_description
attributes.description: Textual description of the precise leak location on the pipeline segment (e.g., valve body, joint, service tee, main-to-lateral connection). Used for repair crew dispatch and work order generation.

attributes.name: leak_longitude
attributes.description: GPS longitude coordinate of the detected leak location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and spatial analysis of leak patterns.

attributes.name: leak_size_estimate_mcf_per_day
attributes.description: Estimated volumetric leak rate in thousand cubic feet (MCF) of natural gas per day. Used for emissions reporting and repair prioritization. Null if no leak detected.
attributes.references: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program, PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: operating_pressure_psig
attributes.description: Operating pressure of the gas distribution system at the survey location in pounds per square inch gauge (PSIG). Used for leak grade classification and hazard assessment.

attributes.name: phmsa_incident_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) Incident Number
attributes.description: PHMSA-assigned incident tracking number for reportable gas leaks. Used for federal regulatory compliance and incident investigation tracking. Null if not PHMSA-reportable.

attributes.name: phmsa_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this leak meets PHMSA federal reporting thresholds (e.g., incident causing injury, death, or significant property damage). True if reportable to PHMSA; False otherwise.

attributes.name: pipeline_diameter_inches
attributes.description: Nominal diameter of the surveyed pipeline segment in inches. Used for leak size estimation and repair planning.

attributes.name: pipeline_material
attributes.description: Material composition of the surveyed pipeline segment. PE is polyethylene; HDPE is high-density polyethylene. Material type affects leak risk and survey frequency requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: steel|cast iron|plastic|PE|HDPE|copper|bare steel|coated steel — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: pipeline_segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the pipeline infrastructure component surveyed. Main is distribution backbone; service lateral is customer connection; riser is vertical pipe to meter.

attributes.name: prior_survey_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent previous leak survey performed on this pipeline segment. Used to verify compliance with PHMSA survey frequency requirements.

attributes.name: puc_reporting_status
attributes.description: Status of regulatory reporting submission to the state Public Utility Commission. Grade 1 and Grade 2 leaks typically require PUC notification.

attributes.name: puc_submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the leak survey record was submitted to the state Public Utility Commission for regulatory compliance reporting. Null if not yet submitted or not required.

attributes.name: repair_completion_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the leak repair was completed and verified. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and SAIDI/SAIFI reliability metrics. Null if repair not yet completed.

attributes.name: repair_due_date
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the detected leak must be repaired. Grade 1 leaks require immediate action; Grade 2 leaks must be repaired within 12 months per PHMSA. Null if no repair required.

attributes.name: repair_priority
attributes.description: Work order priority classification for leak repair. Immediate for Grade 1 hazardous leaks; scheduled for Grade 2; monitor for Grade 3.

attributes.name: service_territory_state
attributes.description: Two-letter state code where the survey was performed. Used for state PUC regulatory reporting and jurisdictional compliance tracking.

attributes.name: survey_crew_size
attributes.description: Number of personnel assigned to the survey crew. Used for workforce planning and cost allocation.

attributes.name: survey_date
attributes.description: The date on which the leak survey or investigation was performed in the field. Principal business event timestamp for the survey transaction.

attributes.name: survey_duration_hours
attributes.description: Total time in hours spent performing the leak survey. Used for labor cost tracking and productivity analysis.

attributes.name: survey_external_code
attributes.description: External business identifier for the survey as recorded in the source system (e.g., Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo work order number or survey ticket number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail.

attributes.name: survey_frequency_months
attributes.description: Regulatory-mandated survey frequency in months for this pipeline segment. PHMSA requires annual surveys for business districts, multi-year for less critical areas. Used for compliance scheduling.

attributes.name: survey_method
attributes.description: The leak detection method or technology used during the survey. CGI is Combustible Gas Indicator; bar-hole is physical probe method; flame ionization is laboratory-grade detector.

attributes.name: survey_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for surveyor observations, special conditions, access issues, or other contextual information relevant to the survey. Used for audit trail and follow-up investigation.

attributes.name: survey_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the survey record. Tracks progression from scheduling through completion and regulatory approval.

attributes.name: survey_type
attributes.description: Classification of the survey activity. Leak survey is routine PHMSA-mandated inspection; leak investigation is response to reported leak; follow-up survey is re-inspection of previously identified leak.
attributes.value_regex: leak survey|leak investigation|follow-up survey|routine patrol|special survey|damage assessment

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this gas leak survey record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Weather conditions at the time of survey (e.g., clear, rain, snow, wind). Weather can affect leak detection equipment performance and survey accuracy.

products.name: load_profile
products.description: Transactional record capturing aggregated interval-level load measurements and demand readings at the feeder, substation, and service transformer level for distribution planning, capacity analysis, hosting capacity studies, and demand response program management. Captures load profile ID, measurement point (feeder/substation/transformer), measurement interval (15-min/30-min/60-min), timestamp, real power (kW), reactive power (kVAR), apparent power (kVA), power factor, peak demand (kW), load factor, temperature-adjusted demand, data source (SCADA/AMI aggregation), and data quality flag. Supports DER hosting capacity analysis by providing baseline load data for feeder-level solar/storage impact modeling. Represents aggregated network-level load data for distribution operations — distinct from raw SCADA telemetry points and AMI meter interval reads (owned by metering domain). Granularity is one record per measurement point per interval. Sourced from OSIsoft PI/GE Proficy SCADA historian.
products.reference: OSIsoft PI / SCADA Load Data / IEEE 1159

attributes.name: load_profile_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the load profile measurement record. Primary key for the load profile data product.

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the substation where load measurements were captured. Links to the substation asset in the distribution network.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.12.00 - General Requirements for Liquid-Immersed Distribution, Power, and Regulating Transformers

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Reference to the distribution feeder where load measurements were captured. Links to the distribution feeder asset in the GIS network topology.

attributes.name: pricing_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to market.pricing_node. Business justification: Load profiles at pricing nodes drive day-ahead and real-time market bid preparation for load-serving entities. Essential for wholesale energy procurement, load forecasting for market operations, and s

attributes.name: service_transformer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.service_transformer. Business justification: Load profiles are measured at various points in the distribution network, including service transformers. The load_profile table has measurement_point_type (STRING) which can indicate 'transformer' le

attributes.name: transformer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service transformer where load measurements were captured. Links to the transformer asset in the distribution network.
attributes.references: IEEE C57.12.00 - General Requirements for Liquid-Immersed Distribution, Power, and Regulating Transformers

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: Ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the measurement location during the interval. Used for temperature-load correlation analysis and weather normalization.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: apparent_power_kva
attributes.description: Average apparent power in kilovolt-amperes during the measurement interval. Represents the total power flow including both real and reactive components.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for the Measurement of Electric Power Quantities

attributes.name: average_voltage_v
attributes.description: Average voltage in volts measured during the interval. Used for voltage regulation analysis and power quality monitoring.

attributes.name: circuit_miles
attributes.description: Total circuit miles of distribution infrastructure served by the measurement point. Used for load density calculations and capacity planning.

attributes.name: computation_method
attributes.description: Algorithm or method used to compute aggregated load values from raw telemetry or AMI interval data. Describes the aggregation logic applied by the historian or MDMS system.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: computed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the load profile record was computed or aggregated by the source system. Distinct from the measurement timestamp, represents the processing time.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this load profile record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Audit timestamp for data lineage and traceability.

attributes.name: current_amperes
attributes.description: Average current flow in amperes during the measurement interval. Used for thermal loading analysis and conductor capacity assessment.

attributes.name: customer_count
attributes.description: Number of customers served by the measurement point during the interval. Used for per-customer load analysis and reliability index calculations.
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 - Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the load measurement data. Flags data that has been estimated, is suspect, missing, or manually overridden for operational or analytical purposes.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Source system that provided the load measurement data. Indicates whether data originated from SCADA telemetry, aggregated AMI meter reads, DMS, EMS, or historian platform.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: demand_response_event_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a demand response event was active during the measurement interval. True when load curtailment or demand-side management programs were in effect.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222 - Participation of Distributed Energy Resource Aggregations

attributes.name: der_penetration_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total load served by Distributed Energy Resources at the measurement point during the interval. Used for DER impact analysis and hosting capacity studies.

attributes.name: energy_delivered_kwh
attributes.description: Total energy delivered in kilowatt-hours during the measurement interval. Represents the integrated real power over the interval duration.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for the Measurement of Electric Power Quantities

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used to estimate or interpolate missing or suspect load data. Describes the algorithm or business rule applied when actual measurements were unavailable.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: gis_feature_code
attributes.description: External identifier linking the load profile to the corresponding feature in the ESRI ArcGIS network topology. Enables spatial analysis and map visualization.

attributes.name: hosting_capacity_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this load profile record is used for Distributed Energy Resource (DER) hosting capacity analysis. True when the data supports feeder-level solar or storage impact modeling.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the measurement point in decimal degrees. Used for spatial analysis, weather correlation, and GIS integration.

attributes.name: load_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of average load to peak load during the measurement interval. Indicates the consistency of load demand. Values range from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating more consistent load.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the measurement point in decimal degrees. Used for spatial analysis, weather correlation, and GIS integration.

attributes.name: measurement_interval_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values are 15, 30, or 60 minutes for distribution load profiling and capacity analysis.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: measurement_point_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the measurement point in the distribution network. Used for operational identification and reporting.

attributes.name: measurement_point_type
attributes.description: Type of distribution network measurement point where load data was captured. Indicates the level of aggregation in the distribution hierarchy.

attributes.name: measurement_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the load measurement interval ended. Represents the real-world event time for the aggregated load reading from SCADA or AMI systems.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum instantaneous real power demand in kilowatts observed during the measurement interval. Used for capacity planning and hosting capacity studies.

attributes.name: planning_area_code
attributes.description: Distribution planning area or zone code where the measurement point is located. Used for capacity planning, load forecasting, and capital investment prioritization.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: power_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of real power to apparent power during the measurement interval. Indicates the efficiency of power utilization at the measurement point. Values range from 0 to 1.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for the Measurement of Electric Power Quantities

attributes.name: reactive_power_kvar
attributes.description: Average reactive power in kilovolt-amperes reactive during the measurement interval. Used for voltage regulation and power factor analysis.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for the Measurement of Electric Power Quantities

attributes.name: real_power_kw
attributes.description: Average real power demand in kilowatts during the measurement interval. Represents the actual power consumed or delivered at the measurement point.
attributes.references: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for the Measurement of Electric Power Quantities

attributes.name: scada_point_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: External identifier for the SCADA telemetry point in the OSIsoft PI or GE Proficy historian system. Links to the source SCADA tag for traceability.

attributes.name: service_territory_state
attributes.description: Two-letter state code for the service territory where the measurement point is located. Used for regulatory reporting and jurisdictional analysis.
attributes.references: NARUC - National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners Guidelines

attributes.name: temperature_adjusted_demand_kw
attributes.description: Real power demand normalized for ambient temperature variations. Used for weather-normalized load forecasting and capacity planning to remove seasonal temperature effects.
attributes.references: NERC Standard MOD-032 - Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this load profile record was last modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Audit timestamp for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: utility_identifier
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the utility company operating the measurement point. Used for multi-utility environments and regulatory reporting to FERC and state PUCs.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 - Annual Report of Major Electric Utilities

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts at the measurement point. Indicates the distribution voltage class for the load profile data.

products.name: demand_response_event
products.description: Transactional record for demand response (DR) and load management curtailment events dispatched through the distribution network — peak shaving, direct load control, and DSM program activations targeting distribution-connected load. Captures DR event ID, event type (peak shaving/direct load control/voluntary curtailment/CPP activation), program name, triggering condition (system peak/grid emergency/price signal), event start timestamp, event end timestamp, target feeder or zone, target load reduction (kW), actual load reduction achieved (kW), number of customers notified, number of customers responding, curtailment compliance rate, and event outcome status. Scoped to the distribution-network dispatch and measurement perspective — DR program enrollment and customer participation records are owned by the customer domain; wholesale market DR bidding is owned by the market domain. Sourced from DERMS and Oracle CC&B/SAP IS-U DR program modules.
products.reference: FERC Order 2222 / NERC / DSM Program Management

attributes.name: demand_response_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the demand response event record. Primary key for the demand response event entity.

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder or circuit targeted by this demand response event, linking to the distribution network topology.

attributes.name: opex_transaction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.opex_transaction. Business justification: Demand response events generate incentive payment transactions to participating customers. Essential for DR program cost tracking, regulatory reporting, and cost recovery mechanisms.

attributes.name: actual_load_reduction_kw
attributes.description: Measured load reduction in kilowatts achieved during the demand response event, calculated from baseline load comparison using Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) or Meter Data Management System (MDMS) interval data.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, NERC DADS, NAESB WEQ-012 Baseline Standards

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: Ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of the demand response event, captured from weather station data to correlate load reduction performance with thermal conditions.

attributes.name: baseline_load_kw
attributes.description: Calculated baseline load in kilowatts representing the expected load absent the demand response event, used as the reference for measuring actual load reduction. Typically calculated using customer baseline load (CBL) methodologies per NAESB standards.
attributes.references: NAESB WEQ-012 Baseline Standards, FERC Order 745

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this demand response event record was first created in the source system, used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: curtailment_compliance_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of notified customers who responded to the demand response event, calculated as (customers_responding_count / customers_notified_count) * 100, used to measure program engagement and effectiveness.

attributes.name: customers_notified_count
attributes.description: Total number of customers or service points notified of the demand response event through automated messaging, mobile app alerts, or direct load control signals.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222, State PUC Consumer Protection Rules

attributes.name: customers_responding_count
attributes.description: Number of customers or service points that actively participated in the demand response event by reducing load, either through voluntary curtailment or direct load control device activation.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system that originated this demand response event record, typically Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS), Customer Information System (CIS) DR module, or Meter Data Management System (MDMS).

attributes.name: derms_integrated_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) Integrated Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether this demand response event was dispatched and managed through the utility's Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) platform, enabling automated control and telemetry.

attributes.name: dispatch_source
attributes.description: System or mechanism that initiated the demand response event dispatch: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS), Distribution Management System (DMS), Outage Management System (OMS), manual operator dispatch, automated schedule, or market signal from Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO).

attributes.name: event_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the demand response event in minutes, calculated from event start to event end timestamp.

attributes.name: event_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the demand response event curtailment period concluded, marking the end of load reduction dispatch and return to normal operations.

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique identifier or reference number for the demand response event, used for external communication and reporting.

attributes.name: event_outcome_status
attributes.description: Assessment of the demand response event outcome relative to target objectives: target met (achieved 90-110% of target), target exceeded (>110% of target), target missed (<90% of target), partial success (50-90% of target), or no response (minimal or no measurable load reduction).

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the demand response event curtailment period began, marking the start of load reduction dispatch.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the demand response event: scheduled (pending activation), active (currently dispatched), completed (event concluded successfully), cancelled (event aborted before or during execution), or failed (event did not achieve operational objectives).

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the demand response event by operational mechanism: peak shaving (load reduction during system peak), direct load control (utility-controlled device curtailment), voluntary curtailment (customer opt-in reduction), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) activation (price-signal driven), emergency DR (grid emergency response), or economic DR (market-driven dispatch).
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, NERC Demand Response Availability Data System (DADS)

attributes.name: incentive_payment_amount

attributes.name: lmp_price_per_mwh

attributes.name: load_reduction_percentage

attributes.name: nerc_reportable_flag

attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) denoting whether this demand response event meets North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) reporting thresholds for Demand Response Availability Data System (DADS) or other reliability reporting requirements.

attributes.name: notification_lead_time_minutes
attributes.description: Number of minutes between customer notification and event start timestamp, representing the advance notice provided to participants.

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: Primary communication channel used to notify customers of the demand response event: Short Message Service (SMS), email, mobile application push notification, Interactive Voice Response (IVR) call, direct control signal to smart devices, or web portal alert.

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: Penalty amount in US dollars assessed for non-compliance or failure to meet contracted demand response obligations, applicable to capacity-based or firm DR programs.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, State PUC Tariff Schedules

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Name of the demand response or demand-side management program under which this event was dispatched, linking to the utility's portfolio of DR offerings.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222, State PUC DSM Program Guidelines

attributes.name: puc_reporting_status
attributes.description: Status of regulatory reporting submission to the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) for this demand response event, used for demand-side management program compliance and cost recovery filings.
attributes.references: State PUC Reporting Requirements, NARUC DSM Guidelines

attributes.name: puc_submission_date
attributes.description: Date when demand response event data was submitted to the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) as part of demand-side management program reporting or rate case cost recovery documentation.

attributes.name: rto_iso_event_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Event ID
attributes.description: External event identifier from the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) if this demand response event was dispatched in coordination with wholesale market operations or grid emergency procedures.

attributes.name: system_peak_load_mw
attributes.description: Total system peak load in megawatts at the time of the demand response event, providing context for the event's contribution to peak shaving and grid reliability.

attributes.name: target_load_reduction_kw

attributes.name: target_zone_code

attributes.name: triggering_condition
attributes.description: The operational or market condition that initiated the demand response event: system peak (forecasted or actual peak load), grid emergency (reliability threat), price signal (high Locational Marginal Price or CPP threshold), capacity shortage (insufficient generation reserves), voltage deviation (distribution voltage issue), or scheduled test (program validation exercise).

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Description of prevailing weather conditions during the demand response event (e.g., extreme heat, cold snap, high humidity), used for event performance analysis and forecasting model refinement.

products.name: gas_service_lateral

products.name: der_dispatch
products.description: This association product represents the operational dispatch of Distributed Energy Resources (DER) in response to demand response events. It captures the participation of individual DER interconnections in specific DR events, including dispatch instructions, actual response performance, compliance measurement, and incentive settlement. Each record links one DER interconnection to one demand response event with attributes that exist only in the context of this dispatch relationship — response capacity committed, actual load reduction delivered, baseline calculation, compliance status, and financial settlement. This is the SSOT for DERMS dispatch operations and DR program settlement.. Existence Justification: In utility DERMS operations, a single DER interconnection (rooftop solar, battery storage, EV charger) participates in multiple demand response events over time — each summer peak event, grid emergency, or price-responsive curtailment dispatches the same DER asset. Conversely, a single demand response event dispatches hundreds or thousands of DER assets simultaneously across a feeder or zone. The business actively manages each dispatch as an operational transaction with performance measurement, compliance tracking, and financial settlement.
products.reference: Internal - M:N Association

attributes.name: demand_response_event_id

attributes.name: communication_status

attributes.name: compliance_flag

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this DER dispatch record was created in the DERMS or DR management system.

attributes.name: dispatch_instruction
attributes.description: Operational instruction sent to this DER asset for this event (e.g., curtail to 50% capacity, discharge battery at 5kW, disable EV charging). Captures asset-specific dispatch commands from DERMS.

attributes.name: dispatch_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the dispatch instruction was sent to this specific DER asset for this demand response event. May differ from event start time due to staggered dispatch or asset-specific lead times. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: incentive_earned

Calculated based on response_kw, compliance_flag, and program tariff rates. Used for DR program settlement. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: opt_out_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the customer or DER asset operator exercised an opt-out right for this specific demand response event. Affects compliance assessment and incentive calculation. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: participation_status
attributes.description: Current status of this DER asset's participation in the demand response event. Tracks lifecycle from dispatch through completion and compliance assessment. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: response_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Actual duration in minutes that this DER asset actively responded to the demand response event. May differ from overall event duration if the asset was dispatched late, released early, or experienced operational issues. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: response_kw
attributes.description: Actual load reduction or curtailment capacity delivered by this DER asset during the demand response event, measured in kilowatts. This is the measured performance specific to this DER-event combination. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this DER dispatch record was last updated, typically after performance measurement and compliance assessment.

products.name: service_point_dr_participation
products.description: This association product represents the operational participation record between a service point and a demand response event. It captures the enrollment status, notification delivery, customer response behavior, load curtailment performance, and incentive settlement for each service point's participation in each DR event. Each record links one service point to one demand response event with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific participation instance — including notification timestamps, baseline load calculations, actual curtailment achieved, compliance status, and earned incentives. This is the operational SSOT for DR program dispatch, customer response measurement, and settlement processing.. Existence Justification: In utility demand response operations, a service point (customer premise) can participate in multiple DR events over time, and each DR event dispatches to multiple service points simultaneously. The business actively manages each participation instance as an operational record — tracking notification delivery, measuring load curtailment performance against baseline, assessing compliance, and calculating incentive payments. This is not an analytical correlation; it is the operational transaction record for DR dispatch and settlement.

attributes.name: demand_response_event_id

attributes.name: service_point_id

attributes.description: Calculated baseline load in kilowatts for this specific service point during the event window, representing expected load absent the DR event. Used to measure curtailment performance. Sourced from detection phase relationship_data.

attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this service point met the contractual curtailment obligation for this event. Determines incentive payment eligibility and potential penalties. Sourced from detection phase relationship_data.

attributes.name: curtailment_percentage

attributes.name: incentive_earned

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: Communication channel used to notify this specific service point (customer) of the DR event. May vary by customer preference or program type. Sourced from detection phase relationship_data.

attributes.name: notification_sent_timestamp

attributes.name: opt_out_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the customer at this service point exercised their opt-out right for this specific event (if program allows per-event opt-out). Affects compliance assessment and incentive calculation. Sourced from detection phase relationship_data.

attributes.name: participation_status
attributes.description: Outcome status of this service point's participation in this DR event. Distinguishes between active response, non-response, opt-out, and technical issues (e.g., AMI communication failure).

attributes.name: response_kw

attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation of the bus, typically reflecting its location, substation, or functional role in the distribution network.

attributes.name: bus_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the bus used in operational systems, network diagrams, and engineering documentation. Serves as the business key for cross-system reference.

attributes.name: bus_type
attributes.description: Classification of the bus based on its electrical function in the power system. Slack bus maintains system voltage and frequency reference; generator bus has active power generation; load bus serves consumption; isolated bus is disconnected.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bus record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: criticality_rating
attributes.description: Business criticality classification of the bus based on number of customers served, load importance, and system redundancy. Drives prioritization for maintenance and restoration.

attributes.name: der_interconnection_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether distributed energy resources such as solar photovoltaic, wind, or battery storage are interconnected at this bus. Critical for DER management and grid stability analysis.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Free-text description providing additional context about the bus, including special operating conditions, historical notes, or engineering remarks.

attributes.name: energized_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the bus is currently energized with voltage. True means the bus has voltage applied; false means it is de-energized for maintenance or due to outage.

attributes.name: grounding_type
attributes.description: Method of neutral grounding at the bus. Critical for fault current calculations, protective relay coordination, and personnel safety.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date when the bus was originally installed and commissioned in the distribution network. Used for asset age analysis and replacement planning.

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent physical or electrical inspection of the bus. Critical for compliance with maintenance schedules and safety regulations.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the bus location in decimal degrees. Enables GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and proximity-based outage correlation.

attributes.name: load_serving_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this bus directly serves customer load. True for buses with connected customers; false for transmission or interconnection buses.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the bus location in decimal degrees. Enables GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and proximity-based outage correlation.

attributes.name: max_voltage_limit_pu
attributes.description: Upper voltage limit for the bus in per-unit. Violations trigger voltage regulation actions or alarms in distribution management systems.

attributes.name: min_voltage_limit_pu
attributes.description: Lower voltage limit for the bus in per-unit. Violations trigger voltage regulation actions or alarms in distribution management systems.

attributes.name: next_maintenance_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the next preventive maintenance activity on the bus. Supports work order scheduling and asset lifecycle management.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the bus in the distribution network. Determines whether the bus is actively participating in power flow calculations and operational dispatch.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Classification of bus ownership. Determines maintenance responsibility, cost allocation, and regulatory jurisdiction.

attributes.name: phase_configuration
attributes.description: Electrical phase configuration of the bus. Determines load balancing requirements and equipment compatibility.

attributes.name: reactive_power_mvar
attributes.description: Net reactive power injection or withdrawal at the bus in megavolt-amperes reactive. Critical for voltage control and power factor management.

attributes.name: scada_monitored_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this bus is monitored by the SCADA system for real-time voltage, power flow, and status telemetry. Essential for distribution management system operations.

attributes.name: short_circuit_mva
attributes.description: Three-phase short circuit capacity at the bus in megavolt-amperes. Critical for protective device coordination, equipment ratings, and safety analysis.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bus record was last modified. Enables change tracking and data synchronization across systems.

attributes.name: voltage_angle_degrees
attributes.description: Phase angle of the bus voltage relative to the system reference bus, expressed in degrees. Critical for power flow calculations and system stability analysis.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal operating voltage level of the bus expressed in kilovolts. Critical for equipment compatibility, safety clearances, and network topology analysis.

attributes.name: voltage_magnitude_pu
attributes.description: Current voltage magnitude at the bus expressed in per-unit of base voltage. Used for voltage regulation monitoring and power flow analysis. Typically ranges from 0.95 to 1.05 pu under normal conditions.

attributes.name: x_r_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of reactance to resistance at the bus, used for short circuit analysis and protective relay settings. Higher ratios indicate more inductive systems.

attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on bus (source_bus_id)
