attributes.name: interaction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interaction purpose. Indicates the primary reason for customer contact or engagement.
attributes.references: Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud Activity Type

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code indicating the language used during the interaction. Supports multilingual customer service tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this interaction record was last updated in the source system. Supports change data capture and incremental load processing.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and comments captured by the agent during or after the interaction. Contains detailed context and customer statements.
attributes.references: Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud Case Comments

attributes.name: nps_score
attributes.description: Net Promoter Score provided by the customer, typically on a scale of 0-10. Measures customer loyalty and likelihood to recommend. Null if not collected.

attributes.name: payment_arrangement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a payment plan or arrangement was established during this interaction. Used for collections and customer assistance program tracking.
attributes.references: CIS (Customer Information System) Payment Arrangement Standard

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Priority classification assigned to the interaction based on urgency and impact. Drives case routing and SLA (Service Level Agreement) targets.
attributes.references: Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud Case Priority

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this interaction must be included in regulatory customer service reports submitted to the PUC (Public Utility Commission). Typically true for complaints and service quality issues.
attributes.references: State PUC (Public Utility Commission) Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: resolution_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating how the interaction was resolved. Used for first-call resolution metrics and quality tracking.
attributes.references: Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud Resolution Taxonomy

attributes.name: resolution_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the resolution or outcome of the interaction. Captures agent notes and actions taken.

attributes.name: service_order_number
attributes.description: Reference number of any field service order or work order created as a result of this interaction. Null if no service order was generated.

attributes.name: sla_met_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interaction was resolved within the target SLA (Service Level Agreement) timeframe. Used for customer service performance reporting.

attributes.name: sla_target_resolution_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Service Level Agreement (SLA) Target Resolution Hours
attributes.description: Target number of hours within which this interaction type and priority should be resolved, per internal SLA (Service Level Agreement) standards.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system that originated this interaction record. Typically Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud, IVR (Interactive Voice Response) system, or web portal.

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the customer interaction began. Represents the moment the customer initiated contact or the utility initiated outreach.

attributes.name: survey_response_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer completed a post-interaction survey. Used to track survey response rates.

products.name: segment
products.description: Customer segmentation classification record assigning a party or account to one or more business-defined segments for targeting, rate design analysis, and program eligibility determination. Segment dimensions include rate class (residential, small commercial, large commercial, industrial), load profile group, income tier (CARE-eligible, FERA-eligible, standard), customer value tier, DER adoption flags (solar, battery storage, EV), demand response eligibility tier, AMI smart meter deployment cohort, and life-support/medical baseline flag. Segment assignments are versioned with effective and expiration dates to support historical trend analysis and regulatory rate case testimony. Used by regulatory affairs for rate case cost-of-service studies, by DSM teams for program targeting, and by load forecasting for IRP class-level projections.
products.reference: CIS Customer Class / Salesforce Account Segment

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the customer segmentation classification record.

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer party being segmented. Links to the customer master record.

attributes.name: ami_deployment_cohort
attributes.description: AMI smart meter deployment wave or cohort identifier indicating when the customer received AMI meter installation. Used for AMI deployment tracking, interval data availability determination, and time-of-use rate migration planning. Examples: WAVE-1-2018, WAVE-2-2019, LEGACY-AMR (not yet upgraded to AMI).
attributes.references: AMI Deployment Plan, MDMS Data Availability Rules

attributes.name: annual_consumption_kwh
attributes.description: Trailing twelve-month total electric energy consumption in kilowatt-hours at the time of segment assignment. Used for load profile group classification, customer value tier determination, and rate case cost-of-service allocation. Nullable for new customers without consumption history.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts, Load Research Methodology

attributes.name: assignment_reason
attributes.description: The business reason or trigger for this segment classification assignment. Initial enrollment occurs at customer onboarding. Rate change reflects tariff modification. Program enrollment occurs when customer joins income assistance or DER program. Annual review reflects periodic re-certification. Customer request reflects customer-initiated rate or program change. System migration reflects data conversion. Regulatory mandate reflects PUC-ordered reclassification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: initial_enrollment|rate_change|program_enrollment|annual_review|customer_request|system_migration|regulatory_mandate — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: assignment_source
attributes.description: The system or process that originated this segment classification. CIS system assignments come from Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U customer master. CRM system assignments come from Salesforce campaign or program enrollment. Manual override reflects analyst or customer service representative adjustment. Third party verification reflects income verification service for CARE/FERA. Regulatory filing reflects PUC rate case assignment. AMI analytics reflects MDMS load profile analysis.

attributes.name: battery_storage_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has an interconnected battery energy storage system. True if customer has active battery storage interconnection agreement. Used for demand response program eligibility, grid services procurement, and DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System) enrollment.
attributes.references: Energy Storage Interconnection Standards, FERC Order 841 Storage Participation Rules

attributes.name: cpp_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer is eligible for Critical Peak Pricing program enrollment. True if customer meets minimum demand threshold and has AMI meter with interval data capability. CPP programs charge higher rates during system peak events (typically 10-15 days per year) to incentivize load reduction.
attributes.references: Critical Peak Pricing Tariff, Demand-Side Management Program Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this segment classification record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: customer_value_tier
attributes.description: Customer lifetime value segmentation tier for retention and engagement strategies. High-value customers have high consumption, low payment risk, and long tenure. Medium-value customers have moderate consumption and stable payment history. Low-value customers have low consumption or short tenure. At-risk customers show indicators of potential churn or payment default.

attributes.name: demand_response_tier
attributes.description: Demand response program eligibility tier based on load flexibility, historical participation, and curtailment capability. Tier 1 customers have high curtailment capability (>50 kW) and reliable participation history. Tier 2 customers have moderate capability (10-50 kW). Tier 3 customers have low capability (<10 kW) or are residential participants. Not eligible customers do not meet minimum requirements for DR program participation.
attributes.references: Demand Response Program Rules, FERC Order 745 Demand Response Compensation

attributes.name: der_adoption_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has adopted any Distributed Energy Resource (DER) technology including solar photovoltaic, battery energy storage, electric vehicle, or combined heat and power (CHP). True if customer has one or more DER assets interconnected or registered. Used for DER program targeting, grid planning, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222 DER Aggregation Rules, State Interconnection Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date when this segment classification becomes effective and active for the customer. Used for historical trend analysis, rate case cost-of-service studies, and program eligibility determination. Segment assignments are versioned to support point-in-time queries.

attributes.name: ev_owner_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer owns or leases an electric vehicle and is enrolled in an EV-specific rate or program. True if customer has registered EV ownership or is on EV time-of-use rate. Used for EV program targeting, managed charging programs, and transportation electrification planning.
attributes.references: Transportation Electrification Framework, EV Rate Design Guidelines

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date when this segment classification expires or is superseded by a new assignment. Nullable for currently active segments with no planned expiration. Used for historical trend analysis and regulatory rate case testimony showing customer migration between segments over time.

attributes.name: income_tier
attributes.description: Income-based program eligibility tier for low-income assistance programs. CARE (California Alternate Rates for Energy) provides 30-35% discount for households at or below 200% of federal poverty level. FERA (Family Electric Rate Assistance) provides 18% discount for households between 200-250% of federal poverty level. Medical baseline provides additional allowance for customers with qualifying medical equipment. Standard tier receives no income-based discount.
attributes.references: PUC Low-Income Assistance Program Rules, CARE and FERA Program Guidelines

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this segment classification record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and incremental data processing.

attributes.name: life_support_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has registered life-support or medical baseline equipment that requires continuous electric service. True if customer has active medical baseline certification. Used for outage prioritization, planned outage notification requirements, and medical baseline rate allowance application.
attributes.references: PUC Medical Baseline Program Rules, Life Support Customer Protection Standards

attributes.name: load_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of average load to peak load over the trailing twelve months, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. High load factor (>0.7) indicates consistent baseload consumption typical of industrial customers. Low load factor (<0.4) indicates peaky consumption typical of commercial customers. Used for load profile group classification and rate design analysis.
attributes.references: Load Research Methodology, IRP Load Forecasting Standards

attributes.name: load_profile_group
attributes.description: Load profile classification grouping customers by consumption pattern for load forecasting and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) projections. Examples: RES-STANDARD (standard residential), RES-HIGH-USE (high-consumption residential), COMM-RETAIL (retail commercial), COMM-OFFICE (office commercial), IND-CONTINUOUS (24/7 industrial), IND-SHIFT (shift-based industrial).
attributes.references: IRP Load Forecasting Methodology, NERC Load Modeling Standards

attributes.name: peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum 15-minute interval demand in kilowatts during the trailing twelve months at the time of segment assignment. Used for rate class determination (small vs large commercial threshold), demand response tier assignment, and capacity cost allocation. Nullable for residential customers without demand metering.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts, Demand Metering Standards

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Numeric priority ranking when a customer has multiple concurrent segment classifications. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used to determine which segment takes precedence for rate application when multiple segments conflict. For example, CARE income tier (priority 1) overrides standard rate class (priority 5) for billing purposes.

attributes.name: program_enrollment_date
attributes.description: The date when the customer enrolled in the program or rate associated with this segment classification. Applicable for income assistance programs (CARE, FERA), demand response programs, time-of-use rates, and DER programs. Nullable for non-program segments such as standard rate class assignments.

attributes.name: rate_class
attributes.description: Primary rate class classification for tariff application and cost-of-service allocation. Residential serves single-family and multi-family dwellings. Small commercial serves businesses under demand threshold (typically <50 kW). Large commercial serves businesses above demand threshold. Industrial serves manufacturing and heavy industry. Agricultural serves farms and irrigation. Street lighting serves municipal and private lighting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Class Definitions, PUC Rate Case Guidelines

attributes.name: recertification_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the customer must recertify eligibility for this segment classification. Required for income-based programs (CARE, FERA) which mandate annual or biennial recertification. Nullable for segments that do not require periodic recertification.
attributes.references: PUC Low-Income Assistance Program Recertification Rules

attributes.name: segment_code
attributes.description: The specific segment classification code assigned to this party or account within the segment type. Examples: RES (residential), COMM-SM (small commercial), IND-LG (large industrial), CARE (California Alternate Rates for Energy), FERA (Family Electric Rate Assistance), SOLAR-NEM (Net Energy Metering solar customer), EV-OWNER (electric vehicle owner), DR-TIER1 (demand response tier 1 eligible).
attributes.references: Utility Rate Schedule, PUC Customer Class Definitions

attributes.name: segment_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the segment classification criteria, business rules for assignment, and intended use cases. Supports regulatory rate case testimony and program design documentation.

attributes.name: segment_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the segment classification for reporting and analytics. Examples: Residential Customer, Small Commercial, Large Industrial, CARE-Eligible Low Income, High-Value Customer, Solar NEM Customer, EV Owner, Demand Response Participant.

attributes.name: segment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this segment classification record. Active segments are currently in effect. Pending segments are scheduled for future effective date. Expired segments have passed their expiration date. Superseded segments have been replaced by a newer assignment. Cancelled segments were voided before becoming effective.

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: The dimension or category of segmentation being applied. Rate class segments customers by tariff eligibility (residential, commercial, industrial). Load profile groups customers by consumption pattern. Income tier identifies program eligibility (CARE, FERA). Customer value tiers support retention strategies. DER adoption flags solar, battery, EV ownership. Demand response eligibility determines DR program participation.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts, PUC Rate Design Guidelines

attributes.name: solar_customer_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has an interconnected solar photovoltaic system under Net Energy Metering (NEM) or other solar tariff. True if customer has active solar interconnection agreement. Used for NEM billing, RPS compliance tracking, and distributed generation forecasting.
attributes.references: Net Energy Metering Tariff, FERC Small Generator Interconnection Procedures

attributes.name: tou_rate_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer is eligible for time-of-use rate enrollment based on AMI meter availability and rate class. True if customer has AMI meter and rate class supports TOU tariff. Used for TOU rate migration campaigns and dynamic pricing program targeting.
attributes.references: Time-of-Use Rate Tariff, PUC Default TOU Transition Rules

products.name: account_hierarchy
products.description: Hierarchical relationship structure linking parent and child accounts for commercial and industrial customers with complex organizational structures — including multi-site enterprises, property management companies, municipal accounts, and master-metered MDU (multi-dwelling unit) complexes. Stores parent account ID, child account ID, hierarchy type (consolidated billing, master-metered, corporate umbrella), hierarchy level, effective date, and end date. Enables consolidated billing statements, enterprise-level usage reporting, and key account management workflows in Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud. Supports large commercial and industrial (C&I) account management and PUC reporting on large customer classes.
products.reference: CC&B Account Hierarchy / Salesforce Account Hierarchy

attributes.name: account_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the account hierarchy relationship record. Primary key for the account hierarchy entity.

attributes.name: child_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the child account in the hierarchy. Represents the subordinate account whose billing and usage data may be aggregated to the parent account. Used for multi-site enterprises, individual units in master-metered buildings, and departmental accounts within large commercial and industrial (C&I) customers.

attributes.name: parent_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent account in the hierarchy. For consolidated billing structures, this represents the master account that aggregates billing and usage from child accounts. Used in corporate umbrella structures, property management companies, and master-metered multi-dwelling unit (MDU) complexes.

attributes.name: allocation_method
attributes.description: Method used to allocate charges or usage from parent to child accounts in master-metered or shared service scenarios. Proportional allocates based on square footage or unit count. Fixed percentage uses predefined allocation percentages. Equal split divides evenly among child accounts. Custom uses business-rule-driven allocation logic. None indicates no allocation is performed. Common in multi-dwelling unit (MDU) complexes and shared facility arrangements.

attributes.name: allocation_percentage
attributes.description: Fixed percentage used to allocate charges or usage from parent to child account when allocation method is fixed percentage. Value between 0.00 and 100.00. Sum of allocation percentages across all child accounts under a parent should equal 100.00. Used in master-metered multi-dwelling unit (MDU) billing and shared facility cost allocation.

attributes.name: billing_aggregation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether billing amounts from the child account are aggregated into the parent account invoice. True enables consolidated billing statements for multi-site enterprises and property management companies. False maintains separate billing while preserving the hierarchical relationship for reporting purposes. Integrates with Oracle CC&B billing engine and Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud for key account management.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the account hierarchy relationship record was first created in the Customer Information System (CIS). Supports audit trail requirements for regulatory compliance and internal controls under Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). Integrates with Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U audit logging.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the account hierarchy relationship becomes active and billing aggregation or reporting begins. Used for move-in/move-out processing, corporate restructuring, and property management transitions. Supports regulatory reporting requirements for customer-of-record tracking to Public Utility Commission (PUC).

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when the account hierarchy relationship terminates. Null for open-ended relationships. Used for move-out processing, corporate restructuring, property management transitions, and account closure workflows. Supports historical analysis of customer account structures and regulatory reporting to Public Utility Commission (PUC).

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of the account in the hierarchy tree structure. Level 1 represents the top-level parent account. Each subsequent level increments by 1. Supports multi-tier organizational structures common in large commercial and industrial (C&I) customers with regional, divisional, and site-level accounts.

attributes.name: hierarchy_type
attributes.description: Classification of the account hierarchy relationship. Consolidated billing aggregates multiple accounts into a single invoice. Master-metered applies to multi-dwelling unit (MDU) complexes where a single meter serves multiple units. Corporate umbrella links accounts under a single enterprise entity. Property management groups accounts managed by a property management company. Municipal account represents government entity hierarchies. Franchise represents utility franchise relationships.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the account hierarchy relationship record was most recently updated. Tracks changes to hierarchy type, effective dates, allocation methods, or status transitions. Supports audit trail requirements for regulatory compliance and internal controls under Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional information about the account hierarchy relationship. May include business justification, special billing instructions, regulatory requirements, or historical context. Used by customer service representatives (CSR) and key account managers for reference during customer interactions and billing dispute resolution.

attributes.name: priority_sequence
attributes.description: Numeric ordering used to determine processing sequence when multiple hierarchy relationships exist for the same account. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used in complex organizational structures where an account may participate in multiple hierarchies (e.g., both a corporate umbrella and a property management relationship). Ensures deterministic billing and reporting behavior.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B Account Hierarchy Processing Rules

attributes.name: relationship_owner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the business user or key account manager responsible for managing this account hierarchy relationship. Used for customer relationship management (CRM) workflows in Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud. Supports large commercial and industrial (C&I) account management and enterprise customer service delivery.
attributes.references: Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud Account Management

attributes.name: relationship_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the account hierarchy relationship. Active indicates the relationship is currently in effect and billing aggregation or reporting is operational. Inactive indicates the relationship has been deactivated but not removed. Pending indicates the relationship is awaiting approval or activation. Suspended indicates temporary hold. Terminated indicates the relationship has been permanently ended.
attributes.references: Oracle CC&B Account Hierarchy Status Model

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record that originated this account hierarchy relationship. CC&B represents Oracle Customer Care and Billing. IS-U represents SAP Industry Solution for Utilities. CRM represents Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud. MDM represents Master Data Management system. MANUAL represents manually entered relationships. Supports data lineage tracking and reconciliation across enterprise systems.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of this account hierarchy relationship in the source operational system. Used for data lineage tracking, reconciliation, and bidirectional synchronization between the lakehouse and operational systems (Oracle CC&B, SAP IS-U, Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud). Supports troubleshooting and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: usage_aggregation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether energy usage (kilowatt-hour (kWh) or thousand cubic feet (MCF) of gas) from the child account is aggregated into parent account usage reporting. True enables enterprise-level usage analysis for large commercial and industrial (C&I) customers. False maintains separate usage tracking. Supports demand response (DR) program enrollment, energy efficiency (EE) program participation, and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance reporting.

products.name: preference
products.description: Customer communication and service preference record capturing opt-in/opt-out settings and notification channel choices at the party or account level. Stores preference category (outage alert, demand response event notification, planned outage notification, billing statement ready, payment confirmation, payment reminder, marketing communication), preferred delivery channel (email, SMS, push notification, mail, IVR), preferred language, preferred contact time window, and preference effective/expiration dates. Does NOT track program enrollments (see enrollment product) or legally binding consents (see consent product). Sourced from Salesforce Energy & Utilities Cloud and CC&B notification preferences. Supports TCPA compliance for automated contact channel selection and CAN-SPAM opt-out requirements.
products.reference: Salesforce Preference / CC&B Notification Preference

attributes.name: preference_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the customer preference record. Primary key.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific customer account this preference applies to. Nullable if preference is set at party level rather than account level.

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer party who owns this preference. Links to the party master entity.

attributes.name: contact_frequency_limit
attributes.description: The maximum frequency at which the customer wishes to receive communications for this preference category. Helps manage communication fatigue and supports customer experience optimization.
attributes.references: CAN-SPAM Act, TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act)

attributes.name: contact_time_window_end
attributes.description: The latest time of day (HH:MM format, 24-hour clock) the customer is willing to receive non-emergency communications. Used for outbound call scheduling and SMS delivery timing to comply with TCPA restrictions on contact hours.

attributes.name: contact_time_window_start
attributes.description: The earliest time of day (HH:MM format, 24-hour clock) the customer is willing to receive non-emergency communications. Used for outbound call scheduling and SMS delivery timing to comply with TCPA restrictions on contact hours.

attributes.name: delivery_channel
attributes.description: The preferred communication channel through which the customer wishes to receive notifications for this preference category. Supports multi-channel customer engagement strategy.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this preference setting expires or is superseded. Nullable for open-ended preferences. Supports time-bound promotional opt-ins and preference lifecycle management.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this preference setting becomes active and should be honored by communication systems. Supports scheduled preference changes and regulatory compliance with opt-out request timing requirements.

attributes.name: external_preference_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier for this preference record in the source system (CC&B, Salesforce, SAP IS-U). Supports cross-system reconciliation and bidirectional synchronization.

attributes.name: is_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contact information associated with this preference has been verified through a confirmation process (e.g., double opt-in for email, SMS confirmation code). Critical for TCPA compliance and reducing communication delivery failures.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The user ID or system identifier that last modified this preference record. Supports audit trail and accountability for preference changes.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this preference record was last updated. Supports change tracking and regulatory compliance audit requirements.

attributes.name: mobile_device_token
attributes.description: The push notification device token for mobile app notifications. Used by mobile notification services (APNS, FCM) to deliver push notifications to the customers registered mobile device.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context or special instructions related to this preference. Supports customer service representatives in understanding unique customer communication requirements.

attributes.name: notification_email
attributes.description: The specific email address to use for this preference category if email is the selected delivery channel. May differ from the primary account email. Supports multi-email management for different communication types.

attributes.name: notification_phone
attributes.description: The specific phone number to use for this preference category if SMS or IVR is the selected delivery channel. May differ from the primary account phone. Supports multi-phone management for different communication types. Format follows E.164 international standard.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), ITU-T E.164

attributes.name: opt_in_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has opted in or out of receiving communications for this preference category and channel combination. Critical for TCPA and CAN-SPAM compliance.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act, GDPR Article 7

attributes.name: preference_category
attributes.description: The type of communication or service preference being configured. Defines what kind of notification or communication this preference controls. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: outage_alert|demand_response_notification|planned_outage_notification|billing_statement_ready|payment_confirmation|payment_reminder|marketing_communication|service_appointment_reminder|energy_usage_report|rate_change_notification|program_enrollment_confirmation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: preference_source
attributes.description: The channel or system through which this preference was originally captured or set. Supports audit trail and preference data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: preferred_language
attributes.description: The language in which the customer prefers to receive communications. Uses 3-letter ISO 639-2 language codes. Supports multilingual customer base and regulatory requirements for language access. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ENG|SPA|FRA|CHI|VIE|KOR|RUS|ARA|POR|GER — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 639-2, Title VI of the Civil Rights Act

attributes.name: set_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this preference was originally established by the customer or system. Critical for TCPA and CAN-SPAM compliance audit trails demonstrating when consent was obtained.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record from which this preference record originated. Supports data lineage tracking and multi-system integration reconciliation in hybrid CIS environments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CC&B|Salesforce|SAP_IS-U|Customer_Portal|Mobile_App|Call_Center|Legacy_Migration — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: suppression_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this preference is currently suppressed due to delivery failures, compliance holds, or customer service blocks. When true, communications should not be sent regardless of opt-in status.
attributes.references: CAN-SPAM Act, TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act)

attributes.name: suppression_reason
attributes.description: The reason why communications are suppressed for this preference. Supports compliance with do-not-contact regulations and customer service escalation management.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act

attributes.name: suppression_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which communication suppression became effective for this preference. Supports time-bound suppression management and audit trail.

attributes.name: unsubscribe_reason
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing the reason provided by the customer when opting out of a communication preference. Supports customer experience analysis and communication strategy improvement.

attributes.name: verification_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the contact information for this preference was verified. Supports audit trail for double opt-in compliance and contact data quality management.
attributes.references: TCPA (Telephone Consumer Protection Act), CAN-SPAM Act

products.name: credit_deposit
products.description: Transactional record tracking the lifecycle of a customer security deposit — from initial assessment at move-in or credit evaluation through refund or application to final bill. Captures deposit amount, type, status, and associated consent/authorization records.

attributes.name: credit_deposit_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the credit deposit record. Primary key for the credit deposit entity.

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Customer deposits are posted to specific GL liability accounts for balance sheet reporting, regulatory financial statements (FERC Form 1), and deposit liability reconciliation. Required for financial

attributes.name: invoice_id
attributes.description: Reference to the invoice to which the deposit was applied. Links deposit disposition to billing transaction.

attributes.name: journal_entry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Deposit receipt, refund, and forfeiture transactions generate journal entries for financial recording. Required for audit trail, financial transaction reconciliation, and regulatory compliance. Links

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the party (customer) who provided the deposit. Links to the customer master record.

attributes.name: payment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the payment transaction record that funded this deposit. Links deposit to payment processing system.

attributes.name: premise_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service premise associated with this deposit. Links deposit to the physical service location.

attributes.name: primary_credit_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account for which this deposit is held. Links deposit to the billing account in the Customer Information System (CIS).

attributes.name: tertiary_credit_transfer_to_account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the destination account if this deposit was transferred to another customer account.

attributes.name: accrued_interest_amount
attributes.description: Cumulative interest earned on the deposit from the received date through the current date. Calculated per PUC-mandated interest rate and compounding rules.

attributes.name: applied_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the deposit (plus interest) that was applied to customer's outstanding bill balance. May be partial if deposit exceeds final bill amount.

attributes.name: applied_to_bill_date
attributes.description: Date when the deposit was applied to the customer's final bill or outstanding balance. Typically occurs at account closure or service disconnection.

attributes.name: authorization_code
attributes.description: Unique code or reference number for the deposit authorization transaction. Used for payment verification and fraud prevention.

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date when customer consent for deposit collection was obtained. Part of regulatory compliance audit trail.

attributes.name: consent_method

attributes.name: consent_obtained_flag

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: credit_score_at_assessment
attributes.description: Customer's credit score at the time deposit requirement was assessed. Used to determine deposit amount and eligibility for waiver. Confidential business data.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the deposit amount. Typically USD for U.S. utilities.

attributes.name: deposit_amount
attributes.description: Original monetary value of the deposit collected from the customer. Recorded in the utility's functional currency (USD). Subject to interest accrual per regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: deposit_number
attributes.description: Externally visible unique business identifier for the deposit transaction. Used for customer communication and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: deposit_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the business reason why the deposit was required. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and customer service analysis.

attributes.name: deposit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the deposit. Tracks the deposit from initial collection through final disposition (refund or application to account).
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts - Account 235

attributes.name: deposit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the deposit instrument or method used by the customer to provide security. Determines handling and refund procedures.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the deposit becomes active and begins securing the customer account. May differ from received date if deposit is held pending verification.

attributes.name: external_deposit_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this deposit in the source operational system (CIS). Enables cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: forfeiture_date
attributes.description: Date when the deposit was forfeited due to customer default, non-payment, or abandonment of service. Triggers revenue recognition per accounting standards.

attributes.name: forfeiture_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the deposit was forfeited. Required for regulatory reporting and customer dispute resolution.

attributes.name: interest_rate
attributes.description: Annual interest rate applied to the deposit balance as required by state Public Utility Commission regulations. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0200 for 2%).

attributes.name: last_interest_calculation_date
attributes.description: Date when interest was most recently calculated and accrued to the deposit balance. Used for audit trail and regulatory compliance verification.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified this deposit record. Part of change management audit trail.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this deposit record was most recently updated. Tracks all lifecycle changes for audit and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional context, special handling instructions, or customer service notes related to the deposit.

attributes.name: received_date
attributes.description: Date when the utility received and recorded the deposit from the customer. Marks the start of interest accrual and holding period.

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: Total amount refunded to the customer, including original deposit plus accrued interest. Null if deposit has not been refunded.

attributes.name: refund_check_number
attributes.description: Check number if deposit was refunded via paper check. Used for payment reconciliation and audit trail.

attributes.name: refund_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the deposit (plus accrued interest) was refunded to the customer. Null if deposit has not been refunded.

attributes.name: refund_eligibility_date
attributes.description: Date when the customer becomes eligible for deposit refund based on payment history and regulatory holding period requirements (typically 12-24 months of on-time payments).

attributes.name: refund_method
attributes.description: Method used to return the deposit to the customer. Determines processing workflow and reconciliation procedures.

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this deposit transaction must be included in regulatory reports to the Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational system of record that originated this deposit transaction (e.g., Oracle CC&B, SAP IS-U). Used for data lineage and integration troubleshooting.

attributes.name: waiver_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the deposit requirement was waived based on credit evaluation, low-income assistance program, or other qualifying criteria.

attributes.name: waiver_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why deposit was waived. Required for regulatory compliance and internal audit.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that created this deposit record. Required for audit trail and compliance.

domains.name: billing
domains.description: Authoritative source for the full revenue cycle — rate schedule application (TOU, CPP, tiered), invoice generation, payment processing, collections, dispute resolution, and revenue recognition for electric and gas services. Owns charge calculations incorporating FAC, CIAC adjustments, and regulatory riders. Integrates with CIS (Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U) and ERP for GAAP revenue reporting.
domains.references: NARUC Uniform System of Accounts, GAAP ASC 606, PUC

products.name: rate_schedule
products.description: Authoritative master catalog of all tariff rate schedules applicable to electric and gas service — TOU, CPP, tiered residential, commercial demand, and special contract rates. Defines rate code, commodity type (electric/gas), customer class (residential/commercial/industrial), effective and expiration dates, regulatory approval reference, rate structure type, and base rate values per tier/period. References applicable rider_charge records for surcharges layered on top of base rates. Sourced from PUC-approved tariff filings and maintained in Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U rate engine. SSOT for all base rate definitions used in charge calculation. Distinct from rider_charge, which defines regulatory surcharges approved separately from base tariff rates.
products.reference: Tariff Rate Schedule (Oracle CC&B Rate Form / SAP IS-U Rate Category)

attributes.name: rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Primary key for rate_schedule

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id

attributes.name: pricing_node_id

attributes.name: superseded_by_rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the rate schedule that supersedes this one. Nullable if this is the current active version. Used to maintain rate schedule lineage and support customer migration from old to new schedules.

attributes.name: tariff_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.tariff_schedule. This FK formalizes the relationship between operational billing rates and regulatory tariff fili

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date the rate schedule was approved by the governing PUC or FERC. Must precede or match the effective date. Used for regulatory compliance reporting.

attributes.name: base_energy_rate
attributes.description: Base rate per unit of energy consumption (dollars per kWh for electric, dollars per Therm or MCF for gas). Excludes riders, surcharges, and adjustments. Represents the foundational commodity charge before layering FAC and other regulatory adjustments.

attributes.name: commodity_type
attributes.description: Type of utility service this rate schedule applies to: electric, gas, or dual (combined electric and gas).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate schedule record was first created in the system. Represents the audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary values in this rate schedule. Typically USD for U.S. utilities.

attributes.name: customer_charge
attributes.description: Fixed monthly charge per customer account, independent of consumption. Covers meter reading, billing, and customer service costs. Expressed in dollars per month.

attributes.name: customer_class
attributes.description: Customer classification segment this rate schedule applies to. Determines eligibility for the rate and drives cost allocation in rate case studies.

attributes.name: demand_charge_rate
attributes.description: Rate per unit of peak demand (dollars per kW or MW). Applicable to commercial and industrial rate schedules with demand-based pricing. Nullable for residential and other non-demand schedules.

attributes.name: demand_charge_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the demand charge: kW (kilowatt) or MW (megawatt). Applicable only when demand_charge_rate is populated.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this rate schedule becomes active and available for customer enrollment and billing application. Must align with PUC approval date for new or modified tariffs.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: eligibility_criteria
attributes.description: Textual description of customer eligibility requirements for enrollment in this rate schedule. May include minimum/maximum usage thresholds, service type requirements, or geographic restrictions.

attributes.name: energy_rate_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the base energy rate: kWh (kilowatt-hour) or MWh (megawatt-hour) for electric, Therm or MCF (thousand cubic feet) or CCF (hundred cubic feet) for gas.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this rate schedule is no longer available for new enrollments. Nullable for open-ended schedules. Existing customers on expired schedules may be grandfathered until migrated.

attributes.name: interruptible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate schedule is for interruptible service, where the utility may curtail service during peak demand or emergencies in exchange for lower rates. True for interruptible schedules; False for firm service.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 - Open Access Transmission Tariff

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate schedule record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: minimum_charge
attributes.description: Minimum total charge per billing cycle regardless of consumption. Ensures cost recovery for low-usage customers. Nullable if no minimum applies.

attributes.name: net_metering_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether customers on this rate schedule are eligible for Net Energy Metering (NEM) programs, allowing bidirectional energy flow and credit for excess generation from DER (Distributed Energy Resources) such as rooftop solar.

attributes.name: rate_case_docket
attributes.description: PUC docket number of the rate case proceeding that established or last modified this rate schedule. Used to trace rate design back to cost-of-service studies and regulatory decisions.

attributes.name: rate_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code identifying the rate schedule in the tariff book. Used as the business identifier for rate lookup in billing calculations. Examples: RES-TOU-1, COM-DEMAND-A, IND-SPECIAL-3.

attributes.name: rate_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the rate schedule as published in the tariff. Examples: Residential Time-of-Use Schedule A, Commercial Demand Rate, Industrial Interruptible Service.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the rate schedule, including eligibility criteria, service characteristics, and any special terms or conditions. Sourced from the tariff filing.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rate schedule. Active schedules are available for new enrollments and billing. Pending approval schedules await PUC approval. Superseded schedules have been replaced by newer versions. Retired schedules are no longer offered.

attributes.name: rate_structure_type
attributes.description: Pricing structure methodology: flat (single rate), tiered (increasing block rates), TOU (Time-of-Use with period-based pricing), CPP (Critical Peak Pricing), demand (based on peak kW), real-time pricing (hourly market-based), or net metering (bidirectional energy credit). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: flat|tiered|tou|cpp|demand|real_time_pricing|net_metering — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: seasonal_definition
attributes.description: JSON or delimited string defining seasonal periods and associated rate adjustments. Example: Summer (June-September): base rate + $0.03/kWh; Winter (October-May): base rate. Nullable if seasonal_variation_flag is False.

attributes.name: seasonal_variation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate schedule has seasonal rate variations (e.g., summer vs. winter rates). True if rates vary by season; False if rates are constant year-round.

attributes.name: special_contract_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate schedule is a special contract rate negotiated individually with a large customer (typically industrial or commercial) rather than a standard tariff rate. True for special contracts; False for standard tariff schedules.

attributes.name: tariff_book_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the section, schedule, or page number in the published tariff book where this rate schedule is documented. Example: Schedule E-1, Page 12 of Electric Tariff Book.

attributes.name: tier_structure_definition
attributes.description: JSON or delimited string defining tiered rate blocks for tiered rate structures. Example: Tier 1: 0-500 kWh at $0.10/kWh; Tier 2: 501-1000 kWh at $0.12/kWh; Tier 3: 1001+ kWh at $0.15/kWh. Nullable for non-tiered schedules.

attributes.name: tou_period_definition
attributes.description: JSON or delimited string defining TOU pricing periods and rates. Example: On-Peak (2pm-8pm weekdays): $0.25/kWh; Off-Peak (all other hours): $0.08/kWh; Super Off-Peak (midnight-6am): $0.05/kWh. Nullable for non-TOU schedules.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number for this rate schedule. Increments with each tariff revision or rate case modification. Used to track rate schedule evolution over time.

attributes.name: voltage_level
attributes.description: Voltage level at which service is delivered. Primary (distribution voltage), Secondary (customer voltage), Transmission (high voltage bulk), Sub-Transmission (intermediate voltage). Affects rate level due to cost-of-service differences.

products.name: invoice
products.description: Core billing document representing a single billing cycle statement issued to a customer account for electric and/or gas service. Captures bill period start/end dates, due date, total amount due, prior balance, current charges, taxes, regulatory riders, and net amount. Tracks invoice status (generated, mailed, paid, disputed, written-off). Links to the rate schedule applied, service agreement, and meter read period. Generated from Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U billing engine and posted to SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP for GAAP revenue recognition. SSOT for all customer billing documents.
products.reference: Bill / Statement (Oracle CC&B Bill / SAP IS-U Invoice)

attributes.name: invoice_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the invoice record. Primary key for the invoice entity. Assigned by the billing system (Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U) upon invoice generation.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account for which this invoice was generated. Links to the customer account master in the Customer Information System (CIS).

attributes.name: bill_cycle_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.bill_cycle. Business justification: Every invoice is generated as part of a specific billing cycle schedule. This FK allows tracking which cycle generated the invoice and supports operational reporting on billing cycle performance. The

attributes.name: billing_rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Code identifying the tariff rate schedule applied to calculate charges on this invoice. Examples include residential TOU (Time-of-Use), CPP (Critical Peak Pricing), tiered rates, commercial demand rates, and industrial interruptible rates. Approved by the Public Utility Commission (PUC).

attributes.name: customer_service_agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the service agreement (contract) under which this invoice was issued. A customer account may have multiple service agreements for different service points or commodity types (electric vs gas).

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Revenue recognition requires mapping invoices to GL accounts for posting to general ledger. Core utility billing-to-finance integration for accounts receivable and revenue accounting.

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: FK to metering.meter.meter_id — Essential for billing-to-meter reconciliation — billing disputes and revenue assurance require tracing an invoice back to the specific meter and its interval reads.

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Invoices generated under rates approved in specific rate cases need traceability for revenue requirement validation, true-up calculations, and rate case reconciliation. Real business process: rate cas

attributes.name: bill_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the billing period covered by this invoice. Represents the last day of consumption included in the bill. Typically corresponds to the meter read date.

attributes.name: bill_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the billing period covered by this invoice. Represents the first day of consumption included in the bill. Aligns with meter read cycle dates.

attributes.name: billing_days
attributes.description: Number of days in the billing period, calculated as the difference between bill period end date and bill period start date. Used to normalize consumption for comparison across billing cycles of varying lengths.

attributes.name: commodity_type
attributes.description: Type of utility service billed on this invoice. Electric-only, gas-only, or dual-commodity (combined electric and gas charges on a single invoice).

attributes.name: consumption_kwh
attributes.description: Total electric energy consumption during the billing period, measured in kWh (Kilowatt-Hours). Derived from meter reads (actual or estimated) from AMI or AMR systems. Null for gas-only invoices.

attributes.name: consumption_therms
attributes.description: Total gas consumption during the billing period, measured in Therms (unit of heat energy for gas billing). One Therm equals 100,000 BTU. Derived from meter reads. Null for electric-only invoices.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the invoice record was first created in the billing system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: current_charges_amount
attributes.description: Total charges for the current billing period before taxes and regulatory riders. Includes energy charges (kWh or Therm), demand charges (kW or MW), customer charges, and any applicable FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause) adjustments. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: customer_charge_amount
attributes.description: Fixed monthly charge for maintaining the customer account and service connection, independent of consumption. Covers meter reading, billing, customer service, and infrastructure maintenance costs. Approved by PUC tariff. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: delivery_method
attributes.description: Method by which the invoice was delivered to the customer. Paper invoices are mailed via postal service. Email invoices are sent as PDF attachments. Online portal invoices are available for download through the customer self-service portal.

attributes.name: demand_charge_amount
attributes.description: Charges for peak demand during the billing period, applicable to commercial and industrial customers. Based on the highest kW (Kilowatt) or MW (Megawatt) demand recorded during on-peak hours. Not applicable to most residential customers. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: disconnection_notice_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a disconnection notice has been issued for this invoice due to non-payment. True if the customer has been notified of pending service disconnection. Disconnection procedures are governed by PUC consumer protection rules.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has disputed this invoice. True if a formal dispute has been filed with customer service or the PUC. Disputed invoices may be placed on hold for collections pending resolution.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for the invoice dispute, as provided by the customer or customer service representative. Common reasons include billing errors, meter read discrepancies, rate application issues, and service quality complaints.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Date by which payment must be received to avoid late fees or service disconnection. Calculated based on invoice date plus payment terms (typically 15-21 days).

attributes.name: energy_charge_amount
attributes.description: Charges for energy consumption during the billing period. For electric service, based on kWh (Kilowatt-Hours) consumed. For gas service, based on Therms or MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet) consumed. Calculated by applying the rate schedule energy rate to metered usage. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: fac_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: Adjustment to energy charges based on fluctuations in fuel costs for generation. FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause) allows utilities to pass through fuel cost changes without a full rate case. Can be positive (surcharge) or negative (credit). Approved by PUC. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: gl_posting_date
attributes.description: Date the invoice was posted to the general ledger in the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Used for financial period closing and reconciliation between the CIS and ERP systems.

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: Date the invoice was generated by the billing system. Used as the official invoice issuance date for revenue recognition and aging calculations.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-visible invoice number printed on the customer bill. Unique within the billing system and used for customer inquiries, payment references, and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: invoice_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the invoice. Tracks progression from generation through payment or write-off. Disputed status triggers collections workflow. Cancelled status applies to voided or reversed invoices. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generated|issued|mailed|paid|partially_paid|disputed|written_off|cancelled — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: invoice_type
attributes.description: Classification of the invoice based on billing cycle context. Regular invoices are standard monthly/bi-monthly bills. Final invoices are issued upon account closure or move-out. Adjustment invoices correct prior billing errors. Estimated invoices are issued when actual meter reads are unavailable. Corrected invoices replace previously issued invoices.

attributes.name: late_fee_amount
attributes.description: Late payment fee assessed if payment is not received by the due date. Late fee rates and grace periods are defined in the PUC-approved tariff. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: meter_read_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the invoice is based on an actual meter read from AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure) or AMR (Automated Meter Reading), an estimated read due to meter access issues, or a customer-provided read.

attributes.name: outstanding_balance_amount
attributes.description: Remaining unpaid balance on this invoice, calculated as total amount due minus payment received amount. Used for aging analysis and collections prioritization. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: payment_plan_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this invoice is part of a payment plan or installment agreement. True if the customer has arranged to pay the balance over multiple billing cycles. Payment plans are offered to customers facing financial hardship.

attributes.name: payment_received_amount
attributes.description: Total payments received and applied to this invoice as of the current date. Updated as payments are posted from various channels (online, mail, phone, in-person). Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: peak_demand_kw
attributes.description: Maximum electric demand recorded during the billing period, measured in kW (Kilowatts). Used to calculate demand charges for commercial and industrial customers. Captured from interval meter data (AMI). Null for residential customers without demand metering.

attributes.name: previous_balance_amount
attributes.description: Outstanding balance carried forward from prior billing cycles. Includes unpaid charges, late fees, and any credits or adjustments from previous invoices. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: print_date
attributes.description: Date the invoice was printed or electronically delivered to the customer. May differ from invoice date if batch printing or electronic delivery is delayed.

attributes.name: regulatory_rider_amount
attributes.description: Total charges or credits from regulatory riders approved by the PUC. Riders recover specific costs such as renewable energy programs (RPS - Renewable Portfolio Standard), energy efficiency (EE) programs, demand response (DR) programs, environmental compliance, and infrastructure investments. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_date
attributes.description: Date on which revenue from this invoice is recognized in the general ledger for GAAP financial reporting. Typically the invoice date or the bill period end date, depending on the utility's revenue recognition policy.

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Total taxes applied to the invoice, including state sales tax, local utility taxes, franchise fees, and any other government-mandated taxes. Tax rates and applicability vary by jurisdiction and customer class. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: total_amount_due
attributes.description: Total amount the customer must pay, calculated as previous balance plus current charges plus taxes plus regulatory riders. This is the net amount due printed on the invoice. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the invoice record was last modified. Updated when invoice status changes, payments are applied, or adjustments are made. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

products.name: invoice_line
products.description: Itemized charge line within a customer invoice representing a single billable component — energy consumption charges (kWh, MCF, Therm), demand charges (kW), fixed customer charges, distribution rider, FAC adjustment, CIAC recovery, RPS surcharge, taxes, or credits. Captures charge type code, unit of measure, quantity, unit rate, extended amount, and applicable rate schedule tier or TOU period. Enables granular revenue decomposition by charge category for regulatory reporting and customer dispute resolution. Sourced from Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U charge calculation engine.

attributes.name: billing_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the billing period for which this charge applies. Defines the beginning of the consumption or service period being billed. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: charge_description

attributes.name: gl_account_code

Examples: '440' (Electric Operating Revenues - Residential), '480' (Gas Operating Revenues - Commercial). Critical for financial close, GAAP revenue reporting, and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this invoice line record was last modified. Captures adjustments, corrections, or dispute resolution updates. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Supports audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: line_amount
attributes.description: Extended charge amount for this invoice line. Calculated as usage_quantity multiplied by unit_rate, or a fixed amount for non-usage-based charges. Represents the pre-tax charge value. Positive values indicate charges; negative values indicate credits or adjustments. Expressed in the invoice currency (typically USD for U.S. utilities).

attributes.name: line_number
attributes.description: Sequential line number within the invoice. Determines the display order of charges on the customer bill. Typically starts at 1 and increments for each charge component.

attributes.name: print_sequence
attributes.description: Display sequence number for printing this line on the customer invoice. Determines the order in which charges appear on the bill. Typically groups charges by type (energy, demand, fixed, taxes) and sorts within groups. Supports customer bill presentation and readability.

attributes.name: proration_factor
attributes.description: Proration factor applied to calculate partial-period charges for move-in, move-out, or mid-cycle rate changes. Expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1 representing the fraction of the billing period for which the charge applies. Example: 0.5000 for a half-month charge. Null for full-period charges. Ensures accurate billing for partial service periods.

attributes.name: rate_component_code
attributes.description: Specific component within the rate schedule being applied. Identifies the tier, block, or Time-of-Use (TOU) period for tiered or time-differentiated rates. Examples: 'TIER1' (first 500 kWh), 'TIER2' (501-1000 kWh), 'ON_PEAK' (summer on-peak hours), 'OFF_PEAK' (off-peak hours), 'SHOULDER' (shoulder period). Enables granular revenue analysis by rate structure element.

attributes.name: regulatory_rider_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the regulatory rider or surcharge applied to this line. Riders are PUC-approved rate adjustments for specific cost recovery mechanisms. Examples: 'FAC' (Fuel Adjustment Clause for fuel cost pass-through), 'DSM' (Demand-Side Management program cost recovery), 'RPS' (Renewable Portfolio Standard compliance surcharge), 'CIAC' (Contribution in Aid of Construction recovery), 'PBR' (Performance-Based Ratemaking adjustment). Null if no rider applies. Critical for regulatory reporting and rate case reconciliation.

attributes.name: revenue_class_code
attributes.description: Customer class or revenue category for regulatory reporting. RESIDENTIAL (single-family and multi-family homes), COMMERCIAL (small and medium businesses), INDUSTRIAL (large manufacturing and industrial customers), STREET_LIGHTING (municipal street and highway lighting), PUBLIC_AUTHORITY (government and public institutions), WHOLESALE (sales to other utilities or power marketers). Aligns with FERC Form 1 and state PUC reporting requirements.

attributes.name: revenue_recognition_date
attributes.description: Date on which revenue for this invoice line is recognized in the General Ledger under GAAP ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers). Typically the invoice date or service delivery date. Critical for financial close, revenue accrual, and GAAP compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Type of utility service being billed on this line. ELECTRIC for electric service charges (kWh, kW), GAS for natural gas service charges (MCF, Therm). Enables revenue decomposition by commodity type for regulatory reporting to PUCs and FERC.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record that generated this invoice line. CC&B (Oracle Customer Care and Billing), IS-U (SAP Industry Solution for Utilities), MDMS (Meter Data Management System for interval data charges), ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning for manual adjustments), MANUAL (manually entered adjustments). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and system integration reconciliation.

attributes.name: source_transaction_reference
attributes.description: Unique transaction identifier from the source system (Oracle CC&B, SAP IS-U, or MDMS) that generated this invoice line. Enables traceability back to the originating billing calculation or charge engine transaction. Supports audit trail, dispute resolution, and system integration reconciliation.

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: Tax amount applied to this invoice line. Includes sales tax, utility tax, franchise fees, or other regulatory taxes. Calculated based on applicable tax rates and jurisdictional rules. Null if the line item is non-taxable or represents a tax charge itself. Supports tax reporting and revenue recognition under GAAP.

attributes.name: taxable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this invoice line is subject to sales tax or utility tax. True if taxable, False if exempt. Determines whether tax_amount is calculated for this line. Tax exemption rules vary by jurisdiction, customer class, and charge type. Supports tax compliance and reporting.

attributes.name: total_line_amount
attributes.description: Total amount for this invoice line including taxes. Calculated as line_amount plus tax_amount. Represents the final charge or credit amount for this line item. Positive values indicate charges; negative values indicate credits. Expressed in the invoice currency.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the usage quantity. KWH (kilowatt-hour) for electric energy consumption, MWH (megawatt-hour) for large commercial/industrial energy, KW (kilowatt) for electric demand, MW (megawatt) for large demand, MCF (thousand cubic feet) for natural gas volume, THERM (unit of heat energy) for gas billing, EACH for count-based charges (e.g., number of reconnections), PERCENT for percentage-based adjustments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: KWH|MWH|KW|MW|MCF|THERM|EACH|PERCENT — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: unit_rate
attributes.description: Rate per unit of measure applied to calculate the charge amount. Expressed in currency per unit (e.g., dollars per kWh, dollars per MCF, dollars per kW). Derived from the approved tariff rate schedule filed with the PUC. Null for fixed charges or lump-sum adjustments. Critical for rate case analysis and revenue reconciliation.

attributes.name: usage_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of utility service consumed or delivered during the billing period. For energy charges, represents kilowatt-hours (kWh), Megawatt-hours (MWh), thousand cubic feet (MCF), or Therms. For demand charges, represents peak kilowatts (kW) or Megawatts (MW). Null for fixed charges, taxes, or credits that are not usage-based. Sourced from MDMS interval data aggregation or Automated Meter Reading (AMR) systems.

products.name: payment

Captures payment date, amount, payment method type, tender type, confirmation number, processing status (received, posted, returned/NSF, reversed), and source channel (web portal, IVR, walk-in, lockbox). Integrates with SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP for cash receipts posting and GAAP revenue recognition. SSOT for all customer payment transactions.

attributes.name: invoice_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific bill or invoice that this payment is intended to satisfy. May be null for advance payments or account credits.

attributes.name: payment_arrangement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.payment_arrangement. attributes.name: allocation_method
attributes.description: Business rule or algorithm used to allocate the payment amount across multiple outstanding bills or charges on the customer account. Common methods include First-In-First-Out (FIFO), Last-In-First-Out (LIFO), pro-rata distribution, or customer-directed allocation.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the payment transaction in the utility's functional currency. Represents the gross amount tendered by the customer before any adjustments or fees.

attributes.name: applied_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the payment amount that was successfully applied to reduce the customer account balance. May differ from payment_amount if payment was partially applied, held in suspense, or subject to fees.

attributes.name: auto_pay_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator denoting whether this payment was automatically initiated through a recurring payment arrangement (auto-pay or budget billing). True if auto-pay, False if manually submitted by customer.

attributes.name: bank_account_number_last_four
attributes.business_glossary_term: Bank Account Number Last Four Digits
attributes.description: Last four digits of the customer's bank account number, stored for customer service reference and payment verification. Full account number is tokenized and stored in secure vault per PCI DSS requirements.

attributes.name: batch_reference

attributes.name: budget_billing_flag

attributes.name: channel

attributes.name: check_number
attributes.description: The sequential number printed on the customer's check. Captured for check payments to support reconciliation and returned check processing. Null for non-check payment methods.

attributes.name: cleared_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the payment was confirmed as cleared by the financial institution or payment processor. Applicable to checks, ACH, and credit card transactions. Null for cash payments.

attributes.name: confirmation_number
attributes.description: Externally visible confirmation or receipt number provided to the customer upon successful payment submission. Used for customer service inquiries and dispute resolution.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp indicating when this payment record was first inserted into the data platform. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: credit_card_last_four

attributes.name: credit_card_type
attributes.description: Brand or network of the credit or debit card used for payment. Common values include Visa, MasterCard, American Express, and Discover.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code indicating the currency in which the payment was tendered. Typically USD for U.S. utilities; supports multi-currency operations for international utilities.

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: The General Ledger account code to which the payment revenue was posted in the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. Aligns with the utility's chart of accounts and FERC Uniform System of Accounts.

attributes.name: gl_posting_date

attributes.name: method_type
attributes.description: The financial instrument or tender type used by the customer to remit payment.
