[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: check|ach|eft|credit_card|debit_card|cash|money_order — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for customer service representatives or payment processors to record additional context, special handling instructions, or dispute details related to the payment transaction.

attributes.name: nsf_fee_amount

attributes.name: payment_date

attributes.name: payment_status

attributes.name: processor_name
attributes.description: Name of the third-party payment processor or financial institution that handled the electronic payment transaction. Applicable to credit card, ACH, and EFT payments.

attributes.name: processor_transaction_reference
attributes.description: Unique transaction identifier assigned by the external payment processor or gateway. Used for reconciliation, dispute resolution, and chargeback processing.

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the payment transaction was received by the utility system, including time zone offset. Used for audit trail and SLA compliance tracking.

attributes.name: reversal_date

attributes.name: reversal_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded explanation for why a payment was reversed or returned. Common reasons include Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF), account closed, stop payment, unauthorized transaction, or administrative error. Null if payment has not been reversed.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the originating system or application that captured and transmitted the payment transaction. Examples include Oracle CC&B, SAP IS-U, third-party payment gateway, or lockbox processor.

attributes.name: third_party_agency_name
attributes.description: Name of the external agency or authorized payment location that accepted the payment on behalf of the utility. Examples include retail payment centers, community action agencies, or government assistance programs. Null for direct payments.

attributes.name: token
attributes.description: Tokenized representation of sensitive payment instrument data (credit card number, bank account number) issued by the payment processor or tokenization service. Used for recurring payments and PCI DSS compliance.

attributes.name: unapplied_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the payment amount that remains unapplied or held in suspense, typically due to account discrepancies, overpayment, or pending dispute resolution. Zero if payment is fully applied.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp indicating when this payment record was last modified in the data platform. Used for change data capture and audit trail purposes.

products.name: payment_arrangement

Captures arrangement type, total deferred amount, number of installments, installment amount, start date, end date, down payment amount, arrangement status (active, broken, completed, cancelled), and associated collections action. Tracks compliance with arrangement terms to support collections workflow in Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U. Distinct from a single payment transaction — represents an ongoing multi-period commitment.
products.reference: Payment Arrangement / Deferred Payment Plan (Oracle CC&B Pay Plan / SAP IS-U Installment Plan)

attributes.name: payment_arrangement_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for the payment arrangement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Reference to the customer account for which this payment arrangement was established. Links to the billing account in Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U.

attributes.name: associated_collections_action_id
attributes.description: Reference to the collections action or case that prompted this payment arrangement. Null if arrangement was proactively requested by customer rather than initiated through collections workflow.

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: Actual date when the arrangement was fully satisfied and all deferred amounts paid. Null if arrangement is still active, broken, or cancelled. May differ from arrangement_end_date if customer paid early or late.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the payment arrangement was formally approved by the utility. May differ from arrangement_start_date if down payment is required before activation.

attributes.name: approved_by_user_code
attributes.description: User ID of the customer service representative, supervisor, or automated system that approved the payment arrangement. Used for audit trail and quality assurance.

attributes.name: arrangement_end_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date when the final installment is due and the arrangement is expected to be completed. Calculated from start date plus (number_of_installments * installment_frequency).

attributes.name: arrangement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for customer service representatives to document special terms, customer circumstances, or other contextual information relevant to the arrangement. Not displayed to customer.

attributes.name: arrangement_number
attributes.description: Externally visible unique business identifier for the payment arrangement, typically displayed on customer correspondence and used in customer service interactions.

attributes.name: arrangement_start_date
attributes.description: Effective date when the payment arrangement becomes active and the first installment is due. Typically the date down payment is received or arrangement is approved.

attributes.name: arrangement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the payment arrangement. Pending: awaiting approval or down payment. Active: in good standing with payments current. Broken: customer missed payment(s) per terms. Completed: all installments paid. Cancelled: arrangement terminated by utility or customer. Suspended: temporarily paused.

attributes.name: arrangement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the payment arrangement plan. Budget billing spreads annual costs evenly; levelized payment smooths seasonal variation; low-income assistance provides subsidized payment terms; collections installment addresses past-due balances; deferred payment postpones a portion of charges; custom represents negotiated terms.

attributes.name: auto_pay_enrolled
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has enrolled in automatic payment for installments via bank draft or credit card. Auto-pay enrollment often reduces the risk of arrangement default.

attributes.name: broken_date
attributes.description: Date when the arrangement was marked as broken due to non-compliance with payment terms. Triggers collections workflow and potential service disconnection per tariff rules.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Reason code explaining why the arrangement was cancelled before completion. Used for reporting and policy analysis.

attributes.name: cancelled_date
attributes.description: Date when the arrangement was cancelled by the utility or customer before completion. Remaining balance typically becomes immediately due.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the payment arrangement record was first created in Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: down_payment_amount
attributes.description: Initial payment required to establish the arrangement, typically a percentage of the total deferred amount as mandated by state Public Utility Commission (PUC) rules or utility policy. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: grace_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days after installment due date before a missed payment is counted against the arrangement. Typically 5-15 days per utility policy or PUC regulation.

attributes.name: installment_amount
attributes.description: Fixed amount due per installment period, calculated as (total_deferred_amount - down_payment_amount) / number_of_installments. May be adjusted for final installment to account for rounding. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: installment_frequency
attributes.description: Cadence at which installment payments are due. Monthly is most common for residential customers; other frequencies may be used for commercial accounts or special assistance programs.

attributes.name: installments_missed
attributes.description: Count of scheduled installment payments that were not received by the due date. Exceeding the allowed threshold (typically 1-2 missed payments) triggers arrangement_status transition to broken.

attributes.name: installments_paid
attributes.description: Count of installment payments successfully received and applied to the arrangement. Used to track compliance with payment schedule.

attributes.name: interest_accrued
attributes.description: Total interest charges accrued on the deferred balance to date. Zero if interest_rate is zero. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: interest_rate
attributes.description: Annual interest rate applied to the deferred balance, if any. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0500 for 5%). Many jurisdictions prohibit interest on residential payment arrangements; commercial arrangements may include interest per tariff.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the payment arrangement record was last updated. Tracks changes to status, payments applied, or other arrangement attributes.

attributes.name: next_installment_due_date
attributes.description: Date when the next scheduled installment payment is due. Updated after each payment is received. Null when arrangement is completed, broken, or cancelled.

attributes.name: notification_preference
attributes.description: Customer's preferred channel for receiving payment reminders and arrangement status notifications. Used by Customer Information System (CIS) to trigger communications.

attributes.name: number_of_installments
attributes.description: Total count of scheduled installment payments over the life of the arrangement. Typically ranges from 3 to 24 months depending on arrangement type and regulatory constraints.

attributes.name: program_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the low-income assistance program, demand-side management (DSM) program, or special rate program under which this arrangement was established. Examples: LIHEAP, CARE, FERA. Null for standard arrangements.

attributes.name: remaining_balance
attributes.description: Current outstanding balance under the arrangement after applying all payments received to date. Decreases with each installment payment. Zero when arrangement is completed. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: total_deferred_amount
attributes.description: Total outstanding balance being deferred under this arrangement at the time of establishment, including principal charges, late fees, and any applicable interest. Expressed in USD.

attributes.description: Target day of the month (1-31) when payment is due for invoices in this cycle. Calculated as bill_date plus payment_due_offset_days.

attributes.name: payment_due_offset_days
attributes.description: Number of days after bill date when payment is due. Typically 15-30 days for residential accounts; may vary by customer class and regulatory requirements.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the Public Utility Commission (PUC) docket, order, or tariff filing that approved this billing cycle configuration. Required for regulatory compliance and audit.

attributes.name: route_grouping
attributes.description: Meter reading route or grouping identifier used to organize field meter readers or AMI collection schedules. May represent physical routes or logical batches.

attributes.name: special_handling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this cycle requires special processing, such as manual review, custom rate application, or non-standard billing rules. True for large C&I or wholesale accounts.

attributes.name: tariff_book_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the section of the utility tariff book that governs billing cycle assignment and payment terms for this cycle. Used for regulatory compliance and customer dispute resolution.

attributes.name: territory_code
attributes.description: Geographic territory or service area code associated with this billing cycle. Aligns with Geographic Information System (GIS) boundaries and operational districts.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of this billing cycle configuration. Incremented when cycle parameters are modified. Supports change tracking and regulatory audit.

products.name: collections_action
products.description: Master reference table for collections_action. Referenced by associated_collections_action_id.

attributes.name: collections_action_id
attributes.description: Primary key for collections_action

attributes.name: action_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the collections action type. Notification includes letters and notices; contact_attempt includes calls and visits; payment_arrangement includes plans and extensions; legal_action includes liens and judgments; service_action includes disconnection and reconnection; account_adjustment includes write-offs and settlements; escalation includes agency referrals; resolution includes payment received and account closure.

attributes.name: action_code
attributes.description: Standardized code representing the type of collections action (e.g., NOTICE_1, CALL_ATTEMPT, PAYMENT_PLAN, DISCONNECT_WARN, SERVICE_SUSPEND). Used as a business identifier for integration with Customer Information System (CIS) and billing workflows.

attributes.name: action_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the collections action (e.g., First Delinquency Notice, Payment Arrangement Offer, Service Disconnection Warning, Final Notice Before Shutoff).

attributes.name: action_sequence
attributes.description: Numeric ordering of this action within a standard collections workflow. Lower numbers represent earlier actions in the escalation path (e.g., 1 for first notice, 5 for final notice, 10 for disconnection).

attributes.name: applicable_customer_class
attributes.description: Customer segment(s) to which this collections action applies. Residential for household customers; commercial for small/medium business; industrial for large commercial and manufacturing; all for universal actions. Different customer classes may have different regulatory protections and collections workflows.

attributes.name: auto_trigger_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action can be automatically triggered by the billing or collections system based on predefined rules (e.g., days past due, balance threshold). True for system-automated actions; false for manual-only actions requiring human review.

attributes.name: auto_trigger_rule
attributes.description: Business rule or condition that automatically triggers this collections action. Examples: 'Balance > $100 AND Days Past Due >= 30', 'Second missed payment on payment plan', 'No response to prior notice within 15 days'. Null if action is manual-only.

attributes.name: cost_amount
attributes.description: Standard cost or fee associated with executing this collections action, charged to the customer account. Includes costs such as certified mail fees, field visit charges, reconnection fees, or collection agency commissions. Null if no cost is assessed.

attributes.name: cost_recoverable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the cost of this collections action can be billed to and recovered from the customer account. True if cost is customer-billable; false if cost is absorbed by the utility as a business expense.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this collections action record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: credit_reporting_impact
attributes.description: Indicates the impact of this collections action on customer credit bureau reporting. None for actions with no credit impact; negative_report for delinquency or charge-off reporting; positive_report for successful payment plan completion; dispute_flag for contested accounts.

attributes.name: delivery_method
attributes.description: The channel or medium through which the collections action is delivered to the customer. Mail for standard postal delivery; certified_mail for proof-of-delivery requirements; email and sms for electronic notifications; phone_call for voice contact; in_person for field visits; portal_notification for customer self-service alerts.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the collections action, including purpose, typical use cases, and any special handling instructions. Provides context for collections staff and system administrators.

attributes.name: dispute_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the customer has the right to dispute or appeal this collections action. True for actions subject to customer dispute rights; false for non-disputable administrative actions.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this collections action definition is retired or superseded. Null for currently active actions. Used for historical analysis and regulatory audit trails.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this collections action definition becomes active and available for use in collections workflows. Used for version control and regulatory compliance tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this collections action record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: legal_action_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action involves or initiates legal proceedings (e.g., filing a lien, initiating small claims, referring to attorney). True for legal actions; false for operational collections activities.

attributes.name: minimum_notice_days
attributes.description: Minimum number of days required by regulation between this action and any subsequent service disconnection or legal action. Null if no regulatory minimum applies. Varies by jurisdiction and customer class (residential vs. commercial).

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this collections action definition. Used for accountability and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: payment_plan_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether customers receiving this collections action are eligible to enter into a payment arrangement or installment plan to avoid further escalation. True if payment plan option is available; false if account is past payment plan eligibility.

attributes.name: protected_customer_exempt
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action is prohibited for protected customer categories (e.g., medical necessity customers, low-income assistance participants, elderly or disabled customers with special protections). True if action cannot be applied to protected customers; false if action is universally applicable.

attributes.name: regulatory_notice_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action must comply with state or federal regulatory notice requirements (e.g., minimum notice periods before disconnection, specific language mandates, customer rights disclosures). True for actions subject to Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) rules.

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation of the specific state Public Utility Commission (PUC) rule, tariff section, or federal regulation that governs this collections action. Examples: 'PUC Rule 25.483', 'Tariff Section 6.2.1', 'FERC Order 2222'. Null if no specific regulatory mandate applies.

attributes.name: requires_customer_response
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action requires an explicit response or action from the customer (e.g., payment, contact, dispute filing). True for actions requiring customer engagement; false for informational or system-driven actions.

attributes.name: requires_supervisor_approval
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action requires managerial or supervisory approval before execution. True for high-impact actions such as disconnection, legal referral, or large write-offs; false for routine automated actions.

attributes.name: response_due_days
attributes.description: Number of days from action delivery date by which the customer must respond or take action. Null if no response deadline applies. Used to calculate follow-up action triggers and compliance with regulatory notice periods.

attributes.name: seasonal_restriction_applies
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action is subject to seasonal restrictions (e.g., winter moratorium on disconnections, extreme weather protections). True if action is restricted during certain months or weather conditions; false if action can be taken year-round.

attributes.name: service_action_type
attributes.description: Specifies the type of field service action triggered by this collections action. Disconnect for service termination; reconnect for service restoration; meter_lock for physical access prevention; meter_removal for complete meter extraction; limiter_install for reduced service capacity; none if no service action is triggered.

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Indicates the urgency and escalation level of the collections action. Informational for early reminders; low for initial notices; medium for follow-up actions; high for pre-disconnection warnings; critical for imminent service termination; final for last action before legal or agency referral.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this collections action definition. Active for in-use actions; inactive for temporarily disabled actions; suspended for actions under regulatory review; retired for obsolete actions retained for historical reference.

attributes.name: template_document_code
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the standard letter, notice, or script template used for this collections action. Links to document management system for content retrieval and version control. Null if no template is used (e.g., for system-automated actions).

attributes.name: third_party_agency_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether accounts subject to this collections action are eligible for referral to external collection agencies. True if action can trigger agency placement; false if action must remain internal.

attributes.name: triggers_service_action
attributes.description: Indicates whether this collections action directly triggers a field service action such as disconnection, reconnection, or meter lock. True for actions that initiate service orders; false for administrative or notification-only actions.

attributes.name: associated_collections_action_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on collections_action (associated_collections_action_id)

domains.name: market
domains.description: Manages participation in wholesale energy markets including day-ahead market (DAM) and real-time market (RTM) bids and schedules, LMP settlement, capacity market obligations, ancillary services, REC tracking, and PPA contract positions. Serves as the SSOT for wholesale energy procurement and sale transactions with RTOs/ISOs. Supports FERC market-based rate authority and IRP resource adequacy analysis.

products.name: wholesale_counterparty
products.description: Master record for all wholesale market counterparties with whom the utility transacts in DAM, RTM, capacity markets, and bilateral PPA arrangements. Captures RTO/ISO membership, FERC market-based rate authorization status, credit ratings, DUNS numbers, and counterparty classification (generator, load-serving entity, marketer, financial participant). Serves as the SSOT for wholesale trading partner identity within the market domain.
products.reference: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority / NERC Registered Entity

attributes.name: wholesale_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the wholesale market counterparty record within the Power and Utilities market domain. Serves as the primary key for all wholesale trading partner identity references.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; ISO/RTO Participant Registry

attributes.name: approval_docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Wholesale counterparty agreements, especially with affiliates, require regulatory approval. Links counterparty to regulatory proceeding for contract approval, affiliate transaction oversight, and prud

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Counterparty relationships are managed by specific business units (wholesale trading, power marketing) for cost allocation of credit management, contract administration, and relationship management ex

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Wholesale counterparties frequently serve dual roles as procurement vendors (fuel suppliers, equipment providers). Enables consolidated vendor master data management, unified credit limit tracking, an

attributes.name: affiliate_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this counterparty is an affiliate of the utility as defined under FERC 18 CFR Part 35 and the applicable OATT. Affiliate transactions are subject to additional FERC disclosure requirements and arm's-length pricing standards.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; FERC OATT Standards of Conduct; FERC Order 697

attributes.name: ancillary_services_participant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this counterparty is registered to provide or procure ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support) in the applicable RTO/ISO market. Supports ancillary services procurement and settlement tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Order 755; NERC BAL Standards; RTO/ISO Ancillary Services Tariff

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which the counterparty was formally approved for wholesale energy trading by the utility's credit and compliance functions. Marks the start of eligibility for DAM/RTM bids, bilateral PPAs, and capacity market transactions.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; Internal Credit Risk Policy; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: capacity_market_participant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this counterparty participates in capacity market auctions (e.g., PJM RPM, MISO Planning Resource Auction) as a buyer or seller. Supports capacity obligation tracking and resource adequacy compliance reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; RTO/ISO Capacity Market Tariff; State PUC Resource Adequacy Rules

attributes.name: collateral_requirement_usd
attributes.description: Current collateral amount (cash, letter of credit, or surety bond) required from the counterparty to support wholesale energy transactions in excess of the unsecured credit limit. Expressed in US dollars.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; ISDA Credit Support Annex; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: counterparty_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the wholesale counterparty master record. Controls eligibility for new transaction execution, credit limit enforcement, and settlement processing. Active status required before DAM/RTM bids or PPA execution.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; Internal Credit Risk Policy

attributes.name: counterparty_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the wholesale counterparty's primary market role. Drives applicable FERC tariff treatment, credit requirements, and settlement logic. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generator|load_serving_entity|marketer|financial_participant|transmission_owner|cooperative|municipal_utility — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the wholesale counterparty master record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under SOX and FERC record retention rules.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; FERC Record Retention Rules 18 CFR Part 125; GAAP

attributes.name: credit_rating
attributes.description: Most recent credit rating assigned to the counterparty by the designated credit rating agency (e.g., Moody's Baa2, S&P BBB+). Drives unsecured credit limit calculations, collateral requirements, and counterparty risk tiering for wholesale energy transactions.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; ISDA Master Agreement; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: credit_rating_agency
attributes.description: Name of the nationally recognized statistical rating organization (NRSRO) that issued the counterparty's most recent credit rating. Used in conjunction with credit_rating to assess counterparty default risk and set credit exposure limits for wholesale transactions.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; NERC CIP; SEC NRSRO Rules

attributes.name: credit_rating_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current credit rating was issued or last affirmed by the rating agency. Used to assess rating staleness and trigger re-evaluation of credit exposure limits per internal credit risk policy.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: doing_business_as_name
attributes.description: Trade or operating name used by the counterparty in day-to-day wholesale market transactions, if different from the legal entity name. Commonly used in RTO/ISO scheduling and settlement communications.

attributes.name: duns_number
attributes.description: Nine-digit Dun & Bradstreet Data Universal Numbering System identifier uniquely identifying the counterparty legal entity. Required for federal contracting, credit assessment, and counterparty due diligence in wholesale energy markets.
attributes.references: Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Standard; FERC Counterparty Registration

attributes.name: ein
attributes.description: IRS-issued Employer Identification Number (Federal Tax ID) for the counterparty legal entity. Required for tax reporting, 1099 issuance, and financial settlement reconciliation under GAAP and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: IRS Publication 15; SOX Section 302; GAAP ASC 740

attributes.name: ferc_mbr_authorization
attributes.description: Indicates whether the counterparty holds a current FERC market-based rate (MBR) authorization under 18 CFR Part 35, permitting them to sell wholesale electricity at negotiated market rates. Required validation before executing bilateral power purchase agreements.

attributes.name: ferc_mbr_docket_number
attributes.description: FERC docket number associated with the counterparty's market-based rate authorization filing (e.g., ER22-1234-000). Used to cross-reference FERC eLibrary filings and validate authorization currency for wholesale trading compliance.

attributes.name: incorporation_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code where the counterparty legal entity is incorporated or organized. Used for legal entity verification, FERC market-based rate filings, and counterparty due diligence.

attributes.name: kyc_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the counterparty has completed Know Your Counterparty (KYC) due diligence verification, including entity authentication, beneficial ownership disclosure, and sanctions screening. Required before initiating wholesale energy transactions.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; FinCEN AML Rules; OFAC Sanctions Compliance; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: last_credit_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent formal credit review conducted for this counterparty. Triggers re-review workflow when the interval since last review exceeds the internal credit policy threshold (typically annual or upon rating change).
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; Internal Credit Risk Policy

attributes.name: legal_name
attributes.description: Full legal registered name of the wholesale counterparty as filed with FERC, the applicable RTO/ISO, and state regulatory authorities. Used for contract execution, FERC market-based rate filings, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: market_participant_class
attributes.description: Functional classification of the counterparty's transactional role in wholesale energy markets — whether they primarily buy, sell, or act as an intermediary. Used to segment DAM/RTM exposure and bilateral PPA counterparty risk.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; RTO/ISO Market Rules

attributes.name: master_agreement_effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the master trading agreement with this counterparty became legally effective. Establishes the earliest date from which transactions under the agreement are valid and enforceable.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; ISDA Master Agreement

attributes.name: master_agreement_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the master trading agreement with this counterparty expires or is scheduled for renewal. Null indicates an evergreen agreement with no fixed termination date. Triggers contract renewal workflow when approaching.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; ISDA Master Agreement

attributes.name: master_agreement_type
attributes.description: Type of master trading agreement governing transactions with this counterparty. EEI MPSA (Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement) is standard for physical power; ISDA governs financial derivatives; NAESB covers natural gas. Determines applicable netting, termination, and default provisions.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; ISDA Master Agreement; NAESB Base Contract

attributes.name: nerc_registered_entity_code
attributes.description: NERC-assigned registered entity identifier for counterparties that are registered as Balancing Authorities, Generator Operators, Transmission Operators, or other NERC functional entity types. Supports NERC reliability compliance tracking and BES transaction validation.
attributes.references: NERC Rules of Procedure; NERC Reliability Standards FAC-001, FAC-002

attributes.name: netting_agreement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a legally enforceable close-out netting agreement is in place with this counterparty. Netting agreements reduce gross credit exposure to net exposure for settlement and capital adequacy purposes under FERC and GAAP.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; ISDA Master Agreement; GAAP ASC 815

attributes.name: ofac_screened_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the counterparty has been screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Blocked Persons list. Must be true before any financial settlement or contract execution with the counterparty.
attributes.references: OFAC 31 CFR Part 501; FinCEN AML Rules; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: parent_company_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the ultimate parent or controlling entity of the counterparty, if applicable. Required for FERC market-based rate affiliate transaction disclosure, credit consolidation, and market power analysis under FERC Order 697.
attributes.references: FERC Order 697; FERC 18 CFR Part 35; FERC Market-Based Rate Affiliate Rules

attributes.name: ppa_counterparty_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this counterparty is a party to one or more active Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with the utility. Used to filter counterparties for IRP resource adequacy analysis and long-term procurement reporting.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; IRP Filing Requirements; State PUC Resource Adequacy Rules

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: Email address of the primary trading contact at the counterparty. Used for scheduling confirmations, settlement notices, and regulatory correspondence related to wholesale energy transactions.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; FERC 18 CFR Part 35

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: Full name of the primary trading desk or commercial contact at the counterparty organization. Used for DAM/RTM scheduling communications, PPA negotiations, and settlement dispute resolution.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; FERC 18 CFR Part 35

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: Direct phone number for the primary trading contact at the counterparty. Used for real-time scheduling coordination, curtailment notifications, and emergency dispatch communications.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; NERC EOP Standards

attributes.name: rec_registry
attributes.description: Name of the REC tracking registry in which this counterparty holds an active account for REC issuance, transfer, or retirement. Supports RPS compliance tracking and REC transaction settlement.
attributes.references: State RPS Regulations; WREGIS Operating Rules; GATS Operating Rules

attributes.name: rec_trading_participant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) Trading Participant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this counterparty is an active participant in Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) trading. Used to identify eligible counterparties for RPS compliance procurement and REC transfer tracking in WREGIS or GATS registries.
attributes.references: State RPS Regulations; WREGIS Operating Rules; GATS Operating Rules; DOE REC Standards

attributes.name: registered_address_city
attributes.description: City of the counterparty's registered legal business address. Used for jurisdictional determination, state regulatory filings, and counterparty due diligence.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; State PUC Filing Requirements

attributes.name: registered_address_country
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the counterparty's registered legal business address (e.g., USA, CAN). Used for FERC foreign ownership disclosure and cross-border transaction compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; FERC 18 CFR Part 35; DOE Cross-Border Electricity Transfer Authorization

attributes.name: registered_address_line1
attributes.description: First line of the counterparty's registered legal business address. Used for FERC filings, contract execution, and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; State PUC Filing Requirements

attributes.name: registered_address_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code of the counterparty's registered legal business address (ISO 3166-2:US). Determines applicable state PUC jurisdiction and state tax reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-2:US; FERC 18 CFR Part 35; State PUC Filing Requirements

attributes.name: rto_iso_membership
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Membership
attributes.description: The RTO or ISO in which the counterparty holds active membership or registration. Determines applicable market rules, settlement protocols, and LMP pricing nodes for DAM and RTM transactions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|MISO|CAISO|ERCOT|NYISO|ISO-NE|SPP|NONE — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000; NERC BES Definition; RTO/ISO Tariff

attributes.name: rto_participant_code
attributes.description: Unique participant identifier assigned by the counterparty's RTO or ISO (e.g., PJM participant ID, MISO market participant code). Used for scheduling, settlement, and transmission service requests under the applicable OATT.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the counterparty relationship was formally terminated or deactivated. Null for active counterparties. Used to enforce transaction eligibility controls and support regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: unsecured_credit_limit_usd
attributes.description: Maximum dollar value of unsecured wholesale energy exposure permitted with this counterparty, expressed in US dollars. Derived from credit rating and internal credit policy; enforced at transaction execution to prevent over-exposure without collateral.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Risk Standards; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; ISDA Credit Support Annex

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the wholesale counterparty master record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture, data lineage tracking, and SOX audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; FERC Record Retention Rules 18 CFR Part 125; GAAP

products.name: ppa_contract
products.description: Master record for Power Purchase Agreements governing long-term wholesale energy procurement and sale. Captures contract type (fixed-price, index-linked, tolling), contracted capacity (MW), energy volume (MWh), delivery point, term dates, REC bundling provisions, curtailment rights, force majeure clauses, and FERC filing status. Supports IRP resource adequacy analysis and long-term supply portfolio management.
products.reference: FERC EQR (Electric Quarterly Report) / NAESB Contract Standard

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the Power Purchase Agreement contract record in the wholesale energy market data product. Primary key for the ppa_contract entity.

attributes.name: approval_commission_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.commission_order. Business justification: PPAs approved via commission orders. Links power purchase agreements to their regulatory approval orders for authorization tracking and compliance verification.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: PPAs are managed by specific business units (generation group, wholesale trading desk) with P&L responsibility. Cost center assignment enables profitability analysis, budget tracking, and performance

attributes.name: cost_recovery_mechanism_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.cost_recovery_mechanism. Business justification: PPA costs recovered through purchased power cost adjustment mechanisms. Links specific power purchase agreements to their regulatory cost recovery riders for tariff rate calculation.

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific generation asset or resource (power plant, renewable facility, or DER portfolio) that is the source of energy supply under this Power Purchase Agreement. Applicable for unit-contingent and tolling contracts.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: PPA revenue and expense must post to specific GL accounts for FERC Form 1 reporting and GAAP financial statements. Essential for revenue recognition, expense matching, and regulatory compliance in uti

attributes.name: interconnection_request_id
attributes.description: Reference to the FERC-filed interconnection agreement governing the physical grid connection of the contracted generation resource. Required for unit-contingent and tolling PPAs.

attributes.name: irp_portfolio_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) resource portfolio to which this Power Purchase Agreement is assigned. Supports IRP resource adequacy analysis and long-term supply planning.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Requirements; NARUC IRP Guidelines

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: PPA costs are major components of utility rate cases for cost recovery. Links wholesale power purchase agreements to rate proceedings for revenue requirement determination and tariff approval.

attributes.name: regulatory_docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Power purchase agreements require regulatory approval and oversight. Links PPA to its regulatory proceeding for approval tracking, prudency review, and cost recovery authorization in utility operation

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: PPAs for generation services often executed with vendors who provide equipment, O&M, or tolling services. Links contract management to vendor performance evaluation, insurance tracking, and consolidat

attributes.name: wholesale_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the wholesale market counterparty (seller or buyer) that is party to this Power Purchase Agreement. Links to the market counterparty master record.

attributes.name: ancillary_services_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserve, non-spinning reserve, voltage support) are included in the scope of this Power Purchase Agreement in addition to energy and capacity.

attributes.name: annual_energy_mwh
attributes.description: Expected annual energy delivery volume in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) under this Power Purchase Agreement. Used for annual budget planning, FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause) forecasting, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Regulatory Reporting

attributes.name: billing_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which financial settlement invoices are generated under this Power Purchase Agreement. Drives integration with SAP S/4HANA accounts payable/receivable and billing cycles.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; GAAP Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: capacity_market_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contracted resource qualifies for capacity market obligations under the applicable RTO/ISO capacity market (e.g., PJM RPM, MISO Planning Resource Auction). True if eligible; False if energy-only.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: capacity_price_per_mw_month
attributes.business_glossary_term: Capacity Price per Megawatt (MW) per Month
attributes.description: Contracted capacity payment in USD per MW per month for capacity-inclusive Power Purchase Agreements. Reflects the resource adequacy value of the contracted capacity. Null for energy-only contracts.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: contract_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the Power Purchase Agreement, typically including the counterparty name and project name (e.g., 'Sunrise Solar Farm PPA'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: contract_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the Power Purchase Agreement, used in counterparty communications, FERC filings, and ERP contract management. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA contract management module.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; SAP S/4HANA Contract Management

attributes.name: contract_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the Power Purchase Agreement. Draft indicates the contract is under negotiation; pending_approval awaits FERC or internal authorization; active means the contract is in force; suspended indicates a temporary halt; terminated reflects early cancellation; expired reflects natural end-of-term.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: contract_term_years
attributes.description: Total duration of the Power Purchase Agreement expressed in years. Used for IRP long-term resource planning, AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) calculations, and CAPEX amortization analysis.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; GAAP ASC 842 Lease Accounting

attributes.name: contract_type
attributes.description: Classification of the Power Purchase Agreement by pricing and delivery structure. Fixed-price contracts lock in a set $/MWh rate; index-linked contracts float with market indices (e.g., LMP); tolling agreements grant the buyer dispatch rights over a generation asset; unit-contingent contracts tie delivery to a specific generating unit's output; heat-rate contracts price energy relative to a fuel heat rate. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fixed_price|index_linked|tolling|unit_contingent|heat_rate|capacity_only — promote to reference product if additional types emerge]
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: contracted_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Maximum contracted generation capacity in Megawatts (MW) that the seller is obligated to make available under this Power Purchase Agreement. Used in NERC resource adequacy assessments and IRP capacity planning.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: contracted_energy_mwh
attributes.description: Total contracted energy volume in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) over the full term of the Power Purchase Agreement. Used for long-term supply portfolio management and IRP resource adequacy analysis.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this Power Purchase Agreement record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking per SOX and FERC record-keeping requirements.

attributes.name: credit_support_amount
attributes.description: Dollar value of credit support or collateral posted under this Power Purchase Agreement. Used for counterparty credit risk exposure monitoring and financial reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Reform; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; SOX

attributes.name: credit_support_type
attributes.description: Type of credit support or collateral arrangement required under this Power Purchase Agreement to mitigate counterparty credit risk. Relevant for SOX financial risk management and FERC credit requirements.
attributes.references: FERC Credit Reform; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; SOX

attributes.name: curtailment_rights
attributes.description: Specifies which party holds curtailment rights under the Power Purchase Agreement. Buyer curtailment allows the utility to reduce scheduled deliveries; seller curtailment allows the generator to reduce output; mutual curtailment permits either party. Relevant for Demand Response (DR) and grid reliability operations.

attributes.name: delivery_point
attributes.description: Named electrical delivery point or pricing node where energy is transferred under the Power Purchase Agreement (e.g., RTO/ISO hub, busbar, interconnection point). Aligns with LMP settlement nodes in the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) and Real-Time Market (RTM).
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; OATT (Open Access Transmission Tariff)

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the Power Purchase Agreement becomes legally binding and energy delivery obligations commence. Used in IRP resource adequacy analysis and long-term supply portfolio management.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: energy_price_per_mwh
attributes.description: Contracted energy price in USD per Megawatt-Hour (MWh) for fixed-price Power Purchase Agreements. For index-linked contracts, this represents the base or floor price. Null for tolling agreements where pricing is fuel-cost-based.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: execution_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which all parties signed and executed the Power Purchase Agreement. Distinct from the effective date; used for FERC filing timelines and contract audit trails.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the Power Purchase Agreement term ends and delivery obligations cease. Nullable for evergreen or open-ended agreements. Critical for IRP long-term supply portfolio planning and contract renewal workflows.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: ferc_docket_number
attributes.description: FERC-assigned docket number for the regulatory filing associated with this Power Purchase Agreement. Used for tracking FERC market-based rate authority approvals and compliance reporting.

attributes.name: ferc_filing_status
attributes.description: Current status of the FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission) market-based rate authority filing associated with this Power Purchase Agreement. Tracks regulatory approval lifecycle for wholesale market transactions.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: force_majeure_clause
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Power Purchase Agreement includes a force majeure clause that excuses performance obligations under extraordinary circumstances (natural disasters, grid emergencies, regulatory actions). True if clause is present.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Primary fuel or generation technology of the contracted resource. Used for Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance tracking, GHG emissions reporting, and IRP resource mix analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: solar|wind|hydro|nuclear|natural_gas|coal|oil|geothermal|biomass|storage|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA GHG Reporting Rule; State RPS Regulations; DOE Energy Information Administration

attributes.name: is_renewable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the contracted generation resource qualifies as renewable energy under applicable state Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) regulations. True if renewable; False if conventional. Drives REC (Renewable Energy Certificate) eligibility determination.
attributes.references: State RPS Regulations; DOE Renewable Energy Standards

attributes.name: minimum_take_mwh
attributes.description: Minimum energy volume in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) that the buyer is contractually obligated to take or pay for during each contract period. Represents the take-or-pay floor for financial settlement purposes.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.description: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) reliability region in which the contracted generation resource is located. Used for NERC compliance reporting and resource adequacy assessments. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NPCC|SERC|RFC|MRO|WECC|TRE|FRCC — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: price_index_reference
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the market price index used for index-linked Power Purchase Agreements (e.g., Day-Ahead LMP at a specific hub, Henry Hub natural gas index, ICE power index). Null for fixed-price contracts.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.description: Name of the generation project or facility that is the source of supply under this Power Purchase Agreement (e.g., 'Sunrise Solar Farm', 'Blue Ridge Wind Project'). Distinct from the contract name; identifies the physical asset.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; DOE Energy Information Administration

attributes.name: puc_approval_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Approval Date
attributes.description: Date on which the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) approved this Power Purchase Agreement. Null if approval is not required or not yet received.

attributes.name: puc_approval_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Approval Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this Power Purchase Agreement requires approval from the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) before becoming effective. True if PUC approval is required; False if the contract is exempt from state regulatory review.

attributes.name: rec_bundled
attributes.description: Indicates whether Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) are bundled with the energy delivery under this Power Purchase Agreement. True if RECs transfer with energy; False if RECs are unbundled or retained by the seller. Critical for RPS compliance accounting.
attributes.references: State RPS Regulations; NERC GATS (Generation Attribute Tracking System)

attributes.name: rec_quantity_annual
attributes.description: Expected annual quantity of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) transferred under this Power Purchase Agreement when rec_bundled is True. Measured in MWh-equivalent RECs. Used for RPS compliance portfolio management.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) ID
attributes.description: Reference to the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) market in which this Power Purchase Agreement is settled (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP). Governs LMP settlement and market rules.

attributes.name: settlement_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for financial settlement of this Power Purchase Agreement (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency contract management for cross-border PPAs.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: state_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code identifying the primary regulatory jurisdiction governing this Power Purchase Agreement. Determines applicable PUC oversight, RPS requirements, and state-level reporting obligations.

attributes.name: termination_provisions
attributes.description: Description of early termination rights, notice periods, and termination payment obligations under the Power Purchase Agreement. Captures key contractual terms for legal and regulatory compliance review.
attributes.references: EEI Master Power Purchase and Sale Agreement; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this Power Purchase Agreement record was most recently modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and data lineage per SOX and FERC record-keeping requirements.

products.name: capacity_obligation
products.description: Master record for capacity market obligations and commitments registered with an RTO/ISO (e.g., PJM RPM, MISO Planning Resource Auction, ISO-NE FCM). Tracks obligation period, committed MW, resource type, zone, auction clearing price ($/MW-day), performance penalty thresholds, and compliance status. Essential for resource adequacy planning and FERC capacity market reporting.
products.reference: RTO/ISO Capacity Market Rules (PJM RPM / MISO PRPA / ISO-NE FCM)

attributes.name: capacity_obligation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each capacity market obligation record registered with an RTO/ISO. Primary key for the capacity_obligation data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards

attributes.name: capacity_resource_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generation or demand response resource registered to fulfill this capacity obligation. Links to the asset or resource master record in the Asset Management domain.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: Capacity obligations often trigger capital investment decisions (generation upgrades, new builds, demand response infrastructure) to meet committed MW. Links obligation to the capital project for cost

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Capacity obligations must link to committed physical asset to validate installed capacity matches market commitment, track mandatory performance testing requirements, coordinate maintenance outages wi

attributes.name: ppa_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) contract under which this capacity obligation is fulfilled, if applicable. Links to the PPA contract master record. Null for obligations fulfilled by utility-owned generation assets.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; GAAP ASC 842 Lease Accounting

attributes.name: procurement_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.procurement_contract. Business justification: Capacity obligations depend on underlying procurement contracts for fuel supply, equipment maintenance, or tolling agreements that enable capacity delivery. Critical for cost allocation, performance g

attributes.name: transfer_agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to a bilateral capacity transfer agreement if this obligation has been partially or fully transferred to or from another market participant. Null if no transfer applies. Used for capacity position management and FERC market-based rate compliance.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the locational deliverability area (LDA), capacity zone, or planning zone within the RTO/ISO footprint where this obligation applies (e.g., PJM MAAC, MISO Zone 7, ISO-NE NEMA). Determines applicable clearing price and performance requirements.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: auction_clearing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the capacity auction cleared and this obligation was established. For bilateral transactions, the date the agreement was executed. Used as the principal business event date for financial recognition and FERC market-based rate reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; PJM RPM Tariff; GAAP ASC 606

attributes.name: auction_code
attributes.description: Reference to the capacity market auction event (e.g., PJM Base Residual Auction, MISO Planning Resource Auction, ISO-NE Forward Capacity Auction) from which this obligation was established. Links to the auction master record.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: auction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the auction mechanism through which this obligation was established. 'base_residual' is the primary annual auction; 'incremental' covers subsequent adjustment auctions; 'bilateral' covers negotiated capacity transactions; 'self_supply' covers vertically integrated utility self-commitment; 'reliability_must_run' covers RMR designations.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: capacity_qualification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the RTO/ISO formally qualified this resource to participate in the capacity market for the applicable delivery year. Marks the point at which the resource's UCAP value was certified and the obligation became binding.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: clearing_price_per_mw_day
attributes.description: The capacity auction clearing price in dollars per Megawatt per day ($/MW-day) at which this obligation was established. Multiplied by committed_mw and the number of days in the delivery year to determine total capacity revenue or cost. Classified confidential as commercially sensitive market pricing data.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: committed_mw
attributes.description: The quantity of capacity in Megawatts (MW) committed under this obligation as cleared in the capacity auction or bilaterally agreed. Represents the principal quantitative fact of the obligation. Used for resource adequacy compliance, FERC reporting, and IRP analysis.
attributes.references: NERC Glossary of Terms; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; PJM RPM Tariff

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current regulatory compliance status of the capacity obligation relative to RTO/ISO performance requirements and FERC market-based rate authority conditions. 'compliant' indicates all performance obligations are met; 'deficient' indicates a shortfall triggering non-performance charges; 'under_review' indicates an open RTO/ISO investigation; 'waived' indicates an approved force majeure or tariff waiver; 'exempt' indicates a regulatory exemption applies.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: curtailment_event_count
attributes.description: Number of RTO/ISO-declared capacity performance events (e.g., PJM Performance Assessment Hours, MISO Emergency Operating Procedures) during which this resource was called upon to perform within the current delivery year. Used for compliance tracking and non-performance charge calculation.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; MISO Emergency Operating Procedures; FERC Order 825

attributes.name: delivery_year
attributes.description: The RTO/ISO-defined delivery year (e.g., '2025/2026') during which the capacity obligation must be fulfilled. Typically spans June 1 through May 31 for PJM; aligns with the planning year used in the auction. Critical for resource adequacy planning and FERC capacity market reporting.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: eford_rate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Equivalent Forced Outage Rate on Demand (EFORd)
attributes.description: The Equivalent Forced Outage Rate on Demand (EFORd) applied to this resource for the delivery year, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0250 = 2.50%). Used by the RTO/ISO to derate installed capacity to Unforced Capacity (UCAP). Sourced from NERC GADS reporting and RTO/ISO capacity qualification processes.
attributes.references: NERC GADS Reporting; PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff

attributes.name: force_majeure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a force majeure event (True) has been declared for this obligation, potentially relieving the utility of non-performance charges for affected performance events. Triggers a separate RTO/ISO review and waiver process.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

attributes.name: installed_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The nameplate or installed capacity in Megawatts (MW) of the resource registered for this obligation, prior to any derating adjustments. Used as the baseline for UCAP calculations and resource adequacy assessments in MISO and ISO-NE markets.
attributes.references: NERC Generator Inventory; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: is_demand_response
attributes.description: Indicates whether this capacity obligation is fulfilled by a Demand Response (DR) resource (True) rather than a generation asset (False). DR capacity obligations are subject to different performance measurement rules under FERC Order 745 and RTO/ISO DR tariff provisions.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; PJM RPM DR Provisions; MISO DR Tariff

attributes.name: is_self_scheduled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this capacity obligation was established through a self-schedule (True) rather than through a competitive auction clearing (False). Self-scheduled resources bypass the auction clearing price and are committed at cost-of-service or bilateral rates. Relevant for vertically integrated utilities under state PUC jurisdiction.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; State PUC Rate Case Requirements

attributes.name: last_performance_test_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent RTO/ISO-administered or utility-conducted capacity performance test for the resource fulfilling this obligation. Used to verify continued eligibility and compliance with performance threshold requirements.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; MISO Tariff; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: locational_deliverability_area
attributes.description: The name or code of the Locational Deliverability Area (LDA) or sub-zone within the RTO/ISO footprint where this capacity obligation must be physically deliverable. Relevant for constrained zones with higher clearing prices. Used for transmission planning and resource adequacy analysis.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; NERC Transmission Planning Standards

attributes.name: non_performance_charge_amount
attributes.description: Cumulative non-performance charge amount in US Dollars (USD) assessed against this obligation for the current delivery year due to resource underperformance during capacity performance events. Used for financial exposure tracking, FERC reporting, and collections management.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; FERC Order 825; GAAP Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: non_performance_charge_rate
attributes.description: The penalty rate in dollars per Megawatt-hour ($/MWh) applied when the resource fails to perform during a capacity performance event below the performance threshold. Used to calculate potential financial exposure for compliance risk management and FERC reporting.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; FERC Order 825; MISO Tariff

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, RTO/ISO correspondence references, regulatory filing cross-references, or other contextual information relevant to this capacity obligation. Not used for structured data.

attributes.name: obligation_end_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the capacity obligation period concludes. Typically May 31 of the delivery year for PJM-style markets. Nullable for multi-year obligations with rolling terms. Used for expiry tracking and resource adequacy planning.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: obligation_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned by the RTO/ISO (e.g., PJM RPM obligation ID, MISO Planning Resource Auction ID, ISO-NE FCM commitment reference) that uniquely identifies this obligation in the market operator's system. Used for FERC reporting and RTO/ISO reconciliation.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: obligation_start_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the capacity obligation period begins and the utility must demonstrate resource availability. Typically June 1 of the delivery year for PJM-style markets. Used for compliance monitoring and IRP scheduling.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE Tariff

attributes.name: obligation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the capacity obligation. 'active' indicates the obligation is in force during the delivery year; 'pending' indicates awaiting RTO/ISO confirmation; 'suspended' indicates temporarily relieved; 'terminated' indicates early exit; 'expired' indicates the obligation period has concluded.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; PJM RPM Tariff

attributes.name: obligation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the capacity obligation by resource category. 'capacity_supply' covers generation assets; 'demand_response' covers DR programs; 'energy_efficiency' covers EE resources; 'import'/'export' cover inter-regional capacity transactions. Drives applicable performance standards and penalty calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; PJM RPM Tariff

attributes.name: performance_test_result_mw
attributes.description: The demonstrated output in Megawatts (MW) achieved during the most recent capacity performance test. Compared against committed_mw to assess compliance with the obligation and determine if non-performance charges apply.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; MISO Tariff; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: performance_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The minimum performance ratio (expressed as a decimal percentage, e.g., 0.9750 = 97.50%) that the resource must achieve during capacity performance events to avoid Non-Performance Charges. Defined by the RTO/ISO tariff for the applicable delivery year and resource type.
attributes.references: PJM Capacity Performance Tariff; MISO Tariff; ISO-NE FCM Tariff; FERC Order 825

attributes.name: planning_reserve_margin_pct
attributes.description: The RTO/ISO-mandated planning reserve margin (expressed as a decimal percentage, e.g., 0.1650 = 16.50%) applicable to this obligation's delivery year and zone. Used to verify that the utility's total capacity portfolio meets resource adequacy requirements for IRP and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; State PUC IRP Requirements

attributes.name: rec_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether the resource fulfilling this capacity obligation is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) under the applicable state Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS). Used for RPS compliance tracking and green energy procurement reporting.
attributes.references: State RPS Requirements; EPA Renewable Energy Programs; DOE REC Tracking Systems

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this capacity obligation record was first captured in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail and data lineage purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls; Enterprise Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this capacity obligation record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Internal Controls; Enterprise Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: resource_type
attributes.description: Technology classification of the resource fulfilling the capacity obligation. Used for resource adequacy portfolio analysis, RPS compliance tracking, and IRP reporting. Aligns with NERC Generator Inventory and FERC Form 1 resource classifications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: thermal|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|storage|demand_response|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC Generator Inventory; FERC Form 1; IRP Resource Adequacy Analysis

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Code
attributes.description: Code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization or Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) with which this capacity obligation is registered. Determines the applicable tariff, auction rules, and compliance framework. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|MISO|ISO-NE|NYISO|CAISO|SPP|ERCOT — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this capacity obligation record was sourced (e.g., ABB or GE Energy Management System, RTO/ISO market portal, SAP S/4HANA, or manual entry). Used for data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: Enterprise Data Governance Policy; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: total_capacity_revenue
attributes.description: Total expected capacity revenue in US Dollars (USD) for the full obligation period, calculated as clearing_price_per_mw_day × committed_mw × obligation days. Stored as a pre-computed contract value for financial planning, EBITDA forecasting, and FERC market-based rate filings. Classified confidential as commercially sensitive financial data.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; GAAP ASC 606 Revenue Recognition

attributes.name: unforced_capacity_mw
attributes.description: The Unforced Capacity (UCAP) value in Megawatts (MW) after applying the Equivalent Forced Outage Rate (EFORd) derating factor to the installed capacity. UCAP is the RTO/ISO-recognized capacity credit used for compliance verification and auction clearing. Distinct from committed_mw which reflects the cleared auction quantity.
attributes.references: PJM RPM Tariff; NERC EFORd Methodology; FERC Market-Based Rate Authority

products.name: energy_bid
products.description: Transactional record capturing individual energy bids and offers submitted to RTO/ISO day-ahead market (DAM) and real-time market (RTM). Stores bid type (energy, ancillary), resource ID, pricing node reference, bid interval (hourly or sub-hourly), bid price ($/MWh), bid quantity (MW), bid curve segments, market (DAM/RTM), submission timestamp, and acceptance/rejection status from the RTO/ISO. Core operational record for wholesale market participation. Note: virtual transactions (INCs/DECs/UTCs) may be captured here as a bid type in MVM scope but warrant a dedicated product at ECM scope for distinct lifecycle and settlement treatment.
products.reference: FERC Order 2222 / RTO/ISO Market Tariff Bid Submission

attributes.name: energy_bid_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each energy bid or offer record submitted to an RTO/ISO market. Serves as the primary key for the energy_bid data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: FERC Market-Based Rate Authority; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: cost_center_id
