attributes.description: Current workflow status of the performance evaluation record. Tracks progression from draft through approval and finalization.

attributes.name: evaluation_type
attributes.description: The type or frequency of the performance evaluation (quarterly for strategic suppliers, annual for standard vendors, project-based for major T&D construction and generation outage contractors, or contract renewal assessment).

attributes.name: evaluator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the person who conducted the vendor performance evaluation.

attributes.name: invoice_accuracy_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of vendor invoices that were accurate and required no correction or dispute during the evaluation period. Expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: invoice_accuracy_weight_percentage
attributes.description: The weighting percentage applied to invoice accuracy performance in the overall performance rating calculation. Default is 10.00%.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this vendor performance evaluation record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: material_rejection_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of received materials or services that failed quality inspection and were rejected during the evaluation period. Expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: on_time_delivery_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of purchase orders or deliverables delivered on or before the scheduled delivery date during the evaluation period. Expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: osha_recordable_incident_rate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Recordable Incident Rate
attributes.description: The number of OSHA recordable safety incidents per 200,000 work hours for contractor field crews during the evaluation period. Critical for T&D construction and generation outage contractors.

attributes.name: overall_performance_rating
attributes.description: Weighted overall performance rating on a 1.00 to 5.00 scale, calculated using configurable weighting: 30% delivery, 25% quality, 25% safety, 10% invoice accuracy, 10% diversity. Used for vendor qualification and contract renewal decisions.

attributes.name: preferred_vendor_list_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the vendor qualifies for inclusion on the preferred vendor list based on this performance evaluation. True if eligible, False if performance does not meet preferred vendor criteria.

attributes.name: quality_weight_percentage
attributes.description: The weighting percentage applied to quality performance (material rejection rate) in the overall performance rating calculation. Default is 25.00%.

attributes.name: safety_compliance_score
attributes.description: Overall safety compliance score based on adherence to utility safety protocols, completion of required safety training, and audit results. Expressed as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00).

attributes.name: safety_weight_percentage
attributes.description: The weighting percentage applied to safety performance (OSHA rate, EMR, compliance score) in the overall performance rating calculation. Default is 25.00%.

attributes.name: total_purchase_orders_evaluated
attributes.description: The total number of purchase orders or delivery events included in this performance evaluation period.

attributes.name: total_spend_amount
attributes.description: The total dollar amount spent with this vendor during the evaluation period. Used to weight vendor importance in strategic sourcing decisions.

products.name: material_reservation
products.description: Transactional record reserving specific materials from inventory stock against a planned work order, CAPEX project WBS element, or maintenance activity. Captures reservation number, material number, required quantity, reserved quantity, movement type (261 goods issue for order), requesting cost center or WBS element, requirement date, reservation status (open, partially issued, fully issued, cancelled), issuing storage location, and SAP reservation document number. Ensures material availability planning for planned maintenance outages, T&D construction projects, and storm restoration pre-staging. Drives the reserved quantity in inventory_stock and prevents over-commitment of critical spare parts.

attributes.name: material_reservation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the material reservation record. Primary key for the material reservation entity.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) project for which materials are being reserved. Links to the project master record for Transmission and Distribution (T&D) construction, generation plant upgrades, or other capital investment initiatives.

attributes.name: material_master_id
attributes.description: Reference to the material master record being reserved. Links to the specific material, equipment, spare part, or supply item from inventory that is being allocated for future use.

attributes.name: purchase_requisition_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.purchase_requisition. Business justification: Material reservations can be created directly from purchase requisitions before PO conversion (e.g., emergency work orders reserve materials while procurement is in progress). This links the reservati

attributes.name: requester_employee_id
attributes.description: Employee identifier for the person who created the material reservation. Links to the human resources system (SuccessFactors or Workday) for organizational hierarchy and authorization validation.

attributes.name: warehouse_id
attributes.description: Reference to the warehouse master record where the reserved material is physically stored. Links to the warehouse entity for detailed facility information, capacity, and operational attributes.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the work order for which materials are being reserved. Links to the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) work order record in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo that defines the maintenance or operational task requiring these materials.

attributes.name: batch_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer batch or lot number for batch-managed materials. Enables traceability for quality control, warranty claims, and regulatory compliance, particularly for critical spare parts, hazardous materials, and generation plant components.

attributes.name: closed_date
attributes.description: Date when the material reservation was closed and removed from active planning. Set when the reservation status transitions to fully issued or cancelled, marking the end of the reservations operational lifecycle.

attributes.name: cost_center_code
attributes.description: Financial accounting code identifying the organizational unit or functional area responsible for the costs associated with this material reservation. Used for Operations and Maintenance (O&M) expense allocation and Operating Expenditure (OPEX) tracking when materials are not charged to a Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) project.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the material reservation record was first created in the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. Audit timestamp capturing the initial transaction event in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the valuation amount. Typically USD for United States-based utility operations, but may vary for international subsidiaries or cross-border procurement.

attributes.name: deletion_indicator
attributes.description: Flag marking the reservation for deletion or archival. True when the reservation has been cancelled, superseded, or is no longer needed. Soft-delete flag that preserves the record for audit trail while excluding it from active operational views.

attributes.name: erp_document_number
attributes.description: Native document identifier from the source Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Provides traceability back to the originating system transaction for audit, reconciliation, and support purposes.

attributes.name: final_issue_indicator
attributes.description: Flag set by the issuing warehouse or planner to indicate that no additional material will be issued against this reservation, even if the full reserved quantity has not been withdrawn. Used to close reservations when requirements change or work is completed with less material than originally planned.

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: General Ledger (GL) account number to which the material cost will be posted when issued. Determines the financial statement line item and expense or asset category for Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) reporting and regulatory rate case cost studies.

attributes.name: goods_issue_completed_flag
attributes.description: Indicator that all required material has been issued from inventory against this reservation. True when issued quantity equals or exceeds reserved quantity and no further withdrawals are expected.

attributes.name: issued_quantity
attributes.description: Cumulative quantity of material that has been physically issued from inventory against this reservation. Tracks the amount already withdrawn via goods issue transactions (movement type 261 in SAP).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the material reservation record was most recently updated. Tracks changes to reservation status, quantities, or other attributes. Audit timestamp in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: material_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the material being reserved. The externally-known material code or Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) from the material master that identifies the specific item type.

attributes.name: movement_type
attributes.description: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) transaction code that defines the type of inventory movement when goods are issued against this reservation. Standard SAP movement type 261 represents goods issue for order, while other codes may apply for returns, scrapping, or transfers.

attributes.name: mutual_aid_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this material reservation supports mutual aid assistance to another utility. True when materials are being pre-staged or allocated for deployment to support neighboring utilities during major storm events or grid emergencies.
attributes.references: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Standards

attributes.name: plant_code
attributes.description: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) organizational unit code representing the physical location or operational facility where the material is reserved. Corresponds to generation plants, transmission substations, distribution service centers, or regional operations hubs in the utility network.

attributes.name: priority_code
attributes.description: Business priority level assigned to the material reservation. Determines the sequence for material allocation when inventory is constrained. Emergency and urgent priorities are used for storm restoration, outage response, and critical infrastructure repairs.

attributes.name: requester_name
attributes.description: Name of the employee, planner, or supervisor who created the material reservation. Identifies the person responsible for requesting the material allocation for the work order or project.

attributes.name: required_quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of material requested for reservation. Represents the full amount needed to complete the associated work order, Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) project, or maintenance activity.

attributes.name: requirement_date
attributes.description: Date by which the reserved material is needed at the work location or project site. Drives material availability planning, warehouse picking schedules, and logistics coordination for Transmission and Distribution (T&D) construction projects, planned maintenance outages, and storm restoration activities.

attributes.name: reservation_date
attributes.description: Date when the material reservation was created in the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. Represents the business event timestamp for the reservation transaction.

attributes.name: reservation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional information, special handling instructions, or business context related to the material reservation. May include details about material substitutions, delivery constraints, safety requirements, or coordination with field crews.

attributes.name: reservation_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the material reservation document. Externally-known unique number assigned by the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud) to track the reservation throughout its lifecycle.

attributes.name: reservation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the material reservation. Tracks progression from open (newly created), partially issued (some quantity issued), fully issued (all quantity issued), cancelled (reservation voided), to closed (reservation completed and archived).

attributes.name: reservation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the material reservation based on the business purpose. Distinguishes between work order reservations, Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) project reservations, maintenance activity reservations, storm restoration pre-staging, planned generation outage reservations, and emergency response reservations.

attributes.name: reserved_quantity
attributes.description: Actual quantity of material successfully reserved from available inventory stock. May differ from required quantity if insufficient stock is available. This quantity is committed and reduces the unrestricted stock available for other reservations.

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Unique serial number for serialized materials and equipment. Provides individual asset-level traceability for high-value components such as transformers, circuit breakers, meters, and generation equipment.

attributes.name: storage_location_code
attributes.description: Warehouse or storage location code within the plant from which the material will be issued. Identifies the specific inventory stocking point, yard, or storeroom holding the reserved material.

attributes.name: storm_event_reference
attributes.description: Identifier for the storm or emergency event associated with this material reservation. Used for storm restoration logistics, mutual aid coordination, and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) or Public Utility Commission (PUC) storm cost recovery reporting.
attributes.references: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Standards

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Standard unit in which the material quantity is expressed. Examples include each (EA), meter (M), kilogram (KG), liter (L), foot (FT), or other industry-standard units aligned with the material master base unit of measure.

attributes.name: valuation_amount
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the reserved material quantity. Calculated as reserved quantity multiplied by the material standard cost or moving average price. Used for inventory valuation, Work in Progress (WIP) tracking, and Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) project cost accumulation.

attributes.name: wbs_element
attributes.description: Hierarchical project structure code from the Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) project Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). Identifies the specific project phase, deliverable, or cost element to which this material reservation is charged. Used for project cost tracking and Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) capitalization.

attributes.name: superseded_material_reservation_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on material_reservation (superseded_material_reservation_id)

products.name: goods_issue
products.description: Transactional record capturing the physical issuance and consumption of materials from inventory stock against a work order, CAPEX project, cost center, or material reservation. Records goods issue document number, posting date, material reference (linked to material_master), issuing storage location (linked to warehouse), reservation reference (linked to material_reservation), receiving cost object (work order, WBS element, cost center, or asset number), issued quantity, unit of measure, movement type (261 goods issue for order, 262 reversal of goods issue, 201 goods issue for cost center, 281 goods issue for network/project), batch/lot number for traceable materials, issuing warehouse clerk, and SAP material document number. Triggers inventory stock position reduction and drives actual material cost posting to work orders and CAPEX projects. Critical for closing the inventory movement lifecycle (goods_receipt IN → material_reservation COMMIT → goods_issue OUT), supporting three-way match completion, work order costing, storm restoration material consumption tracking, and FERC/PUC cost reporting for rate case filings.

attributes.name: goods_issue_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the goods issue transaction. Primary key for the goods issue record.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the CAPEX project that consumed this material. Used for capital project cost tracking and AFUDC calculations.
attributes.references: GAAP, FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Goods issues charge material costs from inventory to consuming cost centers. Core cost accounting process for tracking departmental material consumption, maintenance costs, and operational expenses in

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Goods issues post to GL accounts for expense recognition or asset capitalization (CWIP). Required for proper FERC accounting treatment, distinguishing O&M expense from capital additions, and financial

attributes.name: goods_receipt_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.goods_receipt. Business justification: Goods issues should trace back to the original goods receipt for batch/serial number traceability, FIFO/LIFO costing, and quality issue root cause analysis. This is critical for regulated utility mate

attributes.name: issuing_employee_id
attributes.description: Employee identifier of the person who issued the material, used for accountability and audit trail.

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: Issuing materials to capitalize an asset (vs. expensing to work order) requires proper asset linkage for FERC account classification, regulatory asset base tracking, and depreciation calculation. Util

attributes.name: material_reservation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the material reservation record that committed this inventory for issuance. Links the goods issue to the upstream reservation.

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to metering.meter. Business justification: Tracks specific serialized meter issued from warehouse for field installation. Critical for asset lifecycle tracking, inventory reconciliation, and connecting supply chain to field operations. Utiliti

attributes.name: primary_goods_material_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the material master record identifying the specific material being issued from inventory.

attributes.name: warehouse_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the warehouse from which the material was issued.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the work order that consumed this material. Used for maintenance and operations cost tracking.
attributes.references: SAP ERP, Oracle WAM, IBM Maximo

attributes.name: batch_number
attributes.description: Batch or lot number for traceable materials, enabling traceability for quality control, warranty claims, and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this goods issue record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the valuation amount.

attributes.name: document_date
attributes.description: The date on the physical goods issue document, which may differ from the posting date. Used for audit and reconciliation purposes.

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period (month) within the fiscal year when the goods issue was posted.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year in which the goods issue was posted, used for financial period reporting and cost allocation.

attributes.name: gi_document_number
attributes.description: The externally-known goods issue document number generated by the ERP system (SAP material document number). Used for audit trail and cross-system reconciliation.

attributes.name: issue_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the goods issue transaction indicating whether it has been posted to inventory, reversed, pending approval, or cancelled.

attributes.name: issue_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the material was physically issued from the warehouse or storage location.

attributes.name: issued_quantity
attributes.description: The quantity of material issued from inventory stock. This is the principal quantitative fact for the goods issue transaction.

attributes.name: issuing_person_name
attributes.description: Name of the warehouse clerk or storekeeper who physically issued the material from inventory.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this goods issue record was last modified or updated in the system.

attributes.name: movement_type
attributes.description: SAP movement type code indicating the nature of the goods issue: 261 (goods issue for order), 262 (reversal of goods issue), 201 (goods issue for cost center), 281 (goods issue for network/project).

attributes.name: mutual_aid_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for mutual aid agreements if this material was issued to support another utility during emergency response.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments related to the goods issue transaction, capturing special handling instructions, exceptions, or additional context.

attributes.name: plant_code
attributes.description: The plant or facility code where the goods issue occurred. Used for multi-site inventory management and cost allocation.

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: The date when the goods issue transaction was posted to the financial and inventory ledgers. This is the principal business event timestamp for inventory valuation and cost accounting.

attributes.name: priority_code
attributes.description: Priority level of the goods issue request, used for expediting critical work orders or emergency restoration activities.

attributes.name: receiving_cost_object_type
attributes.description: The type of cost object receiving the material: work order (maintenance), CAPEX project (capital construction), cost center (operational expense), or asset (capitalization).

attributes.name: reversal_document_number
attributes.description: The document number of the reversal transaction if this goods issue was reversed. Null if not reversed.

attributes.name: reversal_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this goods issue has been reversed (movement type 262). True if reversed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: reversal_reason_code
attributes.description: Code indicating the reason for reversing the goods issue (e.g., incorrect quantity, wrong material, data entry error).

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Serial number for individually tracked materials or equipment, enabling asset-level traceability.

attributes.name: storage_location_code
attributes.description: The specific storage location code within the warehouse from which the material was issued.

attributes.name: storm_event_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the storm or emergency event if this goods issue is related to storm restoration or emergency response activities. Critical for tracking storm restoration material consumption for regulatory cost recovery.

attributes.name: three_way_match_completed_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the three-way match (purchase order, goods receipt, goods issue) has been completed for this material consumption. Critical for procurement-to-pay cycle closure.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the issued quantity (e.g., EA for each, FT for feet, LB for pounds, GAL for gallons).

attributes.name: valuation_amount
attributes.description: The total monetary value of the issued material calculated using standard cost or moving average price. This is the principal monetary fact for cost accounting.

attributes.name: wbs_element
attributes.description: The WBS element or network activity to which the material cost is charged for project-based consumption (movement type 281).

attributes.name: reversal_goods_issue_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on goods_issue (reversal_goods_issue_id)

domains.name: regulatory
domains.description: Manages all compliance obligations, tariff filings, rate cases, CPCN applications, IRP submissions, and regulatory reporting to PUCs, FERC, NERC, and EPA. Tracks dockets, testimony, prudency reviews, performance-based ratemaking (PBR), GHG/emissions compliance records, and cost recovery mechanisms including FAC and AFUDC. Ensures adherence to all jurisdictional requirements.

products.name: docket
products.description: Master record for each regulatory docket or proceeding filed with or assigned by a jurisdictional authority (PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA, PHMSA). Captures docket number, proceeding type (rate case, CPCN, tariff filing, IRP, rulemaking, complaint, prudency review, compliance investigation), filing jurisdiction, assigned regulatory body, docket status (open, active, suspended, closed), open/close dates, lead attorney, associated case manager, and key milestone dates. Serves as the SSOT anchor for all regulatory proceedings — the central hub to which rate cases, filings, orders, CPCN applications, IRP submissions, and prudency reviews connect.
products.reference: FERC/PUC Docket Management

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each regulatory docket or proceeding record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: appeal_deadline_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which a party must file a request for rehearing, appeal, or petition for review of the final order. Calculated from the final order date based on applicable statutory or regulatory timelines (e.g., 30 days for FERC rehearing requests under FPA Section 313). Null if no final order has been issued.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 313; State PUC Appeal Statutes; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: appeal_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the utility or any party has filed an appeal, request for rehearing, or petition for review of the final order in this docket. True if an appeal or rehearing request has been filed; False otherwise. Null if the docket has not yet reached a final order. Used to track post-order litigation exposure and contingent liability.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 313; Administrative Procedure Act; State PUC Appeal Rules

attributes.name: approved_rate_of_return
attributes.description: The overall rate of return on equity (ROE) approved by the regulatory authority in the final order, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0975 for 9.75%). Null until a final order is issued or if the proceeding is not a rate case. Critical for financial planning, EBITDA projections, and investor reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Policy Statement on Rate of Return; State PUC Rate of Return Orders; GAAP; SOX

attributes.name: approved_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: The total annual revenue requirement approved by the regulatory authority in the final order for a rate case, expressed in U.S. dollars. Null until a final order is issued or if the proceeding is not a rate case. Used for rate design, billing system updates, and financial reporting under GAAP and SOX.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts 18 CFR Part 101; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP; SOX

attributes.name: case_manager
attributes.description: Full name of the regulatory affairs case manager or project manager responsible for coordinating the utility's internal response, testimony preparation, and milestone tracking for this docket. Typically a regulatory affairs department employee.

attributes.name: close_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory authority formally closed the docket, typically upon issuance of a final order, dismissal, or withdrawal. Null if the docket remains open or active. Used to calculate proceeding duration and track regulatory cycle times.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: confidential_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the utility has requested confidential treatment for some or all documents filed in this docket under applicable protective order or FOIA exemption. True if confidential treatment has been requested; False if all filings are public. Used to enforce data access controls and document management policies.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 388; Freedom of Information Act (FOIA); State PUC Protective Order Rules

attributes.name: cpcn_project_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) Project Name
attributes.description: The name of the capital project or infrastructure investment for which a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) is being sought. Applicable only to CPCN proceedings. Examples: 'North Substation 345kV Upgrade', 'Gas Pipeline Replacement Phase 2'. Null for non-CPCN dockets.
attributes.references: State PUC CPCN Rules; Federal Power Act Section 203; Natural Gas Act

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this docket record was first created in the regulatory case management system or data lakehouse. Represents the audit trail creation event. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Policy; GAAP Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: customer_class_scope
attributes.description: Identifies the customer class(es) affected by this regulatory proceeding. For rate cases and tariff filings, indicates whether the proceeding impacts residential, commercial, industrial, or all customer classes. 'none' is used for proceedings that do not directly affect customer rates (e.g., NERC reliability compliance).
attributes.references: NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Schedule Definitions

attributes.name: docket_number
attributes.description: The official externally-assigned docket or case number issued by the jurisdictional authority (e.g., PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA). This is the primary business identifier used in all regulatory correspondence, filings, and orders. Examples: FERC Docket No. ER24-1234, PUC Case No. 24-0001-EL-RDR.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; NARUC Regulatory Practices

attributes.name: docket_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the regulatory docket or proceeding. 'open' indicates the docket has been initiated but no active proceedings are underway; 'active' indicates proceedings are actively ongoing; 'suspended' indicates proceedings are temporarily halted by order or stipulation; 'closed' indicates the proceeding has concluded with a final order or disposition; 'withdrawn' indicates the utility voluntarily withdrew the filing.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Rules of Practice

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the rates, tariff provisions, or regulatory requirements approved in this docket become effective and binding. For rate cases, this is the date new rates go into effect. For tariff filings, this is the tariff effective date. May be subject to refund if rates are accepted subject to refund under FERC practice.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 205; FERC 18 CFR Part 35; State PUC Tariff Rules

attributes.name: estimated_capex
attributes.description: The estimated capital expenditure (CAPEX) associated with the project or investment subject to this regulatory proceeding, expressed in U.S. dollars. Relevant for CPCN applications, IRP submissions, and major infrastructure rate cases. Used for prudency review tracking and AFUDC calculation. Null for proceedings not involving capital investment.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC; GAAP; State PUC CPCN Rules

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the utility filed the initial application, petition, or complaint with the regulatory authority. This is the principal business event date for the docket — the date the proceeding was formally initiated. Used for tracking regulatory deadlines, statutory timelines, and compliance milestones.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: final_order_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory authority issued the final order, decision, or ruling concluding the proceeding. Null if the docket is still open or active. Used to calculate total proceeding duration, track regulatory cycle times, and trigger downstream actions such as billing system rate updates and financial reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: ghg_program_ref
attributes.description: Reference to the specific GHG compliance program or emissions regulation at issue in an EPA or state environmental compliance docket (e.g., 'EPA Clean Air Act Section 111(d)', 'State GHG Cap-and-Trade Program', 'RPS Compliance'). Applicable to GHG and emissions compliance proceedings. Null for non-environmental dockets.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act; State GHG Regulations; DOE Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: hearing_date
attributes.description: The scheduled or actual start date of the formal evidentiary hearing before the regulatory authority or administrative law judge (ALJ). Null if no hearing is required or if the hearing has not yet been scheduled. Used for legal resource scheduling and milestone tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Hearing Rules

attributes.name: hearing_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the regulatory authority has ordered or is expected to require a formal evidentiary hearing (trial-type proceeding) for this docket. True if a hearing has been ordered or is anticipated; False if the proceeding is expected to be resolved on the written record. Impacts resource planning for testimony preparation and witness scheduling.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Hearing Rules; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: intervenor_count
attributes.description: The number of parties that have been granted intervenor status in the regulatory proceeding. Intervenors may include consumer advocates, industrial customers, environmental groups, competing utilities, and municipal entities. A higher intervenor count typically signals a more complex and contested proceeding. Updated as the proceeding progresses.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Intervention Rules

attributes.name: irp_planning_horizon_years
attributes.description: The planning horizon in years covered by an Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submission. Typically 10, 15, or 20 years. Applicable only to IRP dockets. Used to track long-range resource adequacy planning obligations and RPS compliance trajectories. Null for non-IRP proceedings.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Rules; DOE IRP Guidelines; RPS Statutes

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: The specific jurisdictional scope of the docket — identifies the state, federal, or regional authority. For state PUC proceedings, this is the two-letter state abbreviation (e.g., OH, CA, TX). For federal proceedings, this is 'FEDERAL'. For regional reliability proceedings, this is the NERC region (e.g., RFC, SERC, WECC).
attributes.references: NARUC; FERC; NERC Regional Entity Boundaries

attributes.name: lead_attorney
attributes.description: Full name of the lead regulatory attorney responsible for managing the utility's legal strategy and filings in this docket. Sourced from the legal department's matter management system. Used for workload tracking, attorney assignment reporting, and legal resource planning.
attributes.references: Internal Legal Department Records; State Bar Association

attributes.name: nerc_standard_ref
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Standard Reference
attributes.description: The specific NERC reliability standard(s) at issue in a NERC compliance investigation or reliability proceeding (e.g., 'FAC-001-3', 'CIP-007-6', 'TPL-001-4'). Applicable only to NERC reliability and compliance dockets. Null for non-NERC proceedings. Used for NERC compliance tracking and BES reliability reporting.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; NERC Rules of Procedure; FERC Order 693

attributes.name: open_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory authority formally opened or docketed the proceeding. May differ from the filing date if the authority assigns a docket number on a date subsequent to the initial filing. Marks the official commencement of the regulatory proceeding.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Internal priority classification assigned by the regulatory affairs department to indicate the strategic and financial significance of the docket to the utility. 'critical' indicates proceedings with major rate impact or compliance risk; 'high' indicates significant proceedings; 'medium' indicates routine proceedings; 'low' indicates minor or administrative filings. Used for resource allocation and executive reporting.

attributes.name: proceeding_subtype
attributes.description: Further classification within the proceeding type. For example, within a rate case: electric general rate case, gas general rate case, transmission rate case (OATT). Within tariff filings: initial tariff, tariff amendment, tariff cancellation. Provides granular categorization for reporting and analytics.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; State PUC Tariff Filing Rules

attributes.name: proceeding_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory proceeding or filing type. Defines the nature and purpose of the docket. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rate_case|cpcn|tariff_filing|irp|rulemaking|complaint|prudency_review|compliance_investigation|pbr|ghg_compliance|nerc_reliability|ppa_approval — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; NARUC Regulatory Practices; State PUC Rules of Practice

attributes.name: rate_case_type
attributes.description: Specifies the type of rate case proceeding. 'general' is a full cost-of-service rate case; 'limited' is a focused rate case on specific cost elements; 'formula' is a rate case using a pre-approved formula rate mechanism (common in FERC transmission); 'pbr' is a Performance-Based Ratemaking proceeding; 'settlement' is a negotiated settlement rate case. Null for non-rate-case dockets.
attributes.references: FERC 18 CFR Part 35; State PUC Rate Case Rules; NARUC PBR Guidelines

attributes.name: regulatory_body
attributes.description: The jurisdictional authority or governing body with which the docket is filed or by which it is assigned. Identifies the primary regulator overseeing the proceeding. Values include FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission), PUC (Public Utility Commission), NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation), EPA (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency), PHMSA (Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration), DOE (U.S. Department of Energy), OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FERC|PUC|NERC|EPA|PHMSA|DOE|OSHA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; PHMSA; State PUC Enabling Statutes

attributes.name: requested_rate_of_return
attributes.description: The overall rate of return on equity (ROE) requested by the utility in a rate case, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1050 for 10.50%). Null for non-rate-case proceedings. Used in rate case analytics, benchmarking against peer utilities, and PBR performance tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Policy Statement on Rate of Return; State PUC Rate of Return Guidelines; NARUC

attributes.name: requested_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: The total annual revenue requirement requested by the utility in a rate case filing, expressed in U.S. dollars. Represents the utility's claimed cost of service including OPEX, CAPEX recovery (depreciation), AFUDC, taxes, and allowed return on equity (ROE). Null for non-rate-case proceedings. This is a pre-decision requested amount, not the approved amount.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts 18 CFR Part 101; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: rto_iso_ref
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Reference
attributes.description: Identifies the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) relevant to this docket, if applicable. Examples: PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE. Relevant for FERC transmission rate cases, OATT filings, and market rule proceedings. Null for state-only or non-transmission proceedings.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000; FERC Order 888; OATT; RTO/ISO Tariffs

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Identifies whether the docket pertains to electric service, gas service, or both. Used to route dockets to the appropriate regulatory, legal, and operations teams and to support domain-specific regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: State PUC Service Classification Rules; FERC Jurisdictional Definitions

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the settlement agreement was executed or filed with the regulatory authority. Null if no settlement was reached. Used in conjunction with settlement_reached to track the timeline of negotiated resolutions and their impact on proceeding duration.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385.602; State PUC Settlement Rules

attributes.name: settlement_reached
attributes.description: Indicates whether the parties in the regulatory proceeding reached a negotiated settlement agreement in lieu of a fully litigated final order. True if a settlement was filed and approved; False if the proceeding was fully litigated or is still pending. Used to track settlement rates and litigation complexity across the regulatory docket portfolio.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385.602; State PUC Settlement Rules

attributes.name: statutory_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which the regulatory authority is legally required to issue a final order or decision under applicable statute or rule. For example, FERC has a 60-day default effective date for rate filings under FPA Section 205; state PUCs may have statutory deadlines for rate case decisions. Null if no statutory deadline applies.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 205/206; State PUC Enabling Statutes; FERC 18 CFR Part 35

attributes.name: subject_matter_summary
attributes.description: A concise narrative description of the subject matter, issues, and relief sought in the regulatory proceeding. Provides business context for users who need to understand the docket without reviewing the full filing. Sourced from the utility's regulatory affairs case management system or the regulatory authority's docket management system.
attributes.references: Internal Regulatory Affairs Records; FERC eLibrary; State PUC Docket Management Systems

attributes.name: test_year
attributes.description: The test year or test period used as the basis for cost-of-service calculations in a rate case. May be a historical test year (e.g., '2023'), a future test year (e.g., '2025'), or a hybrid period (e.g., '2023-2024'). Null for non-rate-case proceedings. Fundamental to rate case analytics and cost allocation studies.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Manual; State PUC Test Year Rules; FERC 18 CFR Part 35

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this docket record was most recently modified in the regulatory case management system or data lakehouse. Used for change data capture (CDC), ETL incremental loads, and audit trail compliance. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Policy; GAAP Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: utility_division
attributes.description: The utility operating division or service territory to which this docket primarily applies. Distinguishes between electric distribution, gas distribution, transmission, generation, or combined proceedings. Critical for segregating regulatory obligations by business unit and for rate case cost allocation.
attributes.references: FERC OATT; State PUC Service Territory Definitions; NARUC Utility Classification

products.name: rate_case
products.description: Master record for each general rate case or rate proceeding filed with a state PUC or FERC. Tracks test year, filing date, requested revenue requirement, allowed ROE, rate base, capital structure, final approved rates, effective date, and interim rate/true-up adjustments. For proceedings with Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) components, captures PBR metric definitions (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, customer satisfaction, renewable integration %, EE savings, DR curtailment), approved target values, measurement periods, actual performance values, variance calculations, and earned incentive or assessed penalty amounts per measurement period. Links to parent docket. Serves as the SSOT for the complete rate case lifecycle from filing through final order, including all PBR performance tracking and incentive/penalty calculations. Critical for revenue requirement management, cost recovery authorization, and regulatory performance reporting.
products.reference: PUC Rate Case Filing

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each rate case or rate proceeding record in the system. Serves as the primary key for the rate_case data product.

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent regulatory docket under which this rate case is filed. Links the rate case to its governing docket record for full proceeding traceability.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Docket Management Rules

attributes.name: test_year_financial_period_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Test Year Financial Period Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Rate cases use specific financial periods as test years for revenue requirement calculations. Finance teams extract closed period actuals for rate case cost studies. Direct period linkage enables auto

attributes.name: afudc_rate_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Rate Percentage
attributes.description: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) rate approved or proposed in this rate case, expressed as a percentage. AFUDC capitalizes the cost of financing construction work in progress (WIP) and is a component of rate base.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts 18 CFR Part 101; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: approved_rate_base
attributes.description: Total rate base authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order, expressed in US dollars. Reflects any disallowances, exclusions, or adjustments made by the regulator to the utility's requested rate base.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Base Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: approved_rates_effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the final approved rates became effective for billing purposes. May differ from the final order date if the order specifies a prospective effective date or if rates are subject to a tariff filing lag.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Rules; FERC eTariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: approved_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: Final annual revenue requirement authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order, expressed in US dollars. May differ from the requested amount due to regulatory adjustments, disallowances, or settlements.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: approved_roe_pct
attributes.description: Return on Equity (ROE) percentage authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order. The approved ROE directly determines the equity return component of the utility's allowed revenue requirement.
attributes.references: FERC Policy Statement on ROE; State PUC Capital Structure Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: approved_wacc_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Approved Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) Percentage
attributes.description: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) percentage authorized by the regulatory authority in the final order. Reflects the approved blended cost of debt and equity used to compute the authorized return on rate base.
attributes.references: FERC Capital Structure Guidelines; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: case_name
attributes.description: Official descriptive name or title of the rate case as filed with the regulatory authority (e.g., 'General Rate Case 2024 — Electric Distribution'). Used for identification in regulatory filings and internal reporting.
attributes.references: State PUC Filing Standards; FERC eTariff

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rate case proceeding. Tracks progression from initial filing through regulatory review, interim rate authorization, final order issuance, and case closure or appeal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|pending|suspended|interim_rates_in_effect|final_order_issued|closed|appealed — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385

attributes.name: case_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rate proceeding by regulatory scope and commodity. Distinguishes general rate cases from transmission-only, gas distribution, electric distribution, formula rate, or limited-scope proceedings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: general_rate_case|transmission_rate_case|gas_distribution_rate_case|electric_distribution_rate_case|formula_rate_case|limited_rate_case|cost_of_service|PBR_only — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; State PUC Tariff Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp indicating when this rate case record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the regulatory data product.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: debt_ratio_pct
attributes.description: Approved long-term debt percentage of the capital structure as authorized in the final order. Together with equity_ratio_pct defines the approved capital structure for rate-setting purposes.
attributes.references: FERC Capital Structure Guidelines; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

attributes.name: equity_ratio_pct
attributes.description: Approved equity percentage of the capital structure as authorized in the final order. Together with the debt ratio, defines the capital structure used to compute the weighted average cost of capital and allowed return.
attributes.references: FERC Capital Structure Guidelines; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

attributes.name: fac_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate case includes or establishes a Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) mechanism allowing automatic pass-through of fuel cost changes between rate cases. True = FAC mechanism included; False = no FAC.
attributes.references: State PUC FAC Rules; NARUC Fuel Adjustment Clause Guidelines

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the rate case application or tariff filing was formally submitted to the regulatory authority. Establishes the official start of the regulatory proceeding and triggers statutory review deadlines.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act §205; State PUC Filing Rules

attributes.name: filing_jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code identifying the state PUC jurisdiction where this rate case is filed (e.g., 'CA', 'TX', 'NY'). Null for FERC-only proceedings.

attributes.name: final_order_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory authority issued the final order concluding the rate case proceeding. Marks the official end of the adjudicatory phase and establishes the effective date for approved rates.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385

attributes.name: interim_rate_effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which interim rates became effective pending the final order. Interim rates are provisional rates authorized by the regulator to allow the utility to begin collecting adjusted revenues before the proceeding concludes.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act §205(e); State PUC Interim Rate Rules

attributes.name: interim_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: Annual revenue requirement authorized on an interim basis pending the final order, expressed in US dollars. Subject to refund or true-up adjustment once the final order is issued.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act §205(e); State PUC Interim Rate Rules

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing supplementary information, regulatory conditions, compliance obligations, or material facts associated with the rate case that are not captured in structured fields (e.g., specific disallowances, conditions of approval, appeal status details).

attributes.name: pbr_actual_value
attributes.description: Actual measured performance value achieved by the utility for the PBR metric during the measurement period. Compared against pbr_target_value to determine variance and calculate earned incentives or assessed penalties.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework; IEEE 1366

attributes.name: pbr_incentive_penalty_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) Incentive or Penalty Amount (USD)
attributes.description: Dollar amount of the earned incentive (positive) or assessed penalty (negative) resulting from the PBR performance variance for the measurement period. Directly impacts the utility's allowed revenue recovery.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: pbr_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rate case includes a Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) component with defined metrics, targets, and incentive/penalty mechanisms. True = PBR component present; False = traditional cost-of-service only.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: pbr_measurement_period_end
attributes.business_glossary_term: Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) Measurement Period End Date
attributes.description: End date of the PBR performance measurement period. Together with pbr_measurement_period_start defines the evaluation window for PBR metric assessment.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: pbr_measurement_period_start
attributes.business_glossary_term: Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) Measurement Period Start Date
attributes.description: Start date of the PBR performance measurement period during which the utility's actual performance is evaluated against approved targets. Populated only when pbr_indicator is True.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: pbr_metric_type
attributes.description: Type of PBR performance metric tracked in this rate case. Common metrics include SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index), SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index), CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index), customer satisfaction scores, renewable integration percentage, Energy Efficiency (EE) savings, and Demand Response (DR) curtailment. Populated only when pbr_indicator is True. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAIDI|SAIFI|CAIDI|customer_satisfaction|renewable_integration_pct|EE_savings|DR_curtailment|GHG_emissions — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IEEE 1366 (Reliability Indices); State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: pbr_target_value
attributes.description: Approved target value for the PBR metric defined in pbr_metric_type for the measurement period. Represents the performance threshold the utility must achieve to earn incentives or avoid penalties (e.g., SAIDI target of 90 minutes, customer satisfaction score of 85).
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework; IEEE 1366

attributes.name: pbr_variance
attributes.description: Calculated variance between the PBR actual value and the PBR target value (actual minus target). A positive variance may indicate over-performance (incentive-eligible) or under-performance depending on the metric direction convention.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Identifies the jurisdictional authority governing this rate case: FERC for interstate transmission and wholesale rates, state PUC for retail distribution rates, or dual for proceedings with both jurisdictional components.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act §205-206; State Public Utility Acts; FERC OATT

attributes.name: requested_rate_base
attributes.description: Total rate base (net plant in service plus working capital allowances) requested by the utility in its filing, expressed in US dollars. Rate base is the foundation for calculating the allowed return on equity and overall revenue requirement.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Base Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: requested_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: Total annual revenue requirement requested by the utility in its initial rate case filing, expressed in US dollars. Represents the total cost of service the utility seeks to recover through rates, including O&M, depreciation, taxes, and return on rate base.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: requested_roe_pct
attributes.description: Return on Equity (ROE) percentage requested by the utility in its rate case filing. Represents the equity return component of the weighted average cost of capital used to calculate the allowed return on rate base.
attributes.references: FERC Policy Statement on ROE; State PUC Capital Structure Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: requested_wacc_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Requested Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) Percentage
attributes.description: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) percentage requested by the utility, reflecting the blended cost of debt and equity in the proposed capital structure. Used to calculate the overall allowed return on rate base.
attributes.references: FERC Capital Structure Guidelines; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; GAAP

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the settlement agreement was executed by all parties. Populated only when settlement_indicator is True. Used to track the timeline of negotiated resolutions.
attributes.references: State PUC Settlement Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR §385.602

attributes.name: settlement_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rate case was resolved through a negotiated settlement agreement between the utility and intervening parties rather than a fully litigated final order. True = settled; False = fully litigated.
attributes.references: State PUC Settlement Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR §385.602

attributes.name: test_year_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the test year used to establish the revenue requirement and rate base. Together with test_year_start_date defines the 12-month test period for cost-of-service analysis.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; State PUC Test Year Rules

attributes.name: test_year_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the test year (historical or future) used to establish the revenue requirement and rate base in this rate case. The test year is the 12-month period whose costs and revenues form the basis for rate-setting.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; State PUC Test Year Rules

attributes.name: test_year_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test year is based on historical recorded data, a future projected period, or a hybrid combining historical actuals with known and measurable adjustments.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: true_up_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of the true-up adjustment calculated as the difference between interim rates collected and the final approved revenue requirement. A positive value indicates a refund owed to customers; a negative value indicates additional recovery owed to the utility.
attributes.references: State PUC True-Up Rules; FERC Refund Rules 18 CFR §35.19a

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp indicating when this rate case record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; Internal Data Governance Policy

products.name: tariff_schedule
products.description: Master record for each approved tariff schedule, rate schedule, or tariff sheet on file with a regulatory authority. Captures tariff number, schedule type (electric residential, commercial TOU, CPP, gas distribution, OATT, NEM), effective date, superseded date, jurisdiction, approval order reference, and rate components (energy charge, demand charge, customer charge, FAC rider). Serves as the regulatory SSOT for approved tariff structures distinct from the billing domain's operational rate application.
products.reference: FERC OATT / PUC Tariff Filing

attributes.name: tariff_schedule_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each tariff schedule record in the regulatory master. Serves as the primary key for the tariff_schedule data product on the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: approval_commission_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.commission_order. Business justification: Tariff schedules are approved by commission orders. The tariff_schedule table currently has approval_order_number as STRING; this should be normalized to a FK relationship. Remove approval_order_numbe

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: Tariff schedules are approved under regulatory dockets. The tariff_schedule table currently has docket_number as STRING; this should be normalized to a FK relationship. Remove docket_number STRING and

attributes.name: effective_financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Tariff effective dates must align with financial reporting periods for revenue recognition and regulatory accounting. Revenue accounting maps tariff schedules to financial periods for monthly revenue

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate case proceeding that established or last modified this tariff schedule. Links to the rate case master record for full regulatory proceeding context including testimony, prudency reviews, and cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Management; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: superseded_by_tariff_tariff_schedule_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the tariff_schedule record that replaced this schedule. Enables navigation of the tariff version chain for historical rate reconstruction and regulatory audit. Null if this schedule has not been superseded.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: applicable_season
attributes.description: The seasonal applicability of this tariff schedule or its rate components. Many utility tariffs have differentiated summer and winter rates reflecting seasonal demand patterns and fuel costs. 'All_year' indicates no seasonal differentiation.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Design Standards; State PUC Seasonal Rate Tariff Provisions

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory authority issued the order approving this tariff schedule. Null for schedules that are pending approval or were withdrawn prior to approval.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: commodity_type
attributes.description: The energy commodity covered by this tariff schedule. Distinguishes electric service tariffs from natural gas distribution tariffs, or combined service offerings where applicable.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; AGA Rate Reporting Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this tariff schedule record was first created in the regulatory data product. Provides the audit trail for record origination in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP Record Retention Requirements

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary rate components in this tariff schedule (e.g., 'USD'). Ensures unambiguous currency context for rate values, particularly relevant for utilities operating across jurisdictions.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: customer_charge
attributes.description: The fixed monthly customer charge (in dollars) applicable to all customers on this tariff schedule regardless of consumption or demand. Recovers fixed costs of metering, billing, and service connection. Also referred to as the basic service charge or meter charge.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Design Standards; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: demand_charge_rate
attributes.description: The approved demand charge rate expressed in dollars per kilowatt ($/kW) of measured peak demand. Applicable to commercial and industrial tariff schedules with demand metering. Null for residential schedules without demand billing.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Design Standards; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: demand_threshold_kw
attributes.description: The minimum or maximum kilowatt (kW) demand threshold that determines eligibility for this tariff schedule. Customers above or below this threshold may be required or eligible to take service under a different schedule. Used in rate class assignment and billing validation.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Design Standards; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: dr_program_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this tariff schedule includes or is associated with a Demand Response (DR) or Demand-Side Management (DSM) program provision. True if customers on this schedule are eligible for or subject to DR curtailment events and associated incentives or penalties.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; State PUC DR Program Tariff Provisions; DOE DSM Policy

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this tariff schedule becomes legally effective and applicable to customers, as approved by the regulatory authority. This is the binding start date for rate application and billing purposes.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: energy_charge_rate
attributes.description: The approved volumetric energy charge rate expressed in dollars per kilowatt-hour ($/kWh) for electric tariffs or dollars per therm ($/therm) or dollars per MCF ($/MCF) for gas tariffs. Represents the core consumption-based component of the rate structure.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Design Standards; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: energy_charge_unit
attributes.description: The unit of measure associated with the energy charge rate (e.g., kWh for residential electric, MWh for large commercial/industrial, therm or MCF for gas distribution). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of the energy_charge_rate value.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; AGA Rate Reporting Standards; NARUC

attributes.name: fac_rider_rate
attributes.description: The current approved Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) rider rate in dollars per kWh or therm, applied as a pass-through adjustment to recover actual fuel and purchased power costs above or below the base rate. Updated periodically per regulatory approval.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC FAC Tariff Provisions; NARUC

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which this tariff schedule was formally filed with the regulatory authority. Establishes the official filing record for docket tracking and regulatory compliance timelines.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: filing_state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state code (ISO 3166-2:US) identifying the state in which this tariff is filed. Used for multi-state utility jurisdictional reporting and rate case management. Null for FERC-jurisdictional interstate tariffs.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-2:US; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: interruptible_service
attributes.description: Indicates whether this tariff schedule provides interruptible service, where the utility retains the right to curtail or interrupt supply during system emergencies or peak demand events in exchange for a discounted rate. Common in large commercial and industrial gas and electric tariffs.
attributes.references: FERC Order 636; State PUC Interruptible Service Tariff Provisions; AGA

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: The regulatory jurisdiction under which this tariff schedule is filed and approved (e.g., 'FERC', 'CA PUC', 'TX PUC', 'NY PSC'). Identifies the governing authority responsible for tariff approval and oversight.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this tariff schedule record was most recently modified in the regulatory data product. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP Record Retention Requirements

attributes.name: minimum_bill_amount
attributes.description: The minimum monthly bill amount (in dollars) guaranteed under this tariff schedule, regardless of actual consumption. Ensures recovery of fixed costs for customers with very low usage. Null if no minimum bill provision applies.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Design Standards; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: nem_export_rate
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Energy Metering (NEM) Export Credit Rate
attributes.description: The approved credit rate in dollars per kWh applied to excess energy exported to the grid by customers with Distributed Energy Resources (DER) under Net Energy Metering (NEM) tariff schedules. Null for non-NEM schedules.
attributes.references: State PUC NEM Tariff Provisions; FERC Order 2222; DOE DER Policy

attributes.name: pbr_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this tariff schedule is subject to Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) mechanisms, where utility revenue or earnings are tied to performance metrics such as reliability (SAIDI/SAIFI), customer satisfaction, or clean energy targets. True if PBR provisions apply.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Ratemaking Guidelines

attributes.name: rate_design_type
attributes.description: The rate design methodology applied in this tariff schedule. Distinguishes flat rates, tiered/inclining block rates, Time-of-Use (TOU), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP), Real-Time Pricing (RTP), and declining block structures. Drives billing calculation logic in Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: flat|tiered|tou|cpp|rtp|inclining_block|declining_block — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Design Standards; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: schedule_description
attributes.description: Full narrative description of the tariff schedule as it appears in the approved tariff filing, including applicability conditions, service limitations, and special provisions. Provides the complete regulatory text context for compliance and customer communication purposes.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: schedule_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the tariff schedule as it appears in the approved tariff book (e.g., 'Residential Service', 'General Service Time-of-Use', 'Net Energy Metering', 'Open Access Transmission Tariff'). Used for display and reporting purposes.
attributes.references: NARUC Regulatory Accounting; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the tariff schedule in the regulatory approval and operational workflow. 'Pending' indicates filed but not yet approved; 'Approved' indicates regulatory approval received; 'Effective' indicates currently in force; 'Superseded' indicates replaced by a newer schedule; 'Withdrawn' indicates filing withdrawn; 'Suspended' indicates temporarily suspended by regulatory order.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: schedule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the tariff schedule by service and rate design category. Distinguishes electric residential, commercial Time-of-Use (TOU), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP), gas distribution, Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT), Net Energy Metering (NEM), and demand response schedules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: electric_residential|electric_commercial|electric_tou|electric_cpp|gas_distribution|oatt|nem|demand_response — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 888 (OATT); State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: service_class
attributes.description: The customer service class to which this tariff schedule applies. Segments the tariff applicability by customer category (e.g., residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, street lighting, transmission). Aligns with PUC-approved rate class definitions.
attributes.references: NARUC Regulatory Accounting; State PUC Rate Case Filings

attributes.name: special_conditions
attributes.description: Narrative description of any special conditions, eligibility restrictions, or limitations associated with this tariff schedule (e.g., minimum contract demand, geographic restrictions, equipment requirements, enrollment caps for NEM or DR programs).
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: superseded_date
attributes.description: The date on which this tariff schedule was superseded by a newer approved schedule or withdrawn from effect. Null if the schedule is currently effective. Used to maintain the full historical record of approved tariff structures for regulatory audit and retroactive billing adjustments.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: tariff_book_section
attributes.description: The section or part of the utility's tariff book in which this schedule is filed (e.g., 'Part A - Electric Service', 'Part B - Gas Service', 'Part C - Transmission'). Supports navigation of the regulatory tariff document structure.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: tariff_number
attributes.description: The official tariff or rate schedule number as assigned by the regulatory authority (e.g., PUC or FERC). This is the externally-known identifier referenced in regulatory filings, dockets, and customer bills (e.g., 'Schedule E-1', 'Rate Schedule 10', 'OATT Schedule 1').
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: tariff_sheet_number
attributes.description: The specific tariff sheet or leaf number within the utility's tariff book as filed with the regulatory authority. Tariff books are organized by numbered sheets; this field identifies the precise sheet(s) containing this schedule's terms and conditions.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: territory_code
