attributes.description: Code identifying the utility's service territory or operating division to which this tariff schedule applies. Relevant for multi-territory utilities with distinct rate zones or operating companies filing separate tariffs with different PUCs.
attributes.references: State PUC Service Territory Definitions; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: tou_offpeak_rate
attributes.description: The approved off-peak energy charge rate in dollars per kWh for Time-of-Use (TOU) tariff schedules. Applied during hours outside the defined peak period. Null for non-TOU schedules.
attributes.references: State PUC TOU Tariff Provisions; NARUC Rate Design Standards

attributes.name: tou_peak_end_time
attributes.description: The end time of the on-peak pricing period for Time-of-Use (TOU) tariff schedules, expressed in HH:MM 24-hour format. Null for non-TOU tariff schedules. Paired with tou_peak_start_time to define the peak billing window.
attributes.references: State PUC TOU Tariff Provisions; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: tou_peak_rate
attributes.description: The approved on-peak energy charge rate in dollars per kWh for Time-of-Use (TOU) tariff schedules. Applied during the defined peak period hours. Null for non-TOU schedules.
attributes.references: State PUC TOU Tariff Provisions; NARUC Rate Design Standards

attributes.name: tou_peak_start_time
attributes.description: The start time of the on-peak pricing period for Time-of-Use (TOU) tariff schedules, expressed in HH:MM 24-hour format. Null for non-TOU tariff schedules. Used in billing systems to apply differentiated energy charges by time of day.
attributes.references: State PUC TOU Tariff Provisions; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1366

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this tariff schedule, incremented each time the schedule is revised and re-filed. Version 1 represents the original approved schedule. Supports version chain tracking alongside the superseded_by_tariff_id self-reference.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: voltage_level
attributes.description: The voltage level at which service is delivered under this tariff schedule. Determines applicable line loss factors and delivery charges. Secondary voltage applies to most residential and small commercial customers; primary and transmission voltage applies to large industrial customers taking service at higher voltages.
attributes.references: IEEE Std C57; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

products.name: filing
products.description: Transactional record of each formal document or submission filed with a regulatory body (PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA, DOE, PHMSA). Captures filing type (initial application, testimony, exhibit, compliance filing, annual report, NERC reliability standard filing, EPA emissions report), filing date, filer name, filing status (draft, submitted, accepted, rejected, superseded), regulatory body, associated docket, document reference number, and confidentiality designation. For testimony filings (direct, rebuttal, surrebuttal, errata), additionally captures witness name, witness affiliation (utility, intervenor, PUC staff, independent expert), testimony subject matter (revenue requirement, rate design, capital structure, depreciation, demand forecast), exhibit list, and cross-examination schedule. Links to parent docket. Serves as the SSOT for all documents submitted to regulatory authorities, including the complete evidentiary testimony record for rate cases and contested proceedings.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: cross_examination_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date on which the witness is available for cross-examination by parties to the proceeding. Populated for testimony filings as part of the hearing schedule management. Null for non-testimony filings.

attributes.name: document_title

attributes.name: document_url
attributes.description: Uniform Resource Locator (URL) or document management system path pointing to the filed document in the utility's internal document repository or the regulatory body's public docket system. Enables direct retrieval of the source document.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the rates, tariff provisions, or regulatory requirements established by the filing become operative. For tariff filings, this is the date new rates take effect. For compliance filings, this is the date the compliance obligation is satisfied.

attributes.name: epa_regulation_citation
attributes.description: Citation to the specific U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulation or rule (e.g., 40 CFR Part 75 for acid rain emissions, Clean Air Act Section 111(d)) under which this filing is submitted. Populated for EPA emissions reports and environmental compliance filings.

attributes.name: exhibit_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated or delimited list of exhibit identifiers (e.g., Exhibit A, Exhibit 1, Schedule 1) attached to or sponsored by this filing. Captures the evidentiary exhibit inventory associated with the submission for record completeness.

attributes.name: filer_name

attributes.name: filer_role

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The official date on which the filing was submitted to the regulatory body. This is the principal business event date used for compliance deadline tracking, tariff effective date calculations, and regulatory calendar management.

attributes.name: filing_description

attributes.business_glossary_term: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Reporting Period Start Date
attributes.description: Start date of the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reporting period covered by this filing. Applicable to EPA GHG emissions reports and environmental compliance submissions under the Clean Air Act.
attributes.references: U.S. EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) 40 CFR Part 98

attributes.name: internal_reference_number
attributes.description: Utility-assigned internal tracking number for the filing, used to cross-reference the submission in internal document management and regulatory affairs systems prior to or independent of the regulatory body's assigned number.

attributes.name: is_testimony
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this filing is a formal witness testimony submission (direct, rebuttal, surrebuttal, or errata testimony) as opposed to a non-testimony filing such as an application, exhibit, or compliance report. Drives testimony-specific attribute population.
attributes.references: State PUC Hearing Procedures; FERC Rules of Practice 18 CFR Part 385

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state abbreviation identifying the state jurisdiction applicable to this filing. Populated for state PUC filings; may be null for federal filings (FERC, NERC, EPA) that are not state-specific.
attributes.references: NARUC; State PUC Jurisdictional Rules; ISO 3166-2:US

attributes.name: nerc_standard_number
attributes.description: Identifier of the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) reliability standard (e.g., CIP-002, FAC-001, TPL-001) to which this filing pertains. Populated for NERC compliance filings and reliability standard submissions.
attributes.references: NERC Rules of Procedure; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: page_count
attributes.description: Total number of pages in the filed document. Used for document management, completeness verification, and regulatory record-keeping.

attributes.name: pbr_mechanism_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this filing involves or establishes a performance-based ratemaking (PBR) mechanism, linking utility revenue or earnings to performance metrics such as reliability (SAIDI/SAIFI), customer satisfaction, or clean energy targets.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: prudency_review_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this filing is subject to a regulatory prudency review of capital expenditures or operational costs. Prudency reviews assess whether utility expenditures were made in a reasonable and prudent manner for cost recovery purposes.
attributes.references: State PUC Prudency Review Standards; NARUC

attributes.name: rate_case_year
attributes.description: The test year or rate case year associated with this filing, representing the calendar or fiscal year for which rates or revenue requirements are being established. Applicable to rate case filings, IRP submissions, and annual reports.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Manual; State PUC Rate Case Procedures

attributes.name: regulatory_body
attributes.description: The governmental or quasi-governmental authority to which the filing is submitted. Identifies the jurisdictional regulator: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), State Public Utility Commission (PUC), U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), or Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FERC|NERC|EPA|PUC|DOE|PHMSA|OSHA — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; DOE; PHMSA; OSHA; NARUC

attributes.name: requested_rate_increase_pct
attributes.description: Percentage rate increase requested in this filing relative to currently approved rates. Applicable to rate case and tariff amendment filings. Used for regulatory impact analysis and public reporting.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Manual; State PUC Rate Case Procedures

attributes.name: response_due_date
attributes.description: Deadline by which the utility or other parties must respond to a regulatory body's data request, deficiency letter, or order related to this filing. Critical for compliance deadline tracking and regulatory calendar management.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: revenue_requirement_amount
attributes.description: Total revenue requirement amount (in USD) proposed or established by this filing. Applicable to rate case applications and revenue requirement testimony filings. Represents the total annual revenue the utility is authorized or requesting to collect from customers.
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Manual; State PUC Rate Case Procedures; FERC 18 CFR Part 35

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: Method by which the filing was transmitted to the regulatory body. Most modern filings are submitted electronically via FERC's eFiling system or state PUC e-filing portals; legacy or emergency filings may be submitted by paper, hand delivery, or email.
attributes.references: FERC eFiling Rules 18 CFR Part 385.2001; State PUC Electronic Filing Rules

attributes.name: testimony_subject
attributes.description: Describes the primary regulatory topic addressed by the testimony. Common subjects include revenue requirement, rate design, capital structure, depreciation, demand forecast, cost of capital, performance-based ratemaking (PBR), and demand-side management (DSM). Null for non-testimony filings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: revenue_requirement|rate_design|capital_structure|depreciation|demand_forecast|cost_of_capital|pbr|dsm|ghg_compliance|fuel_adjustment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NARUC Rate Case Manual; State PUC Rate Case Procedures

attributes.name: testimony_type
attributes.description: For testimony filings, classifies the stage of the evidentiary record at which the testimony is submitted. 'direct' is the initial witness statement; 'rebuttal' responds to opposing direct testimony; 'surrebuttal' responds to rebuttal testimony; 'errata' corrects errors in previously filed testimony. Null for non-testimony filings.
attributes.references: State PUC Hearing Procedures; FERC Rules of Practice 18 CFR Part 385

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this filing record in the regulatory data management system. Used to detect changes, support incremental ETL processing, and maintain audit trail integrity.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: witness_affiliation
attributes.description: Organizational affiliation of the testifying witness, indicating which party in the proceeding the witness represents. Distinguishes utility witnesses from intervenor, PUC staff, and independent expert witnesses for evidentiary record management.
attributes.references: State PUC Hearing Procedures; FERC Rules of Practice 18 CFR Part 385

attributes.name: witness_name
attributes.description: Full name of the expert witness sponsoring the testimony filing. Populated only for testimony-type filings. Used to track the evidentiary record and cross-examination schedule in rate cases and contested proceedings.
attributes.references: State PUC Hearing Procedures; FERC Rules of Practice 18 CFR Part 385

products.name: cpcn_application
products.description: Master record for each Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) application filed for new generation, transmission, or distribution infrastructure. Tracks project name, applied capacity (MW or miles), fuel/technology type, service territory, filing date, environmental review status, PUC/FERC approval status, certificate issuance date, conditions of approval, and associated capital project reference. Essential for tracking regulatory authorization of major capital investments.
products.reference: PUC CPCN Proceeding

attributes.name: cpcn_application_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) Application ID
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each CPCN application record in the regulatory data product. Primary key for the cpcn_application table in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Filing Standards

attributes.name: approval_commission_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.commission_order. Business justification: CPCN applications are approved or denied by commission orders. The cpcn_application table should reference the commission_order that issued the final decision. This is a standard parent-child relation

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated capital project record in the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) or ERP system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA or Oracle WAM/Maximo). Links the regulatory authorization to the capital expenditure (CAPEX) project for financial tracking including AFUDC and WIP accounting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Capital Project Management; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: CPCN applications are filed under regulatory dockets. The cpcn_application table currently has docket_number as STRING; this should be normalized to a FK relationship. Remove docket_number STRING and

attributes.name: interconnection_request_id
attributes.description: External identifier assigned by the RTO/ISO or transmission provider for the associated generator or transmission interconnection request. Links the CPCN regulatory authorization to the parallel interconnection study process.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2003; FERC Order 1000; RTO/ISO Interconnection Procedures

attributes.name: irp_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.irp_submission. Business justification: CPCN applications should demonstrate alignment with the utility's Integrated Resource Plan. The cpcn_application table has irp_alignment_flag BOOLEAN; when true, there should be a FK to the specific i

attributes.name: party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the legal entity (utility operating company or subsidiary) filing the CPCN application. Supports multi-jurisdictional utilities with multiple operating companies filing under different PUC jurisdictions.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Filing Standards; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: primary_asset_master_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_master. Business justification: CPCN applications approve construction of specific major assets (transmission lines, substations, generation units). Links regulatory approval to the primary asset constructed. Essential for tracking

attributes.name: acceptance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory agency formally accepted the CPCN application as complete and docketed it for review. Distinct from filing_date; acceptance triggers the official statutory review period.
attributes.references: State PUC Rules of Practice; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 CFR Part 385)

attributes.name: application_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the CPCN application within the regulatory proceeding. Tracks progression from internal drafting through PUC/FERC review to final disposition. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|pending_review|evidentiary_hearing|approved|conditionally_approved|denied|withdrawn|suspended — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Rules of Practice; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 CFR Part 385)

attributes.name: applied_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Nameplate or rated capacity in megawatts (MW) for generation or substation projects as stated in the CPCN application. Null for linear infrastructure (transmission lines, pipelines) where line_length_miles is the primary measurement. Used for IRP capacity planning and PUC capacity need determinations.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; State PUC Certificate of Need Standards; NERC BES Definition

attributes.name: certificate_expiry_date
attributes.description: Date on which the issued CPCN certificate expires if construction has not commenced or the project has not been placed in service. Utilities must seek an extension or re-file if this date passes without project completion.
attributes.references: State PUC Certificate Conditions; FERC Certificate Order

attributes.name: certificate_issuance_date
attributes.description: Date on which the CPCN certificate was formally issued to the utility following approval. This date authorizes commencement of construction or operation and is the key milestone for capital project scheduling and AFUDC accrual start.
attributes.references: State PUC Certificate Issuance Rules; FERC Certificate Order

attributes.name: conditions_of_approval
attributes.description: Narrative description of any conditions, mitigation measures, or compliance obligations imposed by the PUC or FERC as part of a conditional approval. Null for unconditional approvals or pending applications. Populated from the regulatory order text.
attributes.references: State PUC Final Order; FERC Certificate Order; NERC FAC-001

attributes.name: construction_start_date
attributes.description: Earliest date on which construction may commence per the CPCN certificate conditions. May differ from the certificate_issuance_date if the certificate imposes pre-construction conditions (e.g., environmental mitigation plan approval).
attributes.references: State PUC Certificate Conditions; NERC FAC-001; EPA NPDES Permit

attributes.name: cost_recovery_mechanism
attributes.description: Regulatory mechanism through which the utility intends to recover the costs of the project from customers. Rate_base: included in general rate case; rider/tracker: separate cost recovery surcharge; CIAC: customer-funded contribution; PPA: recovered through purchased power costs.
attributes.references: State PUC Rate Case Rules; FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); NARUC Rate Design Manual

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the CPCN application record was first created in the regulatory data system. Audit field supporting data lineage and record provenance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP Internal Controls; NERC CIP-007

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the PUC or FERC issued its final order approving, conditionally approving, or denying the CPCN application. Null until a final decision is rendered.
attributes.references: State PUC Final Order; FERC Order; Federal Power Act

attributes.name: denial_reason
attributes.description: Narrative description of the regulatory agency's stated basis for denying the CPCN application. Null for approved or pending applications. Used for regulatory strategy analysis and re-filing preparation.
attributes.references: State PUC Final Order; FERC Order; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: environmental_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the environmental review process associated with the CPCN application. Tracks progression from initiation through draft and final publication to completion. A prerequisite for certificate issuance in most jurisdictions.
attributes.references: National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); EPA Regulations (40 CFR Parts 1500-1508); State PUC Environmental Rules

attributes.name: environmental_review_type
attributes.description: Type of environmental review required or completed for the project. EIS (Environmental Impact Statement) and EA (Environmental Assessment) are federal NEPA categories; CEQA applies in California; state_environmental_review covers other state-level equivalents. Drives permitting timelines and conditions of approval.
attributes.references: National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA); EPA Regulations (40 CFR Parts 1500-1508)

attributes.name: estimated_capex_usd
attributes.description: Total estimated capital expenditure (CAPEX) in US dollars as stated in the CPCN application. Used for rate base determination, AFUDC calculation, and prudency review. Confidential as it contains commercially sensitive cost estimates submitted in regulatory proceedings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); GAAP ASC 980; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: evidentiary_hearing_date
attributes.description: Scheduled or actual date of the evidentiary hearing before the PUC or FERC administrative law judge. Null if the application is processed on the written record without a hearing.
attributes.references: State PUC Rules of Practice; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 CFR Part 385)

attributes.name: ferc_section_203_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the project also requires separate authorization under Federal Power Act Section 203 (disposition of jurisdictional facilities). True if the project involves a merger, acquisition, or disposition of FERC-jurisdictional assets in addition to the state CPCN.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 203; FERC Regulations (18 CFR Part 33)

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the CPCN application was formally filed with the PUC or FERC. This is the principal business event timestamp that initiates the regulatory review clock and establishes statutory deadlines for agency action.
attributes.references: State PUC Rules of Practice; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 CFR Part 385)

attributes.name: fuel_technology_type
attributes.description: Fuel source or generation technology type for generation projects (e.g., natural gas combined cycle, solar photovoltaic, wind, nuclear, hydro). For transmission and distribution projects, describes the primary technology (e.g., overhead line, underground cable, gas pipeline). Informs environmental review, RPS compliance, and IRP alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas_cc|natural_gas_ct|nuclear|solar_pv|wind|hydro|battery_storage|overhead_transmission|underground_cable|gas_pipeline — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act; State Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS); IRP Filing Requirements

attributes.name: ghg_emissions_impact_tons
attributes.business_glossary_term: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions Impact in Metric Tons CO2e
attributes.description: Estimated annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions impact of the project in metric tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e) as reported in the environmental review. Positive values indicate net emissions increase; negative values indicate net reduction (e.g., for renewable projects displacing fossil generation). Required for EPA and state GHG compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (40 CFR Part 98); State GHG Regulations; FERC Environmental Review

attributes.name: in_service_target_date
attributes.description: Projected date by which the infrastructure is expected to be placed in commercial service as stated in the CPCN application. Used for IRP resource adequacy planning, RTO/ISO interconnection scheduling, and capital project milestone tracking.
attributes.references: State IRP Filing Requirements; FERC Form 1; RTO/ISO Interconnection Procedures

attributes.name: infrastructure_type
attributes.description: Classification of the infrastructure category for which the CPCN is being sought. Determines the applicable regulatory framework, filing requirements, and reviewing authority (PUC vs. FERC). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation|transmission|distribution|gas_pipeline|substation|storage|interconnection — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Order 1000; State PUC General Orders; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: intervenor_count
attributes.description: Number of parties that have formally intervened in the CPCN proceeding as of the most recent update. High intervenor counts indicate contested proceedings and are a leading indicator of hearing complexity and timeline risk.
attributes.references: State PUC Rules of Practice; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 CFR Part 385)

attributes.name: irp_alignment_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the proposed project is included in the utility's most recently approved Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). True if the project is IRP-identified; False if it is an out-of-cycle or supplemental filing. IRP alignment is a key factor in PUC prudency review.
attributes.references: State IRP Filing Requirements; NARUC IRP Guidelines; DOE IRP Standards

attributes.name: jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: Identifies the primary regulatory jurisdiction governing this CPCN application. FERC for interstate transmission and wholesale facilities; STATE_PUC for intrastate distribution and retail facilities; DUAL for projects requiring both federal and state authorization.
attributes.references: Federal Power Act Section 203; State Public Utility Acts; FERC Order 1000

attributes.name: lead_project_manager
attributes.description: Name of the capital project manager responsible for the infrastructure project associated with this CPCN application. Links regulatory authorization tracking to project delivery accountability.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo Project Management; SAP S/4HANA Project System

attributes.name: lead_regulatory_counsel
attributes.description: Name of the internal or external legal counsel designated as lead attorney for the CPCN proceeding. Used for regulatory case management, document routing, and accountability tracking.
attributes.references: State PUC Rules of Practice; Internal Regulatory Affairs Governance

attributes.name: line_length_miles
attributes.description: Total route length in miles for transmission lines, distribution circuits, or gas pipeline projects as stated in the CPCN application. Null for point-source generation and substation projects where applied_capacity_mw is the primary measurement.
attributes.references: State PUC General Orders; PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations (49 CFR Part 192/195)

attributes.name: nerc_bes_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the proposed facility meets the NERC definition of a Bulk Electric System (BES) element, triggering mandatory NERC reliability standards compliance obligations. True for transmission facilities at or above 100 kV and generation above applicable thresholds.
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition (NERC Rules of Procedure); FERC Order 773; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: ppa_associated_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the CPCN application is associated with a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) rather than a utility-owned build. True if the project involves a third-party developer under a PPA; False for utility self-build projects. Affects rate treatment and cost recovery mechanism.
attributes.references: State PUC PPA Approval Rules; FERC Order 888; PURPA

attributes.name: project_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the generation, transmission, or distribution infrastructure project for which the CPCN is being sought. Used in regulatory filings, public notices, and internal capital project tracking.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Filing Standards

attributes.name: rate_base_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the project costs are expected to be included in the utility's regulated rate base upon completion, enabling cost recovery through customer rates. False for projects funded via CIAC (Contribution in Aid of Construction) or other non-rate-base mechanisms.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); State PUC Rate Case Rules; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: rec_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generation project is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) under the applicable state Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS). True for qualifying renewable generation technologies; False for fossil fuel and nuclear projects.
attributes.references: State Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS); NARUC REC Tracking Standards; EPA Green Power Partnership

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Region
attributes.description: The RTO or ISO region in which the project is located (e.g., CAISO, MISO, PJM, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE). Determines interconnection study requirements, transmission planning obligations, and applicable OATT provisions.
attributes.references: FERC Order 1000; FERC OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff and Interconnection Procedures

attributes.name: service_territory
attributes.description: Description of the geographic service territory or region where the proposed infrastructure will be located or will serve. May reference county, utility planning area, load zone, or RTO/ISO region. Used for jurisdictional determination and public notice requirements.
attributes.references: State PUC Service Territory Maps; FERC OATT; RTO/ISO Tariff

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state abbreviation (e.g., CA, TX, NY) identifying the primary state jurisdiction where the CPCN application is filed. Determines the applicable PUC and state regulatory requirements.
attributes.references: ANSI INCITS 38 (US State Codes); State PUC Filing Requirements

attributes.name: statutory_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which the regulatory agency is statutorily required to issue a final decision on the CPCN application. Calculated from the acceptance_date based on applicable state or federal procedural rules. Used for regulatory compliance monitoring and project schedule management.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Act Procedural Timelines; FERC Regulations (18 CFR Part 385)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the CPCN application record was most recently modified in the regulatory data system. Used for incremental ETL processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP Internal Controls; NERC CIP-007

attributes.name: voltage_kv
attributes.description: Nominal operating voltage in kilovolts (kV) for transmission or distribution infrastructure projects. Determines whether the project falls under FERC or state PUC jurisdiction (bulk electric system threshold) and applicable NERC reliability standards.
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition; FERC Order 773; IEEE Standard 1110

products.name: irp_submission
products.description: Master record for each Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submission filed with the state PUC or energy authority. Captures plan cycle year, planning horizon (years), total forecasted peak demand (MW), resource portfolio mix (fossil, nuclear, renewable, DR, EE), RPS compliance percentage, preferred resource plan description, alternative scenarios evaluated, filing date, PUC acknowledgment date, and next update due date. Tracks the utility's long-range resource adequacy planning obligations.
products.reference: State IRP Filing Requirement

attributes.name: irp_submission_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submission record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) IRP Filing Requirements

attributes.name: approval_commission_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.commission_order. Business justification: IRP submissions are acknowledged or approved by commission orders. The irp_submission table currently has puc_order_number as STRING; this should be normalized to a FK relationship. Remove puc_order_n

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.docket. Business justification: IRP submissions are filed under regulatory dockets. The irp_submission table currently has docket_number as STRING; this should be normalized to a FK relationship. Remove docket_number STRING and repl

attributes.name: rto_iso_id
attributes.description: FK to market.rto_iso

attributes.name: alternative_scenarios_count
attributes.description: The number of alternative resource portfolio scenarios evaluated and documented in the IRP filing, beyond the preferred plan (e.g., high renewable, high gas, high EE scenarios).

attributes.name: alternative_scenarios_description
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the alternative resource portfolio scenarios evaluated in the IRP, including key assumptions and distinguishing characteristics of each scenario.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this IRP submission record was first created in the regulatory data system, capturing the audit trail for record origination.

attributes.name: dr_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total Demand Response (DR) capacity in Megawatts (MW) included in the preferred resource portfolio, representing load curtailment and peak shaving programs available to meet resource adequacy requirements.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; State PUC DSM/DR Program Requirements

attributes.name: ee_savings_mw
attributes.description: Total Energy Efficiency (EE) program savings in Megawatts (MW) of peak demand reduction included in the preferred resource portfolio, representing avoided capacity from DSM programs.
attributes.references: State PUC DSM/EE Program Requirements; NARUC EE Guidelines

attributes.name: energy_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the IRP covers electric resource planning, gas supply planning, or a combined electric and gas integrated plan, reflecting the utility's service territory scope.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Filing Requirements; AGA Gas Supply Planning Guidelines

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the IRP was formally submitted to the state PUC or applicable energy authority. Serves as the official commencement date of the regulatory proceeding.

attributes.name: fossil_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total installed or planned fossil fuel generation capacity (coal, natural gas CT/CC, oil) in Megawatts (MW) included in the preferred resource portfolio at the end of the planning horizon.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Resource Portfolio Requirements; U.S. DOE EIA Form 860

attributes.name: ghg_emissions_target_tons
attributes.business_glossary_term: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions Target (Metric Tons CO2e)
attributes.description: The GHG emissions reduction target in metric tons of CO2 equivalent (CO2e) for the utility's generation portfolio at the end of the planning horizon, as required by state climate policy or PUC order.
attributes.references: EPA GHG Reporting Rule (40 CFR Part 98); State Climate Policy

attributes.name: irp_approval_condition
attributes.description: Description of any conditions, modifications, or compliance requirements attached to the PUC's approval of the IRP, such as required supplemental filings, program modifications, or reporting obligations.

attributes.name: irp_consultant_name
attributes.description: Name of the external consulting firm or advisor engaged to support development of the IRP, if applicable. Relevant for procurement transparency and regulatory disclosure.

attributes.name: irp_document_reference
attributes.description: File path, document management system reference, or URL pointing to the official IRP filing document(s) stored in the utility's document management system or the PUC's electronic filing system.

attributes.name: irp_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of the IRP submission: full plan (complete new IRP cycle), update (periodic progress update to an existing IRP), or amendment (correction or modification to a previously filed IRP).

attributes.name: irp_version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for the IRP document, used to distinguish successive drafts, amendments, or errata filings within the same plan cycle year (e.g., v1.0, v1.1, v2.0).

attributes.name: is_rps_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the preferred resource plan as filed demonstrates compliance with the applicable state Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) target for the planning horizon end year. True if compliant, False if a compliance gap exists.
attributes.references: State RPS Statute; State PUC RPS Compliance Rules

attributes.name: jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state abbreviation identifying the regulatory jurisdiction (state PUC) to which this IRP is filed (e.g., CA, TX, NY). Supports multi-state utility operations.
attributes.references: NARUC State Utility Regulatory Directory; ISO 3166-2:US

attributes.name: load_forecast_methodology
attributes.description: Description of the methodology used to develop the long-range load forecast underpinning the IRP, including econometric models, weather normalization approach, and EV/DER adoption assumptions.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Content Requirements; IEEE 1366

attributes.name: nerc_reliability_standard_ref
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standard Reference
attributes.description: Reference to the applicable NERC reliability standard(s) (e.g., TPL-001-4, BAL-502) that inform the resource adequacy and planning reserve margin requirements addressed in this IRP.

attributes.name: next_update_due_date
attributes.description: The date by which the utility is required to file the next IRP update or full plan revision, as mandated by the applicable PUC order or statute.

attributes.name: nuclear_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total installed or planned nuclear generation capacity in Megawatts (MW) included in the preferred resource portfolio at the end of the planning horizon.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Resource Portfolio Requirements; U.S. DOE EIA Form 860

attributes.name: peak_demand_forecast_mw
attributes.description: Total forecasted system peak demand in Megawatts (MW) at the end of the planning horizon, representing the maximum load the utility must be capable of serving. Core resource adequacy metric.
attributes.references: NERC Resource Adequacy Standards; State PUC IRP Requirements

attributes.name: plan_cycle_year
attributes.business_glossary_term: Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) Plan Cycle Year
attributes.description: The calendar year in which this IRP cycle is initiated, typically corresponding to the year of filing. Used to distinguish successive IRP cycles (e.g., 2022, 2025, 2028).
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Filing Requirements; U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) IRP Guidelines

attributes.name: planning_horizon_years
attributes.description: The number of years covered by the IRP's forward-looking resource adequacy analysis, typically 10 to 20 years. Defines the temporal scope of the resource portfolio projections.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Filing Requirements; U.S. DOE IRP Guidelines

attributes.name: ppa_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total generation capacity in Megawatts (MW) to be procured through Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) as part of the preferred resource plan, as opposed to utility-owned generation.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Resource Portfolio Requirements; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: preferred_plan_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the utility's preferred resource plan, summarizing the selected portfolio of generation, storage, DR, and EE resources that best meets reliability, cost, and policy objectives over the planning horizon.

attributes.name: public_comment_period_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which the public comment period for the IRP filing closes, as established by the PUC procedural schedule. After this date, no new public comments are accepted.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Procedural Rules; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: puc_acknowledgment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the state PUC or energy authority formally acknowledged receipt and completeness of the IRP filing, initiating the official review period.

attributes.name: puc_approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the state PUC issued a final order approving, conditionally approving, or accepting the IRP. Null if the IRP has not yet received a final PUC disposition.

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_name
attributes.description: Full name of the state PUC, energy office, or other regulatory authority to which the IRP is submitted (e.g., California Public Utilities Commission, New York Public Service Commission).

attributes.name: renewable_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total installed or planned renewable generation capacity (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass) in Megawatts (MW) in the preferred resource portfolio at the end of the planning horizon.
attributes.references: State RPS Requirements; State PUC IRP Resource Portfolio Requirements

attributes.name: reserve_margin_pct
attributes.description: The planning reserve margin percentage above forecasted peak demand required to ensure resource adequacy, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 15.0 for 15%). Typically set by the RTO/ISO or state PUC.
attributes.references: NERC TPL Standards; State PUC Resource Adequacy Requirements

attributes.name: rps_compliance_pct
attributes.description: The projected Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance percentage achieved by the preferred resource plan at the end of the planning horizon, expressed as a percentage of total retail electricity sales from eligible renewable sources.
attributes.references: State RPS Statute; State PUC RPS Compliance Rules

attributes.name: rps_target_pct
attributes.description: The mandated RPS target percentage that the utility must achieve by the end of the planning horizon, as established by state statute or PUC order.
attributes.references: State RPS Statute; State PUC RPS Compliance Rules

attributes.name: storage_capacity_mw
attributes.description: Total installed or planned energy storage capacity in Megawatts (MW) included in the preferred resource portfolio, including battery storage and pumped hydro.
attributes.references: State PUC IRP Resource Portfolio Requirements; FERC Order 841

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the IRP submission within the regulatory proceeding. Tracks progression from internal drafting through PUC acknowledgment and final disposition. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|acknowledged|under_review|approved|rejected|withdrawn — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: total_capex_forecast_usd
attributes.description: Total projected Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) in U.S. dollars required to implement the preferred resource plan over the planning horizon, as presented in the IRP filing.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: total_opex_forecast_usd
attributes.description: Total projected Operating Expenditure (OPEX) in U.S. dollars associated with the preferred resource plan over the planning horizon, as presented in the IRP filing.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this IRP submission record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail and change tracking requirements.

attributes.name: utility_code
attributes.description: Reference to the utility legal entity or operating company filing the IRP. Supports multi-utility or holding company structures where multiple operating companies may file separate IRPs.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; State PUC Utility Registration

products.name: compliance_obligation
products.description: Master record for each ongoing regulatory compliance obligation the utility must fulfill — including NERC reliability standards (CIP, FAC, MOD, PRC), EPA emissions regulations (Clean Air Act, GHG reporting rule), PHMSA pipeline safety rules (49 CFR 192), PUC service quality standards (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI targets), and FERC OATT requirements. Captures standard/rule identifier, governing body, obligation type, compliance frequency (annual, quarterly, event-driven, continuous), responsible business unit, current compliance status (compliant, non-compliant, under review), evidence retention requirements, next due date, and escalation contacts. Serves as the compliance obligation registry — the authoritative list of everything the utility must comply with and when.
products.reference: NERC Reliability Standards / EPA CFR / PUC Service Quality Rules

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each compliance obligation record in the registry. Primary key for the compliance_obligation data product.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Compliance obligations are assigned to cost centers for execution, budget allocation, and expense tracking. Compliance managers allocate obligations to responsible cost centers for resource planning.

attributes.name: rps_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rps_program. Business justification: RPS programs create specific compliance obligations (annual REC procurement targets, carve-out requirements, reporting deadlines). The compliance_obligation.regulatory_program STRING field should be n

attributes.name: applicability_scope
attributes.description: The utility business segment or operational area to which this obligation applies. Enables filtering of obligations relevant to specific business units (e.g., a NERC CIP standard applies to 'transmission'; a PHMSA rule applies to 'gas_distribution'; an EPA GHG rule may apply to 'generation').
attributes.references: NERC; PHMSA; EPA; FERC Applicability Provisions

attributes.name: asset_class_scope
attributes.description: The specific class of assets or infrastructure covered by this obligation (e.g., 'BES Cyber Systems', 'High Consequence Areas', 'Bulk Electric System', 'Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline', 'Generation Unit > 20 MW'). Supports asset-level compliance mapping in the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system.
attributes.references: NERC BES Definition; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; EPA Subpart C

attributes.name: audit_frequency
attributes.description: How frequently the governing body conducts formal audits or compliance reviews of this obligation. Informs internal audit scheduling and readiness preparation cycles (e.g., NERC conducts triennial audits for most reliability standards; EPA may conduct annual inspections for Title V permits).
attributes.references: NERC CMEP Audit Program; EPA Compliance Monitoring Strategy

attributes.name: cfr_citation
attributes.description: The specific Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) citation for this obligation where applicable (e.g., '40 CFR Part 98', '49 CFR Part 192', '18 CFR Part 35'). Provides the authoritative legal reference for the obligation and supports regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: U.S. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR); FERC 18 CFR; EPA 40 CFR; PHMSA 49 CFR

attributes.name: compliance_frequency
attributes.description: How often the utility must demonstrate or report compliance with this obligation. 'continuous' applies to always-on operational standards (e.g., NERC CIP controls); 'event_driven' applies to obligations triggered by specific incidents or thresholds (e.g., outage reporting, spill notification). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: continuous|annual|semi_annual|quarterly|monthly|event_driven|one_time — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; EPA Reporting Rules; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: compliance_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for compliance staff to record observations, interpretations, open issues, regulatory guidance received, or other contextual information relevant to managing this obligation. Not a substitute for formal evidence documentation.

attributes.name: compliance_owner
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the individual designated as the primary compliance owner responsible for managing and demonstrating compliance with this obligation. This person is accountable for evidence collection, status updates, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Program Governance; NERC CMEP

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current compliance posture of the utility with respect to this obligation. 'compliant' indicates all requirements are met; 'non_compliant' indicates a known gap or violation; 'under_review' indicates an active assessment is in progress; 'pending' indicates the obligation is not yet effective; 'exempt' indicates a formal exemption has been granted; 'remediation' indicates a corrective action plan is active.
attributes.references: NERC Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program (CMEP); EPA Enforcement Policy

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_status
attributes.description: Current status of any Corrective Action Plan (CAP) associated with this obligation. 'not_required' when the utility is compliant; 'in_development' when a CAP is being drafted following a finding; 'active' when a CAP is approved and being executed; 'completed' when all CAP milestones are closed; 'overdue' when CAP milestones have been missed.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP Corrective Action Plan Requirements; EPA Compliance Schedule

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this compliance obligation record was first created in the compliance registry. Provides the audit trail for when the obligation was onboarded into the compliance management system.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which this compliance obligation became or becomes legally binding and enforceable for the utility. For new regulatory rules, this is the compliance date published in the final rule or order.
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; PHMSA Final Rules

attributes.name: escalation_contact
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the senior manager or executive to be notified in the event of non-compliance, missed deadlines, or regulatory inquiries related to this obligation. Supports the escalation workflow in the compliance management process.

attributes.name: evidence_location
attributes.description: The system, repository, or document management location where compliance evidence and supporting documentation for this obligation is stored (e.g., SharePoint path, document management system folder, NERC CMEP portal, EPA e-GGRT system). Enables auditors to quickly locate supporting evidence.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP Evidence Requirements; EPA e-GGRT; Internal Records Management Policy

attributes.name: evidence_retention_years
attributes.description: The number of years that compliance evidence, records, and documentation must be retained for this obligation as required by the governing body. Drives records management policy and data archival schedules (e.g., NERC CIP requires 3 years; FERC OATT requires 5 years; EPA GHG requires 3 years).
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007-6 R5; FERC OATT; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which this compliance obligation expires or is superseded, if applicable. Null for ongoing, open-ended obligations. Used to identify obligations that are no longer active and to manage obligation lifecycle transitions.
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; PHMSA Final Rules

attributes.name: ghg_reporting_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance obligation involves Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions reporting or monitoring requirements under EPA regulations (e.g., 40 CFR Part 98 Mandatory GHG Reporting Rule). Enables filtering of GHG-related obligations for environmental compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 — Mandatory Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule

attributes.name: governing_body
attributes.description: The regulatory authority or standards body that issued and enforces this compliance obligation (e.g., FERC, NERC, EPA, PHMSA, State PUC). Determines the jurisdictional authority and applicable enforcement mechanisms. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FERC|NERC|EPA|PHMSA|PUC|DOE|OSHA|IEEE|AGA|NARUC — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code for state-level obligations (e.g., CA, TX, NY). Null for federal obligations that apply across all jurisdictions. Used to filter obligations by state regulatory authority (PUC) for multi-state utilities.

attributes.name: last_assessment_date
attributes.description: The most recent date on which a formal compliance assessment, audit, or self-certification was completed for this obligation. Used to determine assessment currency and schedule the next review cycle.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; EPA Audit Requirements; Internal Compliance Program

attributes.name: last_audit_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent formal audit or compliance review conducted by the governing body for this obligation. Used to calculate time since last audit and anticipate the next audit window.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; EPA Compliance Monitoring; PHMSA Inspection Records

attributes.name: last_filing_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent regulatory submission, report, or filing made to the governing body in fulfillment of this obligation (e.g., last annual GHG report submitted to EPA, last NERC self-report filed). Supports audit trail and filing history tracking.
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; PHMSA Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this compliance obligation record was most recently modified. Tracks changes to obligation status, ownership, due dates, or other attributes and supports change management auditing.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: nerc_violation_risk_factor
attributes.description: The Violation Risk Factor (VRF) assigned by NERC to this reliability standard requirement, indicating the potential impact of non-compliance on the reliability of the Bulk Electric System (BES). Applicable only to NERC reliability standards; null for non-NERC obligations.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards — Violation Risk Factor Assignments

attributes.name: nerc_violation_severity_level
attributes.description: The Violation Severity Level (VSL) category applicable to this NERC standard requirement, reflecting the degree of non-compliance (Lower, Medium, High, Severe). Used in conjunction with VRF to determine the base penalty amount under the NERC Sanction Guidelines. Null for non-NERC obligations.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards — Violation Severity Level Definitions; NERC Sanction Guidelines

attributes.name: next_due_date
attributes.description: The next calendar date by which the utility must complete a compliance action, submit a report, or demonstrate adherence for this obligation. Drives compliance calendar scheduling and proactive alerting for upcoming deadlines.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; EPA Reporting Deadlines; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: obligation_category
attributes.description: Functional category of the compliance obligation describing the nature of the required action. Supports compliance program segmentation and resource allocation across operational, reporting, recordkeeping, physical security, cybersecurity, financial, and environmental obligations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: operational|reporting|recordkeeping|physical|cybersecurity|financial|environmental — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: obligation_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code or identifier for the compliance obligation, typically matching the regulatory standard or rule identifier (e.g., NERC CIP-014-3, 40 CFR 98, 49 CFR 192.605, FERC OATT Section 37). Serves as the business-facing reference key used in regulatory filings and correspondence.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; 40 CFR Part 98; 49 CFR Part 192; FERC OATT

attributes.name: obligation_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the compliance obligation, including the specific requirements the utility must meet, the actions required, and any conditions or thresholds that trigger compliance activities. Provides context for compliance staff and auditors.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; EPA Regulations; PHMSA 49 CFR; FERC Orders

attributes.name: obligation_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the compliance obligation as published by the governing body (e.g., 'Physical Security of BES Cyber Systems', 'Mandatory GHG Reporting Rule', 'Pipeline Integrity Management in High Consequence Areas'). Used as the human-readable label in dashboards and reports.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; EPA GHG Reporting Rule; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: obligation_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the compliance obligation by regulatory domain. Drives routing to the appropriate compliance team and applicable tracking workflow. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: reliability_standard|emissions_regulation|pipeline_safety|service_quality|tariff_requirement|environmental_permit|safety_regulation|reporting_requirement — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC; EPA; PHMSA; State PUC; FERC

attributes.name: open_violation_count
attributes.description: The current number of open, unresolved violations or findings associated with this compliance obligation. A value greater than zero triggers escalation workflows and corrective action plan (CAP) tracking. Sourced from the compliance management system.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP Violation Tracking; EPA Enforcement Actions

attributes.name: pbr_linked
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance obligation is linked to a Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) mechanism where non-compliance or underperformance results in financial incentives or penalties applied to the utility's revenue requirement. Connects compliance tracking to rate case outcomes.
attributes.references: State PUC PBR Orders; NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework

attributes.name: penalty_exposure_usd
attributes.description: The maximum potential monetary penalty per day or per violation that the utility could face for non-compliance with this obligation, expressed in US dollars. Used for risk prioritization and materiality assessment in the compliance program. For NERC violations, this reflects the NERC Sanction Guidelines maximum.
attributes.references: NERC Sanction Guidelines; EPA Civil Penalty Policy; PHMSA Civil Penalty Regulations

attributes.name: risk_priority
attributes.description: The assessed risk priority level for this obligation, reflecting the combination of likelihood of non-compliance and severity of consequences (financial penalty, operational impact, reputational harm). Used to prioritize compliance resources and management attention.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP Risk-Based Compliance Monitoring; Internal Risk Management Framework

attributes.name: saidi_saifi_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance obligation involves electric distribution service quality metrics including System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), or Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) targets set by the state PUC. Enables filtering of service quality obligations.
attributes.references: State PUC Service Quality Rules; IEEE 1366 — Guide for Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

attributes.name: self_report_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the utility is required to proactively self-report violations or non-compliance events to the governing body for this obligation. True for NERC standards with mandatory self-reporting under the CMEP; False for obligations where reporting is only required upon regulatory request.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP Self-Reporting Requirements; PHMSA Incident Reporting 49 CFR 191

attributes.name: standard_version
attributes.description: The version or revision number of the regulatory standard or rule that this obligation is based on (e.g., 'CIP-014-3', 'Revision 2', '40 CFR 98 as amended 2023'). Critical for tracking when standards are updated and ensuring the utility is complying with the current version.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards Versioning; EPA CFR; PHMSA CFR

attributes.name: tariff_section_reference
attributes.description: The specific tariff section, schedule, or Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) provision that this obligation is associated with, where applicable (e.g., 'OATT Section 37', 'Rate Schedule No. 4', 'General Service Tariff Rule 15'). Links compliance obligations to the utility's filed tariffs.
attributes.references: FERC OATT; State PUC Tariff Filings

products.name: compliance_event
products.description: Transactional record of each compliance activity, evidence submission, or violation event associated with a regulatory compliance obligation. Captures event type (evidence submission, self-report, violation notice, corrective action, audit finding, penalty assessment), event date, obligation reference, responsible party, compliance status (compliant, deficient, remediated), penalty amount if applicable, and corrective action plan reference. Provides the audit trail for demonstrating compliance to NERC, EPA, PUC, and FERC.
products.reference: NERC Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program (CMEP)

attributes.name: compliance_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each compliance event record in the regulatory domain. Primary key for the compliance_event data product.

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent compliance obligation that this event fulfills, violates, or documents. Links the event to the specific regulatory requirement being tracked.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the corrective action plan (CAP) associated with this compliance event, applicable when the event type is a violation, audit finding, or deficiency requiring remediation.
attributes.references: NERC Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program (CMEP); EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Compliance events incur costs (penalties, remediation, legal fees) charged to specific cost centers. Finance allocates compliance expenses to responsible cost centers for budget tracking, variance ana

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory docket or proceeding associated with this compliance event, such as a FERC docket, PUC proceeding, or NERC enforcement action.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific generation, transmission, or distribution asset (e.g., generator unit, transmission line, substation, gas pipeline segment) associated with this compliance event. Links to the asset management system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) for asset-level compliance tracking.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; FERC OATT; PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations

attributes.name: responsible_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or compliance officer designated as the accountable party for this compliance event. Links to the workforce/HR system (SuccessFactors or Workday) for personnel accountability and regulatory contact identification.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Management Procedures; NERC CMEP

attributes.name: closed_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance event has been formally closed by the regulatory authority or internal compliance function. True = closed/resolved with no further action required; False = open and active. Supports compliance dashboard reporting and open-item tracking.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date on which this compliance event was formally closed by the regulatory authority or internal compliance function. Null if the event remains open. Used for compliance lifecycle reporting and regulatory audit trail documentation.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Compliance Assurance; State PUC Enforcement Rules

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date on which the compliance event was fully completed — e.g., evidence successfully submitted, corrective action verified as complete, or penalty paid. Null if the event is still in progress. Used to assess timeliness against due_date.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: compliance_domain
attributes.description: High-level regulatory domain to which this compliance event belongs. reliability = NERC bulk electric system reliability; environmental = EPA GHG/emissions; market = FERC wholesale market rules; safety = OSHA/PHMSA worker and pipeline safety; tariff = OATT/tariff compliance; rate_case = PUC rate proceeding; gas_pipeline = PHMSA gas distribution/transmission; financial = SOX/GAAP financial reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: reliability|environmental|market|safety|tariff|rate_case|gas_pipeline|financial — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC; FERC; EPA; PHMSA; OSHA; State PUC; SOX

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current compliance standing for this event. compliant = obligation met; deficient = obligation not met or violation identified; remediated = deficiency corrected and verified; under_review = regulator or internal team evaluating status; pending = awaiting evidence or determination.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Compliance Assurance; State PUC Enforcement Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this compliance event record was first created in the system, including timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements and Silver layer data lineage tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Regulatory or internal deadline by which this compliance event must be completed — e.g., the filing deadline for evidence submission, the deadline for corrective action completion, or the response deadline for a violation notice. Critical for compliance calendar management.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; State PUC Procedural Rules; EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: emission_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity of regulated emissions associated with this compliance event, expressed in the applicable unit (tons, metric tons CO2e, MCF). Used for EPA GHG reporting compliance verification and environmental penalty calculations under the Clean Air Act.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA GHG Reporting Rule (40 CFR Part 98); Clean Air Act

attributes.name: emission_quantity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the emission_quantity field. short_tons = US short tons; metric_tons_co2e = metric tons CO2 equivalent (standard GHG reporting unit); MCF = thousand cubic feet (gas); MWh = megawatt-hours (for heat rate compliance).
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA GHG Reporting Rule (40 CFR Part 98)

attributes.name: event_date
attributes.description: The principal real-world date on which the compliance event occurred — e.g., the date evidence was submitted, the date a violation was identified, the date a self-report was filed, or the date an audit finding was issued. Distinct from record audit timestamps.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; EPA Compliance Assurance

attributes.name: event_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the compliance event, including the nature of the activity, the specific non-compliance condition identified, or the evidence submitted. Provides the human-readable context required for regulatory filings, audit documentation, and internal compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Compliance Assurance; State PUC Enforcement Rules

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to this compliance event, used in regulatory correspondence, audit trails, and submissions to NERC, FERC, EPA, or PUC. Example: CE-2024-00123.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; Internal Compliance Management Procedures

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time the compliance event occurred or was recorded, including timezone offset. Used for exact sequencing of events within a compliance lifecycle, particularly for NERC real-time reliability events and FERC market compliance incidents.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; FERC Compliance Program

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the compliance activity represented by this event. Values: evidence_submission (documentation submitted to regulator), self_report (voluntary self-disclosure of non-compliance), violation_notice (formal notice received from regulator), corrective_action (remediation activity undertaken), audit_finding (finding from regulatory or internal audit), penalty_assessment (monetary or operational penalty levied).
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Enforcement Policy; State PUC Enforcement Rules

attributes.name: evidence_reference
attributes.description: Document identifier, file path, or external system reference pointing to the evidence package submitted or associated with this compliance event. Examples: document management system ID, NERC COMS submission reference, EPA CDX submission ID, or SharePoint document URL.
attributes.references: NERC COMS (Compliance Operations and Monitoring System); EPA CDX (Central Data Exchange); FERC eFiling

attributes.name: facility_name
attributes.description: Name of the generation plant, substation, transmission facility, or gas distribution facility associated with this compliance event. Provides human-readable facility context for regulatory reporting and audit documentation.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; EPA Facility Registry; FERC OATT

attributes.name: ghg_emission_type
attributes.description: Type of greenhouse gas or regulated air emission associated with this compliance event, applicable for EPA environmental compliance events. CO2 = carbon dioxide; CH4 = methane; N2O = nitrous oxide; SF6 = sulfur hexafluoride (electrical equipment); NOx = nitrogen oxides; SOx = sulfur oxides.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA GHG Reporting Rule (40 CFR Part 98); Clean Air Act

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code identifying the state regulatory jurisdiction applicable to this compliance event. Relevant for PUC-regulated activities. Null for federal-only events (FERC, NERC, EPA).

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.description: The NERC Regional Entity (RE) with compliance monitoring and enforcement authority over this event. Examples: WECC (Western Electricity Coordinating Council), SERC, RFC, MRO, NPCC, TRE. Applicable for NERC reliability compliance events. Null for non-NERC events.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; NERC CMEP; NERC Regional Entity Delegation Agreements

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: Monetary penalty assessed against the utility for this compliance event, denominated in US dollars. Applicable when event_type is penalty_assessment. Includes NERC Notice of Penalty (NOP) amounts, EPA civil penalties, FERC civil penalties, and PUC-imposed fines. Zero if no penalty was assessed.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Civil Penalty Policy; EPA Civil Penalty Policy; State PUC Enforcement Rules

attributes.name: penalty_paid_date
attributes.description: Date on which the assessed penalty was remitted to the regulatory authority. Null if penalty has not been paid or no penalty was assessed. Used for financial reconciliation and regulatory closure confirmation.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Civil Penalty Policy; EPA Civil Penalty Policy

attributes.name: penalty_paid_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the assessed penalty has been paid to the regulatory authority. True = penalty paid; False = penalty outstanding or not yet assessed. Applicable only when penalty_amount is greater than zero.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Civil Penalty Policy; EPA Civil Penalty Policy

attributes.name: recurrence_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance event represents a repeat or recurring violation of the same regulatory standard. True = recurrence; False = first occurrence. Recurrence is an aggravating factor in NERC CMEP and EPA penalty determinations.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; EPA Civil Penalty Policy; FERC Compliance Program

attributes.name: regulator_case_number
attributes.description: The case, docket, or tracking number assigned by the regulatory authority (NERC, FERC, EPA, PUC) to this compliance event or associated enforcement action. Used for cross-referencing with regulator records and official correspondence.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; EPA Enforcement Docket; State PUC Docket System

attributes.name: regulator_response_notes
attributes.description: Notes or summary of the regulatory authority's response to this compliance event, including acceptance of evidence, issuance of a Notice of Penalty (NOP), approval of a corrective action plan, or closure of the enforcement action. Captures key communications from NERC, FERC, EPA, or PUC.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; FERC Compliance Program; EPA Enforcement Policy; State PUC Enforcement Rules

attributes.name: regulatory_body
attributes.description: The governing regulatory authority to which this compliance event pertains. Identifies the jurisdiction and oversight body: NERC (reliability), FERC (wholesale markets/transmission), EPA (environmental), PUC (state retail regulation), PHMSA (gas pipeline safety), OSHA (worker safety), DOE (federal energy policy), NARUC (state commission coordination). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NERC|FERC|EPA|PUC|PHMSA|OSHA|DOE|NARUC — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; PHMSA; OSHA; DOE; State PUC

attributes.name: regulatory_standard_ref
attributes.description: The specific regulatory standard, rule, tariff provision, or statute that this compliance event relates to. Examples: NERC Reliability Standard CIP-007-6, FERC Order 2222, EPA 40 CFR Part 75, State PUC General Order 95. Provides the authoritative citation for audit and enforcement purposes.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards; FERC Orders; EPA Code of Federal Regulations; State PUC General Orders

attributes.name: responsible_party_name
attributes.description: Name of the internal organizational unit, department, or named individual accountable for this compliance event — e.g., the team responsible for submitting evidence, executing a corrective action, or responding to a violation notice. Used for accountability tracking and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: Internal Compliance Management Procedures; NERC CMEP

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Risk severity classification of this compliance event based on potential impact to grid reliability, public safety, environmental harm, or financial exposure. critical = immediate threat to BES reliability or public safety; high = significant regulatory exposure; medium = moderate risk; low = minor administrative non-compliance. Aligns with NERC violation risk factor (VRF) methodology.
attributes.references: NERC Violation Risk Factor (VRF) Methodology; NERC CMEP; EPA Risk-Based Enforcement

attributes.name: rto_iso_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Name
attributes.description: Name of the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) relevant to this compliance event, such as PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, or ISO-NE. Applicable for FERC market compliance and OATT-related events.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000; FERC OATT; RTO/ISO Tariffs

attributes.name: self_report_indicator
