attributes.description: Indicates whether this compliance event was voluntarily self-reported by the utility to the regulator prior to detection. True = self-reported; False = identified by regulator or third party. Self-reporting is a mitigating factor in NERC CMEP and EPA penalty calculations.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; EPA Audit Policy; FERC Compliance Program

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: Method by which evidence or filings associated with this compliance event were submitted to the regulatory authority. electronic = NERC COMS, EPA CDX, FERC eFiling; portal = state PUC e-filing portal; paper = physical filing; email = direct email submission.
attributes.references: NERC COMS; EPA CDX; FERC eFiling System; State PUC E-Filing Rules

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this compliance event record was last modified, including timezone offset. Tracks the most recent update for change management, audit trail, and Silver layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: violation_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which the non-compliance condition was resolved or the violation ceased, as verified by the utility or regulator. Null if the violation is ongoing. Used with violation_start_date to determine violation duration for penalty calculation.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; EPA Enforcement Policy; FERC Compliance Program

attributes.name: violation_risk_factor
attributes.description: NERC-defined Violation Risk Factor (VRF) assigned to the reliability standard requirement associated with this compliance event. Values per NERC methodology: high, medium, lower. Used in NERC CMEP penalty matrix calculations. Null for non-NERC events.
attributes.references: NERC Violation Risk Factor (VRF) Methodology; NERC CMEP

attributes.name: violation_severity_level
attributes.description: NERC-defined Violation Severity Level (VSL) for this compliance event, reflecting the degree of non-compliance with the applicable reliability standard requirement. Values per NERC methodology: severe, high, medium, lower. Used in NERC CMEP penalty matrix. Null for non-NERC events.
attributes.references: NERC Violation Severity Level (VSL) Methodology; NERC CMEP

attributes.name: violation_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which the non-compliance condition began, as determined by the utility or regulator. Applicable when event_type is violation_notice, self_report, or audit_finding. Used to calculate violation duration for penalty assessment under NERC CMEP and EPA enforcement policies.
attributes.references: NERC CMEP; EPA Enforcement Policy; FERC Compliance Program

products.name: emissions_report
products.description: Transactional record of GHG and criteria pollutant emissions reported per generation unit or facility per reporting period. Captures facility/unit identifier, reporting period, pollutant type (CO2, NOx, SO2, CH4, particulates), emissions quantity (tons), emissions intensity (lbs/MWh), measurement methodology (CEMS, fuel-factor), EPA facility ID, REC retirement linkage, and submission status to EPA or state air quality agency. Supports GHG compliance, RPS tracking, and environmental regulatory reporting obligations.
products.reference: EPA GHG Reporting Program (40 CFR Part 98) / EPA CAMD

attributes.name: emissions_report_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each emissions report record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this transactional entity.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT)

attributes.name: compliance_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_event. Business justification: Emissions reports serve as evidence for compliance events. When a compliance_event is related to emissions (e.g., GHG reporting, violation of emission limits), the emissions_report should reference th

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Emissions reports fulfill specific compliance obligations (e.g., EPA GHG reporting, state air quality reporting). Each emissions_report should reference the compliance_obligation it satisfies. This cr

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Emissions monitoring and reporting costs are allocated to operational cost centers (generation facilities, transmission districts). Environmental compliance costs must be tracked by cost center for FE

attributes.name: der_interconnection_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.der_interconnection. Business justification: DER systems offset emissions and generate RECs tracked in emissions reports. Environmental compliance linkage: attributing emission reductions to specific DER interconnections for GHG reporting and RE

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generation facility or plant from which emissions are reported. Links to the asset/facility master record.
attributes.references: EPA Facility Registry Service (FRS); NERC CIP-002

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific generation unit (boiler, turbine, combustion unit) within the facility for which emissions are reported. A facility may have multiple reportable units.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA CAMD Business System

attributes.name: original_report_emissions_report_id
attributes.description: Reference to the original emissions report record that this amended report supersedes. Populated only when amendment_indicator = True. Enables lineage tracking of report corrections and restatements.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT)

attributes.name: rec_transaction_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) retirement transaction linked to this emissions report, used to demonstrate RPS compliance and offset GHG obligations. References the REC tracking system (e.g., WREGIS, PJM-GATS, M-RETS).
attributes.references: State RPS Rules; WREGIS Operating Rules; EPA Green Power Partnership

attributes.name: agency_confirmation_number
attributes.description: Confirmation or acknowledgment number issued by the regulatory agency (EPA, state air agency) upon successful receipt and acceptance of the emissions report submission. Used as proof of filing for compliance audits.
attributes.references: EPA Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT); EPA CAMD Business System

attributes.name: allowance_type
attributes.description: Cap-and-trade or allowance program under which this emissions report is filed. SO2_ARP = EPA Acid Rain Program; NOx_NBP = NOx Budget Trading Program; CSAPR_NOx / CSAPR_SO2 = Cross-State Air Pollution Rule; RGGI_CO2 = Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative; state_cap = state-specific cap program. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SO2_ARP|NOx_NBP|CSAPR_NOx|CSAPR_SO2|RGGI_CO2|state_cap|CA_AB32|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA Acid Rain Program; EPA CSAPR; RGGI; Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: allowances_surrendered
attributes.description: Number of emissions allowances surrendered or retired to cover the reported emissions quantity under the applicable cap-and-trade program (e.g., EPA Acid Rain Program SO2 allowances, RGGI CO2 allowances). One allowance typically equals one ton of the regulated pollutant.
attributes.references: EPA Acid Rain Program; EPA CSAPR; RGGI; Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: amendment_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this emissions report is an amendment (restatement) of a previously submitted report. True = this is an amended filing; False = original submission. Supports audit trail and regulatory compliance tracking.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT)

attributes.name: cems_system_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) System ID
attributes.description: Identifier of the Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS) used to measure emissions for this report, as registered with EPA. Applicable when measurement_methodology = CEMS. Supports audit trail and CEMS certification tracking.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA CAMD Business System

attributes.name: co2e_quantity_metric_tons
attributes.description: Total emissions expressed as metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e), calculated using IPCC global warming potential (GWP) factors. Used for aggregate GHG inventory reporting, RPS compliance, and SEC/state climate disclosure obligations.
attributes.references: IPCC AR6 GWP Factors; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; GHG Protocol Corporate Standard

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this emissions report record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP; Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: emissions_intensity_lbs_per_mwh
attributes.description: Emissions rate expressed as pounds of pollutant per megawatt-hour (MWh) of gross electricity generated during the reporting period. Key performance indicator for environmental compliance, RPS tracking, and EPA rate-based standards under Clean Power Plan successor rules.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 60 (Clean Air Act); EPA CAMD; NERC

attributes.name: emissions_quantity_tons
attributes.description: Total mass of the reported pollutant emitted during the reporting period, expressed in short tons (US tons). This is the primary quantitative result for the emissions report, as required by EPA CAMD and state air quality agency submissions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; Clean Air Act

attributes.name: emissions_quantity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the reported emissions quantity. Short tons is the standard for EPA CAMD reporting; metric tons (MT) is used for GHG Protocol and international reporting; lbs and kg may be used for state-level criteria pollutant reporting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; GHG Protocol Corporate Standard

attributes.name: epa_facility_code
attributes.description: EPA-assigned facility identifier used in the Facility Registry Service (FRS) and Clean Air Markets Division (CAMD) systems. Required for all EPA emissions submissions under 40 CFR Part 75 and Part 98.
attributes.references: EPA Facility Registry Service (FRS); EPA 40 CFR Part 98

attributes.name: epa_unit_code
attributes.description: EPA-assigned unit identifier for the specific combustion or generation unit within the facility, as registered in the EPA Clean Air Markets Division (CAMD) Business System. Used for unit-level emissions tracking and compliance.
attributes.references: EPA CAMD Business System; EPA 40 CFR Part 75

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of fuel consumed during the reporting period, expressed in the unit appropriate to the fuel type (e.g., MCF for natural gas, short tons for coal, barrels for oil). Used in fuel-factor emissions calculations and fuel adjustment clause (FAC) cost recovery.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart C; EIA Form 923; AGA

attributes.name: fuel_consumption_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the fuel consumption quantity. MCF = Thousand Cubic Feet (natural gas); MMBtu = Million British Thermal Units; short_tons (coal); barrels or gallons (oil/liquid fuels).
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98; EIA Form 923; AGA

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: Primary fuel type combusted at the generation unit during the reporting period. Determines applicable emission factors for fuel-factor methodology and influences GHG scope classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|oil|nuclear|biomass|coal_blend|waste_coal|petroleum_coke|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EIA Form 923; EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart C

attributes.name: ghg_scope
attributes.description: GHG Protocol scope classification for the reported emissions. Scope 1 = direct emissions from owned/controlled sources (combustion); Scope 2 = indirect emissions from purchased electricity/heat; Scope 3 = other indirect value chain emissions. Required for corporate GHG inventory and SEC climate disclosure.
attributes.references: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard; SEC Climate Disclosure Rule; EPA 40 CFR Part 98

attributes.name: gross_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total gross electricity generation in megawatt-hours (MWh) produced by the unit or facility during the reporting period. Used as the denominator for emissions intensity calculations and for cross-referencing with EIA generation reporting.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923; EPA 40 CFR Part 75; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: heat_input_mmbtu
attributes.description: Total heat input to the combustion unit during the reporting period, expressed in million British thermal units (MMBtu). Used for fuel-factor emissions calculations and heat rate performance analysis. Required field in EPA CAMD quarterly submissions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA CAMD Business System

attributes.name: measurement_methodology
attributes.description: Method used to quantify emissions for this report. CEMS = Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (direct measurement per 40 CFR Part 75); fuel_factor = EPA-approved fuel emission factor method; mass_balance = material balance calculation; engineering_estimate = approved engineering estimation method for missing data substitution.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; EPA Mandatory GHG Reporting Rule

attributes.name: missing_data_hours
attributes.description: Number of operating hours during the reporting period for which CEMS data was unavailable and EPA-approved missing data substitution procedures were applied per 40 CFR Part 75 Subpart D. Regulatory threshold triggers enhanced scrutiny if exceeded.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75 Subpart D; EPA CAMD Business System

attributes.name: nox_rate_lbs_per_mmbtu
attributes.description: Nitrogen oxides (NOx) emission rate expressed as pounds per million British thermal units (lbs/MMBtu) of heat input. Required for EPA CAMD quarterly reporting and NOx Budget Trading Program compliance. Distinct from the aggregate emissions_intensity_lbs_per_mwh field.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA NOx Budget Trading Program; Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: operating_hours
attributes.description: Total number of hours the generation unit operated during the reporting period. Used to calculate emissions rates, validate CEMS data completeness, and support EPA quarterly report submissions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA CAMD Business System; EIA Form 923

attributes.name: pollutant_type
attributes.description: Type of greenhouse gas (GHG) or criteria pollutant being reported. CO2 = Carbon Dioxide, CH4 = Methane, N2O = Nitrous Oxide, NOx = Nitrogen Oxides, SO2 = Sulfur Dioxide, particulates = particulate matter (PM2.5/PM10), CO2e = Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (aggregated GHG). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CO2|CH4|N2O|NOx|SO2|particulates|CO2e|Hg|HCl|HF — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; Clean Air Act; IPCC GHG Protocol

attributes.name: regulatory_deadline_date
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which this emissions report must be submitted to the applicable agency. Used to monitor on-time compliance and flag late submissions for regulatory risk management.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; State PUC Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: report_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for supplemental notes, explanations of anomalies, missing data justifications, or regulatory correspondence references associated with this emissions report. Used by compliance staff to document context for auditors and regulators.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; State PUC Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier assigned to this emissions report submission, used for tracking with EPA or state air quality agency. Corresponds to the submission tracking number in EPA's Electronic Reporting Tool or state equivalent.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT)

attributes.name: reporting_agency
attributes.description: Regulatory agency or body to which this emissions report is submitted. EPA = U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (federal); state_air_agency = state environmental/air quality agency; FERC = Federal Energy Regulatory Commission; NERC = North American Electric Reliability Corporation; DOE_EIA = U.S. Department of Energy / Energy Information Administration.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; Clean Air Act; FERC; NERC; DOE

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the emissions reporting period. Combined with reporting_period_start_date to define the measurement window for this report.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98 (Mandatory GHG Reporting Rule)

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the emissions reporting period (e.g., calendar year start, quarter start, or compliance period start). Combined with reporting_period_end_date to define the measurement window.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98 (Mandatory GHG Reporting Rule)

attributes.name: reporting_period_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reporting period granularity: annual (calendar year), quarterly, monthly, or compliance_period (custom regulatory compliance window). Determines submission frequency and applicable regulatory deadlines.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98

attributes.name: so2_rate_lbs_per_mmbtu
attributes.description: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rate expressed as pounds per million British thermal units (lbs/MMBtu) of heat input. Required for EPA Acid Rain Program (ARP) compliance and CAMD quarterly reporting under 40 CFR Part 75.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA Acid Rain Program; Clean Air Act Title IV

attributes.name: state_facility_permit_number
attributes.description: State-issued air quality operating permit number (Title V or minor source permit) for the facility, as assigned by the state environmental or air quality agency. Required for state-level emissions reporting submissions.
attributes.references: Clean Air Act Title V; State PUC / State Air Quality Agency

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date on which the emissions report was submitted to the regulatory agency. Used to verify compliance with regulatory submission deadlines and to support prudency reviews.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 75; EPA 40 CFR Part 98; State PUC Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: submission_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the emissions report submission to the regulatory agency. draft = in preparation; submitted = transmitted to agency; accepted = agency confirmed receipt and validity; rejected = agency returned with errors; under_review = agency is reviewing; amended = resubmitted after correction.
attributes.references: EPA Electronic Reporting Tool (ERT); EPA 40 CFR Part 75; Clean Air Act

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this emissions report record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used to detect amendments, data corrections, and track the most recent state of the record in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP; Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: verification_date
attributes.description: Date on which third-party verification of the emissions report was completed. Populated when verified_indicator = True. Used to confirm verification was completed prior to regulatory submission deadline.
attributes.references: California AB 32 (CARB); RGGI Model Rule; ISO 14064-3

attributes.name: verified_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the emissions data in this report has been independently verified by a third-party verifier, as required under certain state GHG programs (e.g., California AB 32, RGGI). True = verified; False = not yet verified or not required.
attributes.references: California AB 32 (CARB); RGGI Model Rule; EPA 40 CFR Part 98

attributes.name: verifier_name
attributes.description: Name of the accredited third-party verification body that reviewed and verified the emissions data. Populated when verified_indicator = True. Required for California ARB and RGGI compliance submissions.
attributes.references: California AB 32 (CARB); RGGI Model Rule; ISO 14064-3

products.name: prudency_review
products.description: Master record for each prudency review or management audit initiated by a PUC or FERC to evaluate the reasonableness of utility expenditures for cost recovery. Captures review type (capital project prudency, O&M prudency, fuel cost prudency, storm cost recovery), triggering docket, review scope description, total expenditure under review (CAPEX/OPEX), reviewer identity (PUC staff, independent auditor), preliminary finding, final determination (prudent/imprudent/partial), disallowed amount, and effective date of determination.
products.reference: PUC Prudency Standard / FERC Cost Recovery Review

attributes.name: prudency_review_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each prudency review or management audit record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete regulatory business event with a defined lifecycle initiated by a PUC or FERC to evaluate the reasonableness of utility expenditures.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: associated_project_capex_project_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the capital project or work order in the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) whose expenditures are under prudency review. Enables traceability from regulatory review to the originating capital project record.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM / IBM Maximo EAM; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: cost_recovery_mechanism_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.cost_recovery_mechanism. Business justification: Prudency reviews evaluate whether costs recovered through cost recovery mechanisms were prudently incurred. The prudency_review table currently has cost_recovery_mechanism as STRING; this should be no

attributes.name: cpcn_application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.cpcn_application. Business justification: Prudency reviews can evaluate CPCN projects to determine if costs were prudently incurred. When a prudency_review is evaluating a CPCN project, it should reference the cpcn_application. This is nullab

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory docket that triggered or is associated with this prudency review. Links to the docket master record in the regulatory domain.
attributes.references: FERC eFiling System; State PUC Docket Management

attributes.name: final_order_commission_order_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Final Order Commission Order Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.commission_order. Business justification: Prudency reviews conclude with a final determination issued via commission order. The prudency_review table should reference the commission_order that contains the final determination. This links the

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate case proceeding in which the results of this prudency review will be or have been incorporated for revenue requirement determination. Links to the rate_case product in the regulatory domain.
attributes.references: FERC Rate Case Procedures; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: review_period_financial_period_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Review Period Financial Period Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Prudency reviews examine costs incurred during specific financial periods (review_period_start/end_date). Regulatory affairs and finance jointly analyze expenditures by financial period to prepare pru

attributes.name: afudc_impact_amt
attributes.business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Impact Amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) associated with the capital expenditures under review. Relevant for capital project prudency reviews where AFUDC capitalization is also subject to reasonableness evaluation.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 835-20

attributes.name: appeal_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which the appeal or request for rehearing of the prudency determination was filed. Null if appeal_indicator is False.
attributes.references: FERC Rehearing Procedures (18 CFR Part 385); State PUC Appeal Rules

attributes.name: appeal_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the utility or any party has filed an appeal or request for rehearing of the final prudency determination. True if an appeal is pending or has been filed; False otherwise.
attributes.references: FERC Rehearing Procedures (18 CFR Part 385); State PUC Appeal Rules

attributes.name: approved_recovery_amt
attributes.description: Final dollar amount of expenditures approved for cost recovery from ratepayers per the final regulatory determination. Equals total_expenditure_under_review_amt minus disallowed_amt. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER MONETARY_TRIPLET net total category.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 980; State PUC Rate Recovery Rules

attributes.name: capex_under_review_amt
attributes.description: Total capital expenditure (CAPEX) amount in USD submitted for prudency review. Represents the gross plant investment being evaluated for reasonableness and cost recovery eligibility. Null if review covers only O&M or fuel costs.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; NARUC Plant Accounts

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this prudency review record was first captured in the data platform (Silver Layer ingestion). Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this prudency review record (e.g., USD). Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER MONETARY_TRIPLET currency code requirement.

attributes.name: disallowed_amt
attributes.description: Final dollar amount of expenditures disallowed from rate base or cost recovery per the final regulatory determination. Represents the imprudent portion that the utility must absorb and cannot recover from ratepayers. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER MONETARY_TRIPLET adjustment category.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 980; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the final prudency determination becomes effective for rate base inclusion or cost recovery purposes. May differ from the final determination date if the order specifies a prospective effective date.
attributes.references: FERC Order 566; State PUC Tariff Effective Date Rules

attributes.name: final_determination
attributes.description: The final regulatory determination on the prudency of the expenditures under review. Prudent allows full cost recovery; Imprudent disallows costs from rate base; Partially Prudent allows partial recovery; Settled indicates a negotiated resolution; Withdrawn indicates the review was dropped.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Order 566; State PUC Final Orders

attributes.name: final_determination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory body issued its final order or determination on the prudency review. Marks the conclusion of the review proceeding and triggers cost recovery or disallowance accounting entries.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; State PUC Final Order Procedures

attributes.name: fuel_cost_under_review_amt
attributes.description: Total fuel procurement cost in USD submitted for prudency review under a Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) proceeding. Covers fossil fuel, purchased power, and gas supply costs. Null if review does not involve fuel cost prudency.
attributes.references: FERC Order 566; FAC Tariff Provisions; State PUC Fuel Clause Rules

attributes.name: initiation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the prudency review was formally initiated by the regulatory body or triggered by a docket filing. Represents the principal real-world business event timestamp (date precision). Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.
attributes.references: FERC eFiling System; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: intervenor_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more intervenors (e.g., ratepayer advocates, industrial customers, environmental groups) formally participated in the prudency review proceeding. True if intervenors are present; False if the review is conducted solely by commission staff.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; State PUC Intervention Rules

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter US state abbreviation (USPS standard) identifying the state PUC jurisdiction for this prudency review. Null for federal FERC reviews. Used for multi-state utility regulatory reporting segmentation.
attributes.references: USPS State Abbreviations; NARUC State Regulatory Directory

attributes.name: opex_under_review_amt
attributes.description: Total operating expenditure (OPEX) / O&M cost amount in USD submitted for prudency review. Represents the operating costs being evaluated for reasonableness. Null if review covers only capital or fuel costs.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420; NARUC O&M Accounts

attributes.name: preliminary_disallowed_amt
attributes.description: Dollar amount of expenditures preliminarily identified as imprudent and proposed for disallowance from rate base or cost recovery by the reviewing body. May be revised in the final determination.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Order 566

attributes.name: preliminary_finding
attributes.description: The initial finding issued by the reviewing body prior to the final determination. Indicates whether expenditures appear prudent, imprudent, or partially prudent based on preliminary staff analysis. May differ from the final determination after hearings and rebuttal testimony.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: preliminary_finding_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reviewing body issued its preliminary finding. Used to track regulatory timeline milestones and compliance with procedural deadlines.
attributes.references: State PUC Procedural Rules; FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Jurisdictional level of the regulatory body overseeing this prudency review. Federal indicates FERC jurisdiction; State indicates a state PUC; Local indicates a municipal or county authority.
attributes.references: FERC Jurisdiction Rules; State PUC Enabling Statutes

attributes.name: review_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, regulatory staff comments, utility responses, or procedural notes relevant to the prudency review. Used for internal tracking and regulatory correspondence documentation.

attributes.name: review_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned by the regulatory body or internal tracking system to uniquely reference this prudency review (e.g., PR-2024-0042). Used in regulatory correspondence, testimony, and filings. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.
attributes.references: FERC eFiling System; State PUC Docket Management

attributes.name: review_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the expenditure period under review. Defines the close of the time window for which costs are being evaluated for prudency.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Case Procedures

attributes.name: review_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the expenditure period under review. Defines the beginning of the time window for which costs are being evaluated for prudency.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Case Procedures

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the prudency review workflow. Progresses from initiated through in-progress, preliminary finding, final determination, and closure. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: review_type
attributes.description: Classification of the prudency review by the category of expenditure under examination. Capital Project prudency evaluates CAPEX reasonableness; O&M Expenditure covers operating costs; Fuel Cost covers FAC-related fuel procurement; Storm Cost Recovery covers major storm restoration costs; General Management Audit covers broad operational spending. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS classification dimension.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Order 566

attributes.name: reviewing_body
attributes.description: The party or organization conducting the prudency review — e.g., PUC Staff, FERC Staff, an independent auditor appointed by the commission, or Office of Attorney General staff. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category (regulatory reviewer as the counterparty).
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: reviewing_body_name
attributes.description: Full legal or organizational name of the entity conducting the prudency review (e.g., 'California Public Utilities Commission Division of Ratepayer Advocates', 'Navigant Consulting Inc.'). Complements reviewing_body code with a human-readable label for reporting and correspondence.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: scope_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the scope of the prudency review, including the specific projects, programs, time periods, and expenditure categories under examination. Provides context for regulatory testimony and rate case filings.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Order 566

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the settlement agreement was executed or approved by the commission, if the prudency review was resolved through settlement. Null if settlement_indicator is False.
attributes.references: FERC Settlement Procedures; State PUC Settlement Rules

attributes.name: settlement_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the prudency review was resolved through a negotiated settlement agreement rather than a litigated final order. True if settled; False if resolved by contested commission order.
attributes.references: FERC Settlement Procedures; State PUC Settlement Rules

attributes.name: total_expenditure_under_review_amt
attributes.description: Aggregate total expenditure in USD across all cost categories (CAPEX + OPEX + fuel) submitted for prudency review. This is the gross amount subject to the regulatory determination. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER MONETARY_TRIPLET gross-base amount category.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this prudency review record was last modified in the data platform. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

attributes.name: utility_witness_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary utility witness or subject matter expert who provided testimony or documentation in support of the prudency of the expenditures under review. Used for regulatory proceeding tracking and testimony management.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure; State PUC Hearing Procedures

attributes.name: wip_balance_amt
attributes.description: Dollar amount of Work in Progress (WIP) balance associated with the capital project under prudency review at the time of review initiation. Relevant for capital project prudency reviews to assess the in-service conversion and rate base eligibility.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 360

products.name: cost_recovery_mechanism
products.description: Master record for each approved regulatory cost recovery mechanism or rider in effect for the utility. Covers FAC (Fuel Adjustment Clause), AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction), CIAC (Contribution in Aid of Construction), infrastructure riders, storm cost recovery trackers, and DSM/EE program cost recovery mechanisms. Captures mechanism type, regulatory approval reference, recovery period, rate base treatment, annual cap (if any), current balance, and true-up frequency. Distinct from billing rate schedules — this is the regulatory authorization record.
products.reference: PUC Rider / FAC / AFUDC Regulatory Order

attributes.name: cost_recovery_mechanism_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each approved regulatory cost recovery mechanism or rider record in the utility's regulatory portfolio.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: cpcn_application_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.cpcn_application. Business justification: Cost recovery mechanisms (CWIP, AFUDC, construction riders) are established for CPCN-approved projects. The cost_recovery_mechanism.cpcn_number STRING field should be normalized to a FK. This links co

attributes.name: current_financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Cost recovery mechanisms (fuel adjustment clauses, storm cost recovery, DSM trackers) have true-up cycles tied to financial periods. Finance calculates quarterly/annual true-ups based on closed period

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory docket record that authorized or governs this cost recovery mechanism. Links to the regulatory.docket product for full proceeding details.

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Cost recovery mechanisms are often established or modified through rate cases. While cost_recovery_mechanism already has docket_id, adding rate_case_id provides direct linkage to the rate case proceed

attributes.name: afudc_rate_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Rate Percentage
attributes.description: The FERC-approved or PUC-approved AFUDC capitalization rate expressed as a percentage, applicable when mechanism_type is AFUDC. Represents the cost of capital applied to construction work in progress (WIP) balances. Null for non-AFUDC mechanism types.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 980; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: annual_cap_amount
attributes.description: Maximum dollar amount that may be recovered through this mechanism in a single calendar or regulatory year, as approved by the regulatory body. Null if no annual cap is imposed. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: State PUC Order; FERC; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory body issued the final order or decision approving this cost recovery mechanism.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Order Issuance Standards

attributes.name: approval_order_number
attributes.description: The official order, decision, or resolution number issued by the regulatory body that authorized this cost recovery mechanism. Used for audit trail and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Order Issuance Standards; NARUC

attributes.name: balance_as_of_date
attributes.description: The date as of which the current_balance was last calculated or reported. Used to determine the staleness of the balance figure for reporting and true-up purposes.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: cost_recovery_mechanism_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the cost recovery mechanism: active = currently in effect and recovering costs; suspended = temporarily halted by regulatory order; terminated = permanently closed; pending_approval = filed but not yet approved; under_review = subject to ongoing prudency or audit review; expired = reached scheduled end date.
attributes.references: NARUC Regulatory Accounting; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: current_balance
attributes.description: Current outstanding balance of costs accumulated in this cost recovery mechanism tracker as of the last true-up or reporting period. Positive balance indicates under-recovery (costs exceed collections); negative balance indicates over-recovery. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: current_rate_amount
attributes.description: The currently approved per-unit recovery rate applied to customer bills under this mechanism (e.g., cents per kWh for FAC, dollars per MCF for gas adjustment). The unit of measure is defined by recovery_method and service_type.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC; NARUC

attributes.name: customer_class_scope
attributes.description: The customer class or classes to which this cost recovery mechanism applies (e.g., 'Residential', 'Commercial', 'Industrial', 'All Classes'). Determines which rate schedules include this mechanism's surcharge.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: disallowed_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of costs disallowed by the regulatory body following a prudency review or audit. Reduces the total recoverable amount. Expressed in USD. Zero if no disallowance has occurred.
attributes.references: State PUC Prudency Review Standards; FERC; NARUC Regulatory Accounting; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: dsm_program_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Demand-Side Management (DSM) / Energy Efficiency (EE) Program Name
attributes.description: Name of the DSM or EE program whose costs are being recovered through this mechanism. Applicable when mechanism_type is DSM_EE_rider. Null for non-DSM mechanisms.
attributes.references: State PUC DSM/EE Program Requirements; DOE Energy Efficiency Standards

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this cost recovery mechanism expires or is scheduled to terminate. Null for open-ended mechanisms with no defined sunset date.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which this cost recovery mechanism becomes effective and the utility may begin recovering costs through rates. Typically aligned with the approved tariff effective date.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: ferc_account_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Number
attributes.description: The specific FERC Uniform System of Accounts account number applicable to this cost recovery mechanism (e.g., Account 182.3 for Other Regulatory Assets, Account 254 for Other Regulatory Liabilities). Required for FERC-jurisdictional utilities.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: filing_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the utility must file reports, rate adjustment applications, or compliance filings with the regulatory body for this mechanism (e.g., monthly FAC filings, annual infrastructure rider updates).
attributes.references: State PUC Filing Requirements; FERC; NARUC

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: The FERC Uniform System of Accounts or company general ledger account code to which costs accumulated under this mechanism are posted. Ensures proper regulatory accounting treatment and financial reporting alignment.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 980; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: interest_accrual_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether interest accrues on the outstanding balance of this cost recovery mechanism as approved by the regulatory body. True = interest accrues on under- or over-recovery balances; False = no interest accrual.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Order; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: interest_rate_pct
attributes.description: The approved interest rate percentage applied to the outstanding balance when interest_accrual_indicator is True. Typically set by the regulatory body in the approval order. Null when interest_accrual_indicator is False.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Order; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: The regulatory jurisdiction governing this mechanism (e.g., state abbreviation for PUC-regulated mechanisms, 'FERC' for federally regulated mechanisms). Determines which regulatory body must approve and oversee the mechanism.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: last_true_up_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recently completed true-up reconciliation for this mechanism. Used to track compliance with the approved true-up frequency and to identify overdue reconciliations.
attributes.references: State PUC Order; FERC; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: mechanism_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code assigned by the utility or regulatory body to uniquely identify this cost recovery mechanism or rider (e.g., FAC-001, AFUDC-2024, STORM-RIDER-TX). Used in tariff filings, rate schedules, and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: mechanism_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the cost recovery mechanism, including its regulatory purpose, the types of costs it covers, and any special conditions or limitations imposed by the approving regulatory body.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC; NARUC

attributes.name: mechanism_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the cost recovery mechanism as it appears in the approved tariff or regulatory order (e.g., 'Fuel Adjustment Clause', 'Infrastructure Modernization Rider', 'Storm Cost Recovery Tracker').
attributes.references: NARUC Regulatory Accounting; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: mechanism_type
attributes.description: Classification of the cost recovery mechanism by regulatory category. FAC = Fuel Adjustment Clause; AFUDC = Allowance for Funds Used During Construction; CIAC = Contribution in Aid of Construction; infrastructure_rider = capital infrastructure surcharge; storm_cost_tracker = storm damage cost recovery; DSM_EE_rider = Demand-Side Management / Energy Efficiency program cost recovery. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FAC|AFUDC|CIAC|infrastructure_rider|storm_cost_tracker|DSM_EE_rider|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: next_filing_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the next required regulatory filing or rate adjustment application for this mechanism must be submitted to the regulatory body. Supports compliance calendar management.
attributes.references: State PUC Filing Requirements; FERC; NARUC

attributes.name: next_true_up_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next true-up reconciliation filing with the regulatory body. Supports proactive compliance monitoring and workload planning.
attributes.references: State PUC Order; FERC; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for regulatory staff to record supplemental information, open issues, pending actions, or contextual notes related to this cost recovery mechanism that are not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: prudency_review_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether costs recovered under this mechanism are subject to a regulatory prudency review before final recovery is confirmed. True = prudency review required; False = costs are pre-approved without individual prudency review.
attributes.references: State PUC Prudency Review Standards; NARUC; FERC

attributes.name: prudency_review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the prudency review for costs recovered under this mechanism: not_required = no review required; pending = review not yet initiated; in_progress = review underway; completed = review finalized; disallowed = costs partially or fully disallowed; approved = costs found prudent and approved for full recovery.
attributes.references: State PUC Prudency Review Standards; NARUC; FERC

attributes.name: rate_base_treatment
attributes.description: Regulatory accounting treatment of costs recovered under this mechanism with respect to the utility's rate base: included = costs are part of the approved rate base; excluded = costs are recovered outside rate base as a rider; deferred = costs are deferred pending future rate case inclusion; amortized = costs are being amortized over an approved period.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: rate_effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current_rate_amount became effective for billing purposes. Changes when a true-up or rate adjustment is approved.
attributes.references: State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; FERC

attributes.name: recovery_method
attributes.description: The billing methodology by which costs are recovered from customers: volumetric = per kWh or MCF consumed; fixed_charge = flat monthly charge per customer; percentage_of_bill = surcharge as a percentage of base bill; demand_charge = per kW of peak demand.
attributes.references: NARUC Regulatory Accounting; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: recovery_period_months
attributes.description: Total approved recovery period in months over which the authorized costs are to be collected from customers. For amortized mechanisms, this defines the amortization schedule length.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Order; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: regulatory_asset_liability
attributes.description: Indicates whether this mechanism creates a regulatory asset (under-recovery, costs deferred for future collection), a regulatory liability (over-recovery, amounts owed back to customers), or neither (pass-through with no balance accumulation). Per GAAP ASC 980.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 980; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: regulatory_body
attributes.description: Name of the specific regulatory authority that approved and oversees this cost recovery mechanism (e.g., 'Texas PUC', 'California PUC', 'FERC', 'Illinois Commerce Commission').
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements; NARUC

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Utility service type to which this cost recovery mechanism applies: electric distribution, gas distribution, or combined electric and gas service.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: tariff_schedule_ref
attributes.description: Reference to the specific tariff schedule, rate schedule, or tariff sheet number in the utility's filed tariff that implements this cost recovery mechanism. Used to cross-reference the regulatory authorization with the billing rate schedule.
attributes.references: FERC OATT; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

attributes.name: total_authorized_amount
attributes.description: Total dollar amount authorized by the regulatory body for recovery under this mechanism over its full approved life. Null for open-ended mechanisms without a defined total cap. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Order; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: true_up_frequency
attributes.description: Regulatory-approved frequency at which the cost recovery mechanism balance is reconciled and rates are adjusted to correct for over- or under-recovery (e.g., monthly for FAC, annual for infrastructure riders).
attributes.references: State PUC Order; FERC; NARUC Regulatory Accounting

attributes.name: wip_balance
attributes.description: Current construction Work in Progress balance associated with this AFUDC or infrastructure rider mechanism. Applicable when mechanism_type is AFUDC or infrastructure_rider. Expressed in USD. Null for non-capital mechanisms.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 980

products.name: commission_order
products.description: Transactional record of each final order, decision, or ruling issued by a regulatory authority (PUC, FERC, NERC, EPA) in connection with a docket or proceeding. Captures order number, issuing authority, order date, order type (final order, interim order, consent order, show cause order, penalty notice), summary of decision, approved revenue requirement or rate change, compliance deadline, appeal period, and appeal status. Serves as the authoritative record of regulatory decisions binding on the utility.
products.reference: PUC / FERC Order

attributes.name: commission_order_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each commission order record in the regulatory data product. Primary key for the commission_order entity in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: docket_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory docket or proceeding that gave rise to this commission order. Links the order back to the originating proceeding tracked in the docket product.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385

attributes.name: effective_financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Commission orders with financial impacts (rate changes, refunds, penalties, regulatory asset approvals) must be recorded in specific financial periods for GAAP compliance. Regulatory accounting posts

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate case record associated with this commission order, when the order results from a rate case proceeding. Nullable for orders not tied to a rate case (e.g., NERC penalty notices, EPA compliance orders).

attributes.name: appeal_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which any party (utility, intervenors, or regulatory staff) must file an appeal, request for rehearing, or petition for review of the commission order. Calculated from order_date per the issuing authority's procedural rules.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: appeal_filed
attributes.description: Indicates whether an appeal, request for rehearing, or petition for judicial review has been filed against this commission order. True when an appeal has been filed; False when no appeal has been filed within the appeal period.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: appeal_filed_date
attributes.description: The date on which an appeal, request for rehearing, or petition for judicial review was formally filed against this commission order. Null when no appeal has been filed.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: appeal_status
attributes.description: Current status of any appeal filed against this commission order: not_appealed (no appeal filed), pending (appeal filed and under review), upheld (appellate authority affirmed the order), reversed (appellate authority overturned the order), remanded (appellate authority returned the order for further proceedings), withdrawn (appealing party withdrew the appeal).
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; Administrative Procedure Act; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: approved_rate_base
attributes.description: The total rate base approved by the commission in this order, expressed in U.S. dollars. Represents the net investment in utility plant and working capital on which the utility is authorized to earn a return. Null for orders not involving rate base determinations.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: approved_rate_change_pct
attributes.description: The percentage change in base rates approved by the commission order relative to existing rates. Positive values indicate a rate increase; negative values indicate a rate decrease. Null for orders not involving base rate changes.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Tariff Rules

attributes.name: approved_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: The total annual revenue requirement approved by the regulatory authority in this commission order, expressed in U.S. dollars. Represents the amount the utility is authorized to collect from ratepayers to recover its prudently incurred costs plus a reasonable return. Null for orders not involving revenue requirement determinations.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: approved_roe_pct
attributes.description: The allowed Return on Equity (ROE) percentage approved by the commission in this order. Represents the authorized rate of return on the equity component of the utility's capital structure. Null for orders not involving ROE determinations.
attributes.references: FERC; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: compliance_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which the utility must complete all compliance actions mandated by the commission order, such as filing compliance tariffs, implementing approved rates, submitting compliance reports, or completing required infrastructure changes.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; NERC Rules of Procedure; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: compliance_filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the utility submitted its required compliance filing to the regulatory authority in response to this commission order. Null when no compliance filing has been submitted or is not required.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: compliance_filing_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the commission order requires the utility to submit a compliance filing (e.g., compliance tariff, compliance report, or compliance plan) to the regulatory authority by the compliance_deadline_date. True when a compliance filing is mandated.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: confidential_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this commission order or any of its associated documents have been designated as confidential or protected from public disclosure by the issuing regulatory authority. True when the order or supporting materials are subject to a protective order or confidentiality designation.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 388; State PUC Protective Order Rules

attributes.name: cpcn_project_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) Project Name
attributes.description: Name of the capital project or infrastructure investment for which a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) is granted or denied by this commission order. Applicable only for CPCN proceedings. Null for all other order types.
attributes.references: State PUC CPCN Statutes; FERC Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, 18 CFR Part 157

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this commission order record was first created in the regulatory data product. Audit field capturing the initial data ingestion or manual entry event in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: customer_class_scope
attributes.description: The customer class or rate class to which the commission order's directives or approved rates apply. Values: residential, commercial, industrial, large_power, or all_classes when the order applies universally across all customer segments.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Tariff Rules

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the commission order's directives, approved rates, or compliance obligations become legally effective and binding on the utility. May differ from order_date when the order specifies a future effective date or when interim rates are superseded.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Tariff Rules

attributes.name: fac_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this commission order involves a Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) or fuel cost recovery mechanism. True when the order approves, modifies, or audits FAC rates or fuel cost pass-through provisions.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC FAC Rules

attributes.name: ghg_program_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) or emissions compliance program associated with this commission order (e.g., EPA Clean Air Act permit number, state GHG program ID, Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance docket reference). Null for orders not related to GHG or emissions compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act; State RPS Statutes; DOE Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: issuing_authority
attributes.description: The regulatory body that issued this commission order. Identifies the jurisdictional authority: Public Utility Commission (PUC), Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), or Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA).
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; EPA; DOE; PHMSA; State PUC Enabling Statutes

attributes.name: jurisdiction_state
attributes.description: Two-letter U.S. state abbreviation identifying the state jurisdiction for state PUC orders. Null for federal orders issued by FERC, NERC, or EPA. Used to segment regulatory obligations by state service territory.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Enabling Statutes

attributes.name: lead_attorney
attributes.description: Name of the utility's lead regulatory attorney or outside counsel responsible for managing the utility's response to this commission order, including compliance filings, appeals, and regulatory correspondence.

attributes.name: nerc_standard_ref
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Standard Reference
attributes.description: The specific North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) reliability standard identifier (e.g., FAC-001, PRC-005, CIP-007) that is the subject of this commission order. Applicable for NERC compliance and enforcement orders. Null for non-NERC proceedings.
attributes.references: NERC Rules of Procedure; NERC Reliability Standards Catalog; FERC Order 693

attributes.name: order_date
attributes.description: The official date on which the regulatory authority issued and signed the commission order. This is the authoritative date of the regulatory decision and is used for compliance deadline calculations and appeal period tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Externally assigned alphanumeric identifier issued by the regulatory authority (PUC, FERC, NERC, or EPA) uniquely identifying this order within the issuing body's docket system. Used for official correspondence and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the commission order: issued (order is in effect), appealed (utility or intervenor has filed an appeal), stayed (order execution suspended pending appeal or court action), vacated (order overturned by appellate authority), superseded (replaced by a subsequent order), closed (all compliance obligations fulfilled and order administratively closed).
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: order_summary
attributes.description: Plain-language summary of the commission order's key findings, directives, and decisions. Captures the substance of the regulatory ruling including approved actions, denied requests, required compliance measures, and any conditions imposed on the utility.
attributes.references: FERC; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; State PUC Procedural Rules

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the commission order by its legal and procedural nature: final_order (definitive ruling concluding a proceeding), interim_order (temporary ruling pending final decision), consent_order (negotiated settlement order), show_cause_order (directive requiring the utility to demonstrate compliance or justification), penalty_notice (formal notice of civil penalty or fine). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: final_order|interim_order|consent_order|show_cause_order|penalty_notice|declaratory_order|compliance_order — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; NERC Rules of Procedure

attributes.name: pbr_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this commission order establishes, modifies, or evaluates a Performance-Based Ratemaking (PBR) mechanism. True when the order includes PBR provisions such as earnings sharing, efficiency incentives, or reliability performance metrics tied to rate adjustments.
attributes.references: NARUC Performance-Based Regulation Framework; State PUC PBR Orders

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: The civil monetary penalty or fine assessed against the utility in this commission order, expressed in U.S. dollars. Applicable for penalty notices, show cause orders, and NERC/EPA enforcement actions. Null for orders that do not impose a financial penalty.
attributes.references: NERC Rules of Procedure; EPA Clean Air Act Enforcement; FERC Civil Penalty Policy

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Internal priority classification assigned to this commission order based on its financial impact, compliance risk, and operational urgency: critical (immediate executive attention required, major financial or operational impact), high (significant compliance obligation with near-term deadline), medium (standard compliance obligation), low (routine or informational order with minimal operational impact).

attributes.name: proceeding_type
attributes.description: Category of the regulatory proceeding that produced this order: rate_case (general rate case), cpcn (Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity), irp (Integrated Resource Plan), tariff_filing (tariff amendment or OATT filing), nerc_compliance (NERC reliability standard compliance), ghg_compliance (Greenhouse Gas/emissions compliance), oatt (Open Access Transmission Tariff), nem (Net Energy Metering), dr_program (Demand Response program approval). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rate_case|cpcn|irp|tariff_filing|nerc_compliance|ghg_compliance|oatt|nem|dr_program|pbr|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FERC; NERC; State PUC Enabling Statutes; EPA Clean Air Act

attributes.name: refund_amount
attributes.description: The total amount the utility is ordered to refund to customers as directed by this commission order, expressed in U.S. dollars. Applicable when the commission determines the utility over-collected revenues or charged rates in excess of approved levels. Null when no refund is ordered.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: refund_deadline_date
attributes.description: The date by which the utility must complete the distribution of ordered customer refunds. Null when no refund is required by this order.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Rate Case Rules

attributes.name: regulatory_case_manager
attributes.description: Name of the internal regulatory affairs staff member or case manager responsible for tracking compliance obligations, coordinating cross-functional responses, and maintaining the utility's records for this commission order.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: The regulated utility service type to which this commission order applies: electric (electric distribution), gas (natural gas distribution), electric_and_gas (combined electric and gas), transmission (high-voltage electric transmission), generation (electric generation). Determines which operational domain is subject to the order's directives.
attributes.references: FERC; State PUC Enabling Statutes; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: stay_expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which a stay of the commission order expires or is lifted, after which the order's directives become effective. Null when no stay has been issued.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: stay_issued
attributes.description: Indicates whether a stay of the commission order has been granted by the issuing authority or an appellate court, suspending the order's effectiveness pending resolution of an appeal or rehearing. True when a stay is in effect.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 CFR Part 385; Administrative Procedure Act

attributes.name: tariff_schedule_ref
attributes.description: Reference to the specific tariff schedule, rate schedule, or Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT) section that is approved, modified, or superseded by this commission order. Used to link the order to the utility's filed tariff documents.
attributes.references: FERC Tariff Filing Requirements; State PUC Tariff Rules; OATT

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this commission order record was most recently modified in the regulatory data product. Audit field tracking the last update to any attribute, used for change detection and incremental processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard; SOX Section 404

products.name: rider_charge
products.description: Regulatory rider and surcharge master defining all PUC-approved cost-recovery mechanisms applied to customer bills as separate line items beyond base tariff rates — Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC), Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) surcharge, CIAC recovery rider, infrastructure investment rider, low-income program rider, demand response program charge, and environmental compliance surcharge. Captures rider code, rider name, regulatory approval order reference, applicable customer classes, charge basis (per kWh, per MCF, per Therm, per kW, fixed monthly), effective date, expiration date, and current rate value. Each rider has its own regulatory approval lifecycle independent of base rate schedule changes. Sourced from PUC-approved tariff riders and maintained in Oracle CC&B / SAP IS-U rate engine. SSOT for all regulatory surcharges — distinct from rate_schedule, which owns base tariff rate definitions.
products.reference: Regulatory Rider / Tariff Surcharge (Oracle CC&B Rate Component / SAP IS-U Rate Fact)

attributes.name: rider_charge_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the regulatory rider or surcharge record. Primary key for the rider_charge product.

attributes.name: cost_recovery_mechanism_id
