attributes.description: The timestamp when this budget record was last modified in the source system or Silver Layer lakehouse (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for incremental ETL processing, change data capture, and SOX audit trail of budget amendments.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

attributes.name: variance_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The allowable percentage deviation between budgeted and actual amounts before a budget variance alert or escalation is triggered. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 10.00 for 10%). Used in monthly budget-vs-actual variance reporting and SOX internal control monitoring.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP Internal Control Framework (COSO)

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Identifies the planning iteration of this budget record. 'original' is the board-approved annual budget; 'revised' reflects mid-year amendments; 'forecast' is the rolling latest estimate; 'long_range_plan' covers multi-year capital programs (IRP/CAPEX plans); 'supplemental' covers emergency or regulatory-driven additions.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 270; FERC Form 1; PUC Rate Case Cost-of-Service Study

attributes.name: wbs_element
attributes.description: The Work Breakdown Structure element code from SAP Project System (PS) or Oracle ERP Project module, used to track CAPEX budgets at the project or sub-project level. Supports AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) tracking and WIP (Work in Progress) capitalization per FERC accounting rules.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107 (Construction Work in Progress); GAAP ASC 835-3 (AFUDC)

products.name: fixed_asset
products.description: Master record for capitalized utility plant assets tracked in the fixed asset subledger, aligned to FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant accounts. Captures asset number, asset description, FERC plant account (e.g., 101 Electric Plant in Service, 303 Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, 376 Distribution Mains — Gas), asset class, vintage year, acquisition date, in-service date, original cost, accumulated depreciation, net book value, depreciation method (straight-line, group/composite), useful life, net salvage rate (including negative salvage/cost of removal), retirement date, retirement type (normal, abnormal, extraordinary), asset location, and CWIP-to-plant transfer reference. Serves as the financial SSOT for utility plant valuation, depreciation studies, rate base calculations, and FERC Form 1 plant schedules (Schedules 204-207). Complements the operational asset record in the asset domain. Vintage year and net salvage rate are critical for group/composite depreciation studies unique to the utility industry.
products.reference: SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting (FI-AA) / FERC USoA Plant Accounts

attributes.name: fixed_asset_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the fixed asset record in the financial subledger. Primary key for the fixed_asset data product.

attributes.name: capex_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.capex_project. Business justification: fixed_asset is capitalized from CAPEX projects. The cwip_transfer_reference and wbs_element attributes suggest a link to the originating project. This FK allows tracing each asset back to its capital

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: fixed_asset has cost_center_code attribute. cost_center is the master for cost centers. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full cost center details (name, responsible_manager, functional

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: fixed_asset has gl_account_code attribute. gl_account is the master for GL accounts. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full account details (account_name, ferc_account_description, acco

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Cross-reference identifier linking this financial fixed asset record to the corresponding operational asset record in the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system (Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo). Enables reconciliation between the financial subledger and the operational asset register for asset lifecycle management and maintenance cost tracking.
attributes.references: Oracle WAM; IBM Maximo; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Fixed assets track original vendor for warranty claims, maintenance contracts, spare parts sourcing, and asset provenance. Essential for asset lifecycle management, vendor performance tracking, and re

attributes.name: accumulated_depreciation
attributes.description: Total depreciation accrued on the asset from in-service date through the current reporting period. Represents the cumulative reduction in the asset's book value due to wear, obsolescence, and passage of time. Used to compute net book value and rate base. Denominated in USD. Corresponds to FERC Account 108 (Accumulated Provision for Depreciation of Electric Utility Plant) or equivalent gas accounts.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 219

attributes.name: acquisition_date
attributes.description: Date on which the utility acquired ownership or control of the asset (purchase date, transfer date, or contribution date). May differ from in-service date for assets acquired from third parties or contributed by developers (CIAC — Contribution in Aid of Construction).
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: afudc_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Amount
attributes.description: Total Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) capitalized into the original cost of this asset during the construction period. AFUDC represents the cost of debt and equity capital used to finance construction before the asset is placed in service. Regulated by FERC and included in rate base. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Accounts 107, 432, 436; GAAP ASC 835-20; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: annual_depreciation_rate
attributes.description: The composite or straight-line annual depreciation rate applied to this asset or asset group, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.033333 for a 30-year life). Derived from the FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Used to compute annual depreciation expense for regulatory reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336

attributes.name: asset_class
attributes.description: Internal asset classification grouping used for depreciation study purposes and rate case cost-of-service analysis (e.g., Transmission Structure, Distribution Transformer, Gas Meter, Generation Turbine, Intangible Software). Maps to depreciation group/composite rates established in the most recent depreciation study approved by the state PUC or FERC.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: asset_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the capitalized utility plant asset (e.g., '138kV Transmission Line Segment — Substation A to Substation B', 'Gas Distribution Main — 4-inch PE Pipe'). Sourced from the asset master record in the ERP fixed asset module.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: asset_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to the capitalized asset in the fixed asset subledger (e.g., SAP S/4HANA Asset Master number or Oracle ERP asset number). Used for cross-system reconciliation between the financial subledger and the operational asset register in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: asset_retirement_obligation
attributes.description: Recorded Asset Retirement Obligation (ARO) associated with this asset, representing the present value of the estimated future cost to retire the asset in accordance with legal or regulatory obligations (e.g., nuclear decommissioning, PCB-contaminated equipment disposal, gas main abandonment). Recognized per GAAP ASC 410-20 and tracked for FERC regulatory accounting. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 410-20; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 230; EPA Regulations; PHMSA

attributes.name: asset_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fixed asset in the utility plant subledger. 'in_service' indicates the asset is placed in service and included in rate base. 'cwip' indicates Construction Work in Progress not yet transferred to plant in service. 'retired' indicates the asset has been removed from service. Aligns with FERC plant account status classifications.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10

attributes.name: asset_type
attributes.description: Broad classification of the asset as tangible utility plant, intangible plant, or Construction Work in Progress (CWIP). Tangible includes physical generation, transmission, and distribution infrastructure. Intangible includes software, licenses, and franchise rights. CWIP represents assets not yet placed in service.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 350; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: capex_category
attributes.description: Strategic CAPEX category classifying the business driver for the capital investment in this asset. 'growth' supports customer or load growth. 'reliability' improves grid or system reliability (SAIDI/SAIFI improvement). 'compliance' meets regulatory or environmental mandates. 'replacement' replaces end-of-life infrastructure. 'technology' supports grid modernization or AMI deployment. Used in IRP and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; IRP Regulatory Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC CAPEX Filings

attributes.name: capitalization_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum dollar threshold applied to determine whether an expenditure on this asset class is capitalized as plant in service or expensed as O&M. Established by the utility's capitalization policy, approved by the board, and subject to SOX internal controls. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: ciac_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) Amount
attributes.description: Amount of Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) received from customers, developers, or third parties that offset the original cost of this asset. CIAC reduces the rate base for regulatory purposes. Tracked per FERC Account 271 and applicable state PUC tariff rules. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 271; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts; IRS Revenue Ruling 2020-23

attributes.name: cost_of_removal
attributes.description: Actual or estimated cost incurred to remove the asset from service upon retirement (excavation, demolition, environmental remediation, disposal). Subtracted from gross salvage to determine net salvage. Frequently exceeds gross salvage for underground utility infrastructure, resulting in negative net salvage. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108.1; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 410

attributes.name: cwip_transfer_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) Transfer Reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) work order or project from which this asset was transferred upon completion and placement in service. Links the capitalized plant record back to the capital project that funded its construction. Corresponds to FERC Account 107 (Construction Work in Progress) transfer transactions.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: depreciation_group_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the depreciation group or composite account to which this asset belongs for group/composite depreciation purposes. Assets within the same depreciation group share a common composite depreciation rate derived from the FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Critical for utility industry group depreciation accounting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 360-10-35-7

attributes.name: depreciation_method
attributes.description: Accounting method used to calculate periodic depreciation expense for this asset. 'straight_line' allocates cost evenly over useful life. 'group_composite' is the predominant utility industry method where assets are depreciated as a group using composite rates derived from depreciation studies approved by FERC or state PUCs. 'units_of_production' is used for generation assets tied to output.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10-35; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines

attributes.name: depreciation_study_year
attributes.description: The year of the most recent FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study from which the depreciation rates, useful life, and net salvage rate for this asset class were derived. Depreciation studies are typically conducted every 3–5 years and filed with the applicable regulatory authority. Tracks which study vintage governs the current depreciation parameters.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; State PUC Depreciation Study Orders

attributes.name: ferc_plant_account
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account
attributes.description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account code to which this asset is classified (e.g., 101 Electric Plant in Service, 303 Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, 350 Land and Land Rights — Transmission, 376 Distribution Mains — Gas). Drives FERC Form 1 plant schedule reporting (Schedules 204–207) and rate base calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1 Schedules 204–207

attributes.name: ferc_plant_account_name
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account Name
attributes.description: Descriptive name corresponding to the FERC plant account code (e.g., 'Electric Plant in Service', 'Distribution Mains — Gas'). Supports human-readable reporting on FERC Form 1 plant schedules without requiring a join to a reference table.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101)

attributes.name: functional_class
attributes.description: FERC functional classification of the utility plant asset: Generation, Transmission, Distribution, General Plant, or Intangible. Drives allocation of rate base and O&M costs across customer classes in rate case cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

attributes.name: gross_salvage_amount
attributes.description: Actual or estimated gross salvage proceeds received or expected upon retirement of the asset (scrap value, resale proceeds). Used in conjunction with cost of removal to compute net salvage for depreciation study updates. Populated upon retirement; null for in-service assets. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; GAAP ASC 360-10-40

attributes.name: in_service_date
attributes.description: Date on which the asset was placed in service and began depreciating. Triggers the start of depreciation accrual and inclusion in the utility rate base. For CWIP-to-plant transfers, this is the date the CWIP balance is transferred to plant in service. Critical for AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) cessation.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 204

attributes.name: is_rate_base_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this asset is eligible for inclusion in the utility's regulatory rate base for cost-of-service rate case purposes. Assets funded by CIAC, regulatory disallowances, or held for future use may be excluded from rate base. Critical for PUC and FERC rate case filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines; State PUC Regulations

attributes.name: is_regulatory_asset
attributes.description: Indicates whether this item is classified as a regulatory asset under GAAP ASC 980 (Regulated Operations), meaning its recovery through future rates is probable. Regulatory assets arise from costs deferred for rate recovery (e.g., storm damage costs, deferred fuel costs, environmental remediation). Affects balance sheet presentation and rate case strategy.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 980; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Regulations

attributes.name: last_physical_inventory_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent physical inventory verification confirming the existence and condition of this asset. Physical inventories are required for SOX compliance (internal controls over financial reporting) and support reconciliation between the fixed asset subledger and the operational asset register in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: location_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the physical or operational location of the asset within the utility's service territory (e.g., substation identifier, distribution circuit code, gas pressure zone, plant site code). Used for geographic cost allocation in rate cases and for reconciliation with the GIS (ESRI ArcGIS) asset network model.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; ESRI ArcGIS GIS Integration; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

attributes.name: net_book_value
attributes.description: Current net book value of the asset, calculated as original cost minus accumulated depreciation. Represents the carrying value of the asset on the utility's balance sheet and is the primary basis for rate base inclusion in cost-of-service rate cases. Denominated in USD. Note: while derivable, this field is stored for performance and regulatory reporting efficiency.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; NARUC Rate Case Guidelines

attributes.name: net_salvage_rate
attributes.description: The net salvage rate applied to this asset class in the depreciation study, expressed as a decimal. Net salvage equals gross salvage proceeds minus cost of removal. For utility assets, net salvage is frequently negative (negative salvage) because cost of removal (e.g., pole removal, underground cable excavation, gas main abandonment) exceeds any scrap value. Negative salvage rates increase the depreciable base and are a critical input unique to utility depreciation studies.
attributes.references: NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Iowa Curve Methodology

attributes.name: original_cost
attributes.description: The original cost of the utility plant asset at the time it was first dedicated to public service, as defined by FERC Uniform System of Accounts. Includes all costs necessary to bring the asset to its intended use (materials, labor, AFUDC, overhead). This is the FERC-defined original cost, not necessarily the acquisition cost paid by the current owner. Denominated in USD.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1 Schedule 204; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fixed asset record was first created in the financial subledger system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Supports SOX audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this fixed asset record was most recently modified in the financial subledger system. Tracks changes to depreciation parameters, status updates, retirement entries, and cost adjustments. Supports SOX audit trail and Silver Layer change data capture (CDC) processing.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: remaining_useful_life_years
attributes.description: Estimated remaining useful service life of the asset in years as of the most recent depreciation study or valuation date. Computed as useful life minus age (years since in-service date), adjusted for condition assessments. Used in rate case depreciation studies, IRP capital planning, and asset replacement forecasting.
attributes.references: NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Iowa Curve Methodology

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the asset was retired, abandoned, or removed from utility plant in service. Triggers cessation of depreciation accrual and removal from rate base. Null for assets currently in service. Required for FERC Form 1 plant retirement schedules.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10-40; FERC Form 1 Schedule 205

attributes.name: retirement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the asset retirement event. 'normal' retirements are expected end-of-life removals consistent with the depreciation study survivor curve. 'abnormal' retirements are premature removals due to accidents, storms, or regulatory mandates. 'extraordinary' retirements involve large-scale plant abandonments. Classification affects regulatory accounting treatment and potential regulatory asset recovery.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360-10-40; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines

attributes.name: service_territory
attributes.description: Name or code of the regulatory service territory or jurisdiction in which the asset is located (e.g., state name, PUC jurisdiction code). Determines which state Public Utility Commission (PUC) has regulatory jurisdiction over the asset's rate base treatment and depreciation rates.
attributes.references: State PUC Regulations; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC

attributes.name: useful_life_years
attributes.description: Estimated useful service life of the asset in years, as established in the most recent FERC or PUC-approved depreciation study. Used to compute straight-line depreciation rates and to project future capital replacement needs in the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). Decimal precision accommodates fractional lives from group/composite depreciation studies.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; Iowa Curve Methodology

attributes.name: utility_type
attributes.description: Identifies whether the asset belongs to the electric utility plant, gas utility plant, common plant (shared between electric and gas), or other. Critical for cost-of-service allocation studies in rate cases filed with state PUCs and FERC.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: vintage_year
attributes.description: The year in which the asset was originally constructed or manufactured. Critical input for group/composite depreciation studies unique to the utility industry, where survivor curve analysis and Iowa Curve fitting require age distribution data by vintage year. Used in FERC-approved depreciation studies and PUC rate case filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Depreciation Guidelines; Iowa Curve Methodology

attributes.name: wbs_element
attributes.description: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element or capital project code from the ERP system associated with the construction or acquisition of this asset. Links the capitalized asset to the CAPEX project that funded it, supporting capital budget tracking and AFUDC calculation. Relevant for assets still in CWIP or recently transferred to plant in service.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; SOX Section 302/404

products.name: depreciation_run
products.description: Transactional record of periodic depreciation calculation runs executed against the fixed asset subledger. Captures run date, fiscal period, fiscal year, depreciation area (book/GAAP, federal tax, state tax, regulatory/FERC, AMT, group/composite), total depreciation amount posted, number of assets processed, run status (planned, simulated, posted, reversed), posting document reference, run initiator, and depreciation method applied (straight-line, group/composite, sum-of-years-digits, declining balance, units-of-production). Supports GAAP straight-line and group/composite depreciation methods commonly used by utilities, regulatory depreciation per PUC-approved depreciation study rates (including interim and final rates), tax depreciation (MACRS with bonus depreciation), and FERC Form 1 depreciation reporting (Schedule 336 — Depreciation and Amortization of Electric Plant). Enables audit trail for SOX compliance over the depreciation posting process, supports depreciation study true-up analysis, and provides the depreciation expense input for rate case cost-of-service calculations.
products.reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA Depreciation Run / FERC Depreciation Accounting

attributes.name: depreciation_run_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each depreciation calculation run executed against the fixed asset subledger. Primary key for this record.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Asset Accounting (FI-AA) — Depreciation Run (AFAB)

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: depreciation_run has cost_center_code attribute. cost_center is the master for cost centers. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full cost center details (name, responsible_manager, funct

attributes.name: depreciation_study_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the PUC-approved depreciation study whose rates were applied in this run. Links the run to the authoritative rate study (interim or final) that established the depreciation rates, supporting depreciation study true-up analysis and rate case cost-of-service documentation.
attributes.references: PUC Depreciation Study Requirements; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: depreciation_run has fiscal_year and fiscal_period attributes. financial_period is the master for fiscal periods. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full period metadata (period dates, s

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: depreciation_run has gl_account_code attribute. gl_account is the master for GL accounts. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full account details (account_name, ferc_account_description,

attributes.name: accumulated_depreciation_amount
attributes.description: Total accumulated depreciation balance (in USD) for the assets processed in this run as of the end of the fiscal period, across the specified depreciation area. Represents the cumulative depreciation charged against the gross plant-in-service balance. Used in FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 and rate base calculations for rate cases.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1 Schedule 336; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the depreciation run was approved for posting by the authorized finance approver. Part of the SOX audit trail for the depreciation posting lifecycle.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICFR)

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the finance manager or controller who approved the depreciation run for posting. Supports SOX segregation of duties controls requiring that the person who initiates a depreciation run is different from the person who approves it.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GAAP Internal Controls over Financial Reporting (ICFR)

attributes.name: asset_class_code
attributes.description: FERC or ERP asset class code identifying the category of fixed assets included in this depreciation run (e.g., '301' = Organization, '303' = Miscellaneous Intangible Plant, '350' = Land and Land Rights, '353' = Station Equipment, '362' = Meters, '391' = Office Furniture). Aligns with FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account codes. If the run covers all asset classes, this field is null.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101 — Electric Plant Accounts 301–399; Gas Plant Accounts 101–399

attributes.name: assets_errored_count
attributes.description: Number of fixed asset records that encountered errors and were excluded from depreciation calculation during this run. A non-zero value requires investigation and potential rerun. Supports SOX completeness controls over the depreciation process.

attributes.name: assets_processed_count
attributes.description: Total number of fixed asset records processed during this depreciation run. Used for run completeness validation, reconciliation against the fixed asset register count, and identifying partial runs or processing errors.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; SOX Section 404 (completeness assertion)

attributes.name: company_code
attributes.description: SAP company code or ERP legal entity identifier representing the regulated utility entity (e.g., electric operating company, gas distribution company) for which the depreciation run was executed. Supports multi-entity utility holding company structures and separate FERC/PUC regulatory reporting by legal entity.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 810

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this depreciation run record was first captured in the data platform. Used for audit trail and SOX compliance over the depreciation posting process.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the depreciation amounts in this run (e.g., 'USD'). Supports multi-currency reporting for utility holding companies with international operations.

attributes.name: depreciation_area_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the depreciation valuation area for which this run was executed. Common utility depreciation areas: '01' = Book/GAAP, '10' = Federal Tax (MACRS), '15' = State Tax, '20' = Regulatory/FERC, '30' = Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT), '40' = Group/Composite. Each area maintains independent depreciation values per SAP FI-AA configuration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 01|10|15|20|30|40 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA Depreciation Areas; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; IRS MACRS Publication 946

attributes.name: depreciation_area_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the depreciation area (e.g., 'Book/GAAP', 'Federal Tax MACRS', 'State Tax', 'Regulatory/FERC', 'Alternative Minimum Tax', 'Group/Composite'). Supports reporting and audit trail readability without requiring a join to a reference table.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: depreciation_method_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the depreciation calculation method applied during this run. 'SL' = Straight-Line (primary GAAP method for utilities); 'GRP' = Group/Composite (common for utility plant accounts per FERC); 'SYD' = Sum-of-Years-Digits; 'DB' = Declining Balance; 'UOP' = Units-of-Production. Determines the mathematical basis for depreciation expense calculation.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360-10; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101; IRS Publication 946

attributes.name: depreciation_method_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the depreciation method applied (e.g., 'Straight-Line', 'Group/Composite', 'Sum-of-Years-Digits', 'Declining Balance', 'Units-of-Production'). Supports FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 reporting and rate case cost-of-service documentation.

attributes.name: depreciation_rate
attributes.description: The composite or average depreciation rate (expressed as a decimal, e.g., 0.033333 for 3.3333%) applied during this run. For group/composite depreciation, this is the PUC-approved composite rate from the most recent depreciation study. For straight-line, this is the reciprocal of the average service life. Key parameter for depreciation study true-up analysis.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Depreciation Study; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: depreciation_rate_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the depreciation rates applied in this run are interim rates (provisionally approved by the PUC pending final order), final rates (approved in a final PUC order), proposed rates (filed but not yet approved), or approved rates (in effect under current tariff). Critical for regulatory accounting and rate case true-up calculations.
attributes.references: PUC Depreciation Study Requirements; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: System-generated error message text when run_status = 'error'. Captures the ERP error description to support troubleshooting and resolution of failed depreciation runs. Null when the run completed successfully.

attributes.name: ferc_plant_account
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Plant Account
attributes.description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts plant account number to which the depreciation expense from this run is attributed (e.g., '403' = Depreciation Expense — Electric, '404' = Amortization of Limited-Term Electric Plant). Required for FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 depreciation and amortization reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Part 101; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year to which this depreciation run applies. Determines the general ledger period into which depreciation expense is posted.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year (four-digit integer, e.g., 2024) to which this depreciation run applies. Aligns with the utility's GAAP and FERC regulatory accounting fiscal year for financial statement preparation and FERC Form 1 reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336

attributes.name: gross_plant_amount
attributes.description: Total gross plant-in-service value (in USD) of the assets processed in this depreciation run as of the run date. Represents the depreciable asset base. Used to validate the depreciation rate applied (total_depreciation_amount / gross_plant_amount) and supports rate base calculations in rate case cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1; GAAP ASC 360; PUC Rate Case Cost-of-Service

attributes.name: is_repeat_run
attributes.description: Indicates whether this run is a repeat execution for a period that was previously processed (True) or a first-time run for the period (False). Repeat runs occur after reversals or corrections. Relevant for SOX controls over duplicate depreciation postings.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: is_simulation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this depreciation run was executed in simulation (test) mode without posting to the general ledger (True) or as a live posting run (False). Simulation runs are used to preview depreciation amounts before period-end close.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the run initiator or approver describing the purpose, scope, or any exceptions associated with this depreciation run (e.g., 'Year-end true-up run applying final PUC-approved rates from Docket 2024-001', 'Repeat run after reversal of period 6 posting error').

attributes.name: planned_depreciation_amount
attributes.description: The budgeted or planned depreciation amount for this fiscal period and depreciation area, as established in the depreciation study or annual budget. Compared against total_depreciation_amount to identify variances for depreciation study true-up analysis and rate case cost-of-service reconciliation.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; PUC Depreciation Study Requirements

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the depreciation amounts were posted to the general ledger. May differ from run_date if the run was simulated first and posted later. Critical for period-end close cutoff and GAAP accrual accounting.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: posting_document_number
attributes.description: ERP financial document number (e.g., SAP FI document number) generated when depreciation amounts are posted to the general ledger. Provides the audit trail linkage between the depreciation run and the actual GL posting for SOX compliance and external audit support.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: reversal_date
attributes.description: The date on which the depreciation run posting was reversed in the general ledger. Null if not reversed. Used in conjunction with reversal_document_number to track corrected depreciation entries.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 250; SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA

attributes.name: reversal_document_number
attributes.description: ERP financial document number of the reversal posting if this depreciation run was reversed. Null if the run has not been reversed. Supports audit trail for corrected depreciation postings and SOX compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 250 (Accounting Changes and Error Corrections)

attributes.name: run_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the depreciation calculation run was executed. This is the principal business event date — the date the depreciation program was triggered in the asset accounting system.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: run_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the depreciation calculation program completed execution. Used with run_start_timestamp to measure total processing duration for operational monitoring of the period-end close process.

attributes.name: run_initiator
attributes.description: User ID or system account that initiated the depreciation run in the ERP system. Required for SOX audit trail to establish accountability over the depreciation posting process and segregation of duties compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP Internal Controls

attributes.name: run_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier assigned to the depreciation run by the ERP system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA depreciation run document number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail reference.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: run_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the depreciation calculation program began execution in the ERP system. Used with run_end_timestamp to measure processing duration and identify performance issues with large asset portfolios.

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the depreciation run. 'planned' indicates scheduled but not yet executed; 'simulated' indicates a test run without posting; 'posted' indicates amounts have been committed to the general ledger; 'reversed' indicates the posting has been reversed; 'error' indicates the run failed during processing.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: run_type
attributes.description: Classification of the depreciation run by its business purpose. 'periodic' = standard monthly/quarterly run; 'year_end' = annual closing run; 'special' = off-cycle run for asset disposals or acquisitions; 'repeat' = rerun of a previously executed period.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA AFAB; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this depreciation run record was sourced (e.g., 'SAP_S4', 'ORACLE_ERP'). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks lakehouse silver layer.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; Oracle ERP Cloud Fixed Assets

attributes.name: total_depreciation_amount
attributes.description: Total depreciation expense amount (in USD) calculated and posted during this run across all assets processed. This is the gross depreciation charge for the period and depreciation area. Key input for rate case cost-of-service calculations, FERC Form 1 Schedule 336 reporting, and GAAP income statement depreciation expense line.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 360; FERC Form 1 Schedule 336; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this depreciation run record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks status changes such as reversal or error correction for SOX audit trail.

products.name: opex_transaction
products.description: Transactional record capturing operating expenditures (O&M costs) posted to the general ledger, including labor, materials, contractor services, fuel costs (FAC-eligible), and overhead allocations. Captures transaction date, amount, FERC O&M account (e.g., Account 500-series for Electric Operation, Account 800-series for Gas Operation), cost center, functional area, expense category, purchase order reference, vendor, and approval status. Supports OPEX tracking against budget, rate case O&M cost-of-service studies, and FERC Form 1/2 O&M expense reporting.
products.reference: FERC USoA O&M Accounts 500-899 / SAP S/4HANA CO Cost Element Accounting

attributes.name: opex_transaction_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each operating expenditure transaction record in the general ledger. Primary key for the opex_transaction data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Reference to the organizational cost center to which this OPEX transaction is charged. Cost centers align with functional areas such as generation, transmission, distribution, or gas operations. Used for departmental O&M budget tracking and rate case cost allocation.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: opex_transaction has fiscal_year and fiscal_period attributes. financial_period is the master for fiscal periods. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full period metadata. fiscal_year and

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: opex_transaction has gl_account_code attribute. gl_account is the master for GL accounts. Normalizing this reference allows joining to get full account details (account_name, ferc_account_description,

attributes.name: master_id
attributes.description: Reference to the utility asset (generation unit, transmission line, distribution equipment, or gas pipeline segment) for which this O&M expenditure was incurred. Links to the asset master in Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo. Critical for distinguishing maintenance OPEX from capital improvements (CAPEX) and for asset-level cost tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NERC FAC-003; IEEE

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the purchase order associated with this OPEX transaction for contractor services, materials, or fuel procurement. Links to the procurement module in SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud. Supports three-way match (PO, goods receipt, invoice) for SOX procure-to-pay controls.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the vendor or supplier associated with this OPEX transaction, applicable for contractor services, materials procurement, and fuel purchases. Links to the vendor master in the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Serves as the PARTY_REFERENCE for external counterparty transactions.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the maintenance or construction work order (from Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo) that generated this OPEX transaction. Enables linkage between O&M labor and materials costs and specific asset maintenance activities. Critical for distinguishing OPEX from CAPEX in rate case filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NERC FAC-003

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the OPEX transaction. Tracks the transaction from initial entry through approval, posting to the general ledger, and potential reversal. Essential for SOX internal controls compliance and financial close processes.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the individual who approved this OPEX transaction per the utility's delegation of authority matrix. Required for SOX internal controls documentation and financial audit trails. Populated upon transition to 'approved' or 'posted' approval_status.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the OPEX transaction received final approval in the ERP workflow. Distinct from created_timestamp and updated_timestamp; captures the specific lifecycle event of approval. Used for SOX controls testing and financial close cycle time analysis.

attributes.name: budget_amount
attributes.description: Approved O&M budget amount for the cost center and FERC account combination for the applicable fiscal period. Enables budget-to-actual variance analysis at the transaction level. Supports financial planning and rate case test-year budget justification.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the OPEX transaction record was first created in the source ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Used for audit trail, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking in the Silver layer.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the transaction amount (e.g., 'USD'). Required for multi-currency ERP environments and FERC financial reporting. Utility operations are predominantly USD but may include CAD for cross-border transmission operations.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: employee_code
attributes.description: Reference to the employee associated with this OPEX transaction, applicable for labor cost postings (direct labor, overtime, benefits allocations) originating from the payroll system (SuccessFactors or Workday). Null for non-labor transactions such as vendor invoices or fuel purchases.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 500-series (labor); GAAP

attributes.name: expense_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the operating expenditure type. Categories align with standard O&M cost-of-service study breakdowns used in rate case filings before state Public Utility Commissions (PUCs) and FERC. Labor includes direct and indirect employee costs; contractor_services covers third-party O&M contracts; fuel covers FAC-eligible fuel costs.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: ferc_account_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
attributes.description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts account number to which this O&M expense is classified. Electric O&M accounts include the 500-series (Electric Operation) and 500-599 range; Gas O&M accounts include the 800-series (Gas Operation). Directly drives FERC Form 1 (electric) and FERC Form 2 (gas) O&M expense schedule reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201)

attributes.name: ferc_account_description
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Description
attributes.description: Descriptive label for the FERC Uniform System of Accounts account code (e.g., 'Account 501 - Fuel', 'Account 510 - Steam Power Generation Operation', 'Account 803 - Natural Gas Purchased for Resale'). Provides human-readable context for financial reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201)

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year in which this OPEX transaction is recognized. Used for period-end close, monthly O&M variance reporting, and regulatory test-year normalization.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year (four-digit integer, e.g., 2024) in which this OPEX transaction is recognized for financial reporting purposes. Aligns with the utility's regulatory fiscal year used in FERC Form 1/2 annual reports and rate case test-year filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: functional_area
attributes.description: Utility functional area to which this OPEX transaction is attributed, aligned with FERC Uniform System of Accounts functional classifications. Used to allocate O&M costs between electric and gas operations and between generation, transmission, and distribution for rate case cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1/2 reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201); NARUC

attributes.name: is_capex_reclassified
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transaction was initially posted as OPEX but subsequently reclassified as a capital expenditure (CAPEX) following engineering or accounting review. OPEX-to-CAPEX reclassifications are common in utility accounting and are subject to regulatory scrutiny in rate cases.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: is_fac_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this OPEX transaction represents a fuel cost eligible for recovery through the Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) mechanism. FAC-eligible costs (e.g., natural gas, coal, nuclear fuel purchases) are tracked separately for regulatory pass-through rate adjustments filed with state PUCs.
attributes.references: State PUC FAC tariff provisions; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 501

attributes.name: is_rate_case_includable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this OPEX transaction is includable in the utility's rate case cost-of-service study as a recoverable O&M expense. Transactions flagged as non-includable (e.g., lobbying costs, penalties, shareholder expenses) are excluded from the revenue requirement calculation per PUC and FERC guidelines.
attributes.references: State PUC rate case guidelines; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC

attributes.name: net_amount
attributes.description: Net total amount of the OPEX transaction after applying overhead allocations, adjustments, and any credits or reversals. Represents the final O&M cost recognized in the general ledger for this transaction. Used as the basis for FERC Form 1/2 O&M expense schedule line items.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: original_transaction_number
attributes.description: For reversal or correcting entries, the transaction_number of the original OPEX transaction being reversed or corrected. Enables audit trail linkage between original postings and their reversals. Null for original (non-reversal) transactions.
attributes.references: GAAP; SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: overhead_allocation_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of indirect overhead costs allocated to this OPEX transaction using the utility's cost allocation methodology (e.g., labor-hour basis, direct-cost basis). Overhead allocations are scrutinized in rate case cost-of-service studies to ensure only appropriate costs are included in revenue requirement calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC; PUC rate case guidelines

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the OPEX transaction was posted to the general ledger accounting period. May differ from transaction_date due to accrual adjustments or late postings. Determines the fiscal period for financial statement inclusion.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: project_code
attributes.description: Internal project or WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) code from the ERP system to which this OPEX transaction is charged. Used for project-level O&M cost tracking, particularly for multi-year maintenance programs, storm restoration activities, and demand-side management (DSM) program cost tracking.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: The quantity of goods, services, or resources consumed in this OPEX transaction (e.g., labor hours, MCF of natural gas, MWh of fuel energy, units of materials). Used in conjunction with unit_of_measure for unit cost analysis and fuel consumption tracking for FAC filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; AGA; IEEE

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: The regulatory jurisdiction (e.g., 'FERC', 'CA-CPUC', 'TX-PUC', 'NY-PSC') under whose rate-making authority this OPEX transaction falls. Used to allocate costs between FERC-jurisdictional (wholesale/transmission) and state PUC-jurisdictional (retail distribution) rate bases in cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: FERC (18 CFR); State PUC tariff provisions; NARUC

attributes.name: reversal_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this OPEX transaction is a reversal entry (credit memo or correcting journal entry) that offsets a previously posted transaction. Reversal transactions are common for accrual reversals at period-end and for correcting misposted O&M costs.
attributes.references: GAAP; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: source_document_type
attributes.description: Classification of the originating document type that generated this OPEX transaction in the ERP system. Distinguishes between vendor invoices, manual journal entries, period-end accruals, payroll cost allocations, intercompany charges, and goods receipts. Used for financial audit and SOX controls testing.
attributes.references: GAAP; SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this OPEX transaction originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver layer and enables source-system reconciliation during financial close. Primary sources are SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud for financial postings, with work order costs originating from Oracle WAM or IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: transaction_amount
attributes.description: Gross base amount of the operating expenditure in the transaction currency before any adjustments, discounts, or overhead allocations. Represents the raw O&M cost posted to the general ledger. Used for OPEX budget variance analysis and FERC O&M expense reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

attributes.name: transaction_date
attributes.description: The principal real-world business event date on which the operating expenditure was incurred or the cost was recognized. Used for period-end accruals, FERC O&M expense reporting, and rate case cost-of-service study period alignment.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

attributes.name: transaction_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the operating expenditure as entered in the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Provides context for the nature of the O&M cost, such as 'Turbine blade inspection labor - Unit 3' or 'Natural gas fuel purchase - Peaker Plant'. Used in audit reviews and rate case cost justification.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SOX Section 302/404

attributes.name: transaction_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the OPEX transaction as assigned by the ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP Cloud). Corresponds to the document number or journal entry number used in financial reporting and audit trails. Supports FERC Form 1/2 O&M expense reconciliation.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 420

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the quantity field (e.g., 'hours' for labor, 'MCF' for natural gas volume, 'MWh' for fuel energy, 'EA' for each/unit of materials). Enables unit cost calculations and fuel consumption analysis for Fuel Adjustment Clause (FAC) regulatory filings.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; AGA; IEEE

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the OPEX transaction record was last modified in the source ERP system. Tracks reversals, corrections, and approval workflow updates. Required for incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Silver layer.

attributes.name: utility_type
attributes.description: Identifies whether this OPEX transaction relates to electric utility operations, gas utility operations, or common/shared utility costs. Required for cost separation between electric and gas rate bases in combined electric-and-gas utility rate cases filed with state PUCs and FERC.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101 / Part 201); NARUC

attributes.name: vendor_invoice_number
attributes.description: The invoice number provided by the vendor or contractor for this OPEX transaction. Used for three-way match (PO, goods receipt, invoice) in the procure-to-pay process and for SOX accounts payable controls. Enables traceability from the general ledger entry back to the source vendor document.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302/404; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

products.name: profit_center
products.description: Master record for profit centers representing the utility's business segments used for internal profitability reporting and regulatory segment reporting. Captures profit center code, description, responsible manager, business segment (electric generation, electric transmission, electric distribution, gas distribution, unregulated), company code, controlling area, and active status. Supports FERC-required segment reporting, ROE (Return on Equity) and ROI analysis by business unit, and EBITDA reporting by segment. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO-PCA) module.
products.reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Profit Center Accounting / FERC Segment Reporting

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the profit center record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key generated by the lakehouse ingestion pipeline from SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA module.

attributes.name: allowed_roe_percent
attributes.description: Regulatory-approved return on equity percentage for this profit center as determined in the most recent rate case or FERC order. Used to calculate the allowed return component in cost-of-service studies and PBR performance tracking.
attributes.references: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission); State PUC Rate Orders; NARUC

attributes.name: business_segment
attributes.description: Regulatory and operational business segment to which this profit center belongs. Drives FERC-required segment reporting and ROE/ROI analysis by business unit. Values align with the utility's FERC Form 1 and state PUC segment reporting requirements: electric_generation, electric_transmission, electric_distribution, gas_distribution, unregulated.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: capex_budget_usd
attributes.description: Approved annual capital expenditure budget allocated to this profit center in US dollars. Used for CAPEX tracking, rate base calculations, and AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) accruals in regulatory accounting.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

attributes.name: ciac_eligible
attributes.business_glossary_term: Contribution in Aid of Construction (CIAC) Eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this profit center is eligible to receive Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC) from customers or developers. CIAC receipts reduce rate base and are tracked separately per FERC Account 271 and state PUC requirements.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (Account 271); State PUC CIAC Rules

attributes.name: company_code
attributes.description: SAP Company Code (BUKRS) representing the legal entity to which this profit center is assigned. Used for GAAP financial statement preparation and SOX compliance segregation. Maps to the utility's legal corporate structure.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI; GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles); SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

attributes.name: controlling_area_code
attributes.description: SAP Controlling Area (KOKRS) to which this profit center belongs. Defines the organizational unit within which cost and profit accounting is performed. All profit centers within a controlling area share the same fiscal year variant and currency.

attributes.name: cost_center_assignment
attributes.description: Default cost center code associated with this profit center for overhead allocation and cost-of-service studies. Used in rate case preparation to allocate shared costs between regulated business segments per FERC and PUC requirements.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Cost Allocation Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this profit center record was first created in the source SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA system. Used for audit trail, SOX compliance, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the profit center's reporting currency (e.g., USD). Defines the currency in which profit center financial results are reported and consolidated.

attributes.name: depreciation_method
attributes.description: Depreciation method applied to capital assets assigned to this profit center. Regulatory depreciation rates are typically set by PUC order and may differ from GAAP depreciation. Impacts rate base calculations and FERC account 403 (Depreciation and Amortization of Electric Plant).
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; State PUC Depreciation Orders

attributes.name: energy_commodity
attributes.description: Primary energy commodity handled by this profit center. Distinguishes electric utility operations from gas distribution operations for FERC Form 1 vs. Form 2 reporting, and for separate rate case cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: FERC Form 1; FERC Form 2; AGA (American Gas Association); State PUC regulations

attributes.name: ferc_account_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Class
attributes.description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts classification associated with this profit center (e.g., Electric Plant in Service accounts 301-399, Gas Plant accounts 101-199). Drives regulatory financial reporting on FERC Form 1 and Form 2.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1; FERC Form 2

attributes.name: fiscal_year_variant
attributes.description: SAP Fiscal Year Variant (PERIV) that defines the fiscal year calendar applicable to this profit center. Determines period boundaries for financial reporting, budget cycles, and FERC annual report preparation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; GAAP; FERC Form 1

attributes.name: functional_area
attributes.description: SAP Functional Area (FUNC_AREA) assigned to this profit center, used to classify costs by business function (e.g., generation operations, transmission operations, distribution operations, customer service, administration). Supports FERC functional cost classification and CAPEX/OPEX segregation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: gl_account_assignment_group
attributes.description: GL account assignment group that governs automatic account determination for revenue and cost postings to this profit center. Ensures correct FERC account mapping for regulated utility accounting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI-CO; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: hierarchy_node
attributes.description: Node identifier within the SAP profit center standard hierarchy (SETCLASS 0106) to which this profit center is assigned. Enables roll-up reporting across organizational levels for EBITDA and segment reporting.

attributes.name: intercompany_elimination_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether transactions posted to this profit center are subject to intercompany elimination in consolidated financial statements. Critical for SOX-compliant consolidation and FERC affiliate transaction reporting.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 810; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); FERC Standards of Conduct

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this profit center record in the source SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA system. Supports change tracking, SOX audit requirements, and incremental data pipeline processing.

attributes.name: long_description
attributes.description: Extended description of the profit center providing full business context, including the scope of operations, regulatory segment, and reporting purpose. Corresponds to LTEXT in SAP CEPC.

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
attributes.description: NERC reliability region (e.g., WECC, SERC, RFC, MRO) associated with this profit center's electric operations. Used for NERC compliance reporting and bulk electric system (BES) reliability cost allocation.
attributes.references: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation); FERC Order 693

attributes.name: opex_budget_usd
attributes.description: Approved annual operating expenditure budget allocated to this profit center in US dollars. Supports O&M cost tracking, rate case cost-of-service studies, and EBITDA reporting by segment.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP; State PUC Cost-of-Service Guidelines

attributes.name: plant_location_code
attributes.description: Geographic or operational location code associated with this profit center, linking it to a specific generation plant, transmission substation, distribution district, or gas service territory. Used in GIS-integrated financial analysis and asset management reporting.
attributes.references: ESRI ArcGIS; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; IEEE

attributes.name: profit_center_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the profit center within the SAP S/4HANA Controlling (CO-PCA) module. Used in journal entries, cost allocations, and regulatory segment reports. Corresponds to the PRCTR field in SAP table CEPC.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: profit_center_group
attributes.description: Grouping identifier used to aggregate profit centers for management reporting, EBITDA analysis, and regulatory segment reporting. Corresponds to SAP profit center groups (SETCLASS 0106) used in report painter/writer reports.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: profit_center_name
attributes.description: Human-readable short name of the profit center as maintained in SAP CO-PCA (KTEXT field in CEPC). Used in financial reports, dashboards, and rate case cost-of-service studies.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: profit_center_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the profit center record. Active profit centers accept postings; locked centers are frozen for new transactions; inactive centers are retired from use. Corresponds to the LOCK_IND and PRCTR_STATUS indicators in SAP CEPC.

attributes.name: profit_center_type
attributes.description: Classification of the profit center by regulatory and operational type. Regulated centers are subject to PUC/FERC oversight and rate-of-return regulation; unregulated centers operate in competitive markets; corporate centers capture holding company costs; shared_services centers allocate common costs.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC regulations

attributes.name: rate_base_usd
attributes.description: Regulatory rate base value assigned to this profit center in US dollars, representing the net investment on which the utility is permitted to earn a regulated return. Used in ROE calculations and rate case cost-of-service studies filed with FERC and state PUCs.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Case Guidelines; NARUC

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Indicates the regulatory jurisdiction governing this profit center's rates and operations. Federal indicates FERC jurisdiction (transmission, wholesale); state indicates PUC jurisdiction (distribution, retail); both indicates dual jurisdiction; unregulated indicates competitive/non-regulated operations.
attributes.references: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission); State PUC regulations; NARUC

attributes.name: responsible_manager_code
attributes.description: Employee identifier of the manager accountable for the financial performance of this profit center. Corresponds to the VERAK field in SAP CEPC. Used for accountability reporting and performance-based ratemaking (PBR) analysis.

attributes.name: responsible_manager_name
attributes.description: Full name of the manager responsible for this profit center's financial performance. Sourced from SAP HR/CO integration. Used in management reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.

attributes.name: revenue_budget_usd
attributes.description: Approved annual revenue budget for this profit center in US dollars. Used in ROE and ROI analysis by business unit, EBITDA reporting by segment, and variance analysis against actual revenues.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP; State PUC Rate Case Guidelines

attributes.name: rto_iso_membership
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Membership
attributes.description: RTO or ISO market area in which this profit center participates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT). Drives energy market cost allocation, LMP-based settlement, and OATT compliance reporting.
attributes.references: FERC (Federal Energy Regulatory Commission); OATT (Open Access Transmission Tariff); RTO/ISO tariffs

attributes.name: segment_reporting_code
attributes.description: Code used to map this profit center to a reportable segment under GAAP ASC 280 (Segment Reporting) and FERC segment reporting requirements. Enables aggregation of profit centers into disclosed business segments in annual reports and FERC filings.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 280 (Segment Reporting); FERC Form 1; SEC Regulation S-X

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the operational source system from which this profit center record was ingested (e.g., SAP_S4HANA_PROD, SAP_S4HANA_QA). Supports data lineage, multi-system reconciliation, and Silver Layer provenance tracking.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; Enterprise Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: sox_relevant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this profit center is within scope for SOX internal controls over financial reporting. SOX-relevant profit centers require documented controls, segregation of duties, and periodic management attestation.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 302 and 404; PCAOB Standards

attributes.name: valid_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this profit center is effective and available for financial postings. Corresponds to DATAB in SAP CEPC. Used to enforce temporal validity in period-based financial reporting and rate case cost studies.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: valid_to_date
attributes.description: Date through which this profit center remains effective. Corresponds to DATBI in SAP CEPC. A value of 9999-12-31 indicates an open-ended profit center with no planned deactivation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: wip_account_indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this profit center is designated to capture Work in Progress (WIP) costs for capital projects prior to asset capitalization. When true, costs posted here are subject to AFUDC accrual per FERC accounting requirements.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (Account 107 - Construction Work in Progress); GAAP ASC 835

attributes.name: parent_profit_center_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on profit_center (parent_profit_center_id)

products.name: rate_case_cost_study
products.description: Master record for cost-of-service studies prepared in support of rate case filings with state PUCs or FERC. Captures rate case identifier, filing jurisdiction (PUC state, FERC), test year, rate case type (general rate case, transmission rate case, gas rate case), total revenue requirement, rate base amount, authorized ROE, WACC, O&M expense allocation, depreciation expense, taxes, and filing status. Links to supporting GL accounts, cost centers, and CAPEX projects. Supports CPCN applications, IRP cost justifications, and PBR performance target derivation.
products.reference: FERC / PUC Rate Case Cost-of-Service Study / NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

attributes.name: rate_case_cost_study_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the rate case cost-of-service study record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: rate_case_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent rate case docket for which this cost-of-service study was prepared. Links to the regulatory.rate_case product.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Filing Requirements

attributes.name: accumulated_depreciation_amount
attributes.description: Total accumulated depreciation deducted from gross plant in service to arrive at net plant in rate base. Expressed in US dollars. Corresponds to FERC Account 108.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108; GAAP ASC 360

attributes.name: adit_amount
attributes.description: Accumulated Deferred Income Tax (ADIT) balance deducted from rate base, representing the tax benefits of accelerated depreciation that have been passed through to customers. Expressed in US dollars. Corresponds to FERC Account 190/282/283.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Accounts 190/282/283; GAAP ASC 740

attributes.name: afudc_amount
attributes.business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Amount
attributes.description: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) capitalized during the test year, representing the cost of financing construction work in progress (WIP). Expressed in US dollars. Corresponds to FERC Accounts 107 and 432.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts Accounts 107/432; GAAP ASC 980-835

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which the regulatory authority (PUC or FERC) issued a final order approving the rates derived from this cost-of-service study. Null if the study has not yet received final regulatory approval.
attributes.references: FERC Rules of Practice and Procedure 18 CFR Part 385; State PUC Final Order Requirements

attributes.name: authorized_roe_pct
attributes.description: Authorized or proposed Return on Equity (ROE) percentage used in the cost-of-service study to calculate the equity component of the allowed return on rate base. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 9.5000 for 9.5%). Benchmarked against comparable utility ROE awards by the PUC or FERC.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; GAAP ASC 980

attributes.name: capex_amount
attributes.description: Total Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) included in or supporting the rate base determination for this cost-of-service study. Represents plant additions during the test year or projected capital investment period. Expressed in US dollars.
attributes.references: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; GAAP ASC 360; NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy

attributes.name: cost_allocation_method
attributes.description: Methodology used to allocate costs among customer classes or rate jurisdictions in this cost-of-service study. Fully Distributed Cost (FDC) allocates all costs; Marginal Cost reflects incremental costs; Embedded Cost uses historical average costs; Hybrid combines approaches.
attributes.references: NARUC Utility Regulatory Policy; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: cost_of_debt_pct
attributes.description: Embedded cost of long-term debt used in the WACC calculation, representing the weighted average interest rate on the utility's outstanding debt instruments. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 4.8500 for 4.85%).
